eurxt-caceis.title: A Euro Token on CACEIS Bank's Balance Sheet
eurxt-caceis.text: EURXT is the euro e-money token Crédit Agricole S.A. launched on July 1 2026, issued on Ethereum by CACEIS Bank S.A. under a MiCA white paper. Only professional clients of CACEIS Bank can buy it from the issuer, with a 10,000 EURXT minimum, yet any Ethereum address that is not blacklisted can hold and transfer it. On November 1 2026, however, one wallet held the entire supply, which has stood at 54,366,000 EURXT since September 25 2026. Crédit Agricole describes the reserve as cash on CACEIS Bank's balance sheet, but the white paper allows up to 70% in highly liquid financial instruments. No independent reserve {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} had been located by November 1 2026, and stable-xt.io computes its reserve figure from the token's on-chain supply. A single-key wallet can blacklist a holder and seize its balance, a second can pause all transfers, and a third can replace the contract logic, whose deployed source is unverified. Pharos lists EURXT pre-launch because no admitted source prices it. Under the white paper, holders are unsecured creditors of CACEIS Bank, with par {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and no issuer fee from 9:00 to 17:00 on French bank business days, after KYC if they are not its clients.

aedz-zand.title: Zand Trust's Dirham Payment Token
aedz-zand.text: AEDZ is the dirham payment token of Zand Trust, a wholly owned Zand Bank subsidiary licensed by the Central Bank of the UAE, issued on Ethereum and Solana. Exactly 1 billion of the roughly 1.006 billion AEDZ on chain on November 1 2026 sat in eleven wallets, each funded by one transfer on September 30 or October 7 2026 and unmoved since. The issuer counts those balances as circulating, and its daily feed showed 1.01 billion AEDZ against AED 1.01 billion of reserves on October 30 2026. AJMS LG's {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} as of October 1 2026 found AED 806.33 million of reserves against 806.30 million AEDZ, mostly term deposits. Pharos lists AEDZ pre-launch because no source prices it, no DEX pool exists and no admitted path sums supply across both chains, though the issuer says it is available on partner exchanges. On Ethereum one admin address has held every role since deployment and can freeze wallets, force transfers, burn from any holder and replace the implementation. Onboarded institutions {{term:redemption}}redeem{{/term}} 1:1 through Zand Bank's corporate banking platform, paying a fee of 10 bps or AED 200, whichever is higher.

ddsc-aedc.title: A Licensed Dirham Token on ADI Chain
ddsc-aedc.text: DDSC is a dirham payment token licensed by the Central Bank of the UAE and issued on ADI Chain, a zk-rollup Layer 2 that settles to Ethereum. Its October 2025 white paper named the issuer AEDC Stable Coin L.L.C., owned 34% by Sirius Investment Holding and 33% each by IHC Capital Holding and 1968B SPV. The DDSC site now names AEDC Stable Coin Network and Distribution L.L.C. as the licensed issuer. Authorized Distribution Partners, not the issuer, onboard holders after KYC/KYB checks and process 1:1 issuance and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} to UAE bank accounts. By November 1 2026 the contract had minted 345.7 million DDSC and burned 297.5 million, leaving 48,280,499 across 87 addresses. The white paper commits 100% AED cash in segregated escrow at qualified banks it does not name. The issuer's feed reported reserves equal to supply on November 1 2026 and names Crowe as attestor, but posts no {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} report. Under the white paper, transfers can be frozen or reversed where law, sanctions or fraud prevention require, and the implementation, whose source is unverified, carries freeze, pause and upgrade selectors. As long as DDSC lives on ADI Chain, which is outside Pharos's chain registry, its deployment and supply cannot enter Pharos runtime data.

zlusd-zelle.title: Zelle's Dollar Token, Issued by Anchorage
zlusd-zelle.text: ZelleUSD is the dollar stablecoin that Early Warning Services, operator of the Zelle network, unveiled on June 11 2026 in a release that named no issuer, chain or launch date. The Solana mint identifies Anchorage Digital Bank N.A. as issuer. All 30 mint transactions were signed by the key that also mints the Anchorage-issued USDPT and USDGO, and the token metadata, hosted by Anchorage, names the bank as issuer for Zelle. Supply was 137,650.11 ZLUSD across 14 funded wallets on November 1 2026. No source prices it and no DEX pool exists, so Pharos lists it pre-launch. The permanent delegate, also the mint authority, signed all nine burns from holder accounts without the owners' signatures, 20,612 ZLUSD in total, and can burn or move any holder's balance. A freeze authority has frozen the accounts of five specific wallets, none since thawed, and a pause authority can halt transfers. Anchorage's covered stablecoin terms back every stablecoin the bank issues with one aggregate reserve in a South Dakota express trust. The announcement and token metadata disclose no ZLUSD reserve composition, custodian or {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. The terms let ZLUSD move to addresses outside Anchorage's client base, but the bank issues to and {{term:redemption}}redeems{{/term}} from its own clients only.

dotusd-polkadot.title: Polkadot's OpenGov Dollar, Minted Against USDT
dotusd-polkadot.text: dotUSD is a dollar stablecoin created by Polkadot OpenGov referendum 1944 and live on Asset Hub since October 8 2026. The Polkadot Community Foundation's proposal asked the Treasury to seed a DOT/dotUSD pool with $2.5 million of DOT and $2.5 million of USDT minted into dotUSD. In this first phase, dotUSD can be minted and redeemed one-to-one only against USDT, through a capped {{term:psm}}peg stability module{{/term}}; DOT-collateral vaults are left to a later phase. The DOT in the pool is swap liquidity, not collateral. On October 26 the Polkadot Technical Fellowship disclosed a cross-consensus messaging (XCM) bug that had removed about 4.06 million dotUSD from the recorded supply while the tokens stayed in the pool. Arbitrage against the resulting imbalance cost the Treasury's liquidity position an estimated $1.3 million. Referendum 1961 recalculated the recorded supply from existing balances on October 30, without changing any holder's balance. Asset Hub showed 4.21 million dotUSD across 60 accounts on November 1 2026. Pharos tracks it pre-launch because no admitted source prices it: CoinGecko's dotusd preview carries a null price and DefiLlama has no listing. Until DOT-collateral vaults ship, the declared backing is entirely USDT, so dotUSD inherits Tether's issuer controls.

usdrf-realfi.title: RealFi's Tranched Credit Dollar on Cardano
usdrf-realfi.text: USDrf is RealFi's dollar token on Cardano, launched on mainnet on October 1 2026 alongside sUSDrf, its junior staked token. Supply was 5.40 million USDrf on November 1 2026. The backing is an off-chain book of Treasury bills, money market funds, floating-rate credit, CLO ETFs and private credit. RealFi publishes allocation ranges, which describe strategy rather than verified current holdings. Protocol first-loss reserves and sUSDrf absorb losses before USDrf does. Pharos classes that mechanism as a credit fund, which places USDrf among stable-value investments rather than in the core stablecoin totals. Direct minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are limited to whitelisted institutions under an Institutional Minting Agreement, through a human-approved first-in, first-out queue with daily and monthly limits. RealFi's docs name TxPipe, Anastasia Labs and Halborn as auditors and HT Digital as reserve {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} provider, but none of their reports had been published by November 1. Pharos tracks it pre-launch because no admitted source prices it: CoinGecko's realfi-usdrf preview has a null price, and DefiLlama's quote is a generic fallback shared by 90 assets rather than a market price. Holders outside the institutional whitelist have no direct redemption; they exit by selling on decentralized exchanges.

swanusd-swan.title: An anonymous wstETH CDP on Monolith
swanusd-swan.text: swanUSD is SwanDAO's dollar stablecoin, minted against wstETH in a single Monolith Lender built by the Inverse Finance team. No legal entity, jurisdiction, team page or terms of service is published, and the only risk disclosure is Monolith's protocol-level risks page rather than an issuer statement. Governance is nominally a DAO, but one 3-of-6 Safe holds 80% of sSWAN votes, manages the Lender, and owns the entire Curve pool LP position. Borrowers post wstETH at an 85% collateral factor. Interest-free debt can be redeemed against at the oracle price less 1.75%; paid debt pays a variable rate, and sSwanUSD stakers receive half of that interest. A USDS peg-stability reserve held as sUSDS mints and burns 1:1, caps sells at its balance, and stops buying at the 2030 immutability deadline. Published audits cover the core contracts but not the DAO stack, the exact deployed bytecode's audit scope is not established, and swanUSD's own contracts sit outside Monolith's live bounty. Exit depth rests on one thin Curve pool and a PSM reserve that shrinks with every sell.

jltxx-jpmorgan.title: Government fund, issuer-controlled tokens
jltxx-jpmorgan.text: JLTXX represents Token Class shares in JPMorgan's government money-market fund, which targets a $1 net asset value and distributes income in additional same-class shares. Treasury securities, overnight collateralized repos and cash support the fund; published class assets do not certify circulating token supply or executable redemption capacity. The legal Investor Register determines ownership. Ordinary redemption pays USD cash, with optional third-party stablecoin conversion. For redemptions worth $250,000 or more, the Fund may instead deliver part or all in readily marketable securities valued at NAV. Converting those securities to cash can expose investors to market risk and may entail taxable gains, brokerage costs or other charges. Ordinary payment within seven days remains subject to suspension exceptions. Pinned Ethereum reads bind minting and upgrades to single-owner accounts without an on-chain collateral ceiling or execution delay; administrators can restrict transfers and redemptions. Pharos keeps the token quarantined while the native-share perimeter, including Solana, and runtime price and supply admission remain unresolved. The prospectus and statement of additional information name an annual auditor, but no current audit report for the exact fund was retrieved, so the class-asset figures remain issuer-published and do not reconcile token liabilities.

armusdcs-wintermute.title: Wintermute USDC lending with private-credit collateral
armusdcs-wintermute.text: Wintermute USDC Select is a Morpho vault that lends USDC into seven markets secured by bitcoin and liquid-staking collateral, principal tokens, 3Jane USD3 and a Wildcat debt-token wrapper. That wrapper, v-wmtUSDC, holds claims on Wintermute's own uncollateralized Wildcat borrowing, so in its market the collateral is credit on the curator's group. Armitage, the curator, acknowledged in July 2026 that both legs share the same ultimate counterparty risk and that the liquidator may not look like a strong backstop in a Wintermute insolvency, arguing instead that the oracle's progressive markdown and third-party incentives to buy discounted claims supply one. The wrapper is priced from the Wildcat market's scale factor and delinquency discounts, so it marks down on delinquency rather than on a traded price. Borrower interest accrues to the share-to-USDC rate, while lending losses reduce it. A four-of-seven Safe owns the vault and a three-of-six Safe curates it, with all six curator signers also on the owner Safe; that overlap does not establish independent control. Fee and force-deallocation-penalty changes have no configured delay, though both rates were zero when observed. Ordinary withdrawals draw on idle USDC and the configured liquidity market, while broader exits need reallocation or in-kind redemption. Armitage's terms bar UK and US access and promise neither withdrawal timing nor loss protection. Whole-book custody and legal recovery remain uncertain, and a Wintermute credit event would reach both the curator and part of the collateral.

pendleusdc-pendle.title: USDC lending against Pendle principal tokens
pendleusdc-pendle.text: Pendle Ecosystem USDC is co-curated by Pendle and Armitage, Wintermute's vault-curation arm. It lends USDC against principal tokens tied to reUSD, sUSDS and sUSDe maturities. Interest increases assets per share, while realized lending losses and fees reduce the holder's return. Pendle approves eligible collateral; Armitage manages curation and risk parameters. The owner and curator are overlapping multisigs, so their different thresholds do not establish independent control. Share-transfer and ordinary-withdrawal gates are permanently disabled, while the deposit gate remains mutable. Direct redemption draws on idle USDC and one selected liquidity market. Force-deallocation can use liquidity elsewhere; an in-kind exit instead leaves the holder with the underlying lending exposure. The market oracles rely on Pendle pricing and fixed-discount formulas, with no independent live USDC dollar feed. Armitage's terms restrict UK and US access. Available market liquidity and collateral recovery, rather than a fixed-dollar issuer promise, determine exit.

susdat-saturn.title: Preferred-credit yield behind a USDat vault share
susdat-saturn.text: Saturn sUSDat turns USDat deposits into a managed credit-vault share whose value depends mainly on STRCon, an Ondo note tracking Strategy preferred shares. Dividends and vested surplus can increase the exchange rate, while preferred-share losses can reduce it. USDat is a liquidity buffer rather than the vault's dominant backing. Holders can trade on secondary markets or request queued USDat redemption, but operator processing and realizable note liquidity determine when requests settle. Elevated mode currently charges 25 basis points on deposits and 50 on processed redemptions; the fee is determined at processing, not guaranteed when a request enters the queue. A five-day timelock controls native upgrades, while a one-hour timelock controls parameters including oracle replacement. Blacklist and recovery powers remain active features. Visible on-chain holdings and NAV arithmetic do not establish exact note terms, Saturn holder priority or independent whole-book financial reconciliation.

arcusdc-galaxy.title: Galaxy USDC lending on Arc
arcusdc-galaxy.text: Galaxy USDC gives holders a proportional USDC lending claim in a cirBTC-collateralized Morpho market on Arc. Interest, fees and realized losses change the share conversion rate. The underlying BTC is held through Circle's custody structure, adding an offchain collateral dependency to the onchain lending position. Holders do not thereby receive a direct claim on Circle's USDC reserve fund. The vault owner and curator are externally owned accounts, and several parameter changes have no delay. The liquidity adapter is configured, so ordinary redemptions can draw available liquidity from the selected lending market. Total assets exceed immediately available cash. The share-transfer and direct-withdrawal gates are permanently disabled, while deposit gating remains configurable. The documented in-kind fallback leaves a direct lending position and requires executable underlying-market transactions. Neither Galaxy's curator terms nor Circle's Guarded Vaults terms commit either firm to make depositors whole.

bbqusdc-steakhouse-v2.title: Steakhouse USDC lending against structured collateral
bbqusdc-steakhouse-v2.text: Steakhouse High Yield USDC is a Morpho Vault V2 share over USDC, distinct from the legacy Smokehouse vault that uses the same bbqUSDC ticker. Its lending book includes wFalconX, mF-ONE, PT-reUSD, reUSD and weETH collateral. Borrower interest increases assets per share, while fees and credit losses reduce what vault-share holders receive. Ordinary redemption pays USDC only when idle assets and the selected liquidity market can fund it. Force-deallocation and in-kind position transfers are separate routes, not guaranteed cash settlement. The curator is a three-of-nine Safe; a separate one-of-seven allocator Safe can move assets within approved limits. The supervisor’s five-of-ten Safe can replace the curator immediately, despite delayed ownership transfers. Share-transfer and ordinary withdrawal gates are permanently disabled, but deposit gating remains mutable and Circle can freeze the underlying USDC. Current onchain accounting identifies the immediate lender positions without establishing whole-book collateral custody, independent financial assurance or legal priority for vault-share holders.

brsrv-blackrock.title: BlackRock government-fund shares with daily reinvestment
brsrv-blackrock.text: BRSRV records ownership of BlackRock's registered Daily Reinvestment Stablecoin Reserve Vehicle, a distinct fund from BUIDL. The portfolio mandate permits cash, Treasury obligations maturing within 93 days and Treasury-secured overnight repos. Its targeted $1 NAV does not capture holder income: dividends are declared daily and normally reinvested in additional shares on the next business day, with a cash-dividend opt-out. Securitize operates the permissioned shareholder register on Ethereum, Tempo and Solana. Newly minted subscription and reinvestment shares have a 24-hour peer-transfer lock, while remaining redeemable and movable between the same investor's whitelisted wallets. Access generally requires U.S. residency and a waivable $3 million initial investment. Good-order business-day redemptions ordinarily receive same-day wire payment, but the fund reserves seven days and specified emergency suspension rights. BNY Mellon is the named custodian and Deloitte the named auditor; appointment does not establish a current signed whole-token reconciliation. Holder exit, registry corrections and token recovery depend on the transfer agent, and the $1 NAV is a target that carries no guarantee of principal.

btd-alpen.title: Planned BTC-only Liquity V2 dollar on Alpen
btd-alpen.text: Alpen announced Bitcoin Dollar in May 2025 as a BTC-only, overcollateralized debt token built from Liquity V2 for its Bitcoin ZK rollup. The January 2026 recap describes the intended flow: deposit BTC, choose an interest rate and mint BTD. Immutable code and no governance remain stated design goals, with BTC/USD oracle providers intended to be fixed at deployment. No exact BTD production contract, executable redemption route or deployed liquidation and backstop evidence is established. Alpen platform testnets and infrastructure audits do not establish a BTD token launch or audit.

chfsafo-spiko.title: CHF UCITS share with overnight swaps
chfsafo-spiko.text: CHFSAFO is the Swiss-franc accumulation share of the Spiko Amundi Overnight Swap Fund. Amundi manages a securities portfolio whose performance is exchanged through total-return swaps for overnight-rate returns. The issuer names BNP Paribas as banking counterparty. If that counterparty defaults, the fund can retain security-market and residual currency exposure. CACEIS is the named depositary, with legal separation from the manager and the depositary's own assets; complete current collateral and delegated-custody allocations remain undisclosed. Published NAV, share totals and signed holdings are issuer data, not an independent reconciliation of every share class and native register. The retrieved semiannual filing contains no CHF share row or audit opinion despite PwC's statutory appointment. Spiko operates eight permissioned native registers. Observed EVM and Solana controls allow upgrades, with the Solana upgrade path requiring one cryptographic signer. Ordinary redemption uses fund NAV and business-day dealing, subject to KYC, gates, suspension and possible swing pricing.

cscbusdc-clearstar.title: Clearstar Coinbase-asset lending vault
cscbusdc-clearstar.text: Clearstar cbAssets Vault is a USDC-denominated Morpho Vault V2 on Base that lends against Coinbase-wrapped assets and other reviewed collateral positions. Its receipt accrues net borrower interest but bears market credit, collateral and smart-contract risk. Ordinary USDC withdrawals depend on the selected liquidity market; force-deallocation is a separate route with a configurable penalty, rather than additional ordinary redemption liquidity. A three-of-six owner Safe and two-of-three curator Safe govern the deployment, while two allocator Safes can change allocations and the liquidity route without a timelock. One allocator has a one-of-seven signing threshold. Adapter additions and allocation-cap increases have three-day delays, distinct from immediately changeable fee parameters. Share-transfer and direct-withdrawal gates are permanently disabled, although deposit gating and underlying USDC freezing remain relevant. Onchain positions identify operational custody, but borrower-side safeguards, signer independence and shareholder insolvency priority remain unproven.

cumiu-chinaamc.title: ChinaAMC USD fund shares with an off-chain register
cumiu-chinaamc.text: CUMIU represents accumulating Class I USD shares in ChinaAMC’s tokenized money-market fund, with daily NAV redemption through eligible distributors. Its portfolio combines bank deposits and investment-grade money-market instruments, so the Treasury-fund classification does not imply Treasury-only backing. Standard Chartered entities administer the fund and token custody, while the official ownership register and investor settlement remain off-chain. Retrieved KPMG financial statements supply annual independent assurance; more recent interim accounts and NAV figures are issuer publications. Two default administrators can mint, set NAV, freeze transfers and replace the token implementation without an on-chain delay. Two delegated minters can also issue shares and publish NAV. Holders depend on the distributor redemption channel rather than a peer-to-peer or intraday secondary market.

czkc-czkc.title: Czech koruna reserve design in testing
czkc-czkc.text: CZKC a.s. describes a Czech koruna token fully backed by CZK reserves, with rCZKC representing those reserves on-chain. The developer book offers testnet guidance and plans Ethereum, Arbitrum and Gnosis, but leaves production entrypoints and implementations unpublished. CzechInvest named CZKC in its February 2026 sandbox testing cohort; that selection is not MiCA authorization. Pharos records the project as pre-launch without inventing an announcement or launch date. Production identity, binding redemption terms and independent reserve assurance remain unresolved.

earnusd-lido.title: Mellow strategies with conditional USDC exits
earnusd-lido.text: earnUSD compounds returns from Mellow-curated dollar strategies into transferable Lido vault shares. The portfolio spans conservative earnUSDc and experimental earnUSDe vaults; the official interface discloses liquidity provision and leverage risk. Ordinary USDC withdrawals require a non-cancellable request followed by a funded claim. A separate instant USDC rail depends on usable oracle reports, liquidity and rolling-limit headroom. Neither route establishes guaranteed settlement under stress. A five-of-eight Safe can replace share logic, and configurable account restrictions remain possible despite inactive pause and whitelist flags at the October 15 Ethereum observation. The curator's three-of-six quorum now matches Lido's deployment table. Current look-through weights, gearing, downstream custody and complete asset-liability reconciliation remain unestablished. USDC settlement denomination does not make the portfolio equivalent to Circle's cash reserves. Lido's interface terms exclude U.S. and UK citizens or residents and access from those countries.

ethenausdc-steakhouse.title: Ethena balance-sheet USDC vault on Base
ethenausdc-steakhouse.text: Ethena x Steakhouse USDC is a Morpho Vault V2 on Base designed for Ethena balance-sheet allocation. Depositors receive NAV-bearing shares against USDC, with lending gains and losses passed through share accounting. At the October 15, 2026 Base review, almost all accounted assets were idle USDC, with only a residual USDe-collateralized lending claim. Ordinary redemption uses idle USDC first and the configured liquidity market second; force-deallocation and in-kind exits require separate execution. The owner is a Supervisor controlled by a five-of-ten Safe, while the curator Safe is three-of-nine. Curator replacement is immediate, and lending-allocation delays do not cover fee changes. Direct share transfers and withdrawals have zero gates with their setters abdicated, but deposit gating remains mutable and USDC retains Circle's freeze exposure. Onchain accounting and protocol security reviews do not establish vault-level financial assurance or statutory holder insolvency priority.

eurw-newrails.title: Holder-wide euro redemption through SEPA
eurw-newrails.text: EURW gives verified holders, including secondary-market buyers, a right to redeem at one euro through an own-name SEPA account without an ordinary issuer redemption fee. Newrails' Lithuanian electronic-money authorization and exact-token whitepaper establish the issuer and safeguarding framework, but not the current reserve portfolio. No dated EURW reserve reconciliation or named reserve banks were retrieved despite the product's monthly-attestation claim. The whitepaper permits cash and money-market investments; a newer issuer guide describes cash and overnight deposits without publishing measured weights. A complete Monad role-event census identifies separate administrator, minter and allowance-approver accounts. None has deployed code, and the administrator can immediately grant upgrade, blacklist and pause powers that are currently unassigned. Their operational signing safeguards remain undisclosed. Ordinary redemptions depend on verification and SEPA settlement without a numerical completion guarantee or executable-capacity bound. The whitepaper also permits exceptional recovery fees, limits and suspension.

filqa-fidelity-international.title: Fidelity accumulating shares with redemption-only exit
filqa-fidelity-international.text: FILQ-A represents an accumulating share in Fidelity International’s Cayman-domiciled USD Digital Liquidity Fund SP. The latest retrieved August factsheet shows commercial paper, certificates of deposit and bank deposits rather than Treasury-only backing; the prospectus also permits securitisations and interest-rate or currency hedges. Ethereum records the share, but the prospectus rejects token transfers for on-chain investors and makes redemption through the transfer agent or Token Distributor the recognized exit. JPMorgan provides custody and fund accounting. The administrator determines the daily class NAV, and an on-chain feed publishes it on Ethereum. Those arrangements do not establish an independently signed token-to-fund reconciliation, current portfolio weights or controller signing safeguards. Privileged accounts can mint without an on-chain collateral cap, and administrators can replace token logic after a one-second delay. With those gaps open, Pharos does not rate FILQ-A: critical evidence is insufficient for a research rating. Redemption normally runs in London market hours, off-hours facilities depend on available liquidity, and gates or suspension can constrain it.

fiusd-sygnum.title: Fidelity fund units in a Sygnum ledger security
fiusd-sygnum.text: FIUSD represents a Fidelity Institutional Liquidity Fund USD Class G Acc unit held through Sygnum, rather than a dollar payment token or bank deposit. Its accumulating NAV reflects a short-term money-market portfolio that includes bank instruments, commercial paper and repos, not just government debt. Fidelity publishes underlying fund holdings and exact share-class NAV and outstanding units, but these do not identify the units Sygnum holds for tokenholders. Current definitive client terms and an independently signed token-to-unit reconciliation remain unavailable. CoinGecko still reports more units than the combined native zkSync and Arbitrum stock, so Pharos values the complete on-chain roster instead of that provider market cap. Operators can mint without an on-chain reserve cap, and the Arbitrum upgrade administrator is a single account. Redemption requires an onboarded bank-client account and permissioned custody; current same-notional capacity, binding settlement deadlines and all-in costs remain unestablished.

frnt-wyoming.title: Wyoming trust-backed dollar with service-provider redemption
frnt-wyoming.text: FRNT is the Wyoming Stable Token Commission's transferable dollar token, backed by Treasury bills, Treasury repos and cash in holder-benefit trust accounts. Approved Licensed Service Providers handle ordinary minting and redemption. The two-business-day rule covers payment submission to an approved provider, not guaranteed bank credit or unrestricted direct holder redemption. The claim is limited to trust assets and carries neither Wyoming's full faith and credit nor federal deposit insurance. Fiduciary Trust International is the disclosed custodian, with Bank of New York Mellon named as subcustodian. LedgerLens publishes itemized reserves, but its dashboard metrics are expressly supplemental and non-assured; a current signed examination opinion was unavailable for review. Eight native liabilities share that reserve book and use Chainlink CCIP transfers. On September 14, 2026, the Commission's CISO alleged failures in LayerZero's production authorization handover and private-key control. LayerZero's CEO disputed key loss and identified a Solana display-scaling authority transferred on June 3. That receipt establishes the display-authority transfer, but does not identify or resolve the Commission's separate key-control allegation. No FRNT exploit or loss is established by these sources. Signing independence and complete transfer governance remain unresolved. Reserve income does not accrue to token holders.

gbp-vvtx.title: Sterling payments programme on a proprietary chain
gbp-vvtx.text: VVTX Limited proposes a fully reserved, 1:1 GBP stablecoin alongside a custodial wallet and planned debit card on a proprietary UK Layer-1. The FCA selected VVTX for stablecoin sandbox testing in February 2026, and the issuer continues to invite a waitlist. AF Payments Limited, an FCA-authorized e-money institution, has controlled VVTX Limited since August 5 2026, holding 75% or more of its shares and voting rights. Two AF Payments directors joined VVTX's board that day. GBP-VVTX is Pharos's descriptive display label because no official token ticker is published. Technical chain identifiers, production contracts and direct holder-redemption terms are undisclosed. Neither card spending, sandbox selection nor a regulated parent proves public token circulation, final authorization or an executable par exit.

gbpa-agant.title: Business-only direct sterling redemption
gbpa-agant.text: GBPA gives approved UK distribution businesses a direct pound mint-and-redeem route while retail holders access the issuer through those businesses. Its monthly reserve-report archive now spans June to September 2026. The September report identifies Griffin Bank cash and State Street money-market holdings in designated trust accounts, without identifying the exact fund, underlying custody chain or enforceable insolvency priority. Nephos reconciles reserves to supply, but its formal-assurance disclaimer conflicts with its examination opening, limiting the claim to independent attestation. Issuer keys can authorize native minting and replace EVM issuance logic; Solana uses a one-signature, two-member mint multisig. LayerZero source-burn/destination-mint transfers add separate external message-validation exposure across the five native deployments. Public redemption fees, executable capacity and a completed bank-payment deadline remain unquantified. Business-only banking access, incomplete holder terms and concentrated token administration constrain holder exit and control.

gldon-ondo.title: SPDR Gold Shares through an Ondo issuer claim
gldon-ondo.text: GLDon tracks SPDR Gold Shares through a secured debt claim on Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited. Holders receive economic exposure, without direct ownership of ETF shares or a physical-gold delivery right. Its value follows the gold fund rather than a fixed dollar peg. Named custodians and a security agent support the legal structure, but the public program-wide Ankura report does not disclose GLDon-specific shares, cash, alternative collateral or liabilities. Native issuer managers can mint to registered recipients without validating a deposit or custody attestation on-chain. Eligible investors redeem through authenticated issuer quotes into USDon; conversion to USDC additionally requires whitelist access and sufficient swapper liquidity. Ethereum, BNB Chain and Solana support native issuance, while HyperEVM adds a bridge representation. Transfer restrictions, issuer operations and the available stablecoin exit rail remain material constraints.

gtusdtp-gauntlet.title: Gauntlet-curated USDT lending shares
gtusdtp-gauntlet.text: Gauntlet USDT Prime V2 earns USDT lending interest through a curated Morpho V2 vault. Its shares represent proportional lender positions, so recognized bad debt reduces their value. The October 15 Ethereum review found lending concentrated in markets secured by wrapped Bitcoin and Savings USDS; borrowers own that collateral, while the vault holds lending claims. Immediate positions are on-chain, but WBTC adds a material Bitcoin-custody dependency, so the complete backing chain is mixed. Ordinary withdrawals use idle USDT and the selected liquidity adapter. Permissionless force-deallocation can reach other market positions, subject to available liquidity and its separate penalty; in-kind exits can leave holders with illiquid lending exposure. Gauntlet controls strategy parameters through multisigs and operational keys. Published company signing policies do not identify the people or custody arrangements behind every controller. No independent whole-vault financial assurance, legal segregation or insolvency priority is established.

gusdcq-galaxy.title: Galaxy USDC Lent Against Custodial Bitcoin
gusdcq-galaxy.text: Galaxy USDC Quality is a share in a Galaxy-curated Morpho V2 vault that lends USDC and compounds the interest. Shares absorb lending losses and redeem at their current proportional asset value rather than a fixed dollar. At the October 15 2026 review, about 97% of the book was lent against custodial WBTC and cbBTC, with a small weETH allocation, so on-chain lender positions sit on top of off-chain bitcoin custody. Independent vault financial assurance, legal segregation and insolvency priority remain unestablished. Ordinary withdrawals draw on idle USDC and the configured liquidity adapter, and idle USDC was zero at that review. Permissionless force-deallocation can pull other available market assets; it cannot make borrowed USDC liquid. Galaxy's terms of use give no guarantee of withdrawal timing. The owner, curator, sentinel and allocator are EOAs without a published key-custody policy, and their powers cover routing, caps and fees, although the share-accounting code is immutable. The same owner address also controls Galaxy's USDT Quality vault, and that shared control path is the cap binding the {{grade}} report card. The durable constraint is that an exit is only as liquid as the markets the curator has lent into.

gusdtq-galaxy.title: Galaxy-curated USDT lending shares
gusdtq-galaxy.text: Galaxy USDT Quality compounds USDT lending interest through a Galaxy-curated Morpho V2 vault. Holders own proportional shares whose value can fall when lending losses are recognized. The current book is concentrated in markets backed by custodial wrapped Bitcoin, so on-chain vault custody does not make every underlying custody layer on-chain. Ordinary redemption draws on idle USDT and the selected liquidity market, which can hold only a small part of the vault’s assets. Permissionless force-deallocation can access other available markets; the documented flash-loan fallback instead leaves the holder with a direct lending position and does not guarantee cash realization. Four controller addresses have no deployed code, while their institutional key custody and human independence remain undisclosed. Share-transfer and asset-access gates are permanently disabled at the reviewed configuration. Galaxy’s terms disclaim withdrawal timing and amount guarantees. Independent vault financial assurance, legal segregation and insolvency priority remain unestablished.

hyperusdca-hyperithm.title: Hyperithm USDC lending on Monad
hyperusdca-hyperithm.text: Hyperithm USDC Apex turns USDC deposits into NAV-bearing shares in a Morpho Vault V2 on Monad. Its lending book includes concentrated loan receipts and principal-token collateral, so a USDC-denominated balance is not a direct cash claim. Accountable loan strategies feed internal collateral values, while Midas receipts use manually submitted prices. These valuation controls sit below the vault's own share accounting. The reviewed vault has no liquidity adapter, leaving ordinary withdrawals dependent on idle USDC; force-deallocation and in-kind exits are separate routes. A two-of-three owner Safe can replace the curator, while adapter admission and allocation-cap increases have specific delays and fee changes do not. A sentinel can restrict allocations. Share-transfer and direct-withdrawal gate setters are abdicated, but deposit gating remains mutable and underlying USDC can be frozen. Credit losses reduce shareholder NAV. Code audits do not establish exact-vault financial assurance, borrower recovery or legal custody protection.

jpydf-deltaforesight.title: Immutable yen CDP on a USDC-heavy, multisig-run vault layer
jpydf-deltaforesight.text: JPYdf is a yen-targeted token borrowed against wstETH or USDC through JPY DeFi, a Liquity v2 fork that DeltaForesight helped build and launched on Ethereum on October 15, 2026. Pharos still lists it as upcoming because neither DefiLlama nor CoinGecko prices it. The token and borrowing core cannot be upgraded, and no function freezes a holder's balance. Control sits one layer down: the dToken vaults holding collateral are upgradeable and pausable, and governance can recognize losses and swap oracle sources. All three governance, operator and guardian Safes are 2-of-3 with the same signers. USDC made up about 71% of collateral value on launch day, so most backing inherits Circle's freeze power. Redemption pays out in dTokens worth ¥1 before fees, with no claim to yen and no entity committed to buy JPYdf back at face value.

kpkusdcprime-kpk.title: Blue-chip collateral, variable lending shares
kpkusdcprime-kpk.text: KPK USDC Prime is a Morpho Vault V2 share over USDC, curated by KPK to lend against blue-chip collateral: wrapped bitcoin, ETH and liquid-staking tokens. Most of the book sits in cbBTC and WBTC markets, and KPK's allocation targets are enforced by its rebalancer rather than by onchain caps. Borrower interest raises assets per share, while realized lending losses lower it for every holder. Ordinary redemptions pay out of idle USDC and whatever the selected market can return; force-deallocation cannot make fully borrowed funds liquid. Economic control is the weakest pillar behind the {{grade}} overall grade. An owner Safe and a two-of-five curator Safe sit above allocator keys and automation agents whose custody rests on KPK's statements rather than address-bound evidence. Most market branches price collateral through external feeds, but rETH relies on its issuer's exchange rate. Holders keep Circle's USDC risk and add KPK's allocation discretion and Morpho market liquidity on top of it.

kpkusdcyield-kpk.title: Broader collateral, more layered credit exposure
kpkusdcyield-kpk.text: KPK USDC Yield is the higher-yield sibling of Prime: a Morpho Vault V2 share over USDC that lends against structured and yield-bearing collateral instead of blue-chip assets. Its largest markets take Avant's savUSD and 3Jane's USD3, alongside InfiniFi's siUSD and its principal tokens, so liquidation recoveries depend on the value of other protocols' dollar claims. USD3 adds an unsecured-credit layer beneath the {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} Morpho loans that accept it. Several branches value collateral through issuer conversion rates or strategy accounting rather than market sale prices, and Pharos cannot yet establish the vault's full oracle topology. That gap, plus the owner Safe and allocator keys it shares with Prime, makes economic control the weakest pillar behind the {{grade}} overall grade. Backing also trails Prime because of the layered credit in the book. Borrower interest raises assets per share, and realized losses lower it for all holders. KPK publishes a liquidity target of at least 30% for this strategy, against 75 to 100% for Prime, but exits depend on the cash the selected market can return, not on that target.

krusdc-keyrock.title: Keyrock USDC lending against cirBTC
krusdc-keyrock.text:
Keyrock Prime USDC places deposited USDC into one Morpho lending market backed by cirBTC. Borrower interest can increase its share conversion rate, while lending losses reduce it. The vault and lending positions are onchain, but the native BTC backing cirBTC is held by Circle National Trust, adding custody risk to the collateral. Borrower valuations use a single BTC/USD feed without a staleness check in the market's oracle adapter.

The owner and curator use externally owned accounts, and fee changes have no configured delay. Share-transfer and direct-withdrawal gates are permanently disabled; deposit gating remains mutable. Ordinary redemption depends on available USDC liquidity. An emergency in-kind exit can leave the holder with an underlying lending position and a configured force-deallocation charge, rather than cash.

krw-kb-kookmin.title: KB won-token pilot awaits commercial framework
krw-kb-kookmin.text: KB Financial Group announced on May 17, 2026 that it had completed an integrated won-stablecoin proof of concept with KG Inicis, Kaia and OpenAsset. The pilot connected issuance, Hollys offline QR payments, merchant settlement and remittance to a Vietnam bank account, with Kaia identifying KB Kookmin as the bank participant. KB says actual services will follow the implementation of Korean digital-asset legislation, and no launch date is announced. In September MoonPay named KB Kookmin Bank as an exploratory partner on issuance, distribution and overseas remittance, again without an issuance date. The final legal issuer, official ticker, token-specific reserves and public-holder redemption terms remain unpublished; KRW-KB is an editorial display label.

mantrausd-mantra.title: MANTRA dollar with an EOA upgrade path
mantrausd-mantra.text: mantraUSD is MANTRA's native settlement dollar and a direct wrapper of M0's M token. Holders receive no interest: the whitepaper directs the Treasury yield to a MANTRA-controlled address, from which MANTRA allocates it at its discretion to qualifying ecosystem participants. On-chain M inventory covered local token supply at the October 15 review, though that observation does not independently assure M0's upstream reserve book or establish holder seniority. Exit is the weakest pillar on the card. The deployed SwapFacility let an unprivileged sample address qualify for conversion into wM, while direct M output required an approved swapper, and the published institutional USDC redemption remains subject to eligibility and possible delay or suspension. A 3-of-5 Safe administers freeze and yield-recipient roles but cannot authorize deposit-free minting under the reviewed implementation. A separate externally owned address can replace the token logic without an on-chain delay, so the parent-token backing sits beneath a local upgrade key that no timelock constrains.

mxnt-tether.title: Peso claim on Tether's shared reserve book
mxnt-tether.text: Mexican Peso Tether gives eligible verified clients a contractual peso redemption claim on Tether International's shared fiat-token reserve book. BDO's June 2026 reasonable-assurance report covers that aggregate book, which includes gold, bitcoin, credit and equity assets alongside Treasury instruments. It does not identify a dedicated MXNT allocation, custodian roster or token-specific insolvency priority. Ethereum is the issuer's currently supported MXNT deployment; its integration roster classifies Tron MXNT as deprecated. A legacy three-of-six wallet controls native minting, holder blocking, blocked-balance destruction and immediate upgrades. Its signer independence and key-custody arrangements remain undisclosed. Direct redemption requires at least USD 100,000 equivalent and costs the greater of USD 1,000 or 0.1%. Published terms provide no unconditional payout deadline or measured same-notional capacity, leaving smaller holders dependent on secondary markets.

net-cloudflare.title: Cloudflare’s planned agent-payment dollar
net-cloudflare.text: Cloudflare announced NET Dollar on September 25, 2025 for automated payments by agents, developers and creators. Its product FAQ promises one U.S. dollar of collateral per coin and still describes availability as forthcoming. CoinGecko identifies the product as net-dollar with symbol NET, but supplies no current price, market cap or deployment. The legal issuer, custody arrangements and NET-specific redemption and freeze terms remain undisclosed. No dated launch window is established.

oned-gennius.title: Coinbase-custodied USDC for Gennius
oned-gennius.text: ONED is Gennius's dollar-referenced token, backed by USDC held in Coinbase custody and issued natively on Base. Eligible Coinbase accounts can deposit externally held ONED and convert it one-for-one with USDC, less any fees and subject to geographic restrictions. Coinbase publishes itemized reserve wallets and supply, which pinned chain balances corroborate. Native holder terms incorporate Coinbase's contractual reserve ownership and creditor-claim protections. Shared custody addresses are permitted, and those protections do not establish statutory bankruptcy remoteness or independent financial assurance. The minter's allowance can be reset or raised, while separate administrators can authorize issuance or replace token logic without a global upgrade delay. Signing-key safeguards remain undisclosed. Coinbase may delay, pause or refuse redemption under its terms, and no unconditional settlement maximum or current same-notional exit capacity is established. ONED therefore retains Coinbase account, custody and operational dependencies beyond the underlying USDC exposure.

plnq-quantoz.title: Deployed złoty token with zero supply
plnq-quantoz.text: Quantoz Payments has deployed PLNQ on Ethereum, but its published token roster says no PLNQ is circulating and no reserve exists yet. A pinned Ethereum read confirms six decimals and zero total supply, while the exact-contract price endpoint returns no quote. The whitepaper proposes 1:1 Polish złoty reserves safeguarded through Stichting Quantoz and par redemption for eligible registered holders after compliance checks. Polygon, Algorand, XRP Ledger and Xahau remain planned networks without verified production identities. Deployment and MiCA issuer registration do not establish an executable market or an operating holder exit.

pyusdx-moonpay.title: MoonPay PYUSD-backed issuer claim
pyusdx-moonpay.text: PYUSDx is issued by MoonPay Digital Assets Limited against PYUSD and uses M0 infrastructure for native issuance and cross-chain transfers. Eligible counterparties can redeem one token for one PYUSD; downstream holders must qualify separately and have no ownership interest in specific reserves. The underlying PYUSD assurance therefore does not reconcile MoonPay holdings against PYUSDx liabilities. Issuer-controlled rewards and upgrades can bypass the gateway queue, while mutable token-bucket limits govern issuance speed rather than reserve coverage. The gateway also has a separately identified operator and executor key. Cross-chain controls include a peer-configuration key alongside the bridge administrator, and the 0G deployment has a different single-key administrator from the other four native deployments. Token-specific reserve assurance, custody segregation and privileged-key signing safeguards remain undisclosed. Holding PYUSDx alone confers no contractual right to rewards or direct Paxos redemption.

regbp-restabilise.title: Institutional sterling token in FCA sandbox
regbp-restabilise.text: ReStabilise proposes reGBP as an institutional sterling token backed 1:1 by high-quality liquid assets held on trust for holders. Its issuer page promises par redemption by any holder on a T+1 basis and invites partnerships, pilots and early access. The FCA selected ReStabilise for stablecoin sandbox testing in February 2026, without granting final issuance authorization through that selection. Production chains, contracts and circulation are not publicly verified. The proposed trust and settlement commitments still need published legal terms, custody evidence and an operating redemption route.

sdai-gnosis.title: Gnosis savings over bridged xDAI
sdai-gnosis.text: Savings xDAI wraps Gnosis Chain’s WXDAI in an immutable savings vault, with yield reflected in the amount of WXDAI each share can redeem. Holders can convert shares back to WXDAI on-chain without a local cooldown, then unwrap into native xDAI. The fixed-asset contract has no local owner or privileged share minter, but that narrow control finding leaves the xDAI bridge and Sky reserve dependencies intact. Its balance and share accounting are reproducible on-chain; this does not establish independently audited financial reconciliation or legal priority over upstream reserves. Backing is the weakest of the three pillars because default-recovery and encumbrance terms are not published. The {{grade}} overall grade is capped at the parent xDAI rating, so local contract strength cannot lift the share above its underlying. The holder’s final dollar exit depends on the underlying bridge and stablecoin system rather than a direct fiat redemption right.

senpathusd-sentora.title: Tempo pathUSD lending vault
senpathusd-sentora.text: Sentora pathUSD is an ERC-4626 vault on Tempo whose shares claim idle pathUSD plus pathUSD lent to a cbBTC-collateralized Morpho market. Share value follows assets per share, including interest, fees and recognized losses, rather than a fixed dollar redemption promise. At Pharos's 15 October 2026 read, almost the whole book sat idle; the lending position was about 0.5% of vault assets. Ordinary withdrawals draw on that idle balance and the configured liquidity adapter. If the market turns illiquid, Morpho's force-deallocation route still allows an in-kind exit: the holder gives up shares for a direct lender position in that market, at a 0.01% penalty, rather than receiving cash. The owner and curator each use a one-signature Safe. New adapters and higher allocation caps wait three days, while fee setters have zero delay. The {{grade}} overall grade is capped at the rating of the parent pathUSD. Custody runs back to Bridge's pathUSD reserves and, for the lent slice, to the Coinbase-held BTC behind cbBTC collateral, so parent-token restrictions, borrower losses and available cash constrain every exit.

senpyusdmain-sentora.title: Sentora PYUSD lending with single-key controls
senpyusdmain-sentora.text: Paypal USD Main is an ERC-4626 share in a Sentora-curated Morpho Vault V2 denominated in PYUSD. Deposited stablecoins fund collateralized loans against Bitcoin wrappers, staked ETH and yield-bearing stablecoin derivatives. Borrower defaults, liquidation conditions and curator allocation choices can affect share value. Interest accrues through NAV, while fees and realized losses reduce the value retained by holders. Owner and curator each use a 1-of-1 Safe with a sole EOA signer. Fee changes and deposit-gate changes have no time delay, but share-transfer and withdrawal-gate setters are permanently abdicated. A zero liquidity adapter means ordinary cash redemption relies on idle PYUSD unless lending positions are first deallocated. Holder-initiated force-deallocation through the current adapter still withdraws market cash and charges a 0.01% penalty; it does not directly hand the holder a lender position. Parent issuer freeze risk remains inherited. Protocol security audits and a successful small redemption do not establish full-size stressed cash recovery.

senpyusdmwin-sentora.title: PYUSD lending against mWIN
senpyusdmwin-sentora.text: Sentora mWIN Main lends PYUSD against mWIN collateral through one Morpho lending market. Its shares earn lending interest net of fees and absorb recognized losses through a changing assets-per-share rate. Ordinary cash withdrawals draw on idle PYUSD because the reviewed vault has no liquidity adapter configured. Market liquidity is not automatically available to redeem shares. Permissionless force-deallocation moves assets from a market into the vault's idle balance and burns shares worth 1% of the assets deallocated. If the market lacks cash, force-deallocation cannot help; a separate in-kind redemption transfers the lending position rather than cash. The owner and curator each use a one-signature Safe. Adapter admission and cap increases have three-day delays, while fee changes can take effect immediately. The adapter registry is permanently fixed, although its owner can extend the registries it consults. PYUSD reserve and freeze risks remain upstream. Public evidence does not establish whole-holder legal custody protections, enforceable default priority or independent vault financial assurance.

senpyusdprimev2-sentora.title: Sentora PYUSD lending against residential credit
senpyusdprimev2-sentora.text: Sentora PRIME Main is a PYUSD-denominated ERC-4626 share in a Sentora-curated Morpho Vault V2. Deployed lending is concentrated in a single market collateralized by Hastra PRIME, which Sentora describes as financing Figure home-equity loans between origination and securitization. That description does not establish vault holders’ direct rights to the loans or insolvency recovery priority. Interest raises NAV, while fees and recognized losses reduce holders’ value. Owner and curator each use a single-signer Safe. Fee and deposit-gate settings have no delay, but the share-transfer and withdrawal-gate setters are permanently abdicated. Ordinary cash redemption depends on idle PYUSD while the liquidity adapter is zero. The current adapter’s holder-initiated force-deallocation path withdraws PYUSD from Morpho and charges 1% on assets deallocated; it does not assign lender positions and still needs market cash liquidity. Underlying PYUSD freeze exposure remains inherited. Neither protocol security audits nor a small successful exit establish full-size stressed cash recovery.

senpyusdpst-sentora.title: PYUSD lending against Huma PST
senpyusdpst-sentora.text: Sentora Huma PST Main lends PYUSD against Huma PST collateral through a Morpho vault. PST represents private payment-financing credit, so the collateral carries borrower, valuation and legal-recovery risks beyond PYUSD's own reserve exposure. Lending interest accrues through the share exchange rate; fees and recognized losses change the PYUSD recovered per share. The deployment holds idle PYUSD alongside one lending-market position. Its ordinary withdrawal path uses idle cash because no liquidity adapter is configured. Permissionless force-deallocation carries a mutable 1% penalty and may not realize cash from an illiquid market. Owner and curator each require one Safe signature. Adapter additions and allocation-cap increases wait three days, but fees and liquidity routing have no selector delay. The adapter registry is permanently locked, although its owner can append eligible subregistries. Parent PYUSD freeze exposure remains inherited. Published terms establish neither enforceable holder insolvency priority nor a funded loss backstop.

senrlusdv2-sentora.title: Sentora RLUSD lending with single-key controls
senrlusdv2-sentora.text: Sentora RLUSD Main is an ERC-4626 share in a Sentora-curated Morpho Vault V2 denominated in RLUSD. Deposits finance collateralized loans, with the reviewed book concentrated in kBTC, weETH and USDe borrower collateral. Borrower defaults, liquidation conditions and allocation choices can reduce the share value. Interest accrues through NAV, while fee shares and realized losses affect what holders retain. Owner and curator each use a 1-of-1 Safe with a sole EOA signer. Fee and deposit-gate changes have no delay, but the withdrawal-gate setter is permanently disabled. The curator also holds allocator and sentinel powers. Ordinary one-share redemption was simulated successfully. A zero liquidity adapter makes immediate cash withdrawal depend on idle RLUSD unless lending positions are first deallocated. Parent issuer freezes remain inherited. Neither the small exit simulation nor protocol security audits establish full-size stressed cash recovery.

sfrax-frax.title: Legacy FRAX savings share and bridge claims
sfrax-frax.text: sFRAX is the savings share for legacy FRAX, distinct from sfrxUSD and its newer reserve architecture. The native Ethereum vault holds FRAX directly and issues shares against deposits. Protocol-funded rewards accrue through a capped, seven-day accounting cycle; permissionless synchronization governs when a new cycle begins, so the IORB benchmark is a target rather than a promised yield. A three-of-six parameter Safe can adjust the reward cap but cannot arbitrarily mint native shares or replace the vault code. Holders redeem into FRAX at the current pro-rata rate, without a local withdrawal fee or cooldown. That claim does not give them direct title to Treasuries or a direct dollar cash redemption right. Cross-chain sFRAX representations add separate bridge controls. Frax explicitly describes LayerZero OFTs as claims on bridge lockboxes rather than direct protocol liabilities. Its historical deployment table also includes addresses now identifying as sfrxUSD, making chain-specific contract identity essential.

sirloinusdc-steakhouse.title: USDC lending shares on Base
sirloinusdc-steakhouse.text: sirloinUSDC is a Steakhouse-curated Morpho Vault V2 share whose value follows net USDC lending assets rather than a fixed-dollar promise. The broader collateral mandate introduces borrower-credit and liquidation risks beyond the underlying stablecoin. At the 15 October 2026 Base snapshot, USDe-backed loans accounted for most of the USDC lender exposure, while the mGLO branch relied on a manual-admin price feed. The immutable core requires USDC deposits for user shares, but fee-share issuance dilutes claims and lending losses reduce NAV. The exact vault charged 25% of interest and no management fee at that pin. Ordinary withdrawals depend on idle USDC and the selected liquidity adapter; emergency force-deallocation is separate and carries a configurable penalty. No exact-vault signed financial reconciliation or funded stressed-recovery guarantee was established.

skymoneyusdsflagship-sky.title: Sky.money USDS lending share
skymoneyusdsflagship-sky.text: sky.money USDS Flagship holds USDS in an immutable Morpho Vault V2 and lends through markets selected by Sky.money. Its share value follows interest and realized losses, while USDS retains its own reserve and control risks. The reviewed book combines idle USDS with loans against PT-sUSDS, wstETH and cbBTC. Share-transfer and asset-withdrawal gate setters are permanently disabled, but lending controls remain active. A 2-of-3 Safe controls curation and can appoint allocators; a separate 1-of-3 Safe allocates within approved caps and can change liquidity routing. The PT market uses a fixed time-discount oracle rather than an external market price. Ordinary redemption pays USDS from available idle cash when no liquidity adapter is configured. Exiting deployed loans requires a separate deallocation action and sufficient market liquidity. Neither onchain accounting nor the Sky.money interface guarantees principal, a completion deadline or fiat redemption.

skymoneyusdtsavings-sky.title: Sky.money USDT lending against sUSDS
skymoneyusdtsavings-sky.text: sky.money USDT Savings supplies USDT through an immutable Morpho Vault V2 curated by Skybase International. Its share value follows lending interest and realized losses; the underlying USDT retains Tether reserve and control risks. The reviewed lender book uses sUSDS collateral, adding Sky exposure to the Tether settlement asset. Local share-transfer and asset-withdrawal gates are permanently disabled. A two-of-three curator Safe sets investment parameters, while it and a separate one-of-three allocator Safe can change allocations and the ordinary withdrawal market. Current allocation caps permit concentration in one market. Ordinary redemption returns USDT only when idle assets or market liquidity are available. Force-deallocation offers a separate exit mechanism with a penalty, without promising immediate cash recovery. Neither protocol accounting nor the curator's terms supplies a fiat redemption guarantee.

sparkusdc-spark.title: Spark's Base cbBTC lending receipt
sparkusdc-spark.text: Spark USDC Vault earns lending interest on Base through a Morpho vault curated by Spark. Its supplied book is concentrated in a cbBTC-collateralized market, while the share is denominated and redeemable in USDC. Holders own a lender receipt, not the borrowers' bitcoin collateral or a segregated fiat claim. The vault's V1.1 loss accounting can preserve the reported share price after market bad debt, leaving later depositors exposed unless someone voluntarily covers the shortfall. An accruing exchange rate therefore does not establish recoverable value under stress. Withdrawals also depend on available Morpho liquidity. Spark governance controls allocations, caps and fees, while Circle can freeze the underlying USDC. Borrower cbBTC adds Coinbase custody exposure through its BTC backing. These dependencies remain even when an ordinary redemption succeeds.

sparkusdtbc-spark.title: Spark's adapter-based USDT lending vault
sparkusdtbc-spark.text: Spark Blue Chip USDT Vault lends USDT through a Morpho adapter to markets secured by wstETH, WBTC and sUSDS, alongside negligible cbBTC exposure. Holders own a transferable lending receipt whose USDT value follows net interest, fees and realized losses. The vault's share-accounting code is immutable, while Spark's owner, curator and allocator retain strategy and fee powers. Local share-transfer and withdrawal gates are permanently disabled; new deposits can still be gated. Ordinary redemptions draw on available market liquidity. Separate force-deallocation mechanics can move exposure out of the vault but do not guarantee cash realization or recover bad debt. The curator is a 2-of-2 Safe controlled by nested 3-of-5 and 1-of-2 Safes; signer independence and key custody remain undisclosed. Tether issuer risk remains upstream, and the vault has no independently reconciled financial assurance or proven insolvency priority.

sreusd-resupply.title: Protocol-revenue savings in REUSD
sreusd-resupply.text: sreUSD is Resupply's savings share for REUSD, funded by protocol revenue released over seven-day reward cycles. Revenue streams through the vault's exchange rate, leaving holders exposed to REUSD's lending-collateral and liquidation risks. The native Ethereum contract holds REUSD and permits share redemption without a local cooldown or penalty fee. Conversion from REUSD into other assets is a separate exit with the parent's costs and liquidity constraints. The savings implementation is nonproxy, while Resupply Core retains reward and potential bridge-configuration powers. At reward-cycle rollover, deposits and redemptions can also depend on the registry-selected fee distributor completing its call. Local balances cover the immediate REUSD position, but do not establish whole-book upstream custody, independent security-audit coverage of the savings implementation or a funded stressed-recovery waterfall.

stbt-matrixdock.title: Rebasing Treasury exposure through unsecured issuer debt
stbt-matrixdock.text: STBT distributes Treasury-portfolio income by increasing token balances while targeting one dollar per token. Governing terms give holders an unsecured claim against Prometheus, without ownership of the Treasury bills or USTB and BUIDL interests held through affiliates. Those affiliates may borrow against or lend the underlying assets. Accredited, allowlisted investors can request issuer redemption, with a limited daily same-day window and T+2 processing for larger requests. The published zero redemption fee does not remove contractual liquidation losses and transaction costs. Native issuance and rebasing require four hours of timelock scheduling, while implementation replacement requires 24 hours; the controller's zero generic minimum does not bypass these selector delays. A separate key can change the issuer reserve-feed budget without delay. The recovered asset statement mixes dates and does not reconcile the complete reserve and token-liability books. Treasury exposure therefore remains mediated by issuer credit, privileged valuation and restricted exit.

steakcusdc-steakhouse.title: Public shares behind confidential USDC deposits
steakcusdc-steakhouse.text: Steakhouse Confidential Prime USDC is the public ERC-4626 share beneath Zama’s confidential deposit service. The confidential service wraps public vault shares into a separate encrypted cShare receipt; this listing tracks the public share, not both supplies. USDC is lent through one Morpho adapter against cbBTC, wstETH and WETH collateral. Interest increases assets per share, while borrower losses can reduce them. The public vault restricts deposits through a whitelist gate; its share-transfer and direct-withdrawal gates are permanently disabled. Ordinary withdrawals pay available USDC at NAV through the configured liquidity adapter, without guaranteeing a full-supply exit under stress. A five-of-ten Safe controls Steakhouse’s Supervisor, which can replace the three-of-nine curator immediately despite separate delays on ownership and allocation changes. The material cbBTC collateral leg brings Coinbase BTC custody into the otherwise onchain lending architecture. Confidential entry protects transaction visibility; it does not remove lending losses, liquidity constraints or inherited USDC freeze exposure.

steakeurcv-steakhouse.title: EURCV lending shares on Ethereum
steakeurcv-steakhouse.text: steakEURCV is a Steakhouse-curated Morpho Vault V2 receipt over EURCV. Lending interest accrues through assets per share, while borrower losses reduce the claim. Holders redeem to EURCV through idle balances and a selected liquidity adapter, so access to underlying assets depends on available liquidity. The immutable core requires deposited assets for user minting; fee governance can dilute shares but cannot mint native EURCV. The October 15 review found a three-of-nine curator Safe and a separate five-of-ten Supervisor-owner Safe. Adapter and allocation-cap increases wait seven days, while curator replacement, fees and allocator appointments do not carry the same delay. Share-transfer and withdrawal gates are permanently disabled. Parent-token reserve protections remain upstream. The reviewed terms do not establish an exact-vault signed financial reconciliation, legal insolvency priority or funded stressed-recovery guarantee.

steakusdg-steakhouse.title: USDG lending shares on Robinhood Chain
steakusdg-steakhouse.text: steakUSDG is Steakhouse’s High Yield Instant USDG lending vault on Robinhood Chain. Its current borrower markets take longer-tail collateral, including productive stablecoins and savings tokens such as syrupUSDG, spUSDG and USDe, so the yield depends on borrower demand and the quality of those collateral positions. ERC-4626 shares accrue lending interest and absorb strategy losses. The immutable core requires deposited USDG before creating user shares, while configurable fees can dilute each holder’s claim. Withdrawals burn shares and pay USDG from idle balances and the selected liquidity adapter; the full lending position has no guaranteed cash-realization timetable. Morpho still flagged deposits disabled on 15 October 2026, separately from existing holders’ liquidity-dependent redemption rights. USDG issuer reserve and freeze risks remain upstream. Whole-book custody, enforceable insolvency priority and independently funded stressed recovery are not established by the vault’s code or the curator’s terms.

strusd-tori.title: Tori savings with a cooldown and seizure powers
strusd-tori.text: strUSD holds Tori's trUSD in an Ethereum savings vault and distributes net trading rewards through a changing share exchange rate. Unstaking currently requires a seven-day cooldown and returns trUSD without a protocol staking or unstaking fee. The admin can extend that cooldown to 90 days; additional requests reset the timer for accumulated cooldown funds. A 24-hour timelock protects implementation upgrades, while separate admin powers can restrict addresses, redistribute blocked shares and seize blocked cooldown funds. Authorized rewarders can burn backing through loss reports capped at 5% per day. Monad and Pharos tokens represent shares locked in one Ethereum CCIP pool, with separately mutable bridge roles and rate limits. Tori's terms exclude acquisition by EU, EEA and U.S. residents or entities with registered offices there. Rewards are discretionary, and neither token gives holders direct recourse to Tori's investments. Unstaking therefore ends in trUSD; a dollar exit still depends on parent liquidity and discretionary issuer repurchase.

susdc-spark-v1.title: Legacy savings shares across five chains
susdc-spark-v1.text: Spark's legacy sUSDC holds one local sUSDS share for each share it issues, earning the Sky Savings Rate rather than Spark Savings V2's Liquidity Layer yield. Ethereum deposits convert USDC into USDS before entering sUSDS. Arbitrum, Base, Optimism and Unichain vaults instead swap USDC for bridged sUSDS through local PSM3 contracts and trusted savings-rate providers. Ordinary USDC redemption depends on the relevant PSM's liquidity; Ethereum also exposes governance-set conversion fees. The exit function returns local sUSDS directly, retaining Sky exposure and, on L2, the bridge representation. All five vaults are upgradeable. Ethereum's reviewed governance scheduling does not establish an asset-wide delay: each L2 executor currently adds zero local delay. On-chain share coverage establishes accounting inventory, while enforceable priority and ultimate custody remain unestablished.

susdf-falcon.title: USDf savings with mutable withdrawals
susdf-falcon.text: sUSDf is Falcon Finance's savings share for deposited USDf, with rewards from the protocol's trading strategies increasing its USDf exchange rate as they vest. The immediate backing is USDf held by the Ethereum vault, while the parent's off-exchange custodians, exchange liquidity and onchain strategies make whole-book custody mixed. Native contract redemption had no cooldown at the October 15, 2026 review. Administrators can introduce a delay of up to 90 days, restrict deposits or withdrawals and burn or move restricted shares. Ordinary share transfers have no local restriction-list check. A four-of-six Safe controls upgrades and withdrawal settings. Native staking has no positive allowlist; Falcon platform account services separately require approved onboarding. Local accounting does not establish independent assurance of Falcon's net hedge positions or enforceable holder priority in default.

susdx-axis.title: USDx rewards behind a serviced exit queue
susdx-axis.text: sUSDx is Axis's accumulating USDx savings receipt. Axis decides how much USDx to fund as rewards; payouts are not a mechanical pass-through of trading results. Funded rewards vest into accounted assets, raising each share's USDx claim while leaving the parent's offchain venue and hedge risks intact. Redemption burns shares and removes the reserved USDx from reward-earning assets. The seven-day cooldown establishes eligibility; a privileged servicer must still make the request claimable, with no promised completion deadline. Cancellation is also pausable and was disabled at Ethereum block 26197360 on October 15, 2026. The vault separately accounts for active assets, unvested rewards and redemption liabilities, but local accounting solvency does not establish the solvency of USDx's trading portfolio. Governance can restrict holders, change operating parameters directly and replace the implementation through a separate two-day timelock. Holders depend on both the parent backing and the administered exit queue.

sxsrlusd-sentora.title: Sentora and Spark RLUSD vault
sxsrlusd-sentora.text: Sentora x Spark RLUSD holds predominantly idle RLUSD alongside a WBTC-collateralized Morpho lending position. Shares earn lending interest after a 10% performance fee, while recognized losses reduce the RLUSD recoverable per share. The exact vault has immutable share accounting and permanently disabled transfer and withdrawal gates, but it inherits RLUSD freeze exposure and WBTC custody risk. Spark's owner proxy is governed through Sky contracts; a 2-of-2 curator Safe uses nested 1-of-1 and 1-of-2 branches without established independent human custody. With no liquidity adapter configured, ordinary redemptions use idle RLUSD. Force-deallocation depends on market liquidity and has a separate penalty; code-enforced accounting does not establish funded recovery or legal insolvency priority.

syrupusdg-maple.title: Maple credit exposure in USDG
syrupusdg-maple.text: syrupUSDG gives holders a proportional claim on Maple's USDG-denominated portfolio of institutional loans and supporting yield strategies. Interest increases share value, while impairments and borrower defaults can reduce principal. The legal structure ring-fences the USDG portfolio, but lenders share its losses and withdrawals depend on liquidity in a first-in, first-out queue with no guaranteed maximum wait. Maple's published independent collateral dashboard covers syrupUSDC and syrupUSDT, leaving syrupUSDG-specific financial reconciliation and current custody coverage unverified. Redemption is also permissioned: the pool delegate and the permission-manager admin can change lender allowlist entries, so an existing holder can be denied redemption. Pharos has not established capacity or settlement terms for a same-size dollar exit.

umint-ubs.title: UBS Ethereum money-market fund shares
umint-ubs.text: uMINT represents accumulating Class AT-acc (USD) shares in a Singapore VCC money-market sub-fund managed by UBS Asset Management. DigiFT's January 2025 native-fund disclosure identifies UBS (Irl) Select Money Market Fund - USD as the all-or-substantially-all underlying investment. Its short-term USD debt mandate includes governmental and other issuers, rather than Treasuries alone. State Street is the named native custodian and administrator, while the disclosed Singapore structure segregates sub-fund liabilities. Current portfolio weights, the exact underlying share class and the binding native private placement memorandum remain unavailable, so Pharos scores the backing as a fund-share claim rather than a look-through portfolio. UBS confirms an in-production subscription and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through DigiFT, but historical minimums and daily T+0 dealing do not establish current settlement terms. Pharos finds no exit path it can verify, so exit scores at the floor and sets the {{grade}} overall grade. The native token has immutable issuance bytecode, yet one administrator EOA and a separate minter/burner EOA retain uncapped mint authority, with no published signing safeguards or independent whole-supply reconciliation. DigiFT depositary receipts are excluded from this listing. The durable constraint is contractual: until the redemption terms are public, the fund's quality cannot reach the token holder's exit.

uscc-superstate.title: Crypto carry shares with conditional redemption
uscc-superstate.text: USCC represents shares of Bitwise's crypto carry fund, with returns from spot-futures basis trades and staking alongside Treasury exposure. Its variable net asset value can decline when market marks move, even while positions remain open. Superstate operates native shares on Ethereum, Plume and Solana; shares held only in book-entry form are outside the public token stock. Public disclosures identify Anchorage Digital Bank for fund digital assets and cash, trading venues for futures and margin, and Circle for temporary USDC settlement custody. The unaudited holdings table reports signed notional exposures, without independently reconciled hedge coverage, margin buffers or funded first-loss support. EY is named as auditor, but no current signed fund-to-token and book-entry reconciliation was publicly retrieved. Issuer-controlled mint keys, upgradeable EVM contracts and wallet allowlists govern issuance and transfers, which leaves economic control near the bottom of the card. Qualified Purchasers ordinarily redeem USD or USDC on market-day T+1/T+2 schedules, but Pharos finds no exit path it can count on, so exit scores at the floor and sets the {{grade}} overall grade. The durable constraint is that the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} program can be modified or terminated, and Pharos records no alternative route behind it.

usdfc-secured-finance.title: Filecoin collateral with upgradeable controls
usdfc-secured-finance.text: USDFC turns FIL collateral into dollar liquidity through Secured Finance’s Filecoin Troves, with direct redemption into oracle-valued FIL. Its single-asset backing avoids off-chain reserve custody but exposes the whole book to Filecoin’s native token and liquidation demand. Stability Pool deposits absorb liquidation debt; uncovered amounts are redistributed to surviving Troves, and the pool has funded only a small fraction of system debt. A two-of-three Safe controls token ownership and immediate contract upgrades, including the mint logic, and it moved the primary price feed from Pyth to RedStone in September 2026 after Pyth left Filecoin. The Tellor fallback behind RedStone depends on an operator-run update job. Those controls make economic control the weakest pillar on the report card. The same month, an attacker exploited Secured Finance’s separate fixed-rate lending markets, which kept the USDFC books there paused until mid-October. The issuer says no tokens were minted, but Pharos has not reconciled the core contracts’ indexed issuance history with current supply, so no incident verdict is drawn for them. Redemption can stop at a Trove’s residual debt floor, charges a request-sensitive fee, and becomes unavailable below the system’s minimum collateral ratio. Pharos recognizes no venue that can absorb a same-notional sale, and the token’s market price comes from a thin, low-volume feed.
