Holder exit depends on functioning collateral markets and a fresh protocol oracle.

usdfr-forest-road.title: Forest Road credit-backed dollar
usdfr-forest-road.text: USDfr turns a USDC deposit into a transferable dollar claim backed mainly by Forest Road-originated specialty-finance credit. The current book is concentrated in renewable-energy lending to one borrower, with a small related-party digital-assets facility. Direct minting and redemption require KYC; nonblocked holders can transfer USDfr or trade in its independent Uniswap market. The reserve ledger includes interest earned before cash arrives, and signed loan facts do not establish independent financial assurance or enforceable holder priority. Forest Road controls governance through a two-day timelock and can authorize a minter outside the controller's backing checks. USDfr itself earns no yield; the separate sUSDfr vault receives credit income through its exchange rate and has a liquidity-budgeted exit queue. Direct USDfr redemption depends on idle USDC, while a holder consenting to sub-par redemption can retain a haircut after finite junior protection is exhausted. Public legal and custody evidence does not resolve whole-book recovery rights.

usdr-rise.title: RISE settlement dollar backed by M
usdr-rise.text: USDR is RISE's native settlement dollar, backed locally by M0's M token. RISE retains reserve yield rather than passing it through to holders. The October 15 on-chain review found enough M to cover outstanding USDR and no accounted non-M collateral, but it does not establish legal priority or independent assurance over the upstream Treasury book. Permissionless conversion through the deployed SwapFacility leads to wM; direct M output requires an approved swapper. Eligibility is conditional on approvals, pauses and holder restrictions, and a successful eligibility read does not prove executable capacity or a completed cash exit. A 2-of-3 operational Safe and a separate 4-of-8 upgrade Safe govern local controls, including holder freezing. Public evidence does not establish independent human signers or their key-custody arrangements. Holders therefore depend on both the M parent and RISE's configurable extension and exit routes.

usdsm-stable-mint.title: Malta-issued dollar with Etherlink-native supply
usdsm-stable-mint.text: USDSM gives holders a dollar redemption claim against Stable mint Ltd, with direct issuance reserved for onboarded legal-person participants. Natural-person holders can also complete onboarding solely for redemption. The terms impose neither an issuer redemption fee nor a minimum, but third-party bank charges and screening-dependent settlement remain relevant. ESMA lists the exact issuer and USD whitepaper as an electronic-money-token issuance by a Malta electronic money institution. The advertised 102% reserve coverage is an issuer claim without a retrieved dated independent reserve-to-liability reconciliation or current portfolio weights. Two native Etherlink minters retain uncapped issuance power, and the issuer also controls token upgrades. LayerZero connects four deployments through burn-and-mint transfers. Fresh pathway reads confirm two required verifiers, while the issuer controls the peers and validation settings. Those technical observations do not establish independent signing custody or financial backing. Holders remain dependent on the issuer's safeguarded reserves and bank redemption operations.

usdso-somnia.title: Multichain frxUSD wrapper with local admin control
usdso-somnia.text: USDso is a Frax-issued, Somnia-branded frxUSD wrapper with twenty-one verified native deployments across EVM chains as of 15 October 2026. Each local custodian takes frxUSD before minting and returns the parent token on redemption. Pinned local inventories matched local USDso liabilities, but those asynchronous observations do not establish complete global or in-flight reconciliation. The cross-chain router redeems USDso to frxUSD, sends the parent through LayerZero and deposits it into destination custody. Chain-specific Safes control issuance and custody logic: Ethereum uses three of five owners, while the other reviewed deployments use three of six. Each administrator can authorize token minting outside the collateral-taking path. The live reserve feed covers Somnia only. Observed zero redemption fees remain configurable, and holder transfers can be frozen or paused. Somnia's terms grant no reserve-yield entitlement. Redeeming into frxUSD leaves holders exposed to its upstream custody and fiat-redemption conditions.

usdu-universal.title: ADGM bank-deposit dollar with professional redemption
usdu-universal.text: Universal USD is issued under Universal Digital’s ADGM fiat-referenced-token permission and backed by dollar bank deposits. Crowe’s published examination reconciles the exact Ethereum liability book to bank-confirmed reserves at its dated checkpoints, separately from smart-contract security assurance. Direct par redemption requires professional-client onboarding through Aquanow. Typical two-business-day processing follows due diligence, carries fees and extension rights, and credits an Aquanow client-money account before any separate bank withdrawal. Ethereum issuance is centrally controlled: two minters have replenishable allowances, and the common owner can immediately upgrade the token and its mint controller. Those onchain powers are established; independent human control and offchain signing policies are not. The issuer describes holder-first, pro-rata insolvency distribution, without independent verification of the legal protections. A Solana integration announced in October has no verified mint identity in the reviewed materials, so the Ethereum evidence does not establish whole-product chain coverage.

usdvb-versabank.title: VersaBank's Tokenized Dollar Deposit
usdvb-versabank.text: VUSD is the commercial name for VersaBank USA's tokenized dollar deposit, piloted internally as USDVB from August 2025. Each token represents one U.S. dollar deposited with the bank, with issuance and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through VersaVault. This exposes holders to a bank deposit rather than a separately segregated stablecoin reserve trust. VersaBank's October 15 2026 release announcing the commercial phase calls VUSD interest-paying and FDIC insurance-eligible, the two features its September 2026 filing had asked regulators to confirm. The release says the phase is in full compliance with U.S. federal banking regulations but names no regulator decision, chain or launch date. It also says VersaBank's technology can freeze, seize and burn tokenized deposits that regulators deem illegal. Since October 1 2026 VersaBank USA has served as issuer of the Bank of North Dakota's Roughrider Coin on Fiserv's digital asset platform, responsible for minting, burning, custody and reserve management. VersaBank's announcement of that role did not mention VUSD or USDVB. The bank plans exchange listings as soon as feasible, but transfer and redemption rights for ordinary external holders, including minimums, fees, timing and capacity, remain unpublished.

usdx-axis.title: Venue-held hedges with restricted primary access
usdx-axis.text: USDx turns Axis's venue-held trading portfolio into a transferable dollar-targeted token, with market-neutral hedges intended to offset directional inventory exposure. Accountable independently observes exchange-account reserves, but its cryptographic reporting does not establish legal segregation, complete hedge coverage or a funded loss-absorption layer. Direct redemption requires an approved primary-market account and an operator-settled signed order, so smaller holders depend on secondary-market liquidity. The governance Safe can mint tokens directly without collateral checks or market limits, while only proxy upgrades pass through a separate two-day timelock. Published portfolio categories explain gross asset form, while unresolved venue identities, margin headroom and custody disclosures limit how much protection can be inferred from them.

ustx-tx.title: Brale-issued dollar for tx settlement
ustx-tx.text: tx launched USTX on October 20, 2026 as a native settlement asset for tokenized stocks, ETFs and other real-world assets, with Brale as issuer. Users mint it on the tx chain against USDC deposited from Ethereum, Solana, Base or Polygon, and Brale states 1:1 backing in US dollar reserves. Brale's program-level policy describes segregated reserves, daily reconciliation and monthly independent attestations, held in short Treasury bills, government money market funds and bank deposits, but none of that is yet tied to USTX-specific allocations or a retrieved reserve report. Brale has published no asset details, but the chain shows that USTX was created on October 8 2026, with 6 decimals and clawback enabled. An issuer-owned extension contract can also pause transfers and blacklist addresses. Supply was 4,833 USTX across 55 holder addresses on November 1 2026. USTX is live and verifiable on its own chain, yet Pharos keeps it pre-launch: the tx chain is not one Pharos supports, and no price listing or USTX {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} terms have been published.

weur-aplauz.title: Aplauz euro token awaiting verified circulation
weur-aplauz.text: Aplauz NL B.V., which trades as WSPN and belongs to the Worldwide Stablecoin Payment Network group through WSPN Fintech Dutch Holding B.V., publishes WEUR as a euro e-money token with reserve assets safeguarded through a separate Dutch foundation. The whitepaper names Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain as its initial networks. The whitepaper grants every holder par redemption after compliance checks and says EUR dispatch should generally occur within five business days of token receipt. ESMA lists the exact issuer and token, but notification does not approve the whitepaper or prove circulation. Public onboarding marketing conflicts with the amended whitepaper's statement that WEUR has not launched. Pharos retains a pre-launch record because production identity and circulation remain unverified.

xgld-unitas.title: XAUt-backed borrowing strategy
xgld-unitas.text: Unitas Gold combines XAUt exposure with a borrowing strategy: XAUt collateral supports USDT loans, and returns from delta-neutral strategies accrue through the token’s net asset value. This adds borrowing, execution and custody dependencies to the gold exposure. Direct minting and XAUt redemption are restricted to whitelisted users on BNB Chain, with a seven-day eligibility cooldown and a 0.1% redemption fee. The cooldown does not establish a guaranteed completion time or funded redemption capacity. Other holders rely on swaps; Base holders must bridge back to BNB for direct redemption. Ethereum and Mantle representations are independently verified on-chain but omitted by issuer interface guides. The native exchange-rate contract measures XAUt per XGLD separately from gold’s dollar price, under privileged administration. Accountable reports gross venue reserves rather than a complete debt-netted strategy inventory. The parent’s gold backing therefore cannot establish the position’s solvency, legal custody or stressed exit capacity.

xgz-goldzip.title: One-gram gold without ownership of stored bars
xgz-goldzip.text: GoldZip Gold references one gram of 99.99%-fine gold, ordinarily redeemable in 1,000-token bar lots after onboarding. Terms deny holders proprietary interests in stored bars; title passes only on collection. The issuer’s 5 October 2026 snapshot maps 39,000 XGZ to 39 Heraeus 1 kg bars at Horsemart Service Limited, 94.9% of it allocated to one address, without independent physical-inventory assurance. Current Rules set appointment-only collection in Hong Kong, a US$100 application fee and a 0.25% gold-value redemption fee, but no completion deadline. A 15 October notice names BVI GoldZip Company Limited as successor to the Singapore issuer on the unchanged Ethereum contract. Holders can elect an entire-balance USDT exit by 5 November 2026 at 23:59 UTC from verified self-custody wallets, priced at XGZ’s own deadline-day traded price on issuer-selected data. One administrator signature can authorize uncapped minting and immediate upgrades, and balances can be frozen or forcibly burned. Exit access and protection therefore depend on issuer operations and legal terms, not ownership of the allocated bars.

zarsc-supercoin.title: Cash-backed rand with exchange-only live exit
zarsc-supercoin.text: ZAR Supercoin transfers rand-denominated value on Solana under Super Money SA's issuer controls. The latest published reserve snapshot places its backing in an Absa current account. Moore's August agreed-upon procedures obtained bank support and reconciled issued tokens to token accounts, then applied management-designated treasury and reserve exclusions to calculate circulating coverage. The engagement provides no assurance opinion and does not establish holder bankruptcy priority. Those historical balances do not prove today's reserve position. Exchange sale and off-ramp routes are available, but the direct app redemption promise applies only after the wallet launches. The terms guarantee neither exchange prices nor settlement timing. Retained freeze, pause and permanent-delegate powers give the issuer direct holder controls, and an unset transfer hook remains mutable. Fireblocks supplies issuance-key infrastructure without establishing independent human approvals. Holders depend on issuer operations and third-party exit liquidity even while the token targets one rand.

zaru-blocktower.title: BlockTower rand with institutional redemption
zaru-blocktower.text: ZAR Universal is issued by BlockTower South Africa (Pty) Ltd, formerly Loop South Africa, with direct minting and redemption restricted to approved institutional accounts and retail access through network partners. Moore's latest issuer-linked report measures the August 31, 2026 Solana book: rand cash and bank deposits at Standard Bank and money-market funds at Sanlam. Its agreed-upon procedures reconcile that historical snapshot without providing an assurance opinion, current whole-token allocations or independently established insolvency priority. Issuer authority remains concentrated in an ordinary Solana signer and an EVM administrator with uncapped mint, immediate upgrade and recovery powers. ZARU itself pays no interest on reserves. Redemption returns rand to an eligible holder's bank account, but the binding platform agreement guarantees no processing period. All-in fees, minimums, fund constituents and independently verifiable key-custody arrangements remain incompletely disclosed.

usd3-3jane.title: 3Jane's Senior Credit Share
usd3-3jane.text: USD3 packages 3Jane's senior credit tranche into an ERC-4626 share: USDC enters, idle cash waits in Aave, and the rest finances fintech receivables and crypto credit lines. Its NAV can rise above a dollar because interest accrues into the share price, so the familiar ticker is doing fund accounting rather than promising a fixed $1 quote. sUSD3 absorbs losses first, but that protection is only as thick as the junior tranche, and Pharos grades recovery as limited because the write-off mechanics have no realized default cycle.  The credit receivables, roughly nine-tenths of the book at Pharos's July 2026 on-chain read, are scored as receivables rather than folded into the dollar they settle in, so the liquid Aave buffer and the deployed book are priced apart instead of averaged into a comfortable middle. Exit scores near the top, because withdrawals return USDC whenever the buffer allows. The overall score is also held at a binding structural cap: the same instant ERC-4626 redemption rail and a critical control identity recur across dozens of reviewed asset paths, so a failure there would not stay local. The durable constraint is that the senior share remains a claim on 3Jane's credit book, with only the junior tranche standing ahead of its losses.

kusd-kerne.title: Base synthetic dollar with USDC PSM
kusd-kerne.text: kUSD is Kerne Protocol's Base-native synthetic dollar. A first external audit from Hexens landed in late July with zero criticals and every finding confined to the yield vault. The audit followed a patched Peg Stability Module cutover that opened permissionless 1:1 USDC minting. The live KerneVault still runs pre-audit bytecode with deposits closed until the remediated version deploys, so the audited code and the deployed code are not yet the same thing. Current backing is USDC in the PSM contracts, covering outstanding kUSD slightly above 1:1. The delta-neutral design, using a WETH vault and Hyperliquid short, remains degraded and excluded from reserves. Since August 6, kUSD role administration and PSM configuration sit behind a 48-hour timelock whose sole proposer and executor is a 2-of-3 Safe, and hourly signed proof-of-reserves is published at kerne.fi/verify. DefiLlama indexes the supply with no usable price, and CoinGecko still does not resolve the coin, so Pharos keeps it on the upcoming tracker. The durable constraint is scale: circulating supply has stayed at genesis levels since minting opened in July.

usdt-tether.title: Treasury Wall, Thin Equity Cushion
usdt-tether.text: USDT carries a {{grade}} overall grade. The peg record and the exit pillar sit at the top of the scale, economic control is strong, and backing is the weakest of the three pillars. That backing line carries secured loans, gold, bitcoin, and equities alongside the {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} wall, and the card flags the attested composition as older than the freshness bound between quarterly reports. BDO's assurance report for June 30, 2026 puts assets about $4.1 billion ahead of roughly $184 billion of liabilities, half the $8.2 billion cushion it reported three months earlier. The same report shows a loss of about $3.2 billion for the first half of the year. Half the supply sits on Tron, a concentration the card prices as a common-mode deployment risk. USDT0 carries the franchise to further chains, but Pharos treats those routes as third-party representations rather than native issuance. The {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} floor is real for eligible Tether customers but runs on Tether's terms and discretion, with quarterly {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} rather than continuous disclosure. The Ethereum and Tron tokens expose owner-only blacklist, fund-destruction and pause functions. In Europe, Pharos records USDT as non-compliant under MiCA, and Revolut has delisted it for affected EEA customers. Issuance, reserves and holder balances all remain under Tether's centralized control.

usdc-circle.title: Circle's Fund-Held Reserve Dollar
usdc-circle.text: USDC is Circle's fiat-backed dollar: most of the reserve sits in the Circle Reserve Fund, managed by BlackRock with assets custodied at BNY Mellon, while monthly Deloitte examinations reconcile reserve assets against the full token liability. At the August 2026 examination, overnight Treasury repo carried about two thirds of the reserve, with short-dated Treasuries and cash at regulated banks splitting the rest; the examination does not break the bank cash out by institution. Its on-chain liquidity is unusually distributed, so a dollar that exits one venue does not have to leave the market altogether, and the SVB weekend remains the reminder that banking access can still interrupt an otherwise conservative reserve stack. The {{grade}} overall grade is doing a narrow job: backing and exit sit near the top of the scale, and economic control is the weakest of the three pillars. That weakness is the point of centralization: direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Circle, Circle can freeze balances and upgrade the token, and several third-party bridge routes carry controls Pharos scores lower. The durable constraint is that dependence: USDC holds its value only as long as Circle, its fund manager, its custodian, and its banks keep operating normally.

dai-makerdao.title: CDP Origins, Shared Sky Balance Sheet
dai-makerdao.text: DAI is MakerDAO's USD stablecoin, first minted from {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}s and now mostly backed by PSM stablecoins and Sky's allocator books. The {{grade}} report card rests on public token governance, with discretionary expansion routed through a 48-hour delay, though the economic-control pillar is the weakest of the three: issuance remains economically unbounded and the voting stake is concentrated. The reserve composition has moved far from its crypto-collateral origins: roughly two-fifths USDC through the {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}, about a third in Spark's lending allocation, a sixth in Grove's real-world-asset book, and only a low single-digit sliver left in the crypto vaults that made DAI famous. It is functionally a hybrid fiat-credit dollar. The peg record is strong over four years of tracking, and the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop, powered by atomic PSM access with fees not activated, earns an exit pillar at the top of the scale. DAI shares one balance sheet with its upgraded successor USDS, so its backing follows Sky's allocation choices for both tokens, which now lean on USDC and allocator credit rather than crypto vaults.

frax-frax.title: Legacy FRAX, Partly Backed by Frax Paper
frax-frax.text: FRAX abandoned its {{term:algorithmic}}fractional-algorithmic{{/term}} origins for a reserve split between tokenized {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} funds and Frax's own tokens. WisdomTree WTGXX, Superstate USTB and BlackRock BUIDL together make up a smaller share of the balance sheet than Frax-issued FRAX, frxUSD, sFRAX and sfrxUSD combined, with a small Ethena USDe sleeve alongside. That self-issued block is the problem the report card keeps flagging: backing is the weakest of the three pillars, and the issuer publishes self-reported USD values with no independent NAV reconciliation for legacy FRAX. The {{grade}} overall grade sits beside a peg history with a long tail of episodes across more than three years of tracking, a token still prone to drift below par, and stress monitoring that has not stayed at the calm end of the scale. Frax's successor dollar, frxUSD, now sits inside the reserve. The durable constraint is circularity: a legacy dollar partly backed by its own successor and its own liquidity cannot be graded on the T-bills alone.

tusd-trueusd.title: Daily Attestation, Illiquid Reserve
tusd-trueusd.text: TrueUSD is Techteryx's dollar stablecoin, and its paperwork is unusually frequent: Moore CPA signs a reasonable-assurance report on the reserve every day. What those reports disclose is the problem. Effectively the entire reserve sits at cost in a single First Digital Trust fund position, in instruments the report's management notes say cannot be readily converted to cash, against a backdrop of redemption litigation and a DIFC worldwide freezing order of up to $456 million. The reserve total still exceeds tokens issued, and most of the supply is held by Techteryx itself rather than the public float. Archblock's Chapter 11 filing, Kraken's delisting, and S&P's weakest stablecoin stability score sit in the notices. On the card, backing scores in the upper half because the attestation and reconciliation are strong even where the asset is illiquid, while exit is the weakest of the three pillars, with {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} running through a single issuer. The peg itself has held near par for over a year. The daily {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} measures that illiquidity precisely without resolving it. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects the durable constraint: par redemption depends on one issuer and a fund position its own disclosures describe as hard to turn into cash.

lusd-liquity.title: The Immutable Benchmark
lusd-liquity.text: LUSD remains the reference design for an ungoverned dollar: ETH-only collateral, immutable contracts, no governance and no upstream stablecoin dependencies. It earns its strongest marks on the exit and control pillars, while ETH-only purity keeps backing a notch lower and a long peg record trims the score further, leaving the overall grade at {{grade}}. The permissionless {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop is the load-bearing piece: anyone can swap LUSD for $1 of ETH from the riskiest Trove, paying a fee of at least 0.5% that rises with redemption volume and decays over time. That floor bounds only the downside, and Pharos has recorded hundreds of peg deviations, including a flight-to-safety premium when the SVB failure broke USDC, DAI and FRAX in March 2023. Troves below the 110% minimum collateral ratio are liquidated against the Stability Pool first, with any shortfall redistributed across the remaining Troves. Liquity's own V2 dollar, BOLD, has since moved to WETH, wstETH and rETH collateral with user-set interest rates. The durable constraint is the immutability itself: the code that removes admin risk also leaves no lever to adapt LUSD to a market that moved on.

mim-abracadabra.title: Abracadabra's CDP Stablecoin After the 2026 Depeg
mim-abracadabra.text: Magic Internet Money was Abracadabra's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin, minted against interest-bearing tokens and crypto collateral in cauldron vaults and once among DeFi's largest, peaking above $3.6B. Its peg relied on borrowers buying discounted MIM to repay debt rather than on a {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} window. The record before the end was already heavy, with three material cauldron exploits between January 2024 and October 2025 and years of thinning liquidity. The final break began on June 8, 2026. Abracadabra injected liquidity, offered SPELL incentives, raised rates across every cauldron and suspended Curve bribes to force repayment, and none of it restored the peg. On July 14, Abracadabra-controlled Safes moved roughly $8.3M of treasury assets with no public explanation found by Pharos, shrinking the visible backstop. By July 26 MIM traded near $0.09 with roughly $3M circulating, and Pharos froze it. The last measured collateral was mostly yvDAI and WBTC, and no credible liquidity or arbitrage path back to one dollar remained.

usdp-paxos.title: The Credentialed Reference Implementation
usdp-paxos.text: Paxos's USDP is a regulated dollar live since 2018, issued under Paxos's OCC National Trust Charter and backed by cash and overnight repurchase agreements collateralized by U.S. Treasuries, with KPMG examining the redemption-asset report every month. Cash makes up about three-quarters of the book, and some of those commercial-bank balances exceed FDIC insurance limits. Backing is the strongest of the three pillars on the {{grade}} card, with economic control behind it; the gap to an elite overall grade lives in exit, the weakest pillar. Direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through Paxos is the primary route, but Pharos measures it settling over about a day and covering only part of a stress-size request. Paxos also issues dollars for partners. It issued Binance's BUSD until New York's financial regulator ordered it to stop minting in February 2023, and it now issues PayPal's PYUSD and the Global Dollar, USDG. No depeg event has been recorded since early 2025, but holders without Paxos accounts still trade through thin on-chain depth.

usdd-tron-dao-reserve.title: Back to TRX-Heavy Backing
usdd-tron-dao-reserve.text: USDD's reserve is once more dominated by TRX posted as CDP collateral, with a sliver of sTRX, alongside a Smart Allocator sleeve of stablecoin DeFi deployments and a thin USDT {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} buffer. That mix follows the August 2024 removal of Bitcoin from collateral, which TRON DAO Reserve carried out without prior DAO approval. The {{grade}} overall grade is dragged down by economic control, the weakest of the three pillars: chain-local governance proxies under the reserve's own control can authorize new mint rails or lift limits immediately, with no independent timelock. Backing is held back too, because the Smart Allocator sleeve, more than a third of the book, cannot be attributed to specific assets at a common checkpoint, and the scored input carries no reserve composition. The peg itself behaves better than the rest of the profile, but that surface stability has been bought across hundreds of brief deviations over the years. The PSM remains the load-bearing piece: permissionless swaps against USDT give the exit pillar a redemption quality the surrounding reserve mix cannot match. The durable constraint is governance: a Dominica-domiciled reserve whose collateral and mint limits change when TRON DAO Reserve decides they should.

dola-inverse-finance.title: Fixed-Rate Lending on Circular Collateral
dola-inverse-finance.text: DOLA is Inverse Finance's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style dollar, minted into FiRM's fixed-rate lending markets and lent against posted collateral. Most FiRM debt is secured by Curve LP positions pairing DOLA or sDOLA against external stablecoins, so much of the collateral base is DOLA backing DOLA. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by exit, the weakest pillar. The Fed chair can only expand supply into registered markets and fixed modules within governance-set ceilings, but the DAO's 48-hour Timelock can mint to any address without collateral or a cap. Inverse identifies the dominant delegated voting power as the founder's own escrowed INV, enough to meet quorum in an unopposed proposal. The canonical USDS {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} held no USDS or sUSDS reserves at Pharos's October 2026 read, leaving the sell direction without funded capacity. Permissionless jrDOLA slashing reaches most FiRM markets, but its capital is a fraction of a percent of outstanding debt. About 2.76 million DOLA of Frontier bad debt remains, and recorded repayments have been sparse since early 2026. The durable constraint is collateral whose value rests largely on DOLA's own price.

sdola-inverse-finance.title: DOLA With an Exchange Rate
sdola-inverse-finance.text: sDOLA is the ERC-4626 wrapper around DOLA's savings account, which means the stablecoin risk is still DOLA and the extra product risk is the exchange-rate wrapper sitting on top. FiRM borrowing revenue is converted through the DBR-DOLA auction and compounded into a rising DOLA:sDOLA exchange rate, so the yield is tied to borrower demand rather than token emissions. The wrapper does not create new base DOLA supply, but holders still inherit DOLA's CDP collateral mix, governance, and any upstream stress in the parent peg. Minting, unwrapping, and yield accrual operate on Ethereum. Governance mill 396, executed August 11, 2026, shut the Chainlink CCIP lanes to Base, Optimism, Arbitrum, and Berachain; those receipt contracts are historical deployments, not live bridge destinations. The {{grade}} overall grade is capped at the parent DOLA rating. Unwrapping has no lock-up but returns DOLA rather than dollars, leaving the parent peg and exit liquidity as the durable constraint.

gusd-gemini.title: Gemini's Bank-Cash Dollar, Thin Exit
gusd-gemini.text: GUSD is Gemini Trust's NYDFS-chartered dollar, redeemable 1:1 through Gemini. The August 31 2026 BPM examination reported its reserves as cash deposits at State Street and Western Alliance Bank, held in segregated accounts for holders. That state charter has not carried into the newer regimes: Pharos's compliance review found no GENIUS approval or application, and GUSD holds no MiCA authorization. The float is small, at {{supplyUsd}} in circulation. Backing and economic control are the strong pillars of the {{grade}} report card, while exit is the weakest. Pharos scores exit on Gemini's own account-based redemption, because the Ethereum AMM route offers no measured same-size alternative. The peg record carries a long tail of brief deviations, the deepest of them below peg, and the price has recovered after each one. The issuance ceiling binds loosely: a single limited-printer key can mint immediately up to 1.36 billion GUSD, many times current supply, and raising that ceiling takes a 2-of-3 custodian plus a one-hour delay. The durable constraint is that exit still runs through Gemini's own redemption desk.

alusd-alchemix.title: Self-Repaying Dollar
alusd-alchemix.text: alUSD is Alchemix's self-repaying {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar: borrowers' collateral earns yield that pays down their debt over time. Since the V2-to-V3 migration in April 2026, that collateral is USDC-denominated MYT vault shares spread across DAO-selected yield strategies. V3 also changed the risk. A position can now be liquidated if strategy losses push it to a fixed 95% loan-to-value threshold, though ETH or USDC price swings alone do not trigger it. The Transmuter converts vested alUSD at face value into MYT, subject to bad-debt haircuts, deposit caps, and strategy liquidity, with early-exit fees on unvested positions, so par depends on a slow, conditional conversion rather than an instant {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. Pharos logs depeg events in the hundreds across alUSD's history, and the peg multiplier pulls its {{grade}} overall grade well below what its pillars alone would earn. Backing is held back because the card admits no current reserve composition. The V3 contracts are administered by 3-of-7 Safes, and legacy token-admin reactivation and upgrade powers remain.

susd-synthetix.title: Retired Below Par
susd-synthetix.text: Synthetix's sUSD was DeFi's original synthetic dollar, minted against staked SNX from 2018. Its peg rested on one reflex: when sUSD slipped below $1, stakers bought it at a discount to repay their debt at par. SIP-420 in April 2025 dismantled that reflex by cutting the collateral ratio from 750% to 200% and pooling debt, so minting got cheaper while no individual staker had a reason to defend the dollar. sUSD fell to about $0.68 within weeks and never recovered. Treasury and SLP-vault activity worked as peg defense rather than backing, and it never brought sUSD back to par. In June 2026 governance chose conversion over repair and passed SIP-423: the contract was frozen, a holder snapshot was taken, and sUSD became permanently non-transferable. Snapshot holders are entitled to 4 SNX per sUSD, locked for one year and then vested over a second, so compensation carries up to two years of SNX price exposure. Unclaimed receipts expire worthless after six months. sUSD left in LP pools or vaults cannot be recovered directly; those holders must claim through a separate Treasury process using their deposit or LP receipt tokens, assessed case by case. Pharos froze its tracking on June 26, 2026.

ousd-origin-protocol.title: Origin's Rebasing USDC Vault
ousd-origin-protocol.text: Origin Dollar is a {{term:yield-bearing}}rebasing{{/term}} USDC wrapper on Ethereum: deposits are minted 1:1 into the OUSD Vault, which deploys the USDC into Morpho lending markets and a Curve {{term:amo}}AMO{{/term}}, and yield reaches holders through daily rebases. Smart-contract balances, multisigs included, do not rebase until the contract opts in, which concentrates that yield on the balances that do. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} back to USDC runs 1:1 through the Vault, usually after a short buffer delay that can stretch to a day when the buffer needs refilling. That floor has absorbed a long tail of depeg episodes, and backing is the strongest pillar on the card: Origin publishes per-strategy USDC amounts, so the book is observable. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by economic control instead. Ordinary minting requires USDC, but the 48-hour governance timelock can approve a strategy that mints without transferring collateral, so Pharos treats issuance as economically unbounded and that cap binds the score. A two-of-eight Strategist Safe with partially reviewed modules sits alongside it. The durable constraint is that OUSD's supply is only as bounded as Origin governance chooses to keep it.

cusd-celo.title: A Reserve Mostly of Other Stablecoins
cusd-celo.text: Mento Dollar (USDm, formerly cUSD) is Mento's oracle-priced dollar on Celo, and its reserve is an exercise in recursive stablecoin nesting: roughly three-quarters of the book is other issuers' stablecoins, with AUSD and sUSDS the largest slices and USDT, EUROP, EURC, and USDC layered on top, so most of USDm's backing is itself backed elsewhere, each layer with its own dependency chain and failure modes. A long tail of mostly minor depeg events and a double-digit worst drawdown are hard numbers to look past. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} runs through Mento reserve swaps rather than fiat off-ramps, and that permissionless route now earns the exit pillar the top line on the card. The {{grade}} overall grade is pulled down by economic control, the weakest of the three: the Mento Safe that owns the Celo token can authorise new minters or burners and replace the implementation immediately, and every reviewed price feed runs through a single relayer. Backing sits between the two, held back because Pharos cannot reconcile the shared reserve's liabilities to one dated anchor. The volatile slice is mostly CELO, roughly a fifth of the reserve, alongside small stETH and ETH positions, so a broad crypto decline hits the reserve chiefly through Celo's own native asset.

eurc-circle.title: Circle's Bank-Cash Euro
eurc-circle.text: Circle's EURC is a MiCA euro stablecoin issued by an ACPR-authorized EMI, {{term:attestation}}examined monthly by Deloitte{{/term}}, and deployed on roughly a dozen chains. The latest examination shows a reserve that is entirely bank cash at regulated financial institutions, with no securities. That is defensible for a euro float, and a reminder that EURC's real counterparty is a set of banks Circle does not name. The {{grade}} overall grade carries that examination: backing and economic control sit close together, and exit is the strongest pillar. EURC's float is still small next to USDC. The peg record shows a handful of episodes across four years of tracking, none of them recent.

eurs-stasis.title: STASIS Euro's Drifting Quote
eurs-stasis.text: EURS is STASIS's euro stablecoin, launched in 2018 as the first of its category and redeemable 1:1 through STSS (Malta) Limited against euro balances at licensed EU institutions. The transparency page allocates the entire reserve to a Lietuvos bankas account reached through NexPay UAB, but the allocation carries no as-of date, the newest dated account statement Pharos retrieved (December 2025) does not reconcile to it, and no independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} exists. Segregated safeguarded accounts remain contractual commitments in STSS's terms rather than verified arrangements. Malta's financial services register shows the issuer's legacy whitepaper as deregistered and no other authorisation. Backing is the weakest of three pillars clustered in a low band, and the peg record pulls the {{grade}} overall grade below all of them: EURS has logged dozens of depeg episodes across four years of tracking. Distribution spans seven chains, three of them third-party lock-and-mint representations including a Multichain route on Arbitrum. The durable constraint is the market: price confidence is low, and redemption at par has not kept the quote there.

ceur-celo.title: Mento's Reserve-Backed Euro
ceur-celo.text: EURm, formerly cEUR, is Mento's oracle-priced euro stablecoin on Celo, minted and redeemed against the shared Mento Reserve through Fixed-Price Market Maker pools that quote a Chainlink EUR rate rather than deriving price from pool depth, with circuit breakers halting trade when the feed is stale or off-peg. The reserve is a mixed basket led by near-equal positions in CELO, AUSD, and sUSDS, with USDT, euro stablecoins, stETH, and smaller dollar and ETH positions behind them. Mento describes it as {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} under a stable-asset mandate, yet about a quarter of it is the network's own volatile token, and Pharos admits no reconciled collateralization ratio. Those reserve swaps are the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route, and the exit pillar is the strongest line on the {{grade}} card. The owner Safe appoints operators and burners that can move or destroy any holder balance, a Wormhole NTT route carries a material share of supply to Monad, and residual Ethereum, Polygon, and Solana balances are legacy bridged cEUR. The peg record is the caution flag: Pharos has logged a long tail of deviation episodes, including one extreme print, and pricing rests on a single source. The durable constraint is a euro claim backed by a dollar-and-CELO reserve whose liabilities Pharos cannot yet reconcile across every chain.

fpi-frax.title: CPI on a Blockchain
fpi-frax.text: FPI is Frax's CPI-tracking stablecoin, with a {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} price designed to grow every second at the trailing 12-month CPI-U rate delivered by a Chainlink oracle. Frax governance proposal FIP-448, dated June 2026, would freeze that reference price and retire minting; Pharos has not established that it was executed. The reserve is mostly FRAX itself, plus a staked Convex FPI/FRAX liquidity position and a small Fraxswap FRAX/FPIS pool, with {{term:amo}}AMO{{/term}} yield meant to cover the inflation accrual and FPIS sales as the backstop when it falls short. That makes FPI both a stablecoin and an inflation derivative with a single-issuer dependency: its collateral is only as good as legacy FRAX. Backing and exit grade similarly on the card. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by economic control, the weakest pillar by a wide margin, because the FPI contract's minter function mints without a collateral check and a 3-of-5 Comptroller Safe can add new minters. The durable constraint is double: whatever weakens FRAX flows straight into FPI's backing, and the issuance gate is a multisig rather than the collateral.

uusd-youves.title: Overcollateralized Vaults, Unanchored Peg
uusd-youves.text: Youves's uUSD is a Tezos {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin minted against vault collateral that, at Pharos's August 2026 read, was overwhelmingly USDt, with residual XTZ, tzBTC and SIRS LP tokens. Its report card carries a {{grade}} overall grade with a Safety Score of {{score}} out of 100. The peg failure is long-running: uUSD has well over a thousand recorded depeg events and an active depeg still flagged, with excursions both below and above the dollar. Backing is the best of the three pillars, because the vault collateral Pharos read comfortably exceeds outstanding supply. That has not been enough. Exit and economic control share the bottom of the card: Pharos has no verified same-value route out, and a 4-of-7 keyholder multisig administers every minting engine, with the Youves DAO as co-administrator on most. V3 contracts enforce only emergency collateral ratios, not the higher targets shown in the front end. The card also carries caps for the active depeg and a single-source oracle topology. uUSD shows that {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} secures a vault, not a market price: without a working arbitrage or redemption loop, the token trades wherever its remaining market puts it.

lisusd-lista.title: A BNB Chain CDP Built on slisBNB
lisusd-lista.text: lisUSD is Lista DAO's BNB Chain {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar, launched in 2022 on the MakerDAO pattern, with a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} that the issuer documents for 1:1 minting against USDT and USDC. The collateral book is far narrower than its list of issuer-listed GemJoin markets implies. Pharos's September censuses put slisBNB, Lista's own liquid-staking token, at roughly nine-tenths or more of the priced collateral, with BTCB and wBETH as small remainders. slisBNB's proxy is owned by the same 24-hour timelock that controls lisUSD, so most of the collateral sits under the protocol's own upgrade keys. Pharos withdrew the live reserve feed because the adapter could not value every branch exactly, and backing is now scored on a selected-slice basis with limited evidence. Admin-role membership is not fully established and effective minting is scored as unbounded. The peg record spans four years of tracking with a long tail of deviation episodes, including one drop of more than half its value. Distribution is BSC-only, so BNB's price, slisBNB's liquidity and the PSM's capacity together set how well the peg holds under {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} pressure.

eure-monerium.title: SEPA Native, DeFi Adopted
eure-monerium.text: EURe is Monerium's MiCA-authorised euro e-money token, issued by an Icelandic EMI and minted and burned against SEPA transfers. Most reserves sit in State Street's AAA-rated EUR LVNAV {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}}, with the rest in segregated deposits at Arion Bank and LHV Bank, at weights Monerium does not publish. That disclosure gap holds the {{grade}} overall grade down. The safeguarding structure is sound in design, but the backing pillar grades what is proven: Monerium's issued and safeguarded totals are self-reported, and the regular public attestations it says it is preparing have not yet appeared. Backing is therefore the weakest pillar, while economic control is the strongest, with issuer-backend minting reconciled across nine native deployments from Ethereum and its L2s to Gnosis, Polygon, Noble and Algorand. The peg record shows a string of brief episodes, and burning EURe for a SEPA {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} remains the exit that does not depend on pool depth. The gap to the top tier is assurance: EURC's reserves are examined monthly by a Big Four firm, and Monerium's are self-reported.

eusd-electronic-usd.title: Lending Basket With First-Loss Risk
eusd-electronic-usd.text: eUSD is a Reserve Protocol RToken that holds Compound V3 USDC, Aave V3 USDC and Compound V3 USDT in equal thirds behind permissionless basket {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, with RSR stakers absorbing first loss. Atomic permissionless redemption makes exit the strongest pillar on the card, and the peg record is strong, though its long tail of historical depeg episodes includes a double-digit break in earlier years. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by economic control, the weakest pillar by a wide margin. Central admin authority sits with a 3-of-5 Safe that the mint-authority review found could grant itself ownership, change the basket and upgrade the token with no timelock. A later October 2026 review reads a three-day timelock in front of RToken upgrades through Main, and Pharos has not yet reconciled the two findings. Backing lands in the middle once the dependencies on Aave, Compound, USDC and USDT are priced in; pinned on-chain reads confirm the equal-thirds basket, and the weights remain governance-set. The durable constraint is a wrapper that inherits every layer beneath it, governed by a key set whose upgrade delay Pharos's own records still dispute.

crvusd-curve.title: LLAMMA on Custodial Bitcoin
crvusd-curve.text: crvUSD is Curve's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin with LLAMMA soft-liquidation, and most of its collateral is custodial WBTC and cbBTC. LLAMMA replaces cliff-edge {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}} with gradual rebalancing through price bands. Bitcoin collateral held through BitGo and Coinbase adds centralized {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} dependencies to a crypto-collateralized design. PegKeeper pools paired with USDC, USDT, PYUSD, frxUSD, and GHO provide active peg machinery. The {{grade}} overall grade comes from the economic-control pillar, the weakest of the three: the Curve DAO's execution path can raise a debt ceiling and mint to an arbitrary recipient without collateral, and the largest veCRV bloc, Convex's pooled position, votes through a caster that a 3-of-5 Safe can replace, so the week-long public vote does not amount to dispersed control. The exit pillar is held back because its routes share a failure domain. The durable constraint is that crvUSD supply has no economic bound beyond Curve governance, so supply discipline rests on who controls that vote.

gho-aave.title: Aave's Lending-Book Dollar
gho-aave.text: GHO is Aave's dollar, minted by borrowing against Aave collateral: a diversified {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar issued through a set of registered facilitators. The {{grade}} overall grade splits sharply across the pillars. Exit sits near the top of the scale on a deeply distributed DEX footprint plus {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}-style GSM redemption. Backing sits in the middle: the collateral is whatever mixed crypto Aave's risk machinery accepts, and the largest issuance bucket, the mainnet GSM facilitator, has no reconciled inventory of what sits behind it.  Pharos's mint review finds that a 2-of-3 Risk Council can mint GHO through that mainnet facilitator to a recipient of its choice, without a deposit or delay and independent of DAO governance, so native issuance is treated as economically unbounded. The long tail of brief sub-peg episodes dates from GHO's earlier years, with no depeg event recorded since February 2025. The durable constraint is governance rather than collateral: the exit works, but the supply ceiling depends on a small council and steward limits, not on code that enforces backing.

fdusd-first-digital.title: Binance's Post-BUSD Dollar
fdusd-first-digital.text: FDUSD is a BVI-issued dollar stablecoin backed by short-dated {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and cash, with every reserve account held by First Digital Trust, a related-party Hong Kong trust company. It rose to prominence when Binance listed it as the BUSD replacement in 2023, and the custodian risk stopped being abstract in April 2025: after Justin Sun publicly called the {{term:custody}}custodian{{/term}} insolvent, FDUSD fell to about $0.87 before recovering. The next day First Digital filed a defamation writ against Sun in Hong Kong's High Court. AOGB's monthly {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} reconciles supply to reserve accounts and lists each Treasury bill by maturity, and backing grades well on that mix. The report does not name the banks beneath the custodian, spread across ten jurisdictions, or their shares, and the issuer's own dashboard has shown a cash figure that conflicts with the signed report. The {{grade}} overall grade puts exit at the bottom of the card, while the peg record is among its strongest lines and later depeg episodes have been brief. The durable constraint is concentration: one related-party trust company stands between holders and every dollar of reserves.

pyusd-paypal.title: PayPal's Paxos-Issued Dollar
pyusd-paypal.text: PayPal's PYUSD is issued by Paxos Trust Company under an OCC national trust charter, and its reserve is examined monthly by KPMG: mostly overnight Treasury-collateralized reverse repos, with Treasury bills and a small cash sleeve, held for token holders in segregated accounts that Paxos's terms describe as bankruptcy remote. The exit pillar is the strongest line on the card, with permissionless 1:1 issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. What holds the {{grade}} overall grade below the reserve quality is the economic-control pillar, the weakest of the three. Issuer-direct minting across four native surfaces is economically unbounded and reconciled only against reserves, and Paxos administrator paths can change controllers, caps, and token logic. In October 2025 a technical error during an internal transfer minted about 300 trillion PYUSD, burned the same day. Pharos also records a live freeze-and-wipe power on the main Ethereum and Solana deployments. Most other chains carry LayerZero omnichain representations, plus a Wanchain bridge to Cardano, so the multichain surface adds external validation risk on top of issuer controls. The reserve is checked monthly; the controls over issuance and holder balances rest on Paxos's own operations.

gyen-gyen.title: NYDFS-Chartered Yen in Wind-Down
gyen-gyen.text: GYEN is GMO-Z.com Trust's yen stablecoin, issued under a New York trust charter and backed by yen held at FDIC-insured institutions, government money-market funds or short-dated {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, with monthly {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} from The Network Firm. Its issuer stack was among the most tightly regulated of any JPY stablecoin. Demand never matched the custody. Thin secondary liquidity and a depeg history left GYEN trading more like a neglected FX instrument than a stablecoin, most visibly in May 2021, when it squeezed above 1.5 times its peg; the class action that followed reached a proposed $6.75M settlement in 2026. On May 15, 2026 GMO-Z.com Trust announced an orderly wind-down of GYEN and ZUSD and began voluntary dissolution under New York banking law. Purchases are disabled, and eligible account holders can redeem during an initial period that runs through November 11, 2026. With issuance ended, redemption during that window is the token's only remaining function.

usdy-ondo-finance.title: Treasury Note Behind an Eligibility Gate
usdy-ondo-finance.text: Ondo's USDY is a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} tokenized note offered under Regulation S to qualifying non-U.S. investors, with yield reflected in a rising redemption price rather than a fixed dollar peg. The assets look conventional. Ankura Trust's September 25, 2026 daily report for the U.S. LLC issuance puts nearly all reported principal in short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills held at Marex and BNY Mellon, with traces of bank and brokerage cash. The gap is scope. About 6% of circulating USDY, including issuance through Ondo's BVI entity, sits outside that report with no USDY-specific allocation published. With that partial reserve review and unresolved control identities, Pharos judges critical evidence insufficient for a rating, and the card reads {{grade}} rather than a measured grade. Among the pillar scores, exit is the weakest. Eligible registered holders can redeem through Ondo's InstantManager for supported stablecoins, subject to compliance checks, limits and router liquidity, but no same-value capacity is established across a footprint of more than a dozen networks. The durable constraint is access: the Treasuries are verifiable for one entity's share, and getting out at their value depends on being an eligible holder.

cadc-cad-coin.title: Backed by Scanned Bank Letters
cadc-cad-coin.text: CADC is a Canadian-dollar stablecoin issued by CADC Reserve Trust, an Ontario special purpose trust, with 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} for CAD held in a segregated account at ATB Financial. The Ontario Securities Commission receipted the trust's final prospectus on October 22, 2026. Loon Payments services the token, and the FINTRAC money-services registrations on record belong to Loon and Paytrie, not to the trust. Issuance is moving to new Ethereum, Base, Polygon and Solana contracts by November 26, 2026, and the addresses Pharos tracks for supply are now labeled legacy. The reserve evidence is thinner than that regulatory profile suggests. Loon publishes monthly scanned bank-confirmation forms that carry no accountant's opinion and do not reconcile the balance against circulating supply. Loon's terms still make the trust indenture available only on request, so holder protection in an issuer insolvency remains unverified. On-chain depth absorbs only a sliver of a stress-size sale. The peg record carries a long tail of deviation events, though none since May 2024. Canada's Stablecoin Act, which received royal assent in March 2026, exempts regulated financial institutions, and the issuer trust, with no financial-institution charter on record, appears to fall in scope. That would require it to register with the Bank of Canada and file reserve reports carrying an independent accountant's opinion. Until those provisions take effect, expected in 2027, the backing evidence remains a balance confirmation rather than an attestation.

cadd-cad-digital.title: Canada's Institutional CAD Rail
cadd-cad-digital.text: CADD launched in May 2026 as Canada's first CAD stablecoin issued by a regulated financial institution: Tetra Trust issues it under Alberta's Loan and Trust Corporations Act, with CAD Digital acting as agent and Shopify, National Bank of Canada, ATB Financial and Wealthsimple among the launch backers. That charter also sets its regulatory position. Canada's Stablecoin Act, assented in March 2026, excludes financial-institution issuers from Bank of Canada registration, so CADD appears to stay under Alberta's trust-company oversight rather than the new federal regime. The reserve evidence is unusually clean for a long-tail fiat coin. Monthly Baker Tilly reasonable-assurance {{term:attestation}}examinations{{/term}} reconcile a pooled trust reserve held entirely in Canadian dollar cash against CADD circulating on Ethereum, Base and Tempo. Direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is at par after registration and sanctions checks, for a fee of the greater of CAD 50 or 0.25%. On the {{grade}} card, exit is the strongest pillar and backing narrowly the weakest, with a track-record cap for the short history. Issuance is operator-mediated, with shared minter, admin and upgrade roles and no on-chain cap or timelock, so supply discipline rests on the attestation cadence rather than code. Circulation remains small next to the backer roster, and the clean peg record so far covers a young, thin market.

usde-ethena.title: Ethena's Hedged Dollar, Now Mostly Cash and Credit
usde-ethena.text: Ethena's USDe was built as a tokenized {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}}: hold crypto and short the same amount in {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} futures so the price moves cancel out. Ethena's October 1, 2026 collateral disclosure shows that trade is now the minority of backing. About four fifths sat in a basket Ethena calls Liquid Cash: stablecoins, DeFi lending, tokenized funds, and institutional loans. Ethena publishes that category split but not the weights inside the basket. The hedged remainder, led by BTC and ETH, sits with the custodians Copper, Ceffu, and Fireblocks while its short positions run on centralized exchanges. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects that mix: exit is the strongest of its three pillars and economic control the weakest. That pillar asks who can change minting, pricing, and bridges. Here a 5-of-10 multisig can replace the contract allowed to mint USDe after a one-day delay, and Pharos has not resolved the controls on many of its bridged versions. On TON, the token administrator can also lock a holder's wallet or move and burn its balance, a power the Ethereum token lacks. The peg record is clean, with a handful of brief deviations in under three years of tracking. A live dashboard shows the split, but custodian reports arrive monthly and every mint is approved by Ethena's own off-chain signer. The token's market price reveals nothing about those custodians, exchanges, or basket holdings, so holders rely on Ethena's reporting to see what backs each USDe.

aeur-anchored-coins.title: Solvent Swiss Euro, Retired by MiCAR
aeur-anchored-coins.text: AEUR was Anchored Coins' euro stablecoin, issued by a Swiss company and backed 1:1 by euro deposits at Swissquote Bank. Its reserve history had one scare: FlowBank, a former reserve partner, went bankrupt in June 2024, and Anchored Coins restructured so that all circulating AEUR is backed at Swissquote, leaving the bankruptcy outside its coverage. The product ended over licensing rather than solvency. MiCAR requires an EU license to run a euro stablecoin business, so the issuer stopped new issuance and announced an orderly withdrawal from stablecoins rather than a relaunch. Binance listed AEUR in December 2023 and halted it hours later after a pump to about $3.25, then delisted it in the EEA in March 2025. Pharos froze AEUR on July 11, 2026. Binance ended AEUR support on July 31, delisting the AEUR/USDT pair, and from August 14 disabled withdrawals and converted remaining balances to euros at 1:1. Token ownership and upgrades sit with a 4-of-6 Safe that can also mint, burn, and pause. Direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} opens only for 250,000 AEUR or more, so smaller holders outside Binance depend on whatever secondary market remains.

buck-bucket-protocol.title: Sui's Legacy Dollar in Migration
buck-bucket-protocol.text: BUCK is Bucket Protocol's original Sui dollar, minted from {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} vaults against SUI, BTC, ETH, and LSTs, with a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} swapping USDC and USDT 1:1. It is now a legacy asset: Bucket's current stablecoin is USDB, the official migration converts BUCK to USDB 1:1 with no fee, and the V1 system is in exit-only wind-down with BUCK minting disabled. That conversion path is load-bearing for holders, because the V1 collateral still attributable to BUCK covers only a fraction of outstanding supply and most of it sits in stable-swap LP positions whose BUCK share cannot be separated from the record, so Pharos scores no usable reserve composition. The {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} swap into USDC and USDT is the exit route Pharos scores, and it keeps the exit pillar the strongest line on the {{grade}} card. The V1 oracle topology is opaque, with forty registered collateral branches fed almost entirely by threshold-one Supra or whitelisted-rule oracles, and the admin and upgrade caps sit with team wallets. The peg record is long and scarred, a long tail of episodes including one extreme crash, though recent history has been quiet. Holders therefore depend on Bucket keeping the fee-free USDB conversion open while those admin and upgrade powers remain in place.

vchf-vnx.title: Six Chains Attested, Avalanche Left Out
vchf-vnx.text: VCHF is a Swiss franc token issued by VNX Global Ltd., a Bermuda company holding a Class M digital asset business licence from the Bermuda Monetary Authority. Issuance moved there from Liechtenstein's VNX Commodities AG, whose vnx.li platform suspended exchange operations on 30 June 2026. The reserve evidence is now monthly. Apex Fund Services' August 2026 {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, a reasonable-assurance engagement under ISAE 3000, found CHF 2,035,962 of cash in a designated Bermuda Commercial Bank account against 2,035,935 VCHF outstanding on Ethereum, Solana, Base, Celo, Stellar and the Internet Computer at the August testing times. Two limits remain. The whole reserve sits with one bank, and the liability table omits legacy deployments that still carry supply, chiefly about 547,000 VCHF on Avalanche, most of it in a single unidentified wallet. Direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through verified institutional accounts with a CHF 100,000 minimum and about one business day to settle, so smaller holders depend on secondary-market liquidity. That record supports a {{grade}} overall grade. The durable constraint is scope: the attestation covers the six-chain float, while Pharos supply data also counts the uncovered deployments.

audd-novatti.title: AUD Cash, Reconciled Monthly
audd-novatti.text: AUDD is AUDC Pty Ltd's Australian dollar stablecoin, issued under an ASIC AFSL and backed by AUD cash held on bare trust for holders. The monthly William Buck procedures are the evidence Pharos leans on: the September 2026 report places most of the reserve with Westpac under the AMAL bare trust and the rest at Banking Circle, all in cash, and agrees it without exception against supply across nine networks, with a small excess over tokens outstanding. That gives backing the strongest line on the {{grade}} card. Exit is now the weakest pillar: redemption runs 1:1 through distributors, with a direct issuer fallback that requires KYC and carries a minimum. Economic control sits between the two, because the mint is economically unbounded and reconciled only after the fact. Pharos has observed the peg since March 2024 and recorded dozens of deviation episodes, the deepest nearly 30% below par and the latest in July 2026. William Buck's engagement is agreed-upon procedures: it expressly gives no assurance opinion and carries no independence requirement. AUDD's durable constraint is that its reserve is checked monthly by procedure rather than opinion, and its exit runs through intermediaries.

cgusd-cygnus-finance.title: Base's Treasury Wrapper
cgusd-cygnus-finance.text: cgUSD is Cygnus Finance's daily-rebasing T-bill dollar on Base, and the gap between off-chain NAV and on-chain price has produced a long tail of depeg events. The reserve model is described rather than shown: Cygnus states the portfolio holds short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} off-chain plus on-chain USDC and USDT, but publishes no weights, no custodian name, and no {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, so Pharos carries the whole reserve as one unsplit basket. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} in USDC runs through a request-and-claim queue that normally settles in five to seven days after the custodian sells bills, less a quoted 35-basis-point fee. That window is why the rebase cannot erase the arbitrage friction: the on-chain price can drift from NAV while exits wait. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by the economic-control pillar, the weakest of the three, because the vault and its NAV oracle sit behind a 10-second timelock controlled by a 2-of-11 Safe and the daily NAV that drives supply is issuer-asserted. Institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} with no published proof path leaves the trust assumptions sitting mostly with the Cygnus team. The reserve is an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} basket; the exit experience is still very much a DeFi product.

fxusd-f-x-protocol.title: Leverage as a Peg Mechanism
fxusd-f-x-protocol.text: fxUSD is f(x) Protocol's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-minted dollar, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} by WBTC and wstETH, with a Stability Pool arbitraging the USDC/fxUSD Curve pool to defend the peg. The protocol turns leveraged long positions into peg defense: xPOSITION NFTs represent looped exposure to a majority-WBTC collateral mix, while fxUSD holders take the stable side of the trade. Below peg, fxUSD can be {{term:redemption}}redeemed{{/term}} at the oracle price for underlying collateral, and the peg record shows dozens of brief deviations that each recovered. The {{grade}} overall grade comes from a split card. Backing and exit both score well, even with WBTC's custodial dependency sitting inside a nominally decentralized machine. Economic control is the weakest pillar by a wide margin: a three-day timelock rooted in a 6-of-9 Safe administers the PoolManager and can register a new mint-critical pool and raise its debt capacity without an independent collateral check, so Pharos treats native issuance as unbounded. The durable constraint sits in governance rather than in the collateral machinery: the supply ceiling depends on who can add pools, not on code that enforces backing.

usdb-blast.title: Yield Dollar Stranded on Blast
usdb-blast.text: USDB is Blast's native rebasing dollar: bridged deposits become DAI held through Blast's yield manager in MakerDAO's DSR, and withdrawals return to Ethereum as DAI. The reserve asset is ordinary stablecoin collateral, and the {{grade}} overall grade comes from the wrapper built around it. The deployment is Blast-only and Pharos recognizes no DEX pool that can absorb a same-notional sale, leaving the {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} withdrawal as the route out. Backing scores clearly higher than exit but still sits low: Blast's manager contracts identify the DSR position, but nothing published reconciles it to the full rebasing liability, pending withdrawals, or a funded recovery order. The depeg history is an unusually long tail of recorded episodes, extending into October 2026. The live token contract carries no blacklist or pause function, though a 3-of-5 Safe owns the proxy admin that can replace the implementation. Governance sets the yield, and the durable constraint is the bridge: a USDB holder's only protocol exit is back to Ethereum as DAI.

buidl-blackrock.title: BlackRock's Tokenized Treasury Fund
buidl-blackrock.text: BUIDL is BlackRock's tokenized institutional {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}}, a Reg D share priced at a $1 NAV and backed by U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills and overnight tri-party repo, custodied by BNY Mellon and administered by Securitize. Chronicle's Proof of Asset feed reports the NAV daily, and Pharos's last retained holdings snapshot, from August 2026, showed five repo positions and thirteen T-bills; Chronicle describes its role as technical verification rather than an audit. That evidence keeps backing the strongest of the three pillars on the {{grade}} card. Exit is the weakest: BUIDL is confined to eligible holders, so leaving means a transfer agent, not a market. Control is where the infrastructure shows. Issuance is uncapped on every reviewed deployment: seven EVM token and trust-service pairs share one immediate EOA master and upgrader, and the Solana issuance programs share a separate immediate EOA upgrade key that also sits behind other tokenized liabilities Pharos tracks, which triggers a dependency cap on the card. Yield is NAV income passed through as a rebase. Eight chain deployments widen the footprint, with Wormhole carrying issuer-controlled burn-and-reissue transfers rather than wrapped supply. Holders therefore depend on the transfer agent for exit and on those immediate EOA keys for issuance integrity.

btcusd-btcfi.title: A Bifrost CDP Dollar With a Yen Sleeve
btcusd-btcfi.text: BtcUSD is BTCfi's {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} dollar, minted on Bifrost from a multi-handler {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} at a 50% borrow limit, with Base and BSC representations. Most collateral is Bitcoin in several wrappers, led by native BTC and BTCB with small cbBTC and WBTC handlers, each bringing its own {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} assumption. The fifth handler is not Bitcoin: Pharos resolved it to Unified JPYC, a Bifrost representation of a yen stablecoin, at about a seventh of the recorded composition, so a BTC-branded dollar also carries yen and bridge exposure. Holders have no {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route of their own, because the CDP close path serves borrowers repaying their own loans, so exit runs through secondary liquidity, the strongest pillar on the card. Economic control is the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card: the CDP handler's owner can replace its logic target immediately with no timelock, the token owner can authorize additional minters, and no bad-debt process beyond an owner circuit breaker was identified. A long tail of recorded depeg episodes adds a peg penalty on top. The CDP's collateral and liquidation rules hold only as long as the handler owner leaves that logic target in place.

usbd-bima.title: WBTC-Backed CDP With an Owner Mint Key
usbd-bima.text: USBD is a Liquity-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin minted from overcollateralized vaults of Bitcoin wrappers, with permissionless {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} against the lowest-ratio vaults and a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} for near-1:1 stablecoin swaps. At the last fixed capture the entire collateral book sat in the WBTC wrapper branch, so the live {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} assumption is WBTC's custodians, while the liquid-staking and restaking collateral in the marketing held no balance. Backing is nevertheless the strongest of the three pillars, priced through Chainlink BTC/USD under a 150% minimum ratio. What drags the {{grade}} overall grade down is economic control, the weakest pillar on the card: the BimaCore owner is a single EOA that can mint USBD directly without limit, install new mint adapters, and raise debt ceilings. The DebtToken's burn function accepts any account when called by a registered TroveManager or adapter, so an owner-installed adapter could reach holder balances. Exit sits in the middle, with a structurally sound redemption backstop but no comparable same-notional route beside it. Most supply sits on Hemi as a LayerZero representation of the Ethereum issuance. Pharos has no usable market price for USBD, so the peg reads at protocol par and the card treats it as missing evidence rather than a clean record. The durable constraint is the owner key: the vault minter is bounded by collateral checks and debt ceilings, while a single EOA can mint without either.

doc-money-on-chain.title: Rootstock CDP With an rBTC Exit
doc-money-on-chain.text: DOC is Money On Chain's dollar on Rootstock, minted against rBTC held in the protocol's own contracts rather than bank deposits or a fiat {{term:custody}}custodian{{/term}}. Mechanically it is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} system with {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}: DOC holds the senior claim on pooled rBTC, while BPRO holders absorb the residual Bitcoin exposure. Holders exit through permissionless {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} for rBTC, which keeps the exit pillar the strongest of the three. That conversion runs on the OMoC BTC/USD oracle, and an April 2026 consensus-bypass flaw in that feed prompted a protocol panic pause before the protocol reported a fix. The {{grade}} overall grade is held back most by economic control: an accepted Money On Chain governance proposal can change collateral parameters or upgrade mint-critical logic. The Arbitrum and Ethereum deployments are external lock-and-mint representations rather than additional collateral. The durable constraint is that every DOC rests on one Bitcoin sidechain, one price feed and one governance system.

usdrif-rif.title: The RIF-Collateralized Dollar
usdrif-rif.text: USDRIF is a Rootstock {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin minted against RIF token collateral. Where Rootstock's DOC is backed by rBTC, USDRIF relies on RIF, so the reserve stays onchain and transparent but is much weaker in quality. A DOC bucket sits alongside it, but RIF makes up almost the entire reserve. The protocol supports minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} positions exposed to {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} risk. Exit leads the card on a measured Uniswap pool on Arbitrum that clears only about a tenth of a stress-size sale, with slow issuer redemption as the alternative; the volatile single-asset reserve keeps backing behind it.  The two collateral buckets are today's only minters, but MOC governance can authorize changers that grant the mint role to any address with no collateral or cap check, and no unavoidable delay applies. That unbounded mint path is the binding cap holding the overall grade at {{grade}}. The structure remains dependent on a single volatile collateral asset.

isc-international-stable-currency.title: The Anti-Dollar Experiment
isc-international-stable-currency.text: ISC deliberately rejects the dollar peg and tries to stabilize purchasing power through a basket of gold, investment-grade bonds, short-term T-bills, global equities, and cash, so its nominal price is designed to drift upward over time. Pharos treats it as a NAV-style {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} token rather than a par dollar. What the issuer dashboard shows is less reassuring than the philosophy. As fetched in August 2026, close to half of the combined reserve holdings were ISC tokens held by the reserve itself, which Pharos treats as circular self-reserve rather than external backing, with the remainder spread across iShares and Vanguard ETFs and USD cash at undisclosed custodians. The dashboard is undated, mutable, and unaudited, and the issuer says an audit scheme is still under consideration. Backing and exit are the two weak pillars on the {{grade}} report card, the first on that reserve evidence and the second on the absence of a comparable same-notional route, while economic control fares better because the Solana mint sits behind an immutable 2-of-3 SPL multisig with no upgradeable program in the path. The catch remains a retained freeze authority, Solana-only issuance, institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and no published holder loss waterfall or recovery process. The durable constraint is that a purchasing-power target is only as good as the reserve that is supposed to buy it.

usd0-usual.title: RWA Dollar With Circular Collateral
usd0-usual.text: USD0 is Usual's {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-backed dollar, minted 1:1 against approved collateral tokens directly or against USDC through a gateway. The approved list includes Hashnote USYC, M0's M and Spiko USTBL, with M and USDC held through Usual's own wrapper contracts. In July 2026 the whole book resolved to USYC, a tokenised share of a {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}}-bill and reverse-repo fund custodied at BNY Mellon through Marex. Pharos no longer treats that capture as current. An October 2026 census of the collateral treasury found positive balances in USYC, the M and USDC wrappers, USTBL and two lending-vault positions that are themselves claims on USD0, lent against bUSD0. Those circular claims cannot count as independent Treasury backing, and no current netted composition exists, so backing is scored as unclassified exposure and is the weakest of the three pillars. Economic control sits mid-card, with 8-of-15 Safes over role grants and the upgrade path and an unbounded DaoCollateral mint role. Exit is the genuine strength: permissionless {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through DaoCollateral returns underlying collateral for a small fee, and it leads the card even though secondary markets have wobbled through a long tail of recorded episodes. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects that split. The durable constraint is that part of what backs USD0 is USD0 itself, lent out against its own staked wrapper.

usr-resolv.title: Frozen at Sixteen Cents
usr-resolv.text: Resolv's USR was a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar: long ETH and BTC held on-chain via Fireblocks, hedged with short perpetual futures on centralized exchanges, with an RLP insurance layer meant to absorb negative {{term:funding-rate}}funding{{/term}} and liquidation losses. Apostro attested the reserves in real time. None of that guarded the mint. USR's off-chain SERVICE_ROLE backend could mint directly with no on-chain oracle, ratio, per-transaction, or supply check. On March 22, 2026, an attacker who had compromised that signer deposited about $100K of USDC and minted 80M unbacked USR, extracting roughly $25M in ETH. USR crashed within minutes, and RLP absorbed the bad debt until it was wiped out. Resolv burned 46M of the unbacked tokens through a blacklist freeze, but by April USR traded at $0.16 with about $95M of collateral against $173M of liabilities. Pharos froze it on April 27, 2026.

usdz-anzen.title: Private-Credit Backing, Fragile Peg Record
usdz-anzen.text: Anzen's USDz is backed 1:1 by SPCT, a permissioned token representing Anzen's portfolio of U.S. private-credit asset-backed securities. Pharos's July 2026 on-chain read found SPCT supply covering USDz supply at roughly 101%, with no {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} or cash sleeve, and Anzen publishes no loan-level weights. The reserve evidence is the issuer's own real-time dashboard; Pharos has no independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} on file.
