Anzen names Percent as its underwriting and custody partner but discloses no trustee, segregation terms or custody allocation for the notes. Its collateral documentation also gives USDz holders no claim on the collateral assets. Minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} against SPCT are reserved for institutions, so other holders rely on secondary-market arbitrage to hold the peg. That arbitrage has been unreliable: Pharos records hundreds of depeg events, the deepest near 16% below a dollar, and a weak peg score. Pharos has not established a same-value route open to ordinary holders. The durable constraint is a token traded as a dollar over permissioned credit that liquidates on loan timelines longer than a week, and to which holders have no stated claim.

ausd-agora.title: Agora's Repo-Heavy Dollar
ausd-agora.text: AUSD is Agora's dollar stablecoin, issued under a Bermuda DABA license and redeemable 1:1 by verified Agora customers. Most of the reserve sits in the Agora Reserve Fund, a Delaware limited partnership held through Agora Bermuda's segregated account; VanEck manages it and Agora names State Street as a reserve partner. Grant Thornton's monthly {{term:attestation}}examinations{{/term}} cover both reserves and outstanding tokens, and the August 2026 report puts overnight Treasury repurchase agreements ahead of short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}}, with company cash and a small USDC and PYUSD slice making up the rest. That evidence gives backing and exit strong lines on the {{grade}} card. Economic control is the weakest pillar: Agora externally owned accounts hold role administration, rate-limit management and proxy-upgrade authority on the EVM deployments, with no multisig found on those paths. Supply has also concentrated on Monad, which carries more than half of it. The peg record is long and quiet, with its recorded episodes clustered in the first year. AUSD's durable constraint is key management: the reserves are examined monthly, while the contracts answer to single keys.

usds-sky.title: PSM Exit on a Shared Balance Sheet
usds-sky.text: USDS is Sky's successor to DAI, minted 1:1 from DAI or against the same Maker balance sheet. Its defining feature is the exit: a permissionless {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} swaps USDS for USDC atomically and without a fee, and Pharos measures a full stress-size request clearing through it at par. That route puts exit at the top of the scale on the {{grade}} card. The reserve behind it is a mixed book rather than a cash pile. Roughly two-fifths sits as USDC in the PSM, with Sky's allocations to Spark lending and Grove {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} credit making up most of the rest, alongside smaller crypto-vault, staking and legacy RWA positions. Economic control is the weakest pillar. Discretionary expansion needs public token governance through a 48-hour delay, but formula interest and activity compensation can execute immediately, and the system has no hard supply ceiling. The peg has stayed at the calm end of the stress scale, with a long tail of brief deviations and none since January 2025. The structural tension remains the PSM itself: the route that makes USDS easy to leave depends on USDC, a centralized stablecoin that a DAO-governed system cannot control.

m-m0.title: The Middleware Dollar
m-m0.text: M0's M is an institutional dollar stablecoin minted 1:1 by permissioned Minters against eligible collateral, principally short-term U.S. {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and cash held in bankruptcy-remote structures, with on-chain Validator attestations replacing periodic audits. The peg record is the strongest line on the page. Exit is now the weakest pillar on the card: the only compiled route is eligibility-gated issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} with eventual settlement and undisclosed fees, so ordinary holders depend on the institutions between them and the Minters. Backing is held back by disclosure rather than asset quality: M0's current Protocol API publishes the aggregate collateral total but no longer exposes the cash-versus-Treasury split or minter-level provider shares. The reviewed structure also routes more than 90% of collateral through one Superstate and UMB Bank chain, which Pharos classifies as institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. Governance can appoint minters and validators and set the attestation threshold to zero, so Pharos scores issuance as economically unbounded despite the attestation design. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects that mix. M's significance is downstream: it anchors the M0 infrastructure cohort of branded and wrapped dollars built on the same rail.

usdm-moneta.title: Cardano's Two-Issuer Dollar
usdm-moneta.text: USDM is a Cardano dollar issued in parallel by two companies: Moneta Digital in the United States and Norwegian Block Exchange (NBX) in the EEA. Each keeps a separate reserve book, and neither backs the other's tokens, so a holder's claim depends on which issuer minted the unit presented for {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. The reserve assets are conventional, bank deposits and {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}} from Fidelity, Western Asset Management and Amundi, and a reserve-verification oracle gates each mint on Cardano. What is missing is a current composition across both books, so backing is held down by disclosure rather than asset quality.  Pharos measures no same-size route, and Moneta's own redemption rail serves KYB-approved institutions with a default $10,000 daily limit. With no market route, arbitrage has little to enforce the peg. USDM has logged well over a thousand deviation events, the widest more than 30% from par, and its peg record grades far down the scale, although the most recent episode ended in March 2026. For holders outside Moneta's institutional rail, Pharos measures no route that connects the reserve to the peg.

satusd-river.title: Omni-CDP Dollar With Vault-Minted Supply
satusd-river.text: River's satUSD began as an Omni-{{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin: users lock BTC, ETH, BNB, or liquid staking tokens on one chain and mint satUSD on another through LayerZero {{term:bridge}}bridging{{/term}}, across eleven native deployments. The trove book is no longer the whole story. River's late-September dashboard figures put most observed deposits in Prime Vault custodial BTC wrappers and a further slice in Smart Vault USDT strategy deposits, both of which support internally minted satUSD that never reaches user wallets. River publishes no current liability-weighted reconciliation of those vaults, so Pharos scores the backing pillar on limited evidence. Exit is the strongest pillar: {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} against the least-collateralized troves is permissionless, though on the reviewed Base branch proceeds arrive as WBTC rather than cash. The weakest pillar is economic control. A single River owner EOA holds upgrade and ward powers across the native deployments, including a path to burn from any holder, and collateral pricing runs through single-source oracle paths with no automatic failover. Hundreds of logged peg deviation events also trim the {{grade}} overall grade. The durable constraint is that overcollateralized troves no longer describe most of what stands behind the token.

usdf-astherus.title: One Exchange, One Exit
usdf-astherus.text: Aster's USDF, issued under the Astherus name before the rebrand, is a Binance-routed {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} stablecoin: USDT deposited at mint sits in Ceffu {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, is mirrored to a Binance sub-account through MirrorX, and is deployed into long-spot-plus-short-{{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} positions on that one exchange. Collateral, hedge, and the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop all run through a single pipeline. The peg is the easy part, with only a handful of brief, modest deviations over the tracking window. The {{grade}} overall grade says the danger is structural. The token's admin timelock can grant minting rights to a new caller that bypasses both the USDT deposit path and the supply cap, and Aster publishes no price-feed topology for the valuation and rebalancing that keep the reserve {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}}. Backing is weak because Aster names its custodian and venue but publishes no itemized balances or independent custody reconciliation, and no attestation gives current weights for retained USDT, spot crypto, or futures margin. Exit is the least weak pillar, yet a BSC-only token with a dormant bridge rail and a global transfer pause leaves holders dependent on issuer redemption, which takes one to two days for standard amounts and up to seven for large ones. Everything that matters about USDF happens off-chain, on one exchange.

usda-avalon.title: BTC Label, Undisclosed Collateral Split
usda-avalon.text: Avalon USDa is marketed as a BTC-backed {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar, but the mechanism mixes two very different books. Users can borrow USDa against FBTC, priced by RedStone and liquidated on centralized exchanges, or mint it 1:1 against USDT and USDC deposits that carry no liquidation at all, with USDT conversion claimable in one business day. Avalon publishes no dated split between those books, so Pharos scores the reserve as one undisclosed CeDeFi envelope rather than as Bitcoin. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} runs through Cobo, Fireblocks and Coinbase Prime, without published addresses, provider shares or segregation terms. A single 5-of-6 Safe can add minters and upgrade both minter proxies, and many of the LayerZero routes across its chains have unresolved bridge controls. Exit is close behind, with no comparable same-notional route beyond the issuer's conversion vault. A depeg that opened in late December 2025, at worst about 31% below par, remains open in Pharos's record, and recent market coverage is too thin to confirm recovery. The {{grade}} overall grade follows from that. The durable constraint is disclosure: until Avalon publishes how much of USDa rests on FBTC debt versus stablecoin deposits, the Bitcoin label describes the marketing rather than a measured reserve.

usdtb-ethena.title: Ethena's One-Fund Treasury Dollar
usdtb-ethena.text: USDtb is Ethena's Treasury-backed dollar, issued by Anchorage Digital Bank under its federal trust charter and positioned as a calmer counterpart to USDe. Its reserve is almost entirely BlackRock's BUIDL, self-custodied in segregated wallets, with a small cash float in segregated fiduciary accounts at unnamed banks, much of it above the FDIC insurance limit. Deloitte examines that reserve monthly against the full outstanding token liability. The trade-off is concentration: one fund carries nearly the whole book, and the holder's claim reaches the bills only through BUIDL's own fund structure. That is why backing edges below exit as the weakest of the three pillars on the {{grade}} card, with economic control the strongest, though all three sit within a few points of one another. Mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at par are customer-gated, while on-chain depth on Ethereum gives other holders a usable exit. Pharos's dependency map also shows USDtb sitting beneath other stablecoins, most heavily Jupiter's jupUSD, so a failure at any link in its chain would travel beyond its own float.

zeusd-zoth.title: Zoth's Deprecated V1 Dollar
zeusd-zoth.text: ZeUSD is the token of Zoth's deprecated V1 stack, an RWA escrow receipt whose router is paused on-chain and whose current backing is unevidenced. Pharos classes it as a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} as the closest fit, but the tracked V1 router records collateral value and debt at mint and returns exactly what was recorded on burn, with no position-health checks and no liquidation path. Two March 2025 exploits hit the stack: a collateral-accounting flaw that minted ZeUSD without sufficient backing, then an admin-key compromise that let the attacker upgrade a vault contract and drain roughly $8.4M. Zoth still lists eligible {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral categories but publishes no current allocation, attestation, or proof of reserves, so the reserve is carried as a fully unresolved envelope and the backing pillar is scored on limited evidence. The exit pillar sits at the floor because no viable exit path is established. Economic control stays low because minting is unbounded and every admin and upgrade key resolves to a single Zoth EOA. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects all three. Pharos's June 2026 notice recorded market pricing far below par on thin public liquidity, and the near-par peg line on the card rests on a single price source. The durable constraint is that the V1 contract still reports about 27.6 million tokens outstanding against a paused router and an unevidenced reserve.

zchf-frankencoin.title: The Oracle-Free Franc
zchf-frankencoin.text: Frankencoin mints ZCHF, a Swiss-franc stablecoin, from overcollateralized positions valued through auction-based {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} challenges rather than price oracles, trading capital efficiency for resistance to oracle manipulation. Governance can whitelist any collateral subject to a public minority-veto window, and {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} is enforced through veto-governed minting limits. Pharos's live read of the positions puts wrapped Bitcoin at over two-fifths of the backing, with liquid-staked ETH next. Tokenized equities make up the tail, led by BOSS (Boss Info AG) alongside quitt.shares, Ondo's tokenized S&P 500 ETF, and smaller RealUnit and Switzerlend lines. That tail and an unresolved mechanism review keep backing below exit, which sits near the top of a card graded {{grade}} overall. Economic control is the weakest pillar, because minting is economically unbounded and five bridged deployments add external-network controls. The peg has held near par, with none of its few recorded deviations in the last 90 days. A February 2026 LEXR memo for the Frankencoin Association finds no identifiable issuer and no contractual rights attached to ZCHF, placing it outside MiCA's issuer regimes, though the memo warns EU supervisors could disagree. The durable constraint is that holders rely on auction discipline over whatever collateral governance fails to veto.

usn-noon.title: Noon's Private-Credit Dollar
usn-noon.text: Noon's USN is a dollar token issued over an institutional credit book. Accountable's October 27, 2026 snapshot puts 64.4% in Fasanara's FTAC private-credit fund, 22.8% in Hyperliquid HYPE funding-rate arbitrage and 0.01% in tokenized Treasury bills through Dinari's permissioned USD+, with the rest in JAAA CLOs, undeployed stablecoins and Morpho and Euler lending. Yield accrues to sUSN; base USN is the settlement token. Fasanara both deploys and custodies the majority position, no trust or special-purpose vehicle is named behind the reserve, and the undeployed bucket is still larger than the USDC and USDT in Noon's two published collateral wallets. That credit book caps the {{grade}} card. Minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are issuer-processed for KYC-verified users. The liquidity page advertises same-day redemption up to 20% of TVL, but the terms set a five-business-day period, allow discretionary delays and gates, and make a submitted claim unsecured debt of the issuer. Noon's documentation says its private-credit positions typically take more than three months to unwind, and that unpublished agreements with unnamed counterparties let it exit within five days. A five-day promise over mostly three-month credit therefore rests on agreements holders cannot read.

honey-berachain.title: Berachain's Basket Dollar, Mostly USDe
honey-berachain.text: Bera USD (BUSD), formerly HONEY, is Berachain's native dollar, minted and redeemed 1:1 through the HoneyFactory against a governance-approved basket of USDC.e, USDT0, BYUSD, and USDe held in dedicated collateral vaults. Settlement is atomic and Basket Mode works like a multi-asset {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}, but {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} still depends on what the vaults hold: in May 2025 redemptions halted for about 50 hours after the USDC.e leg ran dry. What the listing pages miss is the actual mix. Pharos's July 2026 reserve capture found the registered vaults holding USDe almost exclusively, and the official app showed the same split on October 1, so Pharos scores the backing as a single Ethena dependency rather than a diversified basket. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects that trade-off. A 3-of-5 Berachain Safe can upgrade both the token and the factory immediately, can blacklist or pause holders, and leaves minting economically unbounded, which caps the score. The peg record shows a long tail of episodes running into May 2026, including one large upward spike, with none in the last 90 days. The mechanism works, but its backing now rests on USDe and its rules rest on one Safe.

wusd-worldwide.title: WSPN's Dollar After the Delisting Cascade
wusd-worldwide.text: WSPN's Worldwide USD lost its reviewed centralized venues in summer 2026. MEXC delisted it on 25 July, Bitget dropped the WUSD/USDT pair on 31 July, and Coins.ph, the flagship retail venue, ended conversions on 4 August, saying WUSD was "no longer able to adhere to our listing standards" while leaving withdrawals open. Supply contracted in the same window: circulating WUSD fell from 9.99M on 21 July to about 0.61M by 1 August, roughly 94%, with burns on 29 July and 1 August doing most of the work and no issuer statement alongside. Pharos's October scan of exact-contract pools on Ethereum, Polygon and Viction found none above its liquidity admission floor, and CoinGecko returned no tickers, so Pharos publishes no current price. WSPN still advertises 1:1 conversion for qualified, verified businesses, but its documented redemption portal failed to resolve on 19 October, leaving that {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route unverified. On Viction, historical on-chain evidence showed a flat 100 WUSD fee on token calls, approve() included. Reserves are described only as policy ranges of cash and Treasury bills, with no dated reserve-liability report. One WSPN admin address governs roles on every chain, and the token has no supply cap. A holder without a WSPN business relationship has no verified way out.

frxusd-frax.title: A Custodian Dollar Concentrated in WTGXX
frxusd-frax.text: frxUSD is Frax's tokenized-{{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}}-backed dollar, minted and redeemed 1:1 through governance-approved custodian contracts, and it launched in January 2025 as the {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} upgrade path for legacy FRAX. The custodian roster is wider than the reported reserve: Frax governance voted in Superstate's USCC crypto carry fund in December 2024 and Centrifuge's JTRSY Treasury fund in February 2025, yet the current reserve breakdown lists neither fund. The live balance sheet is concentrated: WisdomTree's WTGXX government money-market fund carries the majority of reserves, Superstate USTB and BlackRock BUIDL sit behind it, and an Erebor Bank reserve account plus small USDC, AUSD and USDB balances round it out. Backing and economic control are the card's two stronger pillars; a 4-of-7 Safe owns the token and custodians, and Ethereum upgrades pass through a 24-hour timelock. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by exit, the weakest pillar: redemption works whenever the relevant custodian holds collateral, but Pharos has not established the all-in cost of that route. The durable constraint is reliance on a small set of tokenized-fund issuers, with WTGXX alone holding most of the reserve, plus Frax DAO's power to approve and revoke the custodians that hold the money.

usyc-hashnote.title: Circle's Tokenized T-Bill Fund Share
usyc-hashnote.text: USYC is a share in Hashnote's short-duration yield fund, which Circle acquired in January 2025 and now distributes as Circle USYC. The fund holds short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and reverse repos, and the token accrues at NAV rather than holding a fixed dollar. Circle publishes no durable split between bills and repo, or the repo counterparties, so Pharos carries the reserve as one aggregate row priced by a Chainlink NAV feed. Access is eligibility-gated: subscriptions and {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} run in USDC through issuer-operated Teller contracts, settling in one block up to the instant-redemption capacity and T+0 or T+1 above it. Most measured supply sits on BSC as a Teller-minted representation of the Ethereum fund share, so issuer-controlled bridge minting carries much of the token's footprint. Exit is the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card, because Pharos maps no route beyond the issuer that absorbs size at NAV, so on either chain USYC's liquidity is Circle's redemption capacity.

eurr-stablr.title: A MiCA Euro Frozen by a Mint-Key Breach
eurr-stablr.text: EURR was StablR's MiCA-authorised euro e-money token, issued by a Malta EMI under MFSA supervision with Grant Thornton {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} and a Bitfinex listing, until a May 24, 2026 cybersecurity incident halted it. An attacker compromised StablR's mint and governance key and printed unbacked EURR alongside its dollar sibling USDR. On May 29 StablR's board activated its MiCA Recovery Plan and notified the MFSA; minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} were suspended, and exchanges were asked to halt EURR trading, deposits and withdrawals. The hole has grown since the first disclosure. StablR initially cited 4.5 million unbacked EURR, and its August 25 notice put unauthorised EURR in circulation at about 6.41 million, close to half of the supply Pharos still tracks on Ethereum. StablR says the assets safeguarded before the incident were unaffected, but with redemption suspended, holders cannot reach them. Pharos no longer scores EURR; it sits in the archive as a frozen incident asset, because a report card presumes a working redemption promise. The Ethereum mint path was owner-controlled with no economic cap, so neither MiCA authorisation nor the attestations limited what one compromised key could issue.

usdr-stablr.title: MiCA EMT Broken by a Mint Key
usdr-stablr.text: StablR's USDR was a dollar e-money token from a Malta EMI authorized under MiCA, backed by cash and short-term government bonds at European institutions and reported on quarterly by Grant Thornton. On May 24, 2026 an attacker used a compromised StablR mint key to create unbacked USDR in a coordinated attack that also hit the euro token EURR. StablR suspended minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, stated that both tokens were no longer backed at the 1:1 ratio MiCAR requires, and on May 29 announced that its Board had activated a Recovery Plan. USDR fell to about $0.64, then traded back near par within two days after StablR froze issuance and asked exchanges to halt trading. Pharos froze USDR on the day of the incident. StablR's August 25 notice puts the unauthorised USDR still in circulation at about 14.33M, with no reserve behind it, while tokens issued against payment remain fully backed in segregated accounts. Its October 19 notice reported minting and redemption still suspended, so holders have had no issuer exit since May.

usdo-openeden.title: Rebasing Dollar Over OpenEden's Own TBILL
usdo-openeden.text: OpenEden's USDO is a rebasing dollar that passes tokenized {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} yield to holders by growing balances daily. OpenEden Digital, listed on the Bermuda Monetary Authority's register as a Class F digital-asset business, mints and redeems it 1:1 against USDC. Most of the reserve is OpenEden's own TBILL token, with BlackRock BUIDL, VanEck VBILL and an RLUSD and USDC buffer behind it, so the trust chain runs through a second OpenEden product. Reserve evidence is issuer accounting with no accounting-firm {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and the reported ratio reconciles only part of the liability side. The Chainlink proof-of-reserve feed lists Treasury bills as its reserve asset, and an October 2026 read sat below USDO supply, close to the fund holdings alone. Economic control is the weakest pillar: one issuer key holds the admin, minter and upgrade roles on the Ethereum, Base and BNB Chain tokens and owns the cross-chain CCIP pools. Backing and exit score only slightly higher, leaving the {{grade}} overall grade without a strong pillar. The peg has held through the last quarter; its record carries dozens of deviation events, the latest in March 2026. The durable constraint is concentration in OpenEden, which issues the main reserve asset and holds the minting keys.

usda-anzens.title: Cardano Dollar, One Dated Examination
usda-anzens.text: Anzens USDA is a Cardano-only dollar from a U.S. company that partners describe as a FinCEN-registered money services business. Its terms define the reserve as cash, cash equivalents, {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills and Treasury money-market funds, but publish no current weights. The only examination Pharos could open, signed by The Network Firm for January 31 2026, found reserves slightly above tokens outstanding, almost all in Superstate's short-duration government fund held directly by Anzens, plus a small cash balance at BitGo. Anzens claims monthly reporting, yet no later report has been established, so backing rests on a description plus one dated snapshot. Mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through KYC-verified bank transfers for users in eligible U.S. states, with no comparable same-notional route beside the issuer. Economic control scores best, because the immutable Cardano mint policy executes only on mint and burn and cannot freeze ordinary transfers. The peg record is poor, with hundreds of recorded episodes on a single-source price feed, the most recent in March 2026, and it weighs on the {{grade}} overall grade. The durable constraint is publication: until the monthly reports Anzens promises appear, the reserve is examined history rather than current evidence.

usdf-falcon.title: Falcon's BTC-Heavy Synthetic Dollar
usdf-falcon.text: Falcon Finance's USDf is a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar whose reserve, at the August 2026 reviewed snapshot, was overwhelmingly BTC, with USDC, USDT, an insurance fund, ETH, and an aggregated long tail of altcoins and tokenized assets making up the small remainder. The altcoin-collateral pitch that set Falcon apart from Ethena survives as mintable collateral; it is barely visible in the reserve itself. Pharos does not currently rate USDf: critical evidence is insufficient, because the scored input carries no current reserve composition and Falcon publishes no reconciled hedge notionals or net delta. Economic control is the weakest pillar beneath that verdict. Falcon's terms make an internally calculated spot price, set at its sole discretion, the authority for minting, {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, and settlement, with no independent feed, heartbeat, or fallback published. The Ethereum proxy can be upgraded through a zero-delay admin owned by a 4-of-6 Safe, and the native minter accepts signed requests with no on-chain collateral check or supply cap. Most assets sat in Falcon-controlled multisig wallets at the last custody review, and HT Digital's quarterly assurance has fallen behind its weekly collateral letters. The peg mostly behaves, though its long tail of brief episodes includes a sharp July 2025 drop. USDf is only as sound as the price Falcon chooses to publish.

europ-schuman.title: Credentials Without Scale
europ-schuman.text: EUROP is Schuman Financial's euro stablecoin, issued by SALVUS SAS under a French MiCA e-money authorization supervised by the ACPR and backed by euro cash and cash equivalents at Société Générale and Banking Circle, with quarterly KPMG reserve {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} and direct 1:1 redemption through the issuer. Those regulatory and reserve credentials are in place, but the float remains small. KPMG's June 2026 report, which describes itself as neither an audit nor a review, puts about a third of the reserve in bank cash and two thirds in cash equivalents whose instruments it does not name, with reserves a few percent above tokens in circulation. That undisclosed two thirds, together with an assurance record Pharos now scores as stale, leaves backing as the weakest pillar, a fraction below exit, with economic control the strongest, for a {{grade}} overall grade. The peg holds near the top of the scale, with dozens of brief blips that read as thin-market noise rather than structural instability. Distribution spans XRPL, Plasma and Solana alongside the usual EVM chains, all issuer-native, but on-chain depth covers only part of a stress-size sale, leaving issuer redemption as the full exit.

brz-transfero.title: A 2019 Real With a 2024 Reserve Report
brz-transfero.text: BRZ is Transfero's centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, launched on Ethereum in 2019 and now deployed on 14 chains, minted and redeemed 1:1 for BRL through Transfero's KYC-gated teller process with a historically reviewed 1% {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fee. The reserve evidence has not kept pace with that footprint. The only report Transfero links is dated March 31, 2024, is self-published, covers assets only, and places the BRL cash at an unnamed authorized institution, so Pharos holds no current composition and the backing pillar sits near the floor. Exit is no better, since no reviewed DEX route matches the supply and the issuer window remains the practical way out. Two Safes hold the owner and master-minter roles, and the master minter can authorize minters with arbitrary replenishable allowances. The peg record compounds all of this. Pharos has logged a long tail of depeg episodes, measured from a single price source against an FX-derived BRL reference, including deep swings far below peg, and the peg multiplier pulls the score down further. Until Transfero publishes a dated reserve report that reconciles to circulating supply, the score rests on the peg tape and the issuer's word.

rlusd-ripple.title: Ripple's Trust-Chartered Dollar
rlusd-ripple.text: Ripple's NYDFS-supervised dollar is backed by a reserve split across {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, government {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}}, and cash, examined monthly by Deloitte under a New York trust charter, with BNY as primary reserve custodian. Exit is the strongest pillar on the card, since issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is permissionless and 1:1. The {{grade}} overall grade tracks backing, the weakest pillar by a narrow margin, because the depository institutions, money-market funds, and custodians beyond BNY are not named and bankruptcy remoteness rests on contract rather than statute. Supply sits mostly on Ethereum and XRPL, with smaller native deployments on Base, Optimism, Ink and Unichain. Those EVM deployments also let a Wormhole manager burn and mint RLUSD under a single-transceiver configuration, adding external message-validation risk. On Ethereum, an issuer multisig can pause individual accounts and claw back balances. Pharos records RLUSD as an e-money token that is not MiCA-compliant. Its recorded depeg events date from its first year, with none since October 2025. The protections are a regulated reserve and issuer redemption; on-chain, the issuer keeps account-level control.

feusd-felix.title: Liquity Fork on Hyperliquid
feusd-felix.text: feUSD is a Liquity-v2-fork {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar on Hyperliquid, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} by HYPE ecosystem tokens: concentrated chain risk, sturdy redemption mechanics. Felix Protocol cloned Liquity V2 onto Hyperliquid's L1 and split collateral into four isolated branches: HYPE, its liquid-staking derivatives kHYPE and wstHYPE, and bridged Bitcoin. HYPE itself dominates the collateral, and Pharos rates each HYPE asset very-high risk. Backing still leads the card because every branch is enumerated and priced, and holders can {{term:redemption}}redeem{{/term}} feUSD for a dollar of collateral through an interest-rate-sorted queue. Exit and economic control sit far lower. Pharos has not established a comparable same-notional exit route, and a 3-of-6 Felix multisig with no detected guard holds upgrade authority over the token and can raise each branch's debt cap; the {{grade}} overall grade reflects control as the weakest pillar. The peg score remains strong despite a long tail of brief episodes. The structural caveat remains: when the primary collateral is the native token of the chain the stablecoin lives on, one ecosystem shock hits the collateral and its {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} market at the same time.

dusd-standx.title: Delta-Neutral Dollar, Undisclosed Book
dusd-standx.text: DUSD is StandX's {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar: USDT and USDC deposits buy spot crypto paired with matching short {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} positions, with a stability reserve meant to absorb negative funding. StandX documents the design but publishes no dated balance sheet, component weights, venue inventory or reserve-fund size, so Pharos carries the whole book as one undisclosed aggregate. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} runs through exchange partners and StandX multi-signature arrangements, and the issuer terms deny any trust relationship over the assets. Exit is an issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} into USDT or USDC after a seven-day lock and fees, and reserve losses reduce the quote pro rata. Economic control is the weakest pillar behind the {{grade}} overall grade: issuance on BSC and Solana runs through StandX's Settler controls, whose backend signer set is undisclosed. The peg record shows only a handful of brief episodes, but that record does not reveal the hedge book behind it. The durable constraint is that holders must trust a hedging desk whose positions they cannot see.

eurcv-societe-generale-forge.title: SG-FORGE's Single-Bank Euro
eurcv-societe-generale-forge.text: EURCV is SG-FORGE's MiCA euro stablecoin, issued by the digital-asset arm of Société Générale with reserves held entirely as euro cash at the parent bank, disclosed daily by the issuer. The {{grade}} overall grade is held back by concentration. Backing is the weakest pillar, if narrowly: the reserve is fully cash and reconciled daily against circulation, but the reserve, the {{term:custody}}custodian{{/term}} and the issuer are the same banking group, and the daily disclosure is self-verified rather than examined by an outside auditor. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} is a 1:1 euro right for EEA-resident holders through SG-FORGE after KYC checks, with payment due by the end of the following month; non-EEA holders have no direct right. Economic control concentrates elsewhere: Ethereum minting is restricted to one immutable registrar account, and upgrades run through a single technical account once the registrar approves them, so two externally owned keys stand between EURCV and its contract logic. The peg record is spotless across more than three years of tracking, with no depeg episode logged. Deployment spans Ethereum, XRPL, Stellar and Solana as issuer-native lanes, with Ethereum carrying most of the supply. The durable constraint is single-group exposure: reserve, custodian and issuer all sit within Société Générale.

yusd-aegis.title: Real-Time Proof, Unmeasured Unwind
yusd-aegis.text: Aegis YUSD is a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar built on BTC: spot held under institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at Copper and Fireblocks, hedged with COIN-M {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} shorts, with {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} income passed to holders. The Accountable dashboard publishes the reserve split in real time, and Pharos reads it directly. What it does not publish is the unwind: no position-level hedge size, margin requirements, market depth, or measured time-to-close for the spot and short book. That gap holds backing back on the {{grade}} card, while the exit pillar leads it. Economic control scores lowest: YUSD runs as bridged representations on several other chains whose control semantics Pharos has not resolved, and its pricing path is privileged and internal. Issuance runs through a single trusted-signer path under a 3-of-5 Safe with no timelock and no active mint cap on Ethereum, and the token owner can blacklist holders. The peg score is strong, but Pharos has logged repeated depeg events, including one deep excursion. Real-time disclosure shows the positions; it does not establish how quickly they could be closed.

reusd-resupply.title: CDP Dollar on crvUSD Lending Shares
reusd-resupply.text: Resupply's reUSD is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin minted against Curve Lend and Fraxlend vault shares, so its collateral is itself a lending position in other stablecoins, and a 1% communal {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fee sets the price floor. The live pair registry puts more than nine tenths of that collateral in crvUSD lending markets, with the rest in Fraxlend, so reUSD inherits both crvUSD's and frxUSD's failure domains. Pair pricing converts vault shares at their internal rate and treats crvUSD and frxUSD as a dollar, with no external market feed. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down most by economic control, the weakest of the three pillars: the token's owner, Resupply Core, and its authorized operators can mint any amount without a collateral check or durable supply ceiling. The token itself has no freeze, blacklist or upgrade path. The June 2025 oracle-manipulation exploit created roughly $9.6M of bad debt, repaid through treasury funds, insurance-pool burns and a Yearn DAO loan. Pharos has recorded hundreds of depeg events since the 2025 launch, consistent with a floor that lets price sit below par before redemption arbitrage engages. reUSD's peg rests on a redemption fee and the health of two other stablecoins' lending markets.

tbill-openeden.title: Whitelisted T-Bill Fund, Supply Unproven
tbill-openeden.text: OpenEden's TBILL is a tokenized BVI professional fund holding short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills managed by BNY Investment Management under BNY custody. Subscriptions and transfers are whitelisted, and the token drifts above its original dollar as NAV accrues to holders rather than resetting to par. The paperwork is thinner than the institutional nameplates suggest. Daily NAV figures come from fund administrator Protege Fund Services, the annual auditor has published no report, and the only named controls work is a one-off Ernst & Young procedures review rather than a recurring {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. Pharos's July 2026 reserve review pinned the balance sheet at almost entirely direct Treasury bills, with small money-market fund and USDC cash balances. The listing has nevertheless been quarantined since mid-July 2026. Price resolves, but CoinGecko reports no market cap, DefiLlama carries no list row, and no permitted source yet covers supply across the Ethereum, Arbitrum, Solana and XRPL deployments plus the issuer-listed BNB one. TBILL therefore carries no report card. Until that denominator is proven, Pharos can price the fund share but cannot rate the token.

a7a5-old-vector.title: Ruble Token Under Sanctions
a7a5-old-vector.text: A7A5 is Old Vector LLC's ruble stablecoin, registered with Kyrgyzstan's Finnadzor and built for the cross-border A7 payments network that Pharos's reserve review links to Promsvyazbank. Issuer materials describe the backing only as an undisclosed basket of ruble deposits and short-term assets, and the transparency page carries no current reserve report. Since February 2026 the issuer has passed nearly all reserve income to holders as additional A7A5 at the Central Bank of Russia key rate minus one percentage point, so holders capture a sanctioned banking system's deposit rate. Sanctions now define the asset more than its design. OFAC designated the issuer in August 2025, and the EU and UK have targeted the token and its network. The EU's 21st Russia package in July 2026 added four more designations tied to A7, including its new links to Africa, and on October 1, 2026 Treasury called A7A5 a blocked token. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} runs through KYC'd off-chain partners, while 3-of-5 issuer multisigs control minting on Tron and Ethereum without a firm cap, which leaves economic control the weakest pillar on its {{grade}} card. Pharos prices A7A5 from a single feed and records a long tail of peg episodes. No reserve schedule, bank identity, or custody arrangement has been published, so the backing rests on the issuer's word inside a sanctioned banking perimeter.

usd1-world-liberty-financial.title: World Liberty Financial Dollar
usd1-world-liberty-financial.text: World Liberty Financial's USD1 is a Trump-affiliated dollar stablecoin issued by BitGo Bank & Trust under an OCC national trust charter, backed by a government money-market fund and bank deposits. KPMG examined the August 2026 reserve report, which put roughly three-quarters in money-market fund shares and the rest in demand-deposit cash, and Chainlink publishes a live reserve feed. The report does not name the deposit banks, and holders have a contractual {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} right rather than a property interest in specific reserve assets, which keeps backing mid-card. Direct redemption is limited to registered BitGo clients in good standing; everyone else relies on secondary markets. That is why exit is the weakest of the three pillars: the deepest measured on-chain route covers only a small fraction of a stress-sized exit. Economic control scores highest, though several bridge routes and control identities across its many chains remain unresolved. The peg has held near par for over a year. Together the three pillars set the {{grade}} overall grade. The durable constraint is that most holders can leave only through secondary markets.

usdx-hex-trust.title: Treasury Claims, No Reserve Table
usdx-hex-trust.text: Hex Trust's USDX is a Hong Kong-issued dollar token that its issuer describes as fully backed by U.S. Treasury bills, cash and cash equivalents at tier-1 institutions, with Hex Trust as custodian. Pharos cannot check that description against a current breakdown. At the July 2026 review the issuer page's reserve panel was still an 'Updating Reserves' placeholder, no dated {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} or category weights were linked, and the whole reserve is carried as undisclosed allocation. Direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is open only to approved parties, and Pharos has not verified a same-value route for other holders, who depend on secondary markets. Those markets have not kept the token at par: the peg record runs to hundreds of depeg events, the worst taking the token to a fraction of par, although the latest 90-day window stayed inside the band.  Independent native issuance on Ethereum, Flare and Songbird runs through externally owned minter accounts with no cap, and an admin can grant further roles. Hex Trust's custody role is documented; a reserve breakdown a holder can check is not.

pusd-plume.title: Plume's Safe-Controlled USDC Wrapper
pusd-plume.text: Plume's pUSD wraps USDC 1:1 in Plume-managed Nucleus BoringVaults on Ethereum and Plume Chain, minted through a gateway with off-chain compliance checks and redeemable without protocol fees, though cross-chain redemption can sit pending for up to 12 hours. The reserve side reconciles: Pharos's September 2026 vault reads matched native USDC and legacy bridged USDC.e to pUSD supply almost to the token, with more than a quarter in the bridged representation. The {{grade}} overall grade comes from the control side. A 3-of-6 Safe can call the vault's mint function with zero collateral, change who may mint, and upgrade the native-deposit logic without a timelock. The same owner can burn any holder's pUSD through the vault's exit function. The deviation history records more than a dozen depeg events, including one excursion far below par. Supply is small. The USDC backing is verifiable; what a holder cannot verify is any limit on the Safe that controls issuance, burns and upgrades.

bold-liquity.title: Liquity V2's Immutable Dollar
bold-liquity.text: BOLD is Liquity V2's decentralized dollar stablecoin, minted from immutable {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} vaults against WETH, wstETH, and rETH only: no governance keys, no admin functions, no RWA exposure. On the {{grade}} report card, exit and economic control are the two strongest pillars. Exit rests on permissionless on-chain {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} of BOLD for $1 of collateral, and user-set interest rates, with most interest revenue flowing to Stability Pools, are designed to adjust to peg conditions. Backing is the lowest of the three pillars, though still close to the others, and the collateral is ETH and its staking derivatives rather than T-bills. What holds the overall grade back today is age: the binding cap on the card is a track-record limit for a design still short of two years of implementation history. Deployments now span a multichain footprint transported by Chainlink CCIP rather than native issuance; nearly all supply still sits on Ethereum, but the non-Ethereum balances carry that external validation assumption.

avusd-avant.title: Redeemable Receipt, Leveraged Book
avusd-avant.text: avUSD is Avant's dollar token, redeemable 1:1 for USDC through the protocol and deployed into an actively managed {{term:delta-neutral}}market-neutral{{/term}} book. avUSD itself earns nothing; holders who want yield stake into the separately tracked savUSD. USDC is the mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rail rather than the reserve: capital runs through basis trades, lending arbitrage, yield trading and private liquidity deals, with the avUSDx junior tranche and a separate reserve fund absorbing strategy losses first. Avant's own API shows how leveraged the book is: at the late-September 2026 checkpoint, gross assets were roughly eight times net asset value, funded by debt. Pharos does not admit that gross mix as a reserve composition, which holds backing back on the {{grade}} card. Economic control is the weakest pillar: on Avalanche, the shared token owner and gateway admin, which Avant has disclosed as a 3-of-4 MPC held by core team members, can replace minters and raise the mint cap. Protocol redemption can take up to seven days depending on market liquidity, and the current fee is shown before confirmation. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} sits with unregulated institutions under a BVI domicile. The peg has mostly held, though the worst recorded reading sits several hundred basis points from par. avUSD's durable constraint is that its par claim rests on Avant running a leveraged book well.

ylds-figure.title: The SEC-Registered Yield Coin
ylds-figure.text: YLDS is a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing stablecoin{{/term}} issued by Figure Certificate Company as a face-amount certificate registered under the Securities Act of 1933 and the Investment Company Act of 1940. It pays SOFR minus 35 basis points, accrued daily, and mints and redeems through Figure subject to KYC and the offering terms. The audited FY2025 schedules show overnight {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} repo at UMB Bank as roughly three quarters of the qualified assets and short-dated Treasury bills as most of the remainder, with KPMG's audit opinion covering the schedules of investments. That audit is now the constraint on the card: later quarterly statements are unaudited, the attested composition has aged past Pharos's freshness bound, and the card is published as {{grade}} because critical evidence is insufficient. Native issuance sits on Provenance and Stellar; Hastra's wYLDS is a separate instrument, not a representation of the certificate. Exit is the weakest pillar because redemption is eligibility-gated and its settlement terms are not established, while transfers are restrictable and accounts can be frozen. The certificates remain unsecured obligations of FCC, and Pharos records the deposited assets' bankruptcy protection as contractual only.

usdq-quantoz.title: The Dutch Compliance Standard
usdq-quantoz.text: Quantoz's USDQ is the DNB-supervised, MiCAR-authorized e-money token that treats compliance as the product. The peg record is the strongest line on the card. The reserves read impeccably on paper: about two-thirds U.S. Treasuries and one-third cash at Tier 1 European banks, safeguarded through a bankruptcy-remote foundation at a ratio just above full backing. The catch is that Pharos has to take Quantoz's word for it. The transparency page is a self-published snapshot refreshed ad hoc, with no named auditor, no named banks, no disclosed bond maturities, and one percentage point of the reserve left unexplained. That evidence gap makes backing the weakest of the three pillars despite sovereign-grade assets, and it is why the overall grade sits at {{grade}} for an otherwise clean profile. Direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at face value exists, but Quantoz's webpage and whitepaper disagree on who qualifies, and compliance checks can take up to a week. Circulation is small and spread across Ethereum, Polygon, XRPL, and Algorand. MiCAR authorization does not supply reserve evidence on its own, so until an independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} appears, backing is graded on the issuer's snapshot.

usdn-noble.title: Noble Rebasing T-Bill Dollar
usdn-noble.text: USDN is Noble's representation of M0's M token: M is locked on Ethereum through M0's Portal, and Wormhole NTT messages credit the matching USDN on Noble. The underlying is M0's short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} structure, with M0 minters posting collateral and validators {{term:attestation}}attesting{{/term}} to it on-chain. Noble's dollar module tracks each holder's principal against the M0 index and mints accrued Treasury rewards, which holders must claim before their balances grow. Pharos verified the wrapper directly: at a September 2026 Noble block, locked M principal at the current index matched USDN supply to the last micro-unit, so the remaining risk sits in M0 and the bridge rather than in the wrapper's own reserve. The weaker part is getting out at size. The exit is the reverse bridge back into M, and Pharos maps no comparable same-notional route, so exit is the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card. Noble's authority module can also switch off USDN transfers chain-wide.

usdu-unitas.title: Unitas's Hedged-Book Dollar
usdu-unitas.text: Unitas's USDu is a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar: collateral on Solana and BNB Smart Chain is paired with CEX {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} shorts settled through Copper and Ceffu off-exchange {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. Pharos reads the reserve split from Accountable's proof-of-solvency dashboard, and its October 17, 2026 checkpoint showed reserves about a tenth above outstanding supply. Bitcoin was the largest bucket at over half the reserve, yet neither the dashboard nor HT Digital's October 16 letter states how that Bitcoin is held or whether it is hedged. The letter values assets by instrument, including a Jupiter LP position, but it is not an assurance engagement and does not map assets to venues. The holder's claim is narrow. Unitas's August 2026 terms redeem USDu for a pro-rata share of the collateral, subject to protocol rules and throttles, and disclaim any promise of a one-dollar value. Direct mint and redeem is whitelist-restricted, which makes exit the weakest pillar and leaves most holders on secondary markets. The terms deny Unitas any power to freeze, burn or seize USDu, and the token contracts Pharos reviewed carry no such control. The {{grade}} grade reflects a gated, pro-rata exit over a reserve whose largest holding is only partly described.

usdg-paxos.title: Paxos's MAS-Licensed Global Dollar
usdg-paxos.text: Paxos's USDG is issued by Paxos Singapore under a MAS Major Payment Institution licence, with a MiCA-authorized EU issuance through Paxos Issuance Europe OY layered on top. The reserve is textbook. At the August 2026 KPMG examination, roughly half sat in a BNY Dreyfus government {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}}, most of the rest in Treasury bills maturing within weeks, and a small cash sleeve at commercial banks in Singapore and Luxembourg, all in segregated accounts held for token holders. The report card reads accordingly: backing, exit, and economic control all sit high, with economic control the lowest of the three because a Paxos-operated key can manage supply controllers immediately, outside the 24-hour timelock on upgrades. The gap between those pillars and the {{grade}} overall grade reflects a peg record that carries one severe early dislocation alongside a run of brief episodes, over a tracking history that only began in late 2024. Two structural facts deserve attention: bankruptcy remoteness rests on contract rather than a trust, since Paxos's explicit trust language covers only its Trust Company coins, and X Layer holds the biggest single share of native supply, a concentration Pharos measures as material. Direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through Paxos Singapore for verified users is the core exit. The catch remains on-chain presence: a handful of chains and an institutional pedigree that still outpaces its DeFi footprint.

xsgd-straitsx.title: MAS-Licensed Singapore Dollar Token
xsgd-straitsx.text: XSGD is StraitsX's Singapore dollar stablecoin, issued by a MAS-licensed Major Payment Institution and redeemable 1:1 for SGD directly through the issuer. Its {{grade}} overall grade rests on a well-documented reserve: segregated accounts held on trust for token holders and explicitly excluded from the issuer's unsecured-creditor estate, with KK Yap & Associates examining the position twice a month. The latest examination Pharos holds, as of 31 August 2026, reconciled the reserve against circulation on every chain. The disclosure gap sits in the second half of the book. Roughly half the reserve is cash, and the rest sits in a category of short-dated MAS or government bills or overnight reverse repos that the report does not split, so that slice is described by the bucket it may occupy rather than what it holds. StraitsX names three Singapore banks it may use but publishes no provider shares or rehypothecation terms. Exit scores highest on direct par redemption. Economic control is the weakest pillar, with issuance spread across issuer multisigs and allowance-capped minters on nine native deployments. The peg's only recorded depeg event dates to March 2023. The durable constraint is that holders see the reserve category, not the instruments inside it.

xusd-straitsx.title: StraitsX's Cash-Reserve Dollar
xusd-straitsx.text: XUSD is StraitsX's U.S. dollar stablecoin, issued by the same MAS-licensed Major Payment Institution as its XSGD sibling and redeemable 1:1 into a whitelisted beneficiary bank account. The reserve is the strong side of the card. KK Yap & Associates examines it twice a month, and the 31 August 2026 examination found it held entirely in cash, slightly above XUSD in circulation, with every disclosed chain supply reconciled. StraitsX holds reserves on trust and outside its unsecured-creditor estate, at CIMB, DBS, or Standard Chartered in Singapore or another MAS-permitted institution, but does not say which bank holds the cash or in what shares. Exit is the weakest pillar by a wide margin, and it pulls the overall grade down to {{grade}}. Primary redemption runs through the issuer's bank window, which its terms set at up to five business days, and the only DEX route Pharos tracks, an Ethereum AMM pool, does not qualify as a comparable exit at the same size. The peg record carries a long tail of mostly shallow depeg events from earlier in its life, with none in the most recent 90 days. The durable constraint is that a clean cash reserve still reaches holders only through StraitsX's banking window.

vgbp-vnx.title: A Sterling Float Barely Above One Redemption Ticket
vgbp-vnx.text: VGBP is VNX Global's pound sterling token, issued under the same Bermuda Class M licence and reserve programme as VCHF. Apex Fund Services' August 2026 {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} found GBP 126,596 of cash in a designated Bermuda Commercial Bank account against 126,595 VGBP outstanding, an excess of under one pound. Unlike the VCHF report, the VGBP liability table covers every deployment Pharos tracks: Solana, Celo and Base. Size is the binding fact. VNX sets a GBP 100,000 minimum per institutional transaction, so a single direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at the threshold would retire about four fifths of the attested float. Direct exits are limited to verified institutional customers and settle in about one business day, and Pharos has no established capacity, cost or settlement data for that route. Economic control is the weakest pillar on a {{grade}} card: each of the three deployments can be minted with no multisig, timelock or global supply cap. The durable constraint is concentration: one bank holds the whole reserve, and a single minimum-size redemption would retire most of the float.

cusd-cap.title: Basket Wrapper, Mostly USDC
cusd-cap.text: cUSD is Cap's dollar minted against a governance-whitelisted vault of regulated stablecoins and tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}}, with borrowers underwritten through shared security networks such as EigenLayer and Symbiotic. Pharos's reviewed vault read found only two assets, roughly nine-tenths USDC and the rest WisdomTree's WTGXX fund shares, so the basket is concentrated in USDC rather than diversified across {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} holdings, and backing is the strongest pillar on the card. Cap's October 26, 2026 announcement says anyone can now mint and redeem cUSD 1:1 with USDC, 24/7, without fees, whitelists or delays. The protocol documentation still describes minting at oracle-determined value under dynamic fees and basket {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} for a fixed fee, and that payout returns a proportional slice of every underlying asset, socialising any single reserve depeg across all redeemers. That same design leaves the exit pillar weak, because a basket payout carries no explicit same-notional dollar value for Pharos to score. The {{grade}} overall grade comes from economic control, the weakest of the three: a Safe-rooted one-day timelock can add assets, replace mint logic, or authorize a Tempo issuer with no effective supply cap. cUSD's backing therefore rests mostly on Circle's USDC, plus whatever the vault's credit strategies do with idle capital.

msusd-main-street.title: Frozen After Failed Reserve Verification
msusd-main-street.text: msUSD was Main Street's dollar token with a USDC {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} target, and Pharos has tracked it as frozen since June 20, 2026. Main Street documented 1:1 USDC minting and redemption for verified users, but the route was capacity-managed and cooldown-bound, and settlement could require unwinding strategy positions. The separate msY token carried the options-strategy {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}}, yet nothing Pharos could verify showed unstaked msUSD segregated from the liquidity that strategy needed. On June 20 Accountable terminated its reserve-verification agreement, saying the protocol failed its verification standards, and msUSD fell far below the dollar. Main Street disputed the reserve-failure characterization and said the assets remained backed. With no independent verifier in place, Pharos carries the whole reserve as one very-high-risk, unverified bucket, and the token has traded well under par since.

iusd-infinifi.title: Credit Book Behind a Redemption Queue
iusd-infinifi.text: infiniFi's iUSD is minted against USDC and deployed across a book of DeFi lending positions and longer-dated private credit, with the siUSD wrapper passing the yield to stakers. Pharos's reserve data puts the larger share in Fasanara funds and New Silver and FalconX credit positions that unwind over a week or more, while the Spark and Aave lending positions classed as immediately liquid form a minority buffer. Withdrawals are paid from that buffer and queue when it runs short. The exit pillar is the weakest on the card, because Pharos has no executable same-notional route evidence for a holder leaving at size, and it pulls the overall grade down to {{grade}}. Economic control scores little better: governance can grant a new minter whose mint call checks no collateral or supply ceiling, with a 4-of-8 admin Safe behind a seven-day timelock at the root. The peg has no recorded depeg events and stress readings sit at the calm end of the scale, but both measure price, not the liquidity wall a credit book of this shape can meet. Holders of {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} siUSD earn private-credit {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} returns through a stablecoin interface, with the buffer-driven {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} queue as the gate.

pht-pht.title: Peso CDP Running on One USDT Wrapper
pht-pht.text: PHT is APACX's Philippine-peso stablecoin built as a Maker-style CDP system, but its live collateral is narrower than the architecture suggests. APACX says all existing PHT was minted against custodial apcxUSDT backed 1:1 by USDT at one disclosed Tron wallet, and Pharos's latest Vat read puts nearly all PHT debt in that apcxUSDT branch, with residual debt in four others. No branch-level balances or reserve-to-PHT reconciliation are published, and the wallet's controller is undisclosed. Pharos publishes the overall grade as {{grade}} because critical evidence is insufficient: reserve composition, a same-notional exit, the bridge route and control identity all remain unresolved. Pricing adds its own gap, since the main live branches divide a Chainlink stablecoin/USD numerator by an owner-set APACX PHP/USD denominator with no contract-enforced freshness. Dutch-auction {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}} make the mechanism legible, but APACX's Redeem action only repays a borrower's own debt, so an ordinary holder has no redemption route. The Tron representation runs unverified code. Holder value depends on an apcxUSDT wrapper with no published reconciliation and on a PHP/USD rate the issuer sets.

hyusd-hylo.title: A Stable Tranche Over SOL LSTs
hyusd-hylo.text: Hylo's HYUSD is the stable tranche of a dual-token design in which each pool's xASSET absorbs collateral-price swings before HYUSD holders take any. Leverage buyers carry that volatility by construction. Under Hylo V2 the collateral sits in isolated SOL-LST, cbBTC, HYPE, and USDC pools, and Pharos reads those pools directly from the deployed Solana accounts. At the August 2026 reading SOL liquid-staking tokens made up the bulk of the book and pool liabilities reconciled to HYUSD supply, which is why backing is the strongest pillar on the {{grade}} report card. Exit is weak because no comparable same-notional route out is documented.  The token itself has no freeze authority, but the deployed exchange program is not verified against published source, so Pharos cannot confirm which oracle and liquidation checks it actually enforces. A 3-of-4 Squads multisig behind a six-hour timelock can also replace the program and its mint logic. The peg record shows only a few shallow deviations. The durable constraint is that {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} through a volatility-absorbing tranche is only as sturdy as the leverage demand funding it and the unverified code enforcing it.

meusd-mezo.title: Liquity Mechanics Under a Multisig Owner
meusd-mezo.text: Mezo's MUSD applies Liquity-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics to Bitcoin collateral at a 110% minimum ratio, with permissionless {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} on Mezo's Bitcoin L2, a young chain that is neither Ethereum nor a Stage 1 rollup. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by control and exit rather than collateral. Backing now scores best of the three pillars, even though the collateral is a single BTC envelope in Mezo's ActivePool whose native-versus-wrapped split is not published. The Mezo token owner's 5-of-9 Safe administers the canonical mint list and can authorize additional minters, so Pharos scores issuance as unbounded. The Ethereum and Base representations run through Wormhole NTT under that same Safe, and the owner can add burners able to burn from arbitrary accounts. Exit is held back because no comparable same-notional route is compiled, despite the redemption design. MUSD has logged a long tail of deviation episodes on both sides of par rather than a single break. The redemption floor is inherited from Liquity, but immutability is not: a 5-of-9 owner Safe can still change who mints and burns MUSD.

usdu-usdu-finance.title: A Dollar Backed Mostly by Itself
usdu-usdu-finance.text: USDU is USDU Finance's Ethereum dollar, minted through DAO-approved adapter modules into Curve, Morpho and TermMax positions rather than against collateral posted by outside borrowers. After a sharp supply wind-down, the issuer's transparency endpoint reports backing roughly equal to the small amount still outstanding. The composition is the catch. Pharos's September 2026 split of that backing puts about three-quarters in USDU-denominated Morpho vault shares and the USDU leg of the Curve pool; only the USDC side of the pool is external collateral. Coverage reported at par therefore rests mostly on claims on USDU itself, which would lose value alongside the token under stress. The curator-operated Morpho adapter can mint USDU into its own vault without a fixed cap. Two newer swap modules let any holder route USDC or USDT in and out through Morpho vaults, and exit is the strongest of the three pillars. Backing sits between them, held back by unpublished recovery, allocation and custody inputs. The durable constraint is circular: the collateral that reports full coverage is mostly denominated in the token it covers.

uty-xsy.title: Steady Peg, Seven-Day Exit
uty-xsy.text: UTY (Unity) is YieldPoint's market-neutral synthetic dollar, minted 1:1 from USDC on Base and redeemable for USDC only on Base after a seven-day bonding period. Deposits are swept to managed custody and allocated across strategy modules that may include long-spot and short-perpetual hedges, on-chain lending, liquidity provision and structured yield. Pharos's chain census places the tracked circulating supply on Avalanche, where UTY is a LayerZero representation of tokens locked on Base, so a holder's path to {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} also runs through that bridge. The peg record is steady: dozens of recorded deviations, the worst about 3%. Backing is the strongest pillar on the {{grade}} card but still mid-range, because the Accountable feed itemizes reserves by chain and settlement location (mostly Ethereum, Base and Avalanche) rather than by asset, leaving positions, hedge notionals and venue balances undisclosed. Economic control is held back by an undisclosed oracle topology: the issuer does not publish how the strategy is priced, what freshness bounds apply, or what fails over. Exit is the weakest pillar. A holder who wants out during stress either waits out the bonding period or sells into secondary markets. The peg has held when tested; the risk sits in the week-long bonding period and the bridge a holder must cross to reach USDC.

gusd-gate.title: Par Price, Opaque Ledger
gusd-gate.text: GUSD is Gate's account-linked yield certificate: users subscribe 1:1 with USDT, USDC, or USD1, receive daily GUSD rewards, and {{term:redemption}}redeem{{/term}} through Gate. Gate says tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}} and stablecoins back the product, but publishes no holdings schedule, named backing-asset custody structure, legal segregation, or independent reserve-to-token reconciliation. Its exchange proof-of-reserves now publishes customer and platform GUSD balances, which answers whether Gate holds customer GUSD but does not show what backs every token. The Ethereum control plane remains a single-EOA minter plus a separate no-delay EOA upgrader. GUSD also exists on GateLayer as a LayerZero OFT representation locked against Ethereum tokens, which Pharos reviews as a separate bridge exposure. The displayed market cap inherits DefiLlama's full Ethereum token-supply series and is materially above Gate subscription and CoinGecko circulating figures, so it should not be read as reconciled circulation. The peg has stayed close to par; the {{grade}} overall grade reflects the evidence and control plane behind that price.

usdcv-societe-generale-forge.title: SocGen-FORGE USDCV Bank-Issued Dollar
usdcv-societe-generale-forge.text: SG-FORGE's USDCV is a MiCA-regulated, bank-issued dollar: 100% USD cash in segregated accounts at BNY Mellon's Belgian entity and Societe Generale, an ACPR-supervised EMI licence, statutory segregation with a pro-rata holder claim, and a reserve page the issuer updates daily. That last point is the catch. The reserve could hardly be simpler, but the disclosure is self-reported rather than independently examined, and backing is the weakest of the three pillars behind the {{grade}} overall grade. Assurance, segregation, and custody continuity all score in the middle of the scale for want of outside verification, and with two named banks the reserve is concentrated by construction. Exit scores well because Ethereum DEX depth absorbs much of a stress-size sale at low cost; direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through SG-FORGE is open only to verified EEA residents. Issuance is native on Ethereum and Solana with no third-party {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}, but both chains resolve to SG-FORGE-held keys, and a technical key controls Ethereum upgrades with no timelock. The peg record carries two recorded deviations since launch, the larger one above par. The durable constraint is that the bank's own daily page is still the only check on the bank.

usdai-usd-ai.title: The Liquid Base Token
usdai-usd-ai.text: USDai is the non-yielding base token in USD.AI, backed by PYUSD held in the canonical Arbitrum contract. Its outstanding supply includes USDai held inside the separate sUSDai vault as well as tokens held elsewhere. When funds are deployed into GPU-backed lending, USDai can be burned to release PYUSD while the resulting loan exposure remains in sUSDai's portfolio. Base-token supply can therefore fall without an equivalent withdrawal of assets from the protocol. Loan repayments redeposited as PYUSD can mint USDai again. The issuer's total value locked also includes loan positions and accrued yield, so it is not interchangeable with USDai supply. Adding sUSDai's full asset value to base-token supply would double count the USDai still held by the vault. Pharos tracks the base token separately from that credit strategy. Primary minting and redemption use PYUSD through an eligibility-controlled hub; holders remain exposed to PYUSD, protocol administration, and the controls on their bridge route.

susdai-usd-ai.title: USD.AI GPU-Loan Vault Share
susdai-usd-ai.text: sUSDai is USD.AI's yield-bearing vault share, with a net asset value combining unallocated USDai and GPU-backed lending positions. Its share price reflects portfolio value rather than a fixed dollar redemption promise. Deploying funds into lending can burn the underlying USDai to release PYUSD while preserving the loan exposure in the vault's assets. That movement can reduce base USDai supply without an equivalent fall in protocol value. Conversely, adding the full sUSDai asset value to outstanding USDai would double count the unallocated USDai held by the vault. USD.AI's reserve index separates a liquid PYUSD sleeve from GPU loan exposure, but on-chain balances do not independently verify GPU identity, appraisal, insurance, or borrower-entity enforceability. Exits run through a FIFO queue processed in 30-day epochs, and unfilled requests roll forward. Deployments on five chains beyond Arbitrum add LayerZero burn-and-mint routes and chain-local admin keys, including a Solana freeze authority held by a Squads multisig. Those unresolved bridge controls make economic control the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} report card, which is also held at the parent USDai rating. Redemption ultimately depends on available liquidity and the performance and enforceability of the credit portfolio.

usx-solstice.title: Synthetic Dollar, Aggregate Proof
usx-solstice.text: Solstice's USX is a Swiss-domiciled synthetic dollar on Solana, minted through KYC-gated institutional issuance against a reserve the issuer describes as audited cash, tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}}, and {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} hedged positions, with Copper and Ceffu named as custodians. What Pharos can verify is narrower than that description. The Accountable attestation feed reports aggregate reserves slightly above supply, with cryptographic proof material but no asset-level balances, so the current split among cash, Treasuries, and hedges is unpublished and the backing pillar is scored on limited evidence. Minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} validate collateral through Solstice's own oracle cross-checked against Pyth, and the issuer's program holds live mint and freeze authority.  Redemption is eligibility-gated, so retail holders depend on Solana secondary markets, and a December 2025 thin-liquidity episode took USX to a small fraction of par on a DEX before it recovered. The peg record has been quiet since, but the structure has not changed: an institutional redemption window in front, an aggregate-only solvency proof behind, and everyone else trading the gap.

hollar-hydrated.title: Hydration's Aave-Fork Dollar on Polkadot
hollar-hydrated.text: HOLLAR is Hydration's overcollateralized dollar, minted on an Aave V3 fork against DOT, ETH, BTC, and stablecoin collateral with a Stability Module that anchors the peg through direct stablecoin swaps. The core mechanics are a multi-collateral {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with per-block partial {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}, and a Stability Module that behaves like a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}. That design earns structural credit, and economic control is the strongest pillar on the {{grade}} report card. The weaknesses are evidentiary and market-side. Hydration publishes no dated per-asset collateral weights, so the whole reserve is scored as an unsplit basket; the launch was less than two years ago; and the route out has no stated same-notional dollar output. Governance reach is also wider than a fork label suggests: the admin role can repoint the token's delegated-allowance contract and move any holder's balance, and OpenGov's root track can replace runtime logic wholesale. The peg record carries a short tail of sharp episodes on thin DEX liquidity, with the worst excursions several percent below par. HOLLAR's viability ultimately tracks whether Polkadot DeFi expands or contracts, and the shallow order books around it are the durable constraint.

musd-metamask.title: MetaMask's Wrapper on M0
musd-metamask.text: MetaMask mUSD is a Bridge-issued dollar built as a pure wrapper on M0: each token is minted by depositing M through the M0 SwapFacility and burned to return it, so the reserve Pharos scores is the M token itself. Behind M sit cash and short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} holdings checked by M0's real-time on-chain {{term:attestation}}validator attestations{{/term}}, though M's internal cash-versus-Treasury split and provider allocations stay undisclosed. That inheritance sets the card. The {{grade}} overall grade is held at the ceiling of its required parent, M, and backing is the weakest of the three pillars, while exit scores well above both backing and economic control. The peg record fits the wrapper design: depeg episodes are confined to the first months of tracking, the largest a premium spike, and none has been recorded since February 2026. The less visible risk is where supply now sits. MetaMask's Money Account, launched June 30, 2026, converts deposits to mUSD and routes them into a lending vault on Monad. Monad now holds the largest block of supply, where mUSD exists as a bridge representation minted through M0's Hyperlane-based portal rather than natively, and that share is above the quarter-of-supply threshold at which Pharos flags a critical bridge dependency. The durable constraint is that mUSD cannot rate above M, whatever MetaMask builds on top of it.

cash-phantom.title: Phantom and Bridge's Solana Dollar
cash-phantom.text: CASH is a centralized dollar stablecoin on Solana from Phantom and Bridge Building Inc., redeemable 1:1 and backed by short-term Treasury, money-market-fund, and cash reserves. Disclosure has improved since launch. Bridge now runs a CASH-specific reserve dashboard that reconciles circulating tokens against reserve assets and, in its October 2026 reading, split them into about 7% cash and deposits and 93% in a combined Treasury and government money-market-fund bucket. Bridge's platform-wide disclosures describe segregated, bankruptcy-remote accounts and name BlackRock and Fidelity as custodians, but do not allocate CASH reserves between them. The limits are still material: the figures are self-reported, no independent CASH {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} is published, and the combined bucket does not separate direct T-bills from fund shares. On the {{grade}} card the three pillars sit within a few points of each other, with exit narrowly the weakest because primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is eligibility-gated. Control carries its own findings: a single-key Bridge program upgrader can replace mint logic without delay, and the HyperEVM representation runs on a LayerZero route whose control identity is unresolved. The recent peg record is clean, but the reserve evidence remains Bridge's own reporting until an independent party attests to it.

tgbp-tokenised.title: Sterling Token With Unidentified Bonds
tgbp-tokenised.text: tGBP is BCP Technologies' pound stablecoin, issued under an FCA cryptoasset registration and redeemed through a direct off-chain GBP workflow. Andersen's monthly agreed-upon-procedures report now breaks the reserve into asset classes: the August 2026 table put about three-fifths in GBP money market funds, just over a fifth in bonds and the rest in bank cash. Those are factual findings rather than an audit opinion, and they leave gaps that matter for scoring. The bond slice names no issuer, instrument or maturity, and the banks and fund managers holding the rest are undisclosed, so Pharos scores those slices as bounded unknowns rather than assuming gilts. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} runs through the issuer's sterling rails.
