Economic control scores highest on the card: the LayerZero OFT mesh across eight chains is externally validated, even though a single externally owned key can mint and pause every EVM deployment and upgrade six of the seven. The peg has held near par with a tail of brief dips. The durable constraint is the unnamed bond book: until BCP identifies it, a fifth of the reserve stays unclassified.

eurau-allunity.title: Licensed Reserves, Unnamed Banks
eurau-allunity.text: EURAU is AllUnity's MiCA-licensed euro stablecoin, issued by a BaFin-supervised EMI and backed one-for-one by euro reserves held in segregated accounts at EU credit institutions, with direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through AllUnity. The regulatory packaging is complete; the disclosure is not. The trust center still lists the reserve audit report as coming soon, and neither the white paper nor the site names the current banks, publishes allocations or a cash-versus-HQLA split, or defines what happens if a reserve bank fails, which is why backing grades in the middle of the card rather than at the top. The {{grade}} overall grade is dragged down by exit, the weakest pillar: redemption is eligibility-gated and secondary-market coverage is thin, with a single-source price feed and no depeg episode on record. Distribution now spans eight issuer-native deployments, including Solana, Tempo and BSC alongside the EVM majors, moved by AllUnity's own burn-and-mint mapping bridge; the announced Chainlink CCIP integration was not yet registered on any chain at the last check. On the EVM lanes the minter and admin are single externally owned accounts with no cap and no delay, so the reserve claim and the supply control both rest on AllUnity's backend. Until the audit report appears, backing is graded on the issuer's word.

usdh-native-markets.title: Hyperliquid's Native Dollar, Retired
usdh-native-markets.text: USDH was Native Markets' dollar for Hyperliquid, issued on HyperEVM by Bridge Building Inc., Stripe's stablecoin subsidiary, after a September 2025 validator vote awarded Native Markets the ticker. The reserve was conventional and well documented. Bridge's monthly BPM LLP {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} for March 2026 put most of it in Superstate's USTB tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} fund, with the rest in government {{term:money-market-fund}}money market funds{{/term}}, USDC, and bank cash. That made USDH a stablecoin backed largely by other tokens, so its reserve chain ran through USTB and USDC rather than ending at a bank account. On May 14, 2026, Bridge announced the sunset after Coinbase agreed to buy the USDH ticker from Native Markets and partnered with Hyperliquid on USDC. New issuance stopped from May 19 except in limited circumstances, and Bridge kept fee-free USDH-to-USDC and fiat {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} open for onboarded holders. Pharos froze USDH on July 11, 2026 as an archived migration asset. Its reserve chain was well evidenced, but the product's relevance rested on a single venue's choice of dollar.

sbc-brale.title: Brale's Platform Stablecoin
sbc-brale.text: Brale's SBC is a dollar stablecoin issued by a FinCEN-registered money transmitter across eleven networks, from Ethereum and Polygon to Solana, Stellar, and Tempo, with direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through Brale. Backing is well documented for its size. MCCPA's monthly examination as of August 31, 2026 records mostly cash and cash equivalents plus a small sleeve of U.S. government-backed debt in segregated accounts, fully reconciled to issued SBC, although the examiner relied on company-provided records and the report names neither the banks nor provider allocations. Exit also scores well: Pharos has reviewed Brale's direct redemption route, though the user agreement allows discretionary delays and account limits and sets no settlement deadline or capacity. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by economic control, the weakest of the three pillars. Upgrade powers sit with 3-of-6 Safes on Ethereum, Polygon, and Avalanche but with a single Brale issuance EOA on Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Celo, and Ethereum Classic, and several bridge routes and control identities remain unresolved. The peg record logs dozens of past deviations but none in the latest 90 days. The durable constraint is control: eleven chains of distribution multiply the keys a holder has to trust.

euri-banking-circle.title: A Bank's Euro Without a Reserve Schedule
euri-banking-circle.text: EURI is Banking Circle's euro stablecoin, issued under MiCA by a Luxembourg credit institution supervised by the CSSF, with fee-free 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at par. Banking Circle launched it in August 2024 on Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain, saying it would be available first via Binance. Holder funds sit in a segregated, bankruptcy-remote fiduciary estate of euro cash and low-risk cash equivalents, a sound legal structure that the published evidence does not yet verify. Eurite says Ernst & Young performs periodic reserve attestations, but no dated EURI attestation is publicly retrievable, and no reserve schedule splits cash from cash equivalents or shows where the money sits. That gap leaves backing as the weakest pillar on the card, which is how a licensed bank's stablecoin ends up with a {{grade}} overall grade. Exit grades almost as poorly: the score rests on the issuer's documented redemption terms, which settle slowly, and Pharos does not count the Ethereum pool as a same-notional exit. Issuance on both chains is controlled by issuer-held accounts. The peg itself behaves well, with a near-perfect score and only a couple of brief episodes on record. The durable constraint is that holders must take the reserve on the issuer's word.

msusd-metronome.title: Latency Ate the Backing
msusd-metronome.text: Metronome's msUSD spent years as a niche synth, minted against USDC, DAI, ETH, WBTC and Vesper yield tokens through {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}, with no direct holder {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. Metronome's July 30, 2026 post-mortem traced its failure to the protocol's internal synth swap module: Chainlink price latency at execution had let roughly 4.57 million msUSD accumulate with no debt positions behind them. The market repriced the discovery, and the token fell to about $0.44 on September 2. On September 16 Metronome reported the shortfall closed, with a surplus, through treasury-funded buybacks and an $8 million USDC loan against treasury wstETH, while keeping the synth swap closed indefinitely. The token has not returned to par, and the {{grade}} overall grade reflects a peg score near the bottom of the scale, which roughly halves the composite, alongside an economic-control pillar that is the weakest on the card. The durable constraint is verification: no msUSD-only collateral allocation reconciled against the multi-synth book and treasury debt has been published, so Pharos cannot yet confirm the reported recovery.

aznd-mu-digital.title: An Asia Credit Token, Wound Down
aznd-mu-digital.text: AZND was Mu Digital's KYC-gated dollar token, minted 1:1 against USDC, USDT or AUSD and backed by a Singapore fund vehicle managed under a MAS capital markets licence for Asia credit exposure. Holders locked it in the loAZND vault for yield, while the muBOND junior tranche sat underneath to absorb losses first. The last Accountable snapshot Pharos ingested showed the Asset Pool in short-term cash and liquid bonds, more conservative than a mandate that allowed up to 20% illiquid private credit. Exit was the structural weakness: primary {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} ran weekly on the fund's liquidity calendar, and the only other route was secondary swaps through DEX partners on Monad. Mu Digital announced an orderly wind-down of AZND, loAZND and muBOND on July 10, 2026, and opened its redemption portal on August 7. Secondary trading had already collapsed: Pharos's last admissible price, from a thin Curve pool on July 20, was far below a dollar, and the price providers then stopped covering the token. Pharos froze AZND in September 2026 as an archived wind-down asset. Its record is a fund-style credit product whose exit ran on the fund's schedule.

nect-beraborrow.title: Berachain CDP with a Choppy Peg Record
nect-beraborrow.text: BeraBorrow's NECT runs Liquity-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics on Berachain, minted against a collateral set that leans on WETH and Kodiak LP positions and extends to liquid-staked ETH, wrapped BTC variants and other Berachain-native tokens, with most branches rated high-risk. Backing is the strongest pillar on the card: the debt is {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} and the branch balances are read on-chain. The {{grade}} overall grade comes from elsewhere. NECT has logged hundreds of depeg episodes, the worst several points below par, and that history pulls the measured peg multiplier well below one. The last episode was in March 2026. Exit is the weakest pillar because Pharos has no supported same-notional exit route on record, despite the Liquity-style {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} for collateral at face value. The durable constraint is that the collateral design can be sound while the peg still depends on arbitrageurs showing up.

usp-pikudao.title: Turkish Carry Trade, Tokenized
usp-pikudao.text: PikuDAO's USP is a KYC-gated, NAV-appreciating token whose backing is deployed across yield strategies: a Turkish lira FX arbitrage strategy operated by Balsa Technologies, allocations to DeFi protocols such as Ethena, Aave, Cap, Giza, Almanak and USD.AI, and a USDC/USDT buffer. Ninety percent of strategy yield flows back into the backing pool, which is why the token's value has climbed above $1. Piku's transparency app now reports token and protocol positions, many of them lira-linked basis and FX trades, but the reported position values do not reconcile to the stated book value, and their contracts, custody and assurance are not identified. Pharos therefore still carries the whole reserve as one unresolved strategy envelope rated very-high risk. KYC/KYB is required to mint or redeem, through a FIFO queue that settles within 24 hours for a 0.2% {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fee. A manual issuer price feed sets issuance and redemption prices, and minting is uncapped. The durable constraint is verification: the yield shows up in the NAV, while the exposure that produces it is reported but not reconciled.

pmusd-precious-metals.title: Gold-Backed pmUSD With Sky PSM
pmusd-precious-metals.text: pmUSD is RAAC's dollar fToken from RWf(x), an f(x) fork, minted against a TokenBlender position backed solely by I-ON Digital's ION.au gold claims, with xPM absorbing collateral-price swings. Peg defense runs through a different asset: a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} lets arbitrageurs swap discounted pmUSD for Sky's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} sUSDS at a $1 internal valuation. The swap is one-directional and pauses if sUSDS falls below 20% of PSM assets, so dollar recovery depends on Sky staying healthy and on the module staying funded. That defense has not held: pmUSD has been in a continuous depeg since early May 2026, on top of hundreds of earlier recorded episodes. The overall grade is {{grade}}, with the score already below the F-range limit that the active-depeg cap would impose. Economic control is the weakest pillar: a single RAAC 2-of-3 Safe owns the minting Treasury and can replace the token and mint logic without delay. Chainlink Proof of Reserve and Instruxi data document I-ON's broader gold reserve, not the tranche pledged to pmUSD, and the legal enforceability and recovery liquidity of the in-situ gold claims remain unresolved. Gold collateral cannot restore the peg on its own; recovery runs through a one-way swap into another protocol's savings dollar.

jupusd-jupiter.title: Three Layers to Treasuries
jupusd-jupiter.text: JupUSD is Jupiter's Solana dollar, backed mostly by Ethena's USDtb with a USDC buffer under a 90/10 target rebalanced daily. USDtb in turn holds almost all of its reserve in BlackRock's BUIDL, so the chain runs JupUSD to USDtb to BUIDL to Treasury bills, repos and cash: high-grade collateral reached through three issuers' operations. Issuer documentation names Anchorage Porto for {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and the reserves sit in named Solana token accounts any third party can read, so Pharos credits reconciliation as continuous rather than taking coverage on the issuer's word. That credit has limits. JupUSD itself has no attestor and no supervisor, and a zero-delay 4-of-9 Squads multisig can upgrade the program that holds mint authority, so the centralized-mint cap binds and holds the overall grade at {{grade}}. Exit scores better than the other pillars, but primary mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at 1:1 are open only to whitelisted KYC/KYB participants; everyone else relies on market makers and a peg bot, and the peg record carries several recorded depeg events. USDtb's monthly examination reports cover USDtb's own book, so they say nothing about the balances behind JupUSD. The durable constraint is a mint path that rests on one multisig's restraint.

u-united-stables.title: Variable Reserve Wrapper
u-united-stables.text: United Stables' U is a BVI-issued dollar whose reserve policy is deliberately flexible: cash, U.S. Treasury bills and approved fiat-referenced stablecoins may all sit in the basket, in a mix the issuer can vary. The live reserve feed, which Chainlink republishes, reports one aggregate balance, so Pharos scores the backing as a single envelope. The monthly report for August 31 2026 shows $1.28 billion of reserves covering 100.74% of supply: about a third in USDC, USDT and USD1, mostly held at an exchange; 28% cash and equivalents; 24% Binance RWUSD, a yield product that cannot leave Binance and is not a claim on any underlying asset; and 16% tokenised Treasury fund units. Moore CPA's limited-assurance conclusion on that report expressly gives no assurance that the par-valued stablecoin and RWUSD balances hold their value. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} is limited to approved Mint Users, who receive issuer-selected cash or stablecoins. Backing and exit are the weakest pillars and hold the {{grade}} overall grade down. A 2-of-4 multisig can mint and upgrade without a timelock. The terms let United Stables leave reserves unsegregated and give holders no preferential, secured, or proprietary claim in insolvency, despite the website's description of segregated custody. A month-end snapshot cannot bound a basket the issuer may reshape at will.

reusd-re-protocol.title: Senior Reinsurance Tranche via Notes
reusd-re-protocol.text: Re Protocol's reUSD is the senior NAV-appreciating tranche of a reinsurance-capital structure, issued by Resilience (BVI) Ltd. Holders get off-chain exposure through principal-at-risk notes rather than a direct legal claim on the Regulation 114 trust assets behind the reinsurance contracts. Re Metrics shows the protocol's pooled book dominated by that off-chain capital, with most of the on-chain remainder in sUSDe {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} exposure, but it publishes no reUSD-specific denominator or tranche waterfall, so Pharos cannot attribute those percentages to reUSD. The token price is recalculated daily from a blend of the off-chain SOFR-based return and the trailing sUSDe basis rate plus a fixed spread, so the yield is governance-set rather than passed through. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by economic control, the weakest of the three pillars: issuance has no economic cap, Safes on two chains keep an immediate admin bypass over the deposit contracts, and an Ethereum admin EOA can grant a minter role that burns holder balances without allowance. Instant {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is liquidity-limited and falls back to a quarterly queue. The Network Firm's daily observations rest on one full report covering October 2025, which excludes reUSD backing and liability reconciliation. Holders underwrite reinsurance risk through notes they cannot look through.

rwausdi-multipli.title: Multipli's KYB-Gated Credit Dollar
rwausdi-multipli.text: rwaUSDi is Multipli's KYB-gated institutional credit class: a UAE-domiciled dollar token whose reserve is described as private credit, structured finance, project finance, asset-backed loans, and market-neutral fund strategies, priced periodically at NAV with scheduled rather than instant {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. It is issued natively on seven chains, including Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and Monad. Pharos has recorded no depeg events since tracking began. The AFI proof-of-reserves feed reports aggregate assets well above liabilities and now publishes category weights led by lithium mining, gold, and real estate exposure. It still names no obligors, custodians, legal instruments, maturities, or holder seniority, so Pharos keeps the backing pillar on conservative high-risk tiers. Pharos has no reviewed same-notional exit route to credit. Economic control is the strongest line on the card even though a shared EOA holds uncapped mint rights and chain-local Safes can force-transfer or burn any holder's balance without a timelock. The durable constraint is an exit that runs only through a KYB-gated, scheduled window against assets holders cannot inspect position by position.

usdm-mega.title: Funding the Sequencer
usdm-mega.text: MegaUSD (USDm) is MegaETH's native dollar, launched on Ethena's USDtb issuance rails with reserve yield earmarked for the chain's sequencer costs. The backing has drifted far from that launch framing. The issuer's transparency API now shows the reserve almost entirely in USDC, with USDtb, and the tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} exposure behind it, reduced to a fraction of a percent. Its custody wallets are labelled by address only, so who controls them, and how the reserve would be treated in an insolvency, remains undisclosed. Economic control is the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card: a 4-of-8 Safe owns the upgradeable Ethereum token and can add an arbitrary minter or replace mint logic without a timelock, and the same Safe can blacklist and seize named holders' balances. Backing and exit sit close together above it. Pharos tracks no DEX route, so the measured exit is issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, open only to eligible counterparties and settling over about a day. The peg has held apart from two brief deviations. The reserve is now plain USDC, but nothing on-chain stops the owner Safe from minting around it.

usdm-monetrix.title: Monetrix's Hyperliquid Delta-Neutral Dollar
usdm-monetrix.text: Monetrix USDM is the base dollar token in a small HyperEVM yield stack: users mint it 1:1 by depositing USDC into the Monetrix vault, and sUSDM is the separate staking wrapper where strategy yield accrues. The USDC does not sit idle. Monetrix deploys the backing into a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} portfolio on Hyperliquid, long spot BTC, ETH and HYPE against matching short {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} positions, and returns USDC on {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} after a multi-day governance-set cooldown. The issuer's collateral API reports coverage just above par but marks its own breakdown unreconciled, mixing spot, margin, hedge and buffer accounting with no non-double-counted reserve equation, so Pharos carries the whole reserve as a single unresolved strategy envelope. Strategy positions are valued through Hyperliquid's validator oracle, with no independent fallback. Exit is the weakest pillar: no comparable route out is measured, and a guardian role can pause the token. Mint-logic upgrades pass through a 48-hour timelock. With the reserve envelope unresolved, the card is not rated for insufficient evidence, which records missing disclosure rather than a safety verdict. What backs USDM on any given day is visible only through Monetrix's own unreconciled telemetry.

usat-tether.title: Tether Goes Domestic
usat-tether.text: Tether's USA-T is a GENIUS-era U.S. dollar issued 1:1 by Anchorage Digital Bank under an OCC federal charter, backed by cash and {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}}-collateralized overnight reverse repos with Cantor Fitzgerald {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and monthly Deloitte {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} reports. Deloitte's August 2026 examination put about nine-tenths of reserves in repo with a single broker-dealer and the rest in bank cash, mostly uninsured, with a small surplus over redeemable tokens. The report leaves that repo counterparty unnamed, along with the deposit banks. The {{grade}} overall grade rests on backing and economic control pillars that lead the card and a peg that has held at par since launch. Exit is the softest pillar: {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at par runs through Anchorage for onboarded clients, net of fees and the bank's terms. Supply sits almost entirely on Ethereum, with a small Celo deployment linked by a LayerZero lock-and-mint route, and owner-only minting and upgrades stay with the issuer. Its legal issuer is a different entity from Tether International, which issues USDT. The durable constraint is distribution: one bank, one dominant chain, and a track record still under two years.

yzusd-yuzu.title: KYC-Gated Senior Tranche on Plasma
yzusd-yuzu.text: yzUSD is Yuzu's KYC-gated base dollar on Plasma, minted and redeemed against USDT0 by accredited, qualified, or institutional investors, with yield routed to the separate syzUSD wrapper. The token is the senior claim on a pooled strategy book, and the yzPP junior tranche absorbs first losses. Yuzu's Accountable dashboard shows a leveraged stablecoin carry book: in the split Pharos last reviewed, Ethena USDe loops were the largest line at close to a third, followed by Sky USDS staking and a spread of Aave, Maple, Agora, Superstate, and PayPal USD loop positions, with a small USDT0 liquidity buffer, and nearly every slice is classed high risk. That composition does not reach the fixed scoring input, so backing is scored on limited evidence within the {{grade}} overall grade. The V3 contract installed on 31 August 2026 pays redemptions at the lower of an administered stored NAV and par, so the 1:1 target is not an unconditional conversion. That privileged pricing makes economic control the weakest pillar, even with upgrades behind a 48-hour timelock and limit changes behind a 12-hour one. The peg line on the card is strong, but with minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} restricted to eligible investors, that record reflects who is allowed to sell as much as how the book performs.

nusd-neutrl.title: Paused, Then Offered Half Par
nusd-neutrl.text: Neutrl's NUSD is a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar whose ordinary minting and redemptions were paused in August 2026 for a reserve-liquidity review. The last verifiable reserve snapshot, from August 13, put a little over half of reserves in liquid stablecoins, with the rest in OTC aggregate positions, Jupiter JLP, protocol-owned liquidity and an undisclosed other bucket. On September 17 Neutrl opened a separate fixed-rate {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} program that pays USDC and burns the redeemed tokens, expected to run until November 14, 2026 subject to its terms. At an October 2 on-chain read it quoted 0.51 USDC per NUSD, a 49% discount to the dollar target. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects that record. Minting is unbounded and Pharos cannot resolve who controls the bridged deployments. Exit scores low because no par route exists, and backing is limited by a composition not reconciled since the pause. The tracked market price has stayed near a dollar on a single price source, which the issuer's own redemption quote does not support. The durable constraint is that the issuer's exit now prices NUSD at about half its target.

usdgo-osl.title: OSL's Bank-Issued Enterprise Dollar
usdgo-osl.text: OSL's USDGO is an enterprise dollar issued by Anchorage Digital Bank under an OCC charter, with monthly Deloitte examinations reconciling reserves against the full token liability. The reserve is fund shares rather than bills held outright. At the August 2026 examination, JPMorgan's JLTXX carried about half, BlackRock's tokenized BUIDL fund more than a third, Goldman Sachs' STBXX most of the rest, and bank cash about one percent, all in segregated fiduciary trust accounts. The BUIDL slice is a tracked dependency in its own right, held in Anchorage's self-custody on Solana. The peg record shows no depeg episodes so far, over a short tracking window that began with the February 2026 launch. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by exit, the weakest of the three pillars. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} runs only through Anchorage for onboarded clients, net of fees, and Pharos recognizes no DEX venue that can absorb a same-notional sale, so this is an issuer-API exit rather than an on-chain arbitrage market. Ethereum and Morph deployments now sit beside Solana, which still carries most of the float, but issuer-controlled keys can raise mint limits and upgrade contracts on each chain. The durable constraint is access: holders who are not Anchorage clients depend on a secondary market Pharos cannot yet measure.

fidd-fidelity.title: Fidelity's Chartered Dollar
fidd-fidelity.text: FIDD is Fidelity Digital Assets' dollar stablecoin, issued under an OCC national trust charter and backed by cash and short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} at BNY Mellon. The reserve is T-bill-heavy with a sizeable cash sleeve at a single bank, and PwC examines it monthly in a Big Four {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} that reconciles reserves against outstanding tokens. The {{grade}} overall grade is capped only by time: backing and exit both lead the card, economic control trails both, and under two years of implementation history is the binding limit. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} runs 1:1 through Fidelity Digital Assets platforms, an institutional rail that the card scores as permissionless. The single Ethereum deployment sits behind a UUPS proxy administered by externally owned accounts with no timelock. FIDD's peg record is short and clean; the durable constraint is that individual externally owned keys, not a timelock or multisig, can mint and upgrade it.

aid-gaib.title: GPU Yield, Dollarized
aid-gaib.text: AID is GAIB's dollar stablecoin, minted 1:1 against USDC, USDT, and other approved stablecoins, with staking into sAID as the separate route into GAIB's GPU and AI infrastructure financing. Issuer documentation describes the reserve as {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and accepted stablecoins, but the evidence Pharos can read is murkier. The composition Pharos holds is mostly GPU financing principal booked to GAIB SPV Ltd., plus a thin layer of USDC in the minter and redeemer contracts, and the issuer app attributes that financing to staked AID rather than to AID itself. No source reconciles AID's liabilities to a Treasury and stablecoin split, and the linked accountant's report gives limited assurance over Spiceflow Corp's asset deployment, not AID's reserve. Exits run through an on-chain redeemer that burns AID for USDC after a 10 bps fee, within a daily limit and its actual USDC balance. A 3-of-5 Safe and a bare externally owned account share the admin role that can replace mint-critical logic.

apxusd-apyx.title: Dividends as Collateral
apxusd-apyx.text: apxUSD is Apyx's dollar token backed mainly by preferred shares issued by Digital Asset Treasury companies, with a cash and {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} buffer; primary mint and redemption are limited to whitelisted accounts and settle in USDC. The design bets that variable-rate preferred equity from crypto-holding firms, chiefly Strategy's STRC, trades close enough to par to anchor a dollar. Pharos's latest reserve review puts most of the external backing in STRC exposure, after excluding issuer-held inventory and protocol-owned liquidity that holders cannot redeem against. June 2026 tested the bet: as Bitcoin fell, STRC traded below par and apxUSD followed it down, a move Apyx described as expected behavior for a preferred-equity-backed dollar. Pharos still records apxUSD in an active depeg, and the peg penalty holds the {{grade}} overall grade far below what the three pillars alone would earn; backing is the weakest of them. Wolf & Company's monthly examination covers the securities sleeve only, not the full reserve or apxUSD's redeemable liabilities. The durable constraint is that apxUSD's price tracks its collateral, so a discount on Strategy's preferred stock becomes a discount on the token.

jpyc-jpyc.title: The Yen's Licensed Pioneer
jpyc-jpyc.text: JPYC launched in October 2025 as Japan's first FSA-licensed yen stablecoin, issued by JPYC Inc. under a Type II Funds Transfer Service Provider license and backed by yen bank deposits and Japanese government bonds. Minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through the JPYC EX platform by bank transfer after KYC, and the tokens circulate on Ethereum, Polygon, Avalanche and Klaytn, where the issuer keeps direct freeze and transfer-restriction powers. Circulation remains modest against that regulatory head start. Exit and economic control are the stronger pillars on the card, with exit carried by the bank-rail redemption route. Backing is the weakest. The issuer states that deposits and JGBs cover at least 100% of issuance but publishes no dated split, instrument list or independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and the 80/20 bond-to-deposit mix the CEO has described is a target, not a measured allocation. Customer funds fall under Japan's statutory funds-transfer safeguarding rules, yet JPYC does not disclose which protection method it uses or with which providers. The peg record carries several recorded depeg events, and the peg adjustment trims the overall score further. SBI's trust-bank JPYSC still circulates only inside SBI VC Trade accounts, so public-chain circulation is the clearest difference between JPYC and its trust-bank rival. The durable constraint is reserve opacity: a licensed issuer whose holders take the backing split on its word.

xaut-tether.title: Allocated Gold Bars, Custodian Unnamed
xaut-tether.text: XAUT is Tether Gold's claim on LBMA Good Delivery bars vaulted in Switzerland, each token representing one fine troy ounce. The June 2026 BDO Italia reasonable-assurance report records 707,747 ounces against 707,747 XAUT outstanding, reconciled to the blockchain ledgers, and states that the gold is owned by the holders rather than by the issuer, with undivided rights in specified bars. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} is physical only: whole bars, a 430 XAUT minimum, delivery in Switzerland, through TG Commodities under El Salvador's CNAD licence. Pharos rates the card {{grade}} overall, with economic control the weakest of the three pillars: the XAUt0 representations on fourteen other chains all depend on a LayerZero lockbox on Ethereum, and Pharos cannot yet resolve how much supply sits behind each route. Backing scores higher but is held back by disclosure, since the report does not name the custodian, publish the custody agreement, prohibit rehypothecation, or test insolvency treatment. The token owner can block addresses and destroy blocked funds, and under MiCA Pharos records the asset as non-compliant. The durable constraint is that holders own the bars on paper while the custodian holding them stays unnamed.

paxg-paxos.title: Paxos's Allocated London Gold Token
paxg-paxos.text: PAXG is Paxos's gold token: one fine troy ounce of allocated LBMA Good Delivery gold per token, Brink's and ICBC Standard Bank vaulting in London, KPMG monthly examinations that reconcile redeemable tokens to ounces, and Paxos trust supervision. Backing leads the {{grade}} overall grade, with exit next and economic control the weakest pillar. Verified customers can take USD at a market quote or redeem physical bars from 430 PAXG, and since September 1, 2026 a tiered fee schedule charges rolling 30-day net redemptions. The issuer-direct mint path and centralized controls are still there: Paxos controller keys mint under rate limits, an immediate controller-manager key can add controllers and raise those limits, and the holder-freeze surface is live, although token upgrades now sit behind 24-hour timelocks. PAXG extended to Solana in June 2026, its first chain beyond Ethereum, but KPMG's August 2026 examination still counted more than 99% of redeemable tokens on Ethereum. The remaining gaps are the ones Paxos does not publish: the ounce split between the two vault providers and the LayerZero route details for the Ethereum-to-Solana path.

kau-kinesis.title: Gold Claim Behind a Two-Step Redemption
kau-kinesis.text: KAU on this page is KMS Labs' Ethereum ERC-20, backed 1:1 by Kinesis-native KAU held in a segregated reserve wallet, which in turn is backed by one gram of allocated physical gold in ABX vaults. The layering matters. The ERC-20 balance does not accrue the Kinesis transaction-fee yield that native KAU holders receive, and physical {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} takes two steps: back to native KAU through KMS Labs after compliance onboarding, then to bullion through Kinesis Cayman under platform terms. Bureau Veritas inspects the vaulted bullion behind native KAU twice a year, and Kinesis compares that balance with native KAU in circulation. KMS Labs publishes no equivalent reconciliation of ERC-20 supply against its native-KAU reserve wallet and names no independent digital-asset custodian, so backing scores well below what allocated gold would suggest. No score-eligible runtime redemption route is compiled, and an uncapped minter on the representation weighs on economic control. ABX vault {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} protects the metal, but KMS Labs' terms deny ERC-20 holders legal or beneficial title to the reserves, so their claim runs through KMS Labs first.

xaum-matrixdock.title: Asia-Vaulted Gold, Kilo-Bar Exit
xaum-matrixdock.text: Matrixdock's XAUm represents one troy ounce of LBMA-certified 99.99% gold, vaulted at Brink's in Hong Kong and Singapore and at Malca-Amit in Singapore. Bureau Veritas counted and weighed 508 kilo bars against the 30 June 2026 inventory list with no anomalies, but its certificate never mentions XAUm supply, so the bar-to-token match rests on Matrixdock's own disclosure. The terms add two qualifications a listing page omits: they permit unallocated gold held at a financial institution, with no current split disclosed, and they grant the issuer a security interest under an intercompany note. The token now runs on seven networks Pharos tracks, from Ethereum and BNB Chain to Sui, Solana and Stellar. Primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Matrixdock: holders can redeem for supported USD stablecoins after KYC, while physical pickup in Singapore or Hong Kong requires at least 32.148 XAUm, one kilo bar. Pharos has reviewed that physical route but cannot compile a score-eligible runtime route from it, which is why exit is the weakest pillar on a {{grade}} card. The constraint is the gap between a vault inspected twice a year and a token liability that no inspector reconciles.

cgo-comtech.title: DMCC-Stamped Bullion
cgo-comtech.text: CGO is ComTech Gold's tokenized gold from the UAE, one token per gram of 24-karat 999.9 fineness bullion held in segregated Transguard vaults, with bars registered on DMCC Tradeflow and the issuer licensed under DAFZA. Holders can redeem for physical gold through the ComTech app, but Pharos has reviewed that {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path only on paper: no score-eligible runtime route is compiled, so the exit pillar grades the documentation rather than an observed exit. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by the economic-control pillar, the weakest of the three. The sole XDC deployment is minted through a controller whose owner, executor, and minter roles all resolve to one 2-of-4 Safe with no cumulative cap, and reserve evidence consists of self-signed gold-stock letters with issuer DMCC screenshots rather than a third-party {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}; the newest routine custodian audit entry dates from March 2025. The peg record is the strongest line on the card, tracking gold over several years with a long tail of brief deviations. Dubai's clarity on {{term:rwa}}tokenized commodities{{/term}} is a real credential, but the governing {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} agreement and any rehypothecation prohibition remain unpublished, and until an independent reserve report appears the license carries more weight than the evidence.

dgld-gold-token-sa.title: PAMP-Refined Gold Token
dgld-gold-token-sa.text: DGLD is Gold Token SA's tokenized gold: one token per fine troy ounce of allocated LBMA Good Delivery PAMP bars in Swiss vaults, with the issuer's live registry mapping each chain's supply to named bar serials. The terms give holders Swiss-law co-ownership of the metal, {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} sits with MKS PAMP SA, and physical {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is offered from one gram with KYC. Verification is the weak side: the custodian has owned the issuer since the November 2025 relaunch, the registry is issuer-maintained, and no third-party audit is published. Exit is the weakest pillar because no score-eligible runtime route exists, and the {{grade}} overall grade also reflects issuer EOAs holding uncapped mint and proxy-admin roles on Ethereum and Base. In February 2026 the former Ethereum-to-Base bridge allowed phantom deposits and unbacked minting on Base; the path was frozen, balances were migrated one-for-one, and the bridge was closed in June. Thin single-source quotes have produced a long tail of peg deviations, one of them extreme, though the last 90 days are clean. For a {{term:rwa}}real-world asset{{/term}}, the backing can be checked no further than a custodian-owned issuer's own registry.

kag-kinesis.title: ERC-20 Silver Wrapper With Discretionary Redemption
kag-kinesis.text: KAG on this page is KMS Labs' Ethereum ERC-20, backed by Kinesis-native KAG, which is in turn backed by physical silver at one troy ounce per token. The ERC-20 terms name native KAG, not bullion, as the immediate reserve and deny holders title to it, so the silver sits two claims away. Bureau Veritas's April 2026 work is a commodity vault inspection under agreed-upon procedures, scoped to assets only and expressing no opinion. It counts metal against vault records. The comparison of tokens to silver appears only in the issuer's cover letter, signed by a party who heads both Kinesis and the vault operator ABX, so Pharos records no independent liability reconciliation. Backing scores below the middle of the range, and exit is weaker still. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} to native KAG is at KMS Labs' discretion after compliance onboarding, with no guaranteed availability or processing time, and physical silver then follows Kinesis Cayman's terms. The ERC-20 also earns none of the Kinesis transaction-fee yield paid on native balances. Against the silver reference, Pharos has recorded a long run of depeg events. The durable constraint is that the holder's path to metal runs through KMS Labs' discretion first.

eurq-quantoz.title: A DNB-Licensed Euro on a Thin Tape
eurq-quantoz.text: EURQ is Quantoz Payments' MiCA-authorised euro e-money token, issued by a Dutch EMI supervised by DNB and redeemable 1:1 through the issuer. The transparency page's latest snapshot reports about two thirds of reserves in Dutch and German government bonds and one third in cash at Tier 1 European banks, with a reserve ratio slightly above 100% and one percentage point left unclassified. That {{term:attestation}}disclosure{{/term}} is self-published and static, names neither the banks nor the bond identifiers, and says nothing about the active custodian set or replacement arrangements.  The tape adds a warning the paperwork does not: with a single-source price feed and thin trading across Ethereum, Polygon, XRPL and Algorand, EURQ has logged a handful of depeg episodes, including a double-digit discount in mid-2026. What Pharos can see is a regulated claim with a reserve statement that stops short of proof and a secondary market too thin to hold par under pressure.

deuro-deuro.title: The Oracle-Free Euro
deuro-deuro.text: DEURO is a decentralized euro stablecoin minted from overcollateralized crypto positions, using Frankencoin-style auctions instead of price oracles. Each {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} position carries an owner-set {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} price that anyone can challenge in an auction, trading capital efficiency for resistance to oracle manipulation. Roughly 85% of recorded position collateral is WFPS, the wrapped Frankencoin pool share, with WBTC most of the rest, so dEURO's {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} depends on Frankencoin protocol equity behind a wrapper that can block unwrapping. The core Ethereum contract is immutable, and new minting modules face a 14-day window in which a 2% nDEPS minority can veto them. The Polygon representation, a small slice of supply, can be upgraded by a 5-of-9 Safe with no timelock. One account holds a majority of aged votes, and existing hub settlement paths can mint to cover a reserve shortfall without a fresh veto window. Exit grades almost as low because the bridges to EURC and other euro tokens pay out assets Pharos cannot value at the same notional. Backing is the strongest pillar, yet most of that collateral is another protocol's equity.

cetes-etherfuse.title: Mexican Treasury Bills, Accruing in Pesos
cetes-etherfuse.text: CETES is Etherfuse's tokenized claim on Mexico's short-term {{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}}: zero-coupon federal debt with maturities set at government auctions, held in segregated INDEVAL {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} through participating brokerages. The token accretes in MXN rather than holding a fixed price, and subscription and redemption run through Etherfuse at current NAV behind KYC. Holders therefore carry three dependencies at once: the BBB- sovereign, the issuer and, for anyone measuring in dollars, the peso, whose moves never appear in the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}} headline. The reserve side is well evidenced. BHR México publishes monthly reasonable-assurance {{term:attestation}}examinations{{/term}} that fully reconcile assets against liabilities. Circulation is the open question. The token runs on five chains from Solana to Stellar, and Pharos holds it in quarantine because the issuer's mint totals and positive CoinGecko data disagree on MXN versus USD denomination and on which supply counts as circulating. Live scoring stays withheld until identity-bound pricing and a double-count-safe multichain census agree, which leaves the backing easier to verify than the float.

zarp-zarp.title: Rand Cash Reserve With an Uneven Peg
zarp-zarp.text: ZARP is a South African rand stablecoin minted and burned 1:1 against rand through ZARP Stablecoin (Pty) Ltd's issuing partners, with reserves held only for redemption. The reserve is rand cash, nearly all of it in an Old Mutual Wealth trust account and the rest at Standard Bank. Kempen's report on the 30 September 2026 balances verified those accounts, and management's figures put the cash comfortably above circulating ZARP. Those reports are ISRS 4400 agreed-upon procedures that expressly give no assurance opinion, arrive on no fixed schedule, and leave bankruptcy remoteness and redemption settlement time unaddressed. That is why backing is the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card, below economic control and an exit pillar that leads it. The peg record is the other drag: ZARP has logged dozens of depeg events, including one deep excursion, and crossed thresholds again in the last 90 days, which pulls the overall score down. The issuer's site describes the South African crypto-asset service provider licence held through Inves Capital (Pty) Ltd as still pending. The durable constraint is that a well-funded rand reserve has not yet produced a steady secondary-market price.

syrupusdc-maple.title: Institutional Lending, Vaulted
syrupusdc-maple.text: Maple's syrupUSDC turns USDC into an ERC-4626 receipt for institutional lending. Maple's own disclosures state the token is not backed by USDC one-to-one and carries no redemption guarantee. Deposits fund overcollateralized fixed-rate loans plus supporting yield strategies held in a segregated portfolio, and value accrues through NAV. Withdrawals are served by a FIFO queue as liquidity becomes available; Maple's FAQ still cites 30 days, but its legal risk disclosure promises no maximum period. The Network Firm verifies loan collateral from custodian feeds, but only for syrupUSDC and syrupUSDT combined and without naming custodians or their allocations, so custody remains one of the backing pillar's weakest inputs. Economic control is the weakest of the three pillars, because the bridge controls behind syrupUSDC's deployments on other chains remain unresolved in Pharos's review. Exit sits between the two. No ceiling binds the card, so the {{grade}} overall grade is the plain weighted verdict of its own pillars. A private-credit book denominated in someone else's dollar carries two credit stories: the USDC dependency is scored from independent data, while borrower performance inside the pool rests on Maple's own disclosure.

syrupusdt-maple.title: Maple's USDT Lending Vault
syrupusdt-maple.text: syrupUSDT is Maple's USDT counterpart to syrupUSDC, built on the same machinery: an ERC-4626 vault feeding {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} fixed-rate institutional loans, supported by futures basis trading and DeFi liquidity provision, with exits served by a FIFO queue as liquidity becomes available. Nearly all of the vault sits in deployed positions, and Maple publishes no current split among those three strategies. Lender recourse runs only against a ring-fenced segregated portfolio. Issuance is canonical on Ethereum; Plasma, BNB Chain, Mantle and Ink carry Chainlink CCIP lock-mint claims on shares escrowed in one Ethereum pool. Those bridge controls remain unresolved in Pharos's review, which makes economic control the weakest of the three pillars. Backing scores highest, helped by The Network Firm's collateral verification, although that dashboard covers syrupUSDC and syrupUSDT together and does not reconcile reserves to syrupUSDT's own liabilities. No ceiling binds the card, so the {{grade}} overall grade is the weighted verdict of those pillars. The durable constraint is the queue: a dollar exit depends on liquidity Maple can free from loans and strategies, on no guaranteed timeline.

yousd-yield-optimizer.title: A USDC Aggregator Whose NAV Carries Venue Losses
yousd-yield-optimizer.text:
A USDC-only yield aggregator on Base whose NAV moves with strategy outcomes rather than tracking a fixed dollar claim.

YO Protocol's yoUSD automates what DeFi power users do manually: rebalancing USDC across 50+ yield sources on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and Unichain, ranked by risk scores with per-pool and per-protocol concentration caps. That diversification still leaves holders exposed to venue and allocator risk, which is why backing is the weakest of the three pillars on the {{grade}} card while exit and economic control both grade near the top. The March 22 2026 Resolv exploit produced a reported ~2.95% yoUSD drawdown through Resolv-linked exposure, a useful reminder that NAV-appreciating tokens can also absorb strategy losses. Instant redemptions run only up to the vault's liquidity buffer, and larger withdrawals can take up to a day while cross-chain positions unwind. The durable constraint is that the yield and the losses come from the same set of venues, and both flow through the NAV.

ustb-superstate.title: Invesco's Tokenized T-Bill Fund
ustb-superstate.text: USTB is a tokenized short-duration government-securities fund managed by Invesco and held at BNY Mellon, structured as a private fund open only to qualified purchasers and accredited investors. The share price accrues with daily NAV rather than maintaining a fixed dollar, and qualified purchasers subscribe or redeem in USD or USDC on business days. Public holdings, daily NAV disclosure, and institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} make the underlying {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} exposure unusually legible; the restricted investor base makes open DEX liquidity beside the point. Pharos reserve data also places USTB inside the backing of other tracked tokens, including Midas's mTBILL, Frax's frxUSD, and the retired USDH, so its liquidity terms matter to those tokens as well. The same structure sets its weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card: beyond Superstate's own redemption window, Pharos maps no route that absorbs size at NAV, and instant USDC redemptions depend on available liquidity.

ousg-ondo-finance.title: Ondo's Qualified-Purchaser Treasury Share
ousg-ondo-finance.text: OUSG is Ondo's tokenized U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} fund share: a NAV-accreting token whose price has compounded far above a dollar rather than a pegged coin, restricted to U.S. Qualified Purchasers with on-chain KYC enforcement, so tokens cannot transfer to non-whitelisted addresses. The portfolio is no longer a BUIDL proxy. Ondo's October 2026 position table puts close to half the fund in State Street's Galaxy SWEEP and about a third in BlackRock BUIDL, with Franklin BENJI and Fidelity FYOXX behind them and small USDC and bank-deposit sleeves, so {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} exposure now spans four managers. Backing is the strongest pillar behind the {{grade}} overall grade, but its evidence is limited because not every fund in the book maps to a rated upstream dependency. Ondo I LP is audited annually by BPM LLP. NAV Consulting administers the fund, yet the daily administrator financials Ondo says it publishes sat behind a Google sign-in when Pharos checked in October 2026. Instant {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via OUSGInstantManager against USDC gives eligible holders an on-chain exit at daily NAV. Eligibility is the durable constraint: that USDC route reaches only onboarded Qualified Purchasers.

slvon-ondo.title: Silver ETF Rails
slvon-ondo.text: SLVon is Ondo Global Markets' tokenized exposure to the iShares Silver Trust, tracked as a {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} NAV asset rather than a $1 stablecoin. The token gives eligible non-U.S. investors economic exposure to SLV on Ethereum, BSC, Solana, and HyperEVM, with Ondo handling the issuer, subscription, and redemption infrastructure. The useful feature is composability for a listed ETF; the tradeoff is that holders own an Ondo GM token, not direct ETF shares or physical silver. Risk therefore lives in the Ondo GM legal structure, collateral attestations, access controls, and secondary-market liquidity.

iauon-ondo.title: Gold ETF Rails
iauon-ondo.text: IAUon is Ondo Global Markets' tokenized exposure to the iShares Gold Trust, modeled as a {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} NAV asset rather than a dollar stablecoin. It is gold-linked through the underlying IAU ETF exposure, with no direct claim on allocated bullion and no direct rights in the ETF shares themselves. Ondo's issuer rails make that exposure portable across Ethereum, BSC, Solana, and HyperEVM, while eligibility restrictions and issuer controls remain central to the risk profile. Primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is open only to eligible onboarded investors and pays out in USDon, with conversion to USDC depending on swapper liquidity and whitelist access. The reserve evidence is pooled: Ankura Trust's daily reports reconcile Ondo Stocks, USDY and USDon collateral in aggregate, without IAUon-specific shares, cash or liabilities. Pharos's report card currently shows {{grade}}, because critical evidence on the cross-chain route and control identities is insufficient for a rating. The cleanest way to read IAUon is as tokenized listed-security exposure that borrows stablecoin-style settlement infrastructure, and the durable constraint is that its backing cannot yet be separated from Ondo's wider book.

mtbill-midas.title: USTB-led Treasury exposure through Midas
mtbill-midas.text: mTBILL is Midas's NAV-linked {{term:treasury}}Treasury-bill{{/term}} certificate, rather than a fixed-dollar payment token. The issuer's October 16, 2026 portfolio checkpoint reports mainly Superstate's USTB, a smaller BlackRock BUIDL position and an unclassified remainder. The SAVE registry anchors a signed portfolio date and aggregate value, while the historical issuer API supplies the named positions. This binding does not independently verify each holding, {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} allocation or the full liabilities. The July 2026 final terms name Ankura Trust Company LLC as security agent. Midas describes daily NAV and collateral-eligibility monitoring, but Pharos holds no dated examiner-signed report covering full holdings and liabilities. Pharos therefore treats the composition as issuer-reported evidence, without independent financial-assurance credit. The final terms specify USDC settlement with {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} gates and possible holdbacks. Holders have a claim on the issuer rather than direct ownership of the underlying fund assets. Realizing the Treasury exposure still depends on issuer settlement and fund liquidity; publishing a checkpoint does not establish immediately available redemption capacity.

rusd-reservoir.title: Reservoir's Base Dollar
rusd-reservoir.text: rUSD is the non-yielding base asset under Reservoir's savings tokens. It mints and redeems 1:1 against USDC, USDT, or USD1 through the protocol's {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}, while the balance sheet behind it is deployed into lending markets and credit strategies. The live reserve feed makes that stack visible. Pharos's late-September 2026 review put the largest shares in USDC positions and in USD1 and AUSD lending markets, with smaller GHO lending, a PYUSD deposit in Sentora's PRIME lending vault, and a small carry-vault holding. The permissionless PSM makes exit the strongest of rUSD's three pillars. The {{grade}} overall grade is instead set by a cap for economically unbounded minting: the PSM and the Credit Enforcer share one Reservoir admin EOA. Economic control is the weakest pillar, with bridge routes and control identities still unresolved across the bridged deployments. Reserves sit in protocol-controlled adapters with no third-party custodian or bankruptcy-remote structure, and reserve re-use is the yield model. The {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} promise therefore depends on upstream stablecoin issuers, DeFi venues, and one admin key rather than a cash account.

wsrusd-reservoir.title: Reservoir's rUSD Savings Wrapper
wsrusd-reservoir.text: wsrUSD is Reservoir's non-rebasing ERC-4626 savings wrapper over rUSD: depositing burns rUSD, withdrawing mints it back, and the share price rises as protocol yield accrues, so the token trades above a dollar by design. Its only direct reserve is that rUSD claim, verified from the wrapper's constructor and pinned contract reads; the T-bill, lending-vault, and basis strategies behind it live on the rUSD entry and are inherited rather than duplicated. That inheritance is the trade-off. Upstream rUSD reserves are actively re-deployed into lending markets and credit, no bankruptcy-remote structure is documented for holders, and rUSD {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is immediate only up to available {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} liquidity. The {{grade}} overall grade is held at the parent cap, because a child cannot rate above rUSD, and economic control is the weakest pillar since Pharos cannot yet resolve the supply share behind each bridge route. The wrapper contract is immutable, but its manager role sits with a 3-of-5 Safe that an admin EOA can still reassign, and all but one of its tracked deployments are {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} representations, mostly LayerZero OFTs. The durable constraint is that wsrUSD carries every rUSD risk plus its own bridge and liquidity dependencies.

dusd-alto.title: Isolated Markets, Mostly Credit-Line Supply
dusd-alto.text: DUSD is Alto's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style dollar on Ethereum, minted through isolated markets for frxUSD, ETH and liquid staking tokens, sUSDe and Syrup USDC, with fixed-price USDC and frxUSD stability routes beside them. Those isolated markets carry only a small share of the float. Pharos's minter census reconciles most of the supply to a single Convex credit line whose collateral is a Curve LP of frxUSD and DUSD itself, so part of the backing is the coin's own liability. Among the issuance-path slices Pharos could measure, frxUSD dominates, which ties DUSD to Frax and keeps it classed as centralized-dependent. No complete reserve composition is published, so the backing pillar carries a reserve-evidence gap. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down hardest by economic control: the timelock owner can admit any minter and raise ceilings without token-level collateral checks. The peg record is clean over less than a year of tracking, on a small float. The durable constraint is backing that leans on Frax and on DUSD's own LP, behind a mint gate one timelock can widen.

dusd-dtrinity.title: Chain-Isolated Reserves, Unpublished Weights
dusd-dtrinity.text: dUSD is dTRINITY's dollar stablecoin, minted atomically 1:1 against whitelisted reserve stablecoins and yieldcoins such as USDC, USDT, sUSDS and sfrxUSD, and redeemed for a fee of up to 50 bps. Curve {{term:amo}}AMOs{{/term}} pre-mint dUSD into pools, and buyback operations retire it when it trades at a discount. Each deployment on Ethereum, Fraxtal, Katana and Sonic keeps its own isolated reserve with no cross-chain collateral sharing. The protocol exposes eligible assets and vault accounting, but no dated attestation and no weighted reserve table across chains; on Ethereum the vault is dominated by AMO accounting receipts rather than itemised Curve legs, so backing is graded on an undisclosed composition. Six contracts hold minter roles across the four tokens, the token has no supply cap, and Sonic's proxy admin sits under a 2-of-4 Safe with no timelock. Emergency pause roles can halt all transfers of the Ethereum, Sonic and Fraxtal tokens. The peg score stays high despite a long tail of brief episodes, and the binding terms disclaim any fiduciary, custodian or recovery obligation to holders. Until dTRINITY publishes a reconciled reserve balance sheet, that gap is the constraint.

sdusd-dtrinity.title: The dUSD Lender Receipt
sdusd-dtrinity.text: sdUSD is dTRINITY's yield-bearing wrapper for dUSD deposits in dLEND, so the token is best read as liquid dUSD lender exposure rather than a separate reserve asset. The wrapper is chain-isolated like dUSD itself: Ethereum sdUSD and Fraxtal sdUSD use separate deployments and are not fungible across chains. Yield comes from dLEND supply APY and accrues through the vault's NAV, while exits depend on available dUSD liquidity in dLEND or secondary-market depth. The important dependency is direct: sdUSD inherits dUSD reserve, peg, exploit, and dLEND bad-debt risk, and the report card cannot rate it above its parent. The wrapper adds a control risk of its own. On Ethereum, the timelock holding the vault's admin role can swap in a new router, and that router can mint shares without checking that any dUSD arrived. That makes economic control the weakest pillar on its {{grade}} card.

thbill-theo.title: Treasury Basket, Weights Undisclosed
thbill-theo.text: thBILL is Theo's NAV-accreting tokenized Treasury product. Its reserve is a basket of two institutional funds, Wellington/Libeara ULTRA and Fidelity International FILQ, held through tokenized wrappers, with Theo managing the allocation and publishing no current weights. FILQ may hold asset-backed commercial paper as well as government securities, and holders have no claim on the underlying fund units, so Pharos treats the basket as an opaque fund-share exposure rather than direct T-bill ownership.  Governance upgrades on the Ethereum vault sit behind a two-day timelock, but the accepted tULTRA receipt lets Theo's service router and a delegated signing account issue shares before underlying assets arrive, and that path has no timelock. Backing sits just above it, because the composition is missing and no dated basket-to-supply reconciliation is published. Mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are KYC-gated and limited to institutional and non-U.S. accredited investors, and Theo's own sources disagree on whether redemption settles T+0 or T+1. LayerZero carries the token to four other chains. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects institutional underlying assets behind disclosure that stops one layer above them, and a mint path that does not wait for them.

thusd-theo.title: A Dollar Running a Gold Carry Trade
thusd-theo.text: thUSD is Theo's non-yield-bearing dollar token, backed mainly by a managed, hedged gold-carry book, with thBILL as the smaller reserve leg and little USDC/USDT liquidity. Gold leasing, short CME futures and Treasury margin expose the backing to lease credit, futures basis and margin risk, and the dashboard reports the carry position only as an aggregate. Only sthUSD earns yield. Theo's reserve dashboard is issuer-run; independent aggregate assurance remains unfinished. Whitelisted depositors sign Theo's quoted USDC/USDT orders, which a privileged minter submits, and the contract does not enforce exact 1:1 pricing. The minter contract stops a mint from exceeding the collateral deposited, but the token itself checks only that the caller is the registered minter. Pharos's October 2026 review found that the timelocked owner, run by Theo's 4-of-6 Safe, can install a replacement minter with no collateral check; the two-day delay slows that change without bounding it. Economic control is therefore the weakest of the three pillars behind the {{grade}} overall grade, with backing close behind. The Guardian can pause minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} instantly. Primary redemption remains issuer-gated, fee-bearing and capped per block, with payouts dependent on the Cash Wallet. Without a published processing SLA or full-supply liquidity bound, holders cannot establish how quickly the managed reserves can become spendable stablecoins.

thgold-theo.title: One-Ounce Gold Token Backed by Leased Metal
thgold-theo.text: thGOLD is Theo's tokenized gold, deployed on Ethereum on September 15 2026, and its design has shifted since the January 27 2026 announcement. That post framed it as a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} share tracking the MG999 Onchain Gold Fund, a Singapore sub-fund run by FundBridge Capital with Libeara tokenization that lends gold to retailers and already backs thUSD's gold carry. Theo's current documentation instead makes one thGOLD one troy ounce of physical gold that never rebases or accrues. Lease income goes only to stakers in a separate sthGOLD vault with a 5-day exit lockup. Staking sets lease tenor and income rights, yet Theo may lend all thGOLD backing to institutional lessees, so holders who never stake still carry lease-counterparty and recall risk without the income. A 4-of-6 operator Safe holds the sole minter role, and a Timelock owns the upgradeable contracts. Direct mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} against metal are still marked coming soon, so the token is obtainable only on secondary venues. With no public price feed on record, Pharos keeps thGOLD pre-launch. Until redemption opens, nothing on record shows how quickly a holder could turn a token back into a recalled ounce.

usdp-parallel.title: Parallelizer Basket Dollar
usdp-parallel.text: Parallel USDp is minted and burned at oracle value against a governed basket of other stablecoins through the Parallelizer, a licensed fork of Angle's Transmuter. The accepted list spans frxUSD and sfrxUSD, USDe and sUSDe, USDS and sUSDS, and USDC, including a ygamiUSDC vault on Avalanche, with composition and exposure limits set by sPRL holders. Pharos reads the backing live from the four Parallelizer contracts, and it has leaned on yield-bearing wrappers, chiefly sfrxUSD and sUSDe, rather than their base dollars. Each of those carries its own issuer, custody, and strategy risk, so USDp's backing is a stack of other protocols' assumptions. Adaptive fees widen when collateral depegs. Economic control is the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card: Parallel's 5-of-8 Safes administer the minting role and can change mint-critical diamond logic without a configured delay.

usdpt-western-union.title: Western Union's Settlement Dollar
usdpt-western-union.text: USDPT is Western Union's on-chain dollar for agent and treasury settlement. Anchorage Digital Bank issues it on Solana, and Deloitte examines the reserve every month against the redeemable-token liability. The latest examination puts about four-fifths of the reserve in money-market funds identified only by CUSIP and the rest in demand deposits, most of them above the FDIC insurance limit, with a small surplus over tokens outstanding. The launch use case was B2B agent settlement, starting in the Philippines and Bolivia. The consumer leg followed on August 4, 2026, when Western Union and Rain launched Stablecard in 37 markets: a USDPT wallet paired with a USDPT-backed Visa secured credit card that receives Western Union transfers and spends wherever Visa is accepted. On-chain circulation is still small next to that network. On the card, reserve quality scores near the top of the class while exit is the weakest of the three pillars by a wide margin, because the only measured route is an issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} gated to eligible parties and slow to settle. The Solana mint also carries a freeze authority and a permanent delegate that can move or burn any holder's balance. Stablecard widens where USDPT can be spent, but holders outside the eligible set still have no exit route that Pharos measures.

roughrider-bnd.title: A State Bank's Permissioned Settlement Coin
roughrider-bnd.text: Roughrider Coin is the Bank of North Dakota's dollar-backed token for moving money between the state's banks and credit unions, and it is designed to stay inside that network. On October 1 2026 Fiserv put its digital asset platform into production with Roughrider as the first use case. VersaBank USA issues the token and manages custody and reserves, Fireblocks supplies the infrastructure, and transactions settle on Solana. On October 5 the state bank named Gate City Bank, First International Bank & Trust, Capital Credit Union and North Star Community Credit Union as its first pilot partners. Participation is voluntary, limited to approved institutions, and expands in phases with no end date. The public and merchants cannot hold the coin, so there is no market price or circulating supply for Pharos to track. Pharos therefore keeps it in the pre-launch registry while it runs as a bank-to-bank settlement pilot. The durable constraint is access: the coin circulates only among approved institutions, and no public or merchant route has been announced.

fiusd-fiserv.title: Fiserv's Stablecoin After the Partner Pivot
fiusd-fiserv.text: FIUSD is Fiserv's planned dollar stablecoin for the roughly 10,000 financial institutions and six million merchant locations already on its processing network. The June 2025 plan built it on Solana with Paxos and Circle infrastructure and promised it by the end of that year. That plan no longer stands. On October 5 2026 Fiserv's head of embedded finance said the company had pivoted away from Paxos and Circle toward a more proprietary coin, and he gave no launch date. Fiserv joined the Open USD consortium in September and says it will name wallet partners before year-end. Its digital asset platform went live on October 1, yet the first token it hosts is Bank of North Dakota's Roughrider Coin, which VersaBank issues and custodies. Neither the end-2025 target nor the July 2026 go-live set by former CEO Mike Lyons produced a launch; the Q2 results did not mention FIUSD, and his successor left it out of a September strategy presentation. Pharos therefore tracks FIUSD as a product whose issuer, reserve custodian and timetable are all unannounced, sitting on infrastructure that already runs another bank's coin.

gelt-tether.title: Georgia's Lari, Tether's Rails
gelt-tether.text: GEL₮ is Tether's pre-launch Georgian Lari stablecoin, announced on May 25, 2026 alongside the Government of Georgia and framed by Tether as the country's official stablecoin. The framing is the story: a government placing its national currency on a private issuer's digital rails, while the National Bank of Georgia runs a separate digital-lari pilot. The legal scaffolding is real. NBG Order No. 52/04 lets licensed issuers mint Lari-pegged tokens with prior NBG consent, 100% reserves, full redemption rights and a GEL 500,000 capital floor, and was built for compatibility with the US GENIUS Act. Everything an assessment needs is still blank: no chains, no contracts, no reserve {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, no named {{term:custody}}custodian{{/term}}, no launch date, and no milestone recorded since the announcement. The prime minister and the central bank's governor have both endorsed it, but Pharos cannot yet price the Lari peg. Until reserve disclosures appear, the 'official' label describes political sponsorship rather than how the tokens will be backed.

eur-qivalis.title: Thirty-Seven Banks, One Euro
eur-qivalis.text: Qivalis is a consortium of 37 banks across 15 countries preparing a euro stablecoin, and De Nederlandsche Bank granted it electronic money institution authorisation in October 2026. Its members include BNP Paribas, ING, UniCredit, BBVA, ABN Amro, Intesa Sanpaolo, Rabobank and Nordea, which makes this the euro banking sector's own bid for a MiCA electronic money token. The planned reserve puts at least 40% in bank deposits and the remainder in short-term euro-area sovereign bonds spread across EU countries, with 24/7 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} promised. The stated plan is Ethereum first, using the Fireblocks ERC-20F standard with built-in allowlist and denylist controls and a permissioned KYC layer, then Polygon and Base; the September 2026 Ethereum confirmation came through secondary reports rather than a Qivalis press release. The licence clears the regulatory gate, but issuance still waits on the remaining MiCA requirements and a published white paper, and Qivalis has published neither a ticker nor a launch date. Until then, reserves, {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and redemption rights remain pre-launch commitments.

pusd-polaris.title: Pre-Launch pETH CDP Dollar With Earn Pool Yield
pusd-polaris.text: USDp (formerly pUSD) is Polaris's pre-launch Liquity-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin on Ethereum, minted against pETH collateral at a 115% minimum collateral ratio. Polaris's documentation describes an immutable core with no admin privileges and no freeze or blacklist function. A bounded Stewardship role still sits above it: Stewardship can change interest rate splits and flow recipients and replace faulty oracle feeds, and its decisions run through sPOLAR (formerly vePOLAR) stakers with no timelock disclosed. The {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} angle comes from inside the protocol. USDp deposited in the Earn Pool absorbs liquidations and earns a share of minter interest plus pETH liquidation gains, so each liquidation converts part of a deposit's dollars into ETH exposure. Holder yield therefore tracks borrowing demand and liquidation activity rather than Treasury rates. A public testnet runs on Sepolia, the app is labelled Alpha, and Polaris's docs say no production addresses, audit status or launch status can be inferred from testnet values. Polaris's former roadmap placed professional audits ahead, and a $1M angel round reported in September 2026 came without a mainnet date. Until mainnet contracts and audits exist, USDp's design claims cannot be checked against deployed code.

pgold-polaris.title: Synthetic Gold Minted Against pETH
pgold-polaris.text: GOLDp (formerly pGOLD) is Polaris's pre-launch synthetic gold token: borrowers post pETH collateral in {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}} and mint GOLDp debt that tracks one troy ounce of gold by oracle, at a 115% minimum collateral ratio. There is no physical gold, vault or custodian behind it, which separates it from bullion-claim tokens whose value rests on an issuer's metal and redemption desk. The design swaps custody risk for market risk: positions are collateralized in ETH-derived pETH while the debt tracks gold, so solvency depends on the ETH price relative to gold. Exit runs through Polaris redemption and liquidation mechanics rather than bullion delivery. GOLDp shares its Sepolia testnet with sibling USDp; the app is labelled Alpha, professional audits are still ahead, and no mainnet date is set. A $1M angel round reported in September 2026 came without one. Until contracts and an oracle configuration are deployed, the design's gold tracking and liquidation behaviour cannot be checked against live code.

usg-tangent.title: Productive Collateral, Dynamic Rates
usg-tangent.text: Tangent Finance built USG as an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin for productive DeFi collateral: Curve LP tokens, Pendle PTs and other {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} positions, with current exposure tied heavily to stablecoin LP routes, including USDC-paired pools. The peg design skips {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}; Peg Keepers, price-dependent interest and reward deductions tighten as USG weakens, pushing borrowers to repay. Most of the headline supply is protocol inventory. On October 19, 2026 the two peg-keeper contracts each held 20 million preminted USG, about nine-tenths of totalSupply, and Pharos counts only the circulating remainder.  A 3-of-5 Safe owns the token, can mint uncapped USG into either peg keeper and can appoint new minters, all without a timelock. The product remains in disclosed beta, with five audit reports referenced in its docs. Its one recorded discount reached about two percent, and the live record still marks that event as active. Because the collateral is DeFi-native, USG inherits the risk of every protocol whose tokens it accepts, with a {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} surface only as deep as each underlying market.

klarnausd-klarna.title: KlarnaUSD testnet stablecoin on Tempo
klarnausd-klarna.text: Klarna's planned USD stablecoin is built on Stripe's Bridge Open Issuance infrastructure for the Tempo L1, and it remains on Tempo's testnet. The November 2025 announcement targeted a mainnet launch in 2026 and cited a base of 114 million customers and $118 billion in annual GMV; no launch date has followed. Tempo's mainnet went live on March 18, 2026 with a Machine Payments Protocol aimed at AI-agent payments and launch partners including Anthropic, Mastercard, Visa and Revolut; Klarna was not among them. World Liberty Financial's USD1 became Tempo's first native stablecoin on May 8. The regulatory groundwork is further along than the product: Bridge received a conditional OCC national bank trust charter in February 2026 that would let it {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} crypto assets, issue stablecoins and manage reserves as a federally regulated entity. Reserve composition, {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} terms remain unpublished pending mainnet. Since the announcement, Klarna's Q1 and Q2 2026 earnings, Stripe Sessions 2026 partner announcements and Bridge's live issuer list have all omitted KlarnaUSD.

trusd-tori.title: Tori's Delta-Neutral Synthetic Dollar
trusd-tori.text: trUSD is Tori Finance's run at the playbook Ethena popularized: a synthetic dollar backed by {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} trading positions ({{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} arbitrage, calendar spreads, hedged money markets) with a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} staked wrapper, strUSD. Launch sequencing put Sherlock and Nethermind audits came before deployment, Accountable's real-time proof-of-solvency started on day one, Nexus Mutual covered the pre-deposit vault, and the $50M pre-deposit cap filled in seven days. Accountable's dashboard splits the reserve into a few buckets led by hedged money-market positions, and Pharos treats that split as verified. The open questions are the classic synthetic-dollar ones. Primary NAV mint and redeem are KYC-whitelisted in the contract itself, so the 'no verification' marketing refers only to secondary swaps. The custodian banks holding most of the attested backing are unnamed by policy, and independent tracing of the sole custodian wallet shows collateral flowing to exchange deposit addresses. Tori's BVI terms make repurchase discretionary and keep the reserves as company property. Mint and redemption quotes are set by Tori's own backend with no on-chain price feed, which leaves economic control as the weakest of the three pillars, with backing close behind. Together they hold the {{grade}} overall grade low despite a peg that has held at par since launch. trUSD is Delphi-backed and single-entity operated, issued on Ethereum with small CCIP-bridged floats on Monad and Pharos, and its track record is still under six months.

ussd-sonic-labs.title: Branded Wrapper Over frxUSD
ussd-sonic-labs.text: Sonic Labs's USSD is a permissionless 1:1 wrapper around Sonic frxUSD: a BrandedCustodian contract on Sonic holds frxUSD against every USSD minted, so the reserve story belongs upstream to Frax. Minting carries no fee and the custodian's redemption fee reads zero, but holders earn nothing. Sonic Labs's March 2026 launch post says the yield on the backing assets is designed to flow back into the Sonic network, where it could support buybacks and ecosystem incentives. Holders unwrap USSD to frxUSD first; any further {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Frax or its authorized providers. That layering caps the {{grade}} card, because a binding rule keeps a wrapper from rating above the parent it requires. Pharos has not established a same-value route beyond the unwrap. On Sonic, the BrandedFactory and a terminal Safe authorize minters, set the mint cap and can upgrade the proxy immediately. Deployments on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism and Scroll are branded representations whose local custodians and LayerZero routes add bridge risk. A USSD holder carries Frax's reserve exposure plus Sonic's operational controls and earns none of the reserve's yield.

pgold-pleasing.title: Pleasing's Partly Assured Gold Token
pgold-pleasing.text: PGOLD is Pleasing's Hong Kong gold token: one PGOLD is intended to represent one troy ounce of LBMA-standard 99.99% bullion held with unnamed custodians, with KYC-gated physical {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through the Pleasing platform.
