Arbitrum is the only native issuance chain; Ethereum, Pharos, and ApeChain carry Chainlink CCIP and LayerZero representations. VISTO CPA's June 2026 assurance report physically counted about half of the claimed bullion, relied on shipping and issuer assertions for the rest, excluded weight, purity, and valuation, and covered only the Arbitrum liability. Nothing assures custody continuity after that date, and segregation, rehypothecation and insurance terms remain unresolved. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by the economic-control pillar, the weakest of the three: a single EOA can mint directly on Arbitrum, a separate EOA-owned ProxyAdmin can replace the mint logic with no delay, and the token owner runs a live per-address blacklist. The exit pillar is nearly as weak because physical redemption is documented but no score-eligible same-notional route exists. The bullion claim rests on one partial report and unnamed custodians, and the admin keys remain unbounded.

ggbr-goldfish-gold.title: Gold Token on a Mining Claim
ggbr-goldfish-gold.text: GGBR is Goldfish Gold's gold-tracking token, priced at 1/1000 of a troy ounce against the LBMA spot price and minted and redeemed through issuer-controlled contracts on Ethereum. The backing is where it parts company with XAUT or PAXG: the issuer's collateral disclosure describes 1,000,000 troy ounces of in-situ gold in the Happy 2 mining claims in Arizona, held by a GGBR Trust for holders. That is a claim on unmined ore. The issuer says an August 2026 restructuring replaced the earlier lease of an affiliate's ION.au tokens with this trust and named a trustee, but the trust deed, title records and geological report behind it are not public, and nobody independently attests the gold against token supply. Pharos scores the {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} as institutional and unregulated, with self-reported reserves only. A single issuer key mints through a factory whose reserve-verification checks are commented out, a 2-of-3 Safe can freeze any holder immediately, and a timelocked admin can blacklist or force-transfer balances. Exit is barely stronger, since physical redemption is described only through a KYC'd app with a high minimum and fees, and no score-eligible runtime route is compiled. The durable constraint is that the token references gold in the ground, and every link in the trust chain runs through Goldfish's own disclosures.

gldt-gold-dao.title: NFT Gold, Fungible Wrapper
gldt-gold-dao.text: GLDT is Gold DAO's fungible wrapper over GLD NFTs, each token standing for a hundredth of a gram of gold in Swiss vaults, minted when NFTs are locked in a swap canister on the Internet Computer and carried to Ethereum, Base, and Arbitrum through a single-operator lock-mint {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}. Gold DAO's own terms state that GLDT is not legal ownership of gold and that redemption is not guaranteed; a holder must first reverse-swap into a GLD NFT, which alone is described as a deed to a bar. The independent evidence trail stops in September 2025. KPMG SA Neuchâtel's report from that month is a Swiss Auditing Standard 920 report of factual findings, expressly neither an audit nor a review, that counted 7.9 kilograms of gold at a Loomis vault in Kloten and reconciled it to GLD NFT certificates issued by Bity Tokenisation; GLDT supply itself was not reconciled. The card now carries a {{grade}} overall grade, with the backing pillar drawing on Pharos's live read of the locked NFTs, but its assurance component is marked stale. Exit is the weakest pillar: physical pickup needs Bity KYC and a vault charge in Zurich, and no score-eligible runtime exit route is compiled. The durable constraint is evidence: the record shows gold counted against NFT certificates in 2025, never against the GLDT a holder actually holds.

axcnh-anchorx.title: AnchorX's Kazakh-Licensed Offshore Yuan
axcnh-anchorx.text: AnchorX's AxCNH is an offshore-yuan stablecoin issued under a license from Kazakhstan's AFSA, redeemable 1:1 for CNH through the issuer and described as backed by CNH cash at regulated financial institutions. The trust stack is almost entirely issuer-side: AnchorX handles minting, redemption and reserve reporting, and on Ethereum and Conflux a 3-of-4 multisig acts as master minter while separate owner and proxy-admin multisigs can replace it or the mint logic. Kreston's agreed-upon procedures report for June 30, 2026 matched CNH cash against tokens outstanding with a small excess, but it names no banks and no later report has been reviewed. Pharos therefore carries the whole reserve as an unresolved envelope. It has also not established the capacity, cost or settlement terms of the redemption route, which leaves exit as the weakest line. The evidence falls short of what a research rating requires, so Pharos does not rate AxCNH. The durable constraint is that holders rely on one issuer's account of a reserve that no current independent report describes.

idrt-rupiah-token.title: Rupiah Deposits Behind a Loose Peg
idrt-rupiah-token.text: Rupiah Token's IDRT is backed 1:1 by IDR bank deposits held by PT Rupiah Token Indonesia and issued natively on Ethereum, BSC, and Polygon, with a dormant legacy Harmony representation. The proof story has inched forward: the issuer now publishes monthly accountant-prepared AUP reports, a form of {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} that inspects bank statements without expressing assurance, and the August 2026 report reconciled bank collateral to circulating supply at 1:1 without naming the banks. Supply itself needed reconciling. In September 2026 Pharos restated IDRT's circulating supply to the contracts it can read, excluding an issuer-declared 40 billion tokens attributed to legacy BNB Beacon Chain and Luniverse ledgers that cannot be checked. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} remains institutional and unregulated, and the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path still depends on the issuer honoring KYC-gated fiat exits. The {{grade}} report card splits sharply: economic control is the strongest pillar because each active native token sits under a chain-local 4-of-6 Safe with the same six signers, while backing and exit are both weak on undisclosed bank custody and an eligibility-gated route out. The peg holds only loosely, with a long tail of recorded deviation events across a seven-year operating life. The durable constraint is that the reserve check covers balances, not the banks or the terms that hold them.

tryb-bilira.title: Quarterly Examined Lira Token
tryb-bilira.text: TRYB is BiLira's Turkish-lira stablecoin, tracked across nine deployments, with issuer-held TRY cash in Turkish bank accounts and centralized mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. Polygon carries a bridged lock-and-mint representation; the other deployments are the issuer's own. BiLira's reserve reports come from Corpus Denetim as a genuine examination with full asset-and-liability reconciliation, a stronger form of assurance than an agreed-upon-procedures letter. The August 2026 examination found lira balances exceeding tokens outstanding, and Pharos anchors composition to that examined date. The catch is cadence: on a quarterly cycle an honest examination goes stale between filings, so the backing pillar rises and falls with the calendar rather than with the reserve. The banks holding the cash are not named, and the auditor's notes on custody sit outside the assurance opinion. Exit is the weakest of the three pillars, because there is no comparable same-notional route out of the position beyond the issuer. The peg record adds a further drag, with a long tail of episodes measured on a low-volume fallback price source. Together they hold the {{grade}} overall grade down while economic control, run through 2-of-3 and 3-of-6 Safes, scores well. The durable constraint is that holders exit only through the issuer, against reserve evidence refreshed once a quarter.

ebusd-ebisu.title: Exotic Collateral, Orderly Exit
ebusd-ebisu.text: Ebisu's ebUSD was a Liquity V2-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with a mixed collateral basket: sUSDe, WBTC, LBTC, stcUSD and weETH in {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} branches deployed natively on Ethereum and Plasma. The market never showed up. Supply peaked near $815K and was below $25K when the team announced a wind-down on July 29, 2026: minting paused, users were asked to close Troves and pull Stability Pool and DEX deposits, and the frontend is slated for deprecation on October 30. Ebisu could not grow ebUSD liquidity enough to support meaningful borrowing activity. Collateral redemption stayed open throughout, so the ending was solvent, orderly and announced in advance.

usdaf-asymmetry.title: Immutable CDP, Recursive Collateral
usdaf-asymmetry.text: USDaf is an immutable Liquity V2 {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} minted against yield-bearing stablecoin and BTC collateral on Ethereum. The collateral stack is recursive by design: ysyBOLD, a Yearn position built on Liquity's BOLD, carries more than half the book, while tBTC, scrvUSD, sfrxUSD, sUSDS, and WBTC split the rest. BoldToken ownership is renounced, no admin can freeze a balance or register a new minter, and the six branches carry conservative {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}, so backing and economic control both score respectably. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by exit, the weakest of the three pillars. Supply is small enough that measured DEX depth covers only a sliver of Pharos's $100,000 exit test, and the permissionless {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route into collateral is not modeled as a same-notional exit, so the remaining routes share one failure domain. The peg record shows the same thinness: a long run of recorded depeg episodes, measured on a single price source with limited coverage. {{term:liquidation}}Liquidation{{/term}} mechanics and branch isolation inherit Liquity's design. The durable constraint is depth: immutable code cannot buy market liquidity, and until USDaf grows, sellers meet a thin pool, and redemption fees set no fixed price floor beneath it.

usnd-nerite.title: Immutable CDP, Broken Collateral Branch
usnd-nerite.text: Nerite's USND was a Liquity V2-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar on Arbitrum, built on immutable contracts with user-set interest rates, per-market Stability Pools, and permissionless {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} against collateral. The token's owner was renounced and only registered branch contracts could mint, so no individual could print USND or change which collateral markets existed. That removed admin risk, and with it the ability to respond. One approved branch accepted rsETH, and when the rsETH hack impaired that collateral, Nerite could not patch the market away or rewrite its risk controls. Supply fell from a peak near $2.7M to under $100K, and Pharos froze USND on May 10, 2026.

ftusd-flying-tulip.title: On-Chain Carry, Concentrated Control
ftusd-flying-tulip.text: ftUSD is Flying Tulip's non-yielding base dollar, minted and redeemed on-chain against supported stablecoins, while sftUSD is the optional wrapper that receives strategy yield. The reserve is not idle: deposits sit in Aave-based strategy wrappers that lend USDC and USDT and run borrow-and-stake carry, borrowing WETH into wstETH on Ethereum, wS into stS on Sonic and WBNB into asBNB on BNB Smart Chain, rather than hedging with short perpetuals. Yield attributable to unstaked ftUSD accrues to the protocol, an opportunity-cost transfer rather than a fee. Flying Tulip indexes the reserve feed itself, but the underlying wrapper balances are publicly verifiable on-chain. The {{grade}} overall grade comes from three closely bunched pillars, with economic control slightly the weakest: one 3-of-5 Safe with no timelock owns the token on Ethereum and Sonic and can admit new mint modules or lift debt ceilings, and core minting checks authorization, not posted collateral. The remaining risks are lending-venue, staking and liquidation exposure plus upstream USDC and USDT dependencies, all governed by that single key set.

brla-brla-digital.title: Avenia's Audited Real
brla-brla-digital.text: BRLA is Avenia's centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, minted and redeemed 1:1 for BRL after KYC and deployed natively on Polygon, Gnosis, Celo, and Moonbeam without wrapping or bridge dependencies. Most stablecoins help users leave a local currency for dollars; BRLA tokenizes the real for on-chain settlement instead. The reserve disclosure is detailed: UHY Bendoraytes issues monthly reasonable-assurance reports that itemize BRL cash across named Brazilian banks and payment institutions plus overnight repurchase agreements collateralized by corporate debentures, and reconcile the total against BRLA in circulation. That supports a backing pillar in the upper half of the card. The weak line is exit: on the {{grade}} card the exit pillar is the weakest of the three because no comparable secondary route is established for the supply, so the practical way out is Avenia's own redemption window. Issuance is issuer-direct on every chain, gated by an operator role held by Avenia keys and contracts, with blacklist and upgrade authority in the same hands. The native BRL peg record shows a handful of episodes since Pharos began native-quote monitoring in mid-2026. Exit, issuance, and upgrade authority all run through Avenia on every chain the token uses.

silk-shade-protocol.title: Basket-Pegged CDP on Secret Network
silk-shade-protocol.text: SILK is Shade Protocol's basket-pegged stablecoin on Secret Network: a governance-set basket of major currencies, gold and bitcoin, minted against {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} vaults in ShadeLend. Pharos's August 2026 registry read found nineteen vaults priced through one oracle router with a single default provider, no failover and an empty deviation-guard list. The finding that matters sits in the WBTC vault, second-largest at 18.3% of aggregate elastic debt. It is governance-frozen with about 37.9k SILK of debt against roughly 0.00002 WBTC of collateral, its {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} query reverts on a divide-by-zero, and its collateral staleness bound has been widened from the 600 seconds used elsewhere to a fourteen-digit number. Two derivative collateral oracles were also rejecting queries as stale, one since February 2025 and one since July 2026. No bad-debt socialization path is documented for a shortfall the Stability Pool cannot cover. Pharos has held SILK out of the active set since 18 August 2026, after its upstream circulating supply was understated roughly twelvefold from 5 August. By 19 October neither feed had recovered: CoinGecko's market data last updated on 17 August, and DefiLlama marks SILK dead from 1 September. Collateral identities and weights remain private on Secret Network, so the stranded WBTC debt cannot be checked against the rest of the book.

idrx-idrx.title: Rupiah Rails With Accountant Reports
idrx-idrx.text: IDRX is PT IDRX Indo Inovasi's rupiah stablecoin, backed 1:1 by IDR held across Indonesian bank deposits, balances at local exchanges and a payment firm, and an Indonesian government bond, with KYC-gated mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through the issuer. A September 2026 agreed-upon-procedures report from a registered public accountant itemised eight reserve balances slightly exceeding reported circulation, though it is explicitly not an audit opinion and its chain list does not establish full multichain liability coverage. Backing is nonetheless the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} report card, held back by where the money sits: more than two-thirds at a single bank, Bank Ina Perdana, with segregation and bankruptcy remoteness unestablished. Exit leads the card, with a permissionless route out. The control surface is centralized: minting is issuer-controlled through per-chain Safes, an ops key holds the admin role that can regrant minter and upgrader rights without delay, and the issuer runs its own burn-and-mint bridge across its deployments with no third-party validator. The peg record is close to spotless. The durable constraint is that every reconciliation runs through the issuer.

mxnb-juno.title: Peso Stablecoin, New Issuer Jurisdiction
mxnb-juno.text: MXNB is a 1:1 Mexican peso token deployed as the same FiatToken-style contract on Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base and Arc. Since April 8, 2026 it has been issued by Nvio Pagos El Salvador, S.A. de C.V., registered with El Salvador's CNAD as a stablecoin issuer, so the regulatory owner is no longer Mexican even though the reserves remain peso assets. The {{grade}} overall grade rests on economic control and exit, and on a peg record with a single recorded depeg episode. Backing is the weakest pillar because of what the reserve evidence leaves out. The quarterly BDO Mexico report is a valuation engagement with no assurance opinion: it shows one aggregate line of bank-account reserves above circulating supply, expressly does not confirm those balances with the banks, and does not name the banks holding them. Control is concentrated as well. Pharos reads the same owner and master-minter address on all six deployments, confirmed as an EOA on Ethereum, Arbitrum and Arc, where a second EOA administers the upgradeable proxy. The durable constraint is that a CNAD registration does not substitute for bank-confirmed reserves.

cjpy-yamato.title: ETH-Only Yen CDP
cjpy-yamato.text: CJPY is Yamato's decentralized JPY stablecoin, minted from ETH-only {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}s. The mechanism follows the Liquity v1 design: deposit ETH at 130% minimum collateralization, borrow CJPY with a one-time fee and no accruing interest, and use accumulated protocol fees to absorb underwater positions. Its {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route lets CJPY return one yen worth of ETH from the riskiest pledge, giving the peg an on-chain floor without a bank account. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by the economic-control pillar, the weakest of the three: upgrade authority over Yamato and CurrencyOS sits with a 2-of-4 Safe, and the already-bound CurrencyOS route can burn any holder's CJPY balance without allowance, so the design has no named blacklist but does have an operator with reach. The loss buffer is small: the fee-funded pool behind the subrogation path is a sliver of outstanding debt, so a sharp ETH drawdown leans on redeemers buying CJPY rather than on reserves.

usdkg-gold-dollar.title: Kyrgyz Gold Dollar, Ended by Cabinet Order
usdkg-gold-dollar.text: USDKG was a Kyrgyz Republic dollar token backed by physical gold, issued by the state-owned OJSC Virtual Asset Issuer with Gold Dollar operating the reserve. The backing was about 376 kilograms of gold bars, listed as LBMA Good Delivery, sourced from the Ministry of Finance through the state miner Kyrgyzaltyn and stored in sealed boxes at an unnamed bank under LLC Virelint Group's custody. The only reserve evidence was a November 2025 Kreston agreed-upon-procedures report that counted the bars but neither expressed an assurance opinion nor established Good Delivery certification, and the bank withheld the vault access log. On October 5, 2026, the issuer announced that issuance, circulation and blockchain operations would cease under a Kyrgyz Cabinet order that directed the issuer's liquidation. Holders were told to email the issuer to exchange tokens for fiat or USDT, with no published payout timeline. The issuer said it would consolidate and burn tokens and suspend the Ethereum and Tron contracts, whose 3-of-7 owner multisigs already controlled pause, blacklist and blacklisted-balance destruction. Completed burns and full holder repayment have not been established. Pharos preserves USDKG's market record as a frozen archive.

usdh-hermetica.title: A Stacks Dollar Backed by Tokenized Credit
usdh-hermetica.text: Hermetica's USDh is a synthetic dollar on Stacks. Its documentation still describes a BTC {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}}: spot bitcoin paired with short {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} futures, with the {{term:funding-rate}}funding{{/term}} paid to holders who stake into sUSDh. Hermetica's September 2026 report shows different holdings. About two thirds of backing sat in STRCx, a tokenized credit product with exposure to Strategy, Inc., held in a new Ethereum wallet, while the custodian Ceffu held nothing. Most of the rest sat with Copper as a mix of BTC, USDT, and USDC that the report does not break down, plus a small USDC reserve fund. One credit instrument carries different risks from a hedged bitcoin position, and the {{grade}} overall grade reflects that gap. Minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} require KYC through Hermetica's app on one chain, and the queued redemption path has no established cost or settlement terms. Backing evidence is limited because only Copper's share is independently attested and the report only partly matches assets to tokens outstanding. Economic control is held back by the risk engine that values the book: it may pause redemptions if its price feeds fail, and Pharos has not established which feeds those are. An active emergency-recovery contract also lets the protocol burn any holder's balance and re-mint it elsewhere. The peg has held over the tracking window, measured from a single price source. What backs USDh can change between monthly reports, and those reports are the only place holders can see it.

usdsc-startale.title: Startale's M0 Wrapper for Soneium
usdsc-startale.text: USDSC is Startale's 1:1 wrapper around M0's M, carrying the same short-term {{term:treasury}}Treasury-bill backing{{/term}}, Validator {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} and bankruptcy-remote SPV structure into the Soneium app ecosystem. The token is issued on Ethereum as an M0 extension, but its entire supply lives on Soneium, reached through M0's Portal over Hyperlane: holders unwrap, M crosses the bridge, and it is rewrapped on the other side. Each layer adds a control surface. A 3-of-5 Safe can replace the token's mint logic immediately, a freeze manager can lock individual holders, and the bridge route adds its own portal, adapter and validator dependencies. On the {{grade}} card, backing is the weakest pillar because it is simply M's own score, and the overall grade is capped at M's rating, since a wrapper cannot rate above the asset it wraps. The on-chain unwrap back to M is the strongest pillar. Any change in M's own rating passes straight through to USDSC's ceiling.

ctusd-citrea.title: Bitcoin's Dollar, MoonPay's Rails
ctusd-citrea.text: ctUSD is Citrea's native dollar, issued by MoonPay USA LLC on M0 infrastructure for a young Bitcoin ZK-rollup. Its direct backing is M0's base M token held by the ctUSD extension; Citrea describes the underlying reserves as cash and short-term {{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}}, and M0 Validators post on-chain {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} before minting. ctUSD cannot rate above its M parent, and that cap holds the {{grade}} overall grade, with backing the weakest of the three pillars. MoonPay's terms promise segregated reserve accounts but name no institutions, and Pharos has verified no ctUSD-specific SPV, insolvency instrument, or rehypothecation limit. MoonPay sells ctUSD through card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and PayPal rails. Par {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is open only to eligible onboarded MoonPay customers, and customers in the European Economic Area cannot buy or redeem directly. An active freeze manager can freeze any holder and force transfers, and a single externally owned account holds the token's upgrade key. The peg record is clean so far, but every route to par runs through MoonPay's onboarding.

usdat-saturn.title: PYUSD Underneath, Strategy Preferred Above
usdat-saturn.text: Saturn's USDat is a permissioned dollar token whose reserve changed in August 2026. It launched as an M0 extension backed by the M token; at Ethereum block 25789911 Saturn upgraded the proxy to a MultiMint implementation and wound the M reserve down to zero. The proxy now holds PYUSDx, the MoonPay-issued M0 token backed by PayPal USD, and fixed-block reads reconcile it exactly to USDat supply. The base token is therefore a serial claim on PYUSD, and Pharos's parent cap keeps it from rating above that asset. Backing carries a disclosure caveat: Saturn publishes a self-reported reserve dashboard rather than an independent reconciliation. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by economic control, the weakest of the three pillars, because the Chainlink CCIP representations on Monad and BNB carry bridge controls Pharos has not resolved, and Monad holds a large share of supply. The Strategy exposure sits one floor up in the sUSDat vault, which holds almost entirely STRCon, an Ondo structured note tracking Strategy's STRC preferred shares, behind a queued exit. USDat itself stays permissioned, with KYC-gated wrapping and compliance whitelist, freeze, and forced-transfer controls retained in the upgraded contract. The durable constraint is that base USDat is only as good as PYUSD, and the yield above it is only as good as Strategy's preferred.

usdk-orki.title: Stranded on a Dead Chain
usdk-orki.text: Orki's USDK brought Liquity V2-style CDP mechanics to Swellchain, minted against WETH, weETH, rswETH, and swETH. Branch assignments were locked at construction, no individual admin could mint, and collateral redemption was permissionless, though the token itself sat behind an upgradeable proxy. Swellchain closed its bridge-withdrawal window on June 23, 2026 and ended chain operations on June 30. USDK never had a verified deployment outside Swellchain, so Pharos now carries it as a frozen, abandoned single-chain CDP. Any remaining positions depend on direct contract access against a network that has wound down. The durable constraint was the host chain: USDK existed only on Swellchain, and it did not survive the network's shutdown.

usdq-quill.title: Scroll's Liquity Outpost
usdq-quill.text: Quill's USDQ deploys Liquity V2's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} blueprint on Scroll, with separate borrowing markets for wETH, wstETH, weETH and SCR, the host chain's own token. The SCR market, the design's most reflexive choice, has been permanently shut down since April 2026 and now holds only residual collateral. In practice the collateral book is almost entirely wstETH, so liquid-staking collateral is the real exposure, and the whole book is small. Each market prices off a single Chainlink feed with no alternate provider, and a feed failure shuts that market down for good. The {{grade}} overall grade follows the economic-control pillar, the weakest of the three: token logic is upgradeable through roles held by a 3-of-6 Safe, and interest minting bypasses the debt caps that admin controls can raise. Exit is close behind, because Pharos cannot measure a same-size route through Liquity-style {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and tracks no market depth. Backing also carries adverse readings on its shutdown, liquidation and backstop mechanics. Scroll got its native {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} dollar from a familiar blueprint, but durable exit liquidity has not formed around it.

chfau-allunity.title: BaFin-Licensed Franc, Unaudited Reserves
chfau-allunity.text: CHFAU extends AllUnity from the euro to the Swiss franc: the same DWS, Galaxy, and Flow Traders joint venture behind EURAU, issuing under the same BaFin e-money license as a MiCA e-money token. Reserves are stated as CHF held 1:1 in segregated accounts at CRR credit institutions, and the published policy offers par {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} subject to identity, AML, and banking checks. Direct minting is limited to institutional and professional accounts, and the token pays no {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}}. The footprint is wider than the float: AllUnity issues natively on six chains, yet Pharos's direct supply reads place all but a sliver of tokens on Ethereum. AllUnity's trust center still lists the reserve audit report as coming soon; without a dated report or a published cash-versus-HQLA split, backing is the weakest of the three pillars behind the {{grade}} overall grade. The peg record has been clean since the February 2026 launch. Bank identities, allocations, and successor-custody mechanics remain unpublished, so until a dated reserve report appears the 1:1 claim rests on the issuer's own disclosure.

buck-buck-assets.title: USDC-Redeemable Wrapper on Strategy Preferred
buck-buck-assets.text: BUCK was Bridge Building's USDC-redeemable savings stablecoin, launched in January 2026 and wound down that April. Its {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}} came from Strategy Inc.'s perpetual preferred stock (STRC), which made up about three quarters of the reserve, with a USDC liquidity reserve covering redemptions. That made BUCK less a cash dollar than a dollar wrapper around a preferred-equity claim on a company whose balance sheet rests on bitcoin. The structure was over-reserved on paper, with The Network Firm's March 2026 attestation reporting a 1.79 reserve ratio, but the excess sat in an equity instrument whose value moves with Strategy and bitcoin. Mint and redemption ran 1:1 against USDC through an issuer-controlled LiquidityWindow contract open only to AML-verified participants, and yield arrived as monthly rebases. Governance sat with a single BVI entity. By April 2026 the project site had become a shutdown notice saying funds were returned to token holders, and only residual supply remains from a peak market cap under $3 million. The wind-down was orderly, with no oracle or collateral break.

bd-basedollar.title: Base's Liquity V2 Fork
bd-basedollar.text: BD is Base Dollar's Liquity V2 fork, deployed to Base mainnet in August 2026, with {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} borrowing against ETH, wstETH, rETH, cbETH and cbBTC rather than the AERO and Aerodrome LP collateral planned before launch. Borrowers set their own interest rates, holders can redeem BD directly for system collateral, and branch Stability Pools absorb liquidations in exchange for borrower and liquidation fees. The AERO and LP branches remain planned; before launch, audit remediation merged in April 2026 fixed a high-severity LP-price manipulation flaw. Circulation is still small, so a dollar print is evidence of launch rather than of depth. The control model is mixed: the five launch branches are collateral-gated and the token owner is renounced, but the collateral registry's 4-of-6 Safe can register new minting branches with no token-level cap and no execution delay. That path makes economic control the weakest of the three pillars on BD's {{grade}} card, while backing and exit both read well. Until that registry path is capped or delayed, BD's supply is bounded by collateral only as far as the Safe allows.

wm-m0.title: M Without the Yield
wm-m0.text: wM is M0's non-rebasing ERC-20 wrapper over M, backed by short-term U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills in bankruptcy-remote SPVs. Ordinary wM holders do not receive that yield. Underneath sits the same reserve framework and Validator {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} as M, while approved earner accounts claim the underlying yield and `claimExcess()` sends excess reserves to a configured recipient, leaving wM as a flat dollar for downstream integrations. Wrapping and unwrapping run 1:1 through the M0 SwapFacility and return M, not fiat, so the wrapper itself opens no path to M0's institutional {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. The Ethereum contract also carries freeze, forced-transfer and pause roles, all assigned to one address, so Pharos records direct freeze reach. Exit is the weakest pillar on a {{grade}} card because Pharos observes no exact DEX, redemption or retained route for wM. The durable constraint is structural: wM inherits M's reserve and attestation framework, and a wrapper cannot rate above its parent.

usdnr-nerona.title: Yield-Free T-Bill Wrapper
usdnr-nerona.text: Nerona's USDnr is a 1:1 wrapper over M0's $M, the tokenized short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} exposure, minted through the M0 SwapFacility. The T-bill carry accrues to the M0 reserve and Nerona rather than to holders, who must stake into the separate sUSDnr vault for yield. The USDC deposit path is open to any address, with no protocol-level KYC, under an admin-set asset cap, while M-path wrap and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are limited to M-swapper-role addresses. The canonical token is on Ethereum, but at the latest read nearly all of the {{supplyUsd}} outstanding sat on Fluent, an M0 spoke reached through Hyperlane bridge adapters. Parts of that route, including one module of its message-security check and the mailbox's ownership path, remain unverified, which makes economic control the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card. The wrapper adds keys of its own: a single externally owned key controls the Ethereum proxy admin and can replace the wrap, unwrap and freeze logic immediately, while a freeze manager can lock individual accounts. The overall grade is capped at M's own rating, since a wrapper cannot rate above the asset it wraps, and the on-chain unwrap back to $M is the strongest pillar. Holders carry every M0-layer risk plus the discretion of the wrapper's and the bridge route's administrators.

usdk-kast.title: KAST's M0 Wrapper on Solana
usdk-kast.text: KAST's USDK is a 1:1 Solana extension of M0's M token, domiciled under the Anjouan Offshore Finance Authority and distributed through the KAST app, with the underlying yield retained by KAST rather than passed to holders. With {{supplyUsd}} outstanding, all of it on Solana, the token is a thin layer over its parent: wrapping moves M into an extension vault before USDK is minted, and unwrapping burns USDK to release it. Fixed-slot reads have shown the vault covering supply, and the report card treats M as the whole reserve claim, so USDK cannot rate above it. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by backing, the weakest of the three pillars, because the T-bill and cash collateral behind M is scored without published valuation, duration, or loss-recovery terms specific to USDK. Economic control is close behind: the extension program remains upgradeable with no delay and its deployed code has not been verified against published source, so Pharos does not yet classify USDK as a pure wrapper. KAST also retains a freeze authority over holder accounts on the Token-2022 mint. Exit runs through the KAST app and licensed partners for eligible users, with no recognized on-chain route. The durable constraint is that USDK adds one offshore operator's keys on top of everything M already asks a holder to trust.

xo-exodus.title: Self-Custody's Custodial Dollar
xo-exodus.text: XO Cash is a MoonPay-issued dollar token on Solana, built as an M0 extension and distributed through the Exodus self-custody wallet and Exodus Pay. Its reserve is M held in the extension's vault, and M in turn rests on collateral that M0's permissioned minters pledge and validators attest. Pharos's October 2026 on-chain read found the vault holding slightly more M than XO's supply, but the extension program is upgradeable and its deployed code is unverified, so Pharos does not yet treat XO as a pure wrapper. The Token-2022 mint carries freeze, pause, permanent-delegate, and transfer-hook authorities held by MoonPay, so self-custody describes the wallet while the token's controls stay with the issuer. MoonPay's terms require onboarding, exclude Canada, New York, Colorado, and the EEA, and promise only commercially reasonable redemption efforts with no settlement maximum. Backing is held down by what MoonPay does not publish: XO's reserve custodians, provider allocation, and an XO-specific reconciliation. Exit is the weakest pillar because the redemption route's settlement terms are not established. The score falls below the F threshold without a measured adverse fact, so the card publishes {{grade}}. The durable constraint is that XO borrows M0's reserve framework while leaving its own {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and exit terms undocumented.

jpysc-sbi-startale.title: Japan trust-bank JPY stablecoin
jpysc-sbi-startale.text: JPYSC went live on June 24, 2026 as Japan's first trust-bank-issued yen stablecoin: SBI Shinsei Trust Bank issues it as a Type III electronic payment instrument, SBI VC Trade distributes it, and Startale Group built the rails. Reserves sit in segregated trust accounts that may hold up to half in {{term:treasury}}Japanese government bonds{{/term}}; the trustee's September 30 balance table showed nearly all of the trust property in ordinary and term yen deposits, with a small JGB slice. That table is issuer self-verification rather than independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, the deposit banks are unnamed, and backing scores in the middle of the range. The weakest pillar is exit. JPYSC circulates only inside verified SBI VC Trade accounts, with no external-wallet withdrawals and no trading venue, so the tracked price is peg-derived and cannot show stress. Direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs by application and identity checks, with yen paid to the holder's bank account within a standard two bank business days that verification can extend. Startale says public-chain circulation is technically ready and waiting on legal and tax clarity. SBI VC Trade's lending service and a DigiFT settlement partnership add uses inside that perimeter. Until the gate opens, the trust-law structure reaches only as far as SBI's own account network.

rgbp-revolut.title: Revolut Pre-Launch Sterling Stablecoin
rgbp-revolut.text:
Revolut's proposed sterling stablecoin is still a sandbox test, waiting on UK rules that have softened but are not yet final.

The FCA picked Revolut for its stablecoin sandbox cohort in February 2026, and testing began that quarter. Revolut received its full UK banking licence in March, yet any GBP coin would come from Revolut Ltd, its e-money entity, because proposed Bank of England rules restrict issuance across affiliated subsidiaries. The BoE's June 2026 policy statement removed the main commercial blockers: the proposed £20,000 individual holding cap gave way to a temporary per-coin issuance cap of roughly £40bn, and the share of reserves allowed in short-dated UK Treasury bills rose from 60% to 70%. The remainder sits at the Bank, holders receive no yield, and par {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} within 24 hours is mandatory. Rules are due to be finalised by end-2026, and the FCA regime starts in October 2027. Revolut's priority use case, per its House of Lords testimony, is the UK-to-India remittance corridor rather than retail payments. Its first live stablecoin, the euro EURR launched in August 2026, is issued by Stripe's Bridge under MiCA rather than by a Revolut entity, which says nothing direct about who would issue sterling. No contract, reserve report or redemption terms exist yet; until the UK rules are final, RGBP exists only inside the sandbox.

ausdt-tether-alloy.title: Gold Collateral, Dollar Target
ausdt-tether-alloy.text: aUSDT was Alloy by Tether's dollar stablecoin: a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} where KYC-verified users deposited Tether Gold (XAUT) into an Ethereum vault and minted dollars at up to a 75% mint-to-value ratio, so the peg sat on {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} gold rather than a bank account. Holders had no direct redemption right. The peg relied on overcollateralization, whitelisted {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}} and secondary-market liquidity, and returning aUSDT was how a borrower recovered XAUT. The vault kept the collateral observable on-chain, but the token also inherited Tether Gold {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, gold-price volatility, whitelist access, and Tether's control of the upgradeable vault contracts. Tether halted minting on June 17, 2026, citing activity, demand and product priorities, and set September 17, 2026 as the deadline for returning aUSDT and recovering XAUT collateral. That deadline has passed. Pharos froze the token in July 2026 as an archived wind-down asset.

usdsui-sui.title: Sui Gets Its Native Dollar
usdsui-sui.text: USDsui is Sui's native dollar, issued through Bridge, Stripe's stablecoin infrastructure arm. The reserve model is conventional Bridge Open Issuance: cash, short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}}, repos, and government {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}} in segregated accounts support mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, with institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at Lead Bank, BlackRock, and Fidelity. Bridge's public transparency endpoint reports a USDsui-specific split of roughly nine-tenths Treasuries and one-tenth cash, but it is self-reported with no independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} and no publication cadence. That keeps backing below what the asset mix alone would earn: the disclosed composition is clean, the assurance behind it is thin. Exit is the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card. Redemption runs through Bridge for eligible customers only, settles slowly and covers only part of a stress-size request, and Pharos tracks no market route alongside it. Minting is issuer-controlled and reconciled against reserves. USDsui gives Sui a native dollar whose exit, for most holders, runs through Bridge's onboarding.

brlv-crown.title: Brazilian Bonds On Chain
brlv-crown.text: BRLV is Crown's centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, minted and redeemed 1:1 for BRL by KYC'd users and backed almost entirely by Brazilian federal government bonds and Treasury-linked ETFs pledged to token holders through a security-agent structure in segregated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. The backing is local sovereign debt rather than offshore dollar liquidity, and the security-agent structure is designed to keep reserve claims separate from Crown itself. The risks are equally specific: BRL liquidity, Brazilian sovereign-rate volatility, and KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. The evidence has limits too. Monthly reserve memos come from Fact Finance; the September 2026 memo carries its signer's accounting credentials but no identified assurance standard or opinion, and it omits security identifiers, fund look-through, and the reserve-account institutions behind the segregation claim. Native issuance is on Base, with issuer-relayed representations on Ethereum and Tempo. On the {{grade}} card the exit pillar is the weakest of the three, since primary exit is eligibility-gated and that gate is the route Pharos scores.

usdglo-glo.title: Glo Dollar Public-Goods Reserve
usdglo-glo.text: Glo Dollar is a Brale-issued dollar with an unusual allocation decision: reserve yield is directed to extreme-poverty alleviation instead of being rebated to holders, exchanges, or the issuer's distribution partners. The backing itself is deliberately ordinary, mostly cash and cash equivalents with a small sleeve of U.S. government-backed debt, and 1:1 mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through Brale for eligible customers. Its differentiation is distributional rather than mechanical. The report card scores the evidence gap rather than the reserve mix. Backing is the weakest of the three pillars behind the {{grade}} overall grade, because Brale's monthly management reports carry no accountant's opinion and name no banks, custodians, or instruments behind the cash and government-debt lines. Economic control is held back too: on the six EVM deployments, one Brale-operated key holds the minter, admin, pauser, and upgrader roles with no on-chain cap. Exit scores well, with issuer-native deployments across EVM chains and Stellar and direct redemption through Brale. The durable constraint is disclosure: until a third party checks the reserve, USDGLO's backing rests on Brale's own assertion.

usdon-ondo.title: Ondo Settlement Cash
usdon-ondo.text: USDon is the cash leg inside Ondo Global Markets, used to settle purchases and redemptions of tokenized assets on Ondo's platform. Ondo states each token is backed one-for-one by dollar cash or cash equivalents in brokerage accounts. Daily and monthly platform reports now name accounts at Alpaca, BitGo and SVB, list USDon quantities by chain, and carry Ankura's confirmation of the aggregate collateral. They do not assign accounts or instruments to USDon or reconcile its backing separately from the rest of the platform, so Pharos still records the composition as undisclosed. Issuance runs through Ondo-controlled minters on Ethereum, BNB Chain and Solana, and Ondo retains freeze authority over holders. Pharos treats {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} as a Global Markets route gated by eligibility and measures no same-size exit, so exit is the weakest pillar. With both gaps open, the card is not rated for insufficient evidence. Both gaps leave a holder's position dependent on Ondo's platform disclosures and eligibility rules.

audm-macropod.title: AUD in Trust, Minted by Single Keys
audm-macropod.text: AUDM is Macropod's institutional Australian dollar: approved clients deposit AUD into a trustee-held reserve, Macropod mints against it, and redemption runs back through the same KYC-gated bank-transfer channel. The paper trail is fuller than the float suggests. Monthly issuer self-verification reports reconcile AUD cash at Westpac, held by Macropod as trustee for the AUDM Trust, against supply on Ethereum, Solana, Base and Redbelly, and the September 2026 report left a small excess. A quarterly Hall Chadwick agreed-upon-procedures engagement sits alongside it, though that report expresses no opinion and did not require the firm to be independent. On Ethereum, Base and Redbelly, the admin and minter roles sit with externally owned accounts, and the mint is economically unbounded and reconciled only after the fact. Backing sits just above it, with the monthly evidence issuer-signed rather than independent. Exit leads, reflecting the direct 1:1 redemption route. AUDM's constraints are a short track record and reserve checks that are mostly self-reported.

audf-forte.title: Audited Cash, Unnamed Bank
audf-forte.text: AUDF is Forte Securities Australia's Australian dollar stablecoin, issued under an ASIC AFSL and redeemable 1:1 for AUD by eligible account holders through Forte. Its reserve evidence is an audit rather than agreed-upon procedures: Horizon Nexus audited the whole AUDF reserve bank-account balance as of 31 August 2026 and issued an unmodified opinion. The audit covers assets only. It names no bank and reconciles no token liabilities, and Forte's Terms of Use give holders no entitlement to the reserves, no security interest, and no trust or fiduciary relationship. Those gaps leave backing the weakest of the three pillars on the {{grade}} card, while the direct redemption route gives exit the strongest line. Economic control sits between them: an issuer Admin Safe holds mint authority, 2-of-5 on Ethereum, Polygon and Base and 2-of-3 on Avalanche, and minting is economically unbounded. Circulating supply stands at {{supplyUsd}}. AUDF's durable constraint is that a clean audit of cash does not establish what a holder could recover if Forte failed.

busd0-usual.title: Fixed-Maturity USD0 Bond
busd0-usual.text: bUSD0 is Usual's bond-leg wrapper of USD0: a fixed-notional bond maturing June 11, 2028 that trades as a discount instrument before that date. It replaced USD0++ under Usual's UIP-12 governance proposal of December 2025, which moved early-exit rights into a separate token. Depositing one USD0 now mints one bUSD0 plus one rt-bUSD0 early-exit right. Par {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} before maturity requires both, while bUSD0 alone redeems 1:1 for USD0 only at maturity and can trade below one dollar until then. Standalone holders earn daily USUAL token coupons rather than dollar NAV growth. Borrowers earn none: in January 2026 the Usual Stability Loan, which lets bUSD0 collateralize USD0 borrowing, opened a one-way migration from Euler to the zero-rate UZR market on Fira, where positions receive no USUAL emissions and return comes only from the discount to par. Underneath sits the USD0 {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} stack, and an Arbitrum representation adds a LayerZero burn-and-mint route. Pharos reactivated the listing on 30 October 2026 after CoinGecko began reporting a positive market cap; the discount before maturity is now measured rather than inferred.

susde-ethena.title: Ethena's USDe Staking Wrapper
susde-ethena.text: sUSDe is the yield wrapper over USDe, converting Ethena staking rewards into a rising exchange rate rather than a separate payout. Economically it inherits the same USDe reserve and custody stack: liquid stablecoin backing, delta-neutral BTC and ETH/LST hedges, off-exchange custody, and CEX execution. Unstaking burns the shares at once and moves USDe to a silo for a cooldown Ethena can reconfigure; it stood at one day on 19 October 2026. Exit therefore scores as the strongest of the three pillars. Economic control is the weakest, because the bridge controls behind sUSDe's deployments across more than two dozen chains remain unresolved in Pharos's review. The {{grade}} overall grade is held at the parent USDe rating, since a wrapper cannot rate above the asset it wraps. The durable constraint is USDe itself: sUSDe adds yield accounting and a short wait, not a separate claim.

susds-sky.title: Sky Savings Rate Vault for USDS
susds-sky.text: sUSDS is the savings receipt in the Sky stack: deposit USDS, receive an ERC-4626 token whose exchange rate compounds with the Sky Savings Rate. Its sibling stUSDS funds SKY-backed borrowing and makes holders absorb shortfall and slashing losses; sUSDS carries no such risk-capital layer. The wrapper still inherits the USDS reserve mix, Sky governance, and the USDS PSM exit surface, so it stays attached to the parent system. Exit is the strongest of the three pillars, since USDS is withdrawable directly from the vault with no protocol fee. Economic control is the weakest: the vault is a ward-gated UUPS proxy, and the Base, Optimism, and Arbitrum representations sit behind administered SkyLink bridges whose supply materiality Pharos has not resolved. The {{grade}} overall grade sits below the parent USDS limit, which is not binding. Every sUSDS exit returns USDS, so a dollar exit still runs through the USDS PSM.

sdai-sky.title: The Classic DSR Wrapper
sdai-sky.text: sDAI is the original Dai savings receipt: deposit DAI and receive a token whose redeemable DAI balance grows with the Dai Savings Rate. It adds very little conceptual complexity beyond the base asset, but it still belongs on its own row because holders are choosing a NAV-appreciating {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper with its own liquidity, integrations, and wrapper-contract risk rather than plain DAI. The underlying still inherits DAI's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} collateral profile. The Ethereum wrapper is a non-upgradeable contract with no owner, pause, or blacklist function, and almost all supply sits there rather than on the Base, OP Mainnet, and World Chain bridge representations. Even so, economic control is the weakest pillar behind the {{grade}} overall grade: those representations run through upgradeable OP Stack bridges, and Pharos cannot yet resolve their supply share at runtime. Redemption into DAI is immediate on Ethereum, so the durable constraint is the parent DAI system rather than the wrapper.

sfrxusd-frax.title: Frax's Yield Sleeve
sfrxusd-frax.text: sfrxUSD is the savings wrapper for frxUSD: a vault share whose exchange rate rises as Frax deploys staked frxUSD through its Benchmark Yield Strategy across carry-trade, DeFi, and Treasury venues. Pharos's pinned reads found no idle frxUSD in the vault, so the share is a claim on deployed strategy positions whose current allocations are not established. The parent stablecoin risk remains the frxUSD custodian and reserve stack. In the live Ethereum implementation, the ordinary ERC-4626 deposit, mint, withdraw, and redeem paths are disabled. Supply instead changes through an authorized minter path with no token-level amount cap, and that minter role can also burn any holder's balance. Thirty-one of thirty-three registered deployments are LayerZero OFT representations whose validation configuration remains unresolved. Economic control is therefore the weakest of the three pillars. Exit is scored on Ethereum AMM pools rather than a reviewed protocol redemption route. The {{grade}} overall grade is capped at the parent frxUSD rating, even though backing is the strong line. The durable constraint is control: a multichain share whose mint, burn, and bridge keys sit with Frax.

scrvusd-curve.title: Borrower Interest Receipt
scrvusd-curve.text: scrvUSD is Curve's ERC-4626 savings share over crvUSD, so the wrapper adds yield and exchange-rate behavior without inventing a new dollar. Deposited crvUSD backs the share, while borrower interest and protocol revenue make the redeemable crvUSD balance climb over time. Pharos's review found the Ethereum vault runs no strategies and keeps deposits idle, so converting shares back into crvUSD is immediate, although Curve's role manager could still install a withdrawal-limit module. The parent risk is still Curve's CDP and LLAMMA machinery, with BTC and ETH collateral doing the heavy lifting underneath, and the {{grade}} overall grade is capped at the parent crvUSD rating. Economic control is the wrapper's own weak point: bridged representations on nine other chains retain upgrade-mediated, owner-grantable mint powers, and the Etherlink route remains unresolved. The durable constraint is that the share can be no sounder than crvUSD itself.

cusdo-openeden.title: Non-Rebasing OpenDollar
cusdo-openeden.text: cUSDO is OpenEden's non-rebasing wrapper for USDO, built for protocols that would rather watch a price rise than reconcile changing balances. It keeps the same underlying OpenDollar claim: tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} exposure and issuer-controlled {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rails, but moves the yield expression into NAV appreciation. That makes the product mechanically useful without making the reserve chain any shorter: cUSDO still depends on USDO, OpenEden, and the underlying tokenized T-bill stack. Its {{grade}} overall grade is set by the binding parent cap: a child cannot rate above its required parent, so cUSDO's ceiling is USDO's score. Backing is held back on the card for exactly that inherited reason, while exit grades near the top. The wrapper's own admin surface is issuer-held upgrade and pause authority across its deployments, plus a Solana signer that holds both mint and freeze power, so the wrapper adds its own issuer control layer. Any change in USDO's reserves or OpenEden's controls passes straight through to cUSDO.

syusd-aegis.title: Aegis Cooldown Wrapper
syusd-aegis.text: sYUSD is Aegis's staking wrapper over YUSD, capitalizing funding-rate income into a rising exchange rate instead of paying out a separate coupon. The parent stablecoin risk is YUSD's BTC spot plus short-perpetual hedge model and off-exchange custody assumptions; the wrapper risk is the ERC-4626 vault, its upgradeable proxy under a 3-of-5 Safe, and the exit terms. On Ethereum, holders choose between a seven-day cooldown and instant unstaking for a 50-basis-point fee, while the BSC wrapper offers only the cooldown, which an admin can lengthen to 90 days. Accountable publishes a real-time reserve feed for YUSD, from a provider Pharos classes as a niche attestor. Backing is the weakest of the three pillars, carried over from YUSD's hedge book, and the parent YUSD limit binds the {{grade}} overall grade. Every wrapper route returns chain-local YUSD, not cash, and onward redemption needs Aegis's authorization.

stusds-sky.title: Sky Risk-Capital USDS
stusds-sky.text: stUSDS is Sky's risk-capital module over USDS: depositors mint ERC-4626 shares, their USDS funds SKY-backed borrowing, and the module pays the stUSDS Rate in return. That return comes with losses passive USDS holders do not face, since borrower shortfall on staked-SKY loans or a governance slashing decision can cut redeemable value. Withdrawals return USDS only up to the module's unutilized liquidity, so a busy loan book can slow exits. Backing is the weakest of the three pillars because the module's loss backstop and reserve concentration score low, while economic control is the strongest. Exit routes share a failure domain with the rest of the Sky stack. The {{grade}} overall grade is held at the parent USDS rating, since a wrapper cannot rate above the asset it wraps. The durable constraint is that stUSDS holders, not the wider USDS base, absorb shortfalls on staked-SKY loans.

stcusd-cap.title: Cap Yield Wrapper
stcusd-cap.text: stcUSD is the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} version of Cap cUSD: users stake cUSD into an ERC-4626 vault whose exchange rate rises as idle-reserve yield and operator repayments accrue. Operators borrow reserve assets under underwriting from restaking networks. Per Cap's documentation, they repay a fixed premium to those underwriters plus a hurdle rate to stcUSD holders, set at the greater of a protocol benchmark floor and the market rate and rising with reserve utilization. Cap's design attempts to keep stablecoin holders whole through {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} and slashing, but stcUSD still adds operator, underwriter, strategy and vault risk on top of the underlying cUSD basket and its {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanics. The wrapper has no separate privileged mint path, and its upgrade authority sits behind a one-day timelock whose proposer and executor roles belong to Cap's 3-of-5 governance Safe. The {{grade}} overall grade is therefore capped at the parent cUSD rating rather than set by a wrapper-specific finding.

said-gaib.title: AI Infrastructure NAV Token
said-gaib.text: sAID is GAIB's ERC-4626 vault share over AID, and it floats with the NAV of AI infrastructure financings rather than holding AID's dollar peg. Staking AID buys exposure to GPU, robotics and related compute financings plus a buffer of T-bills and stablecoins kept for liquidity. Exit is slow by design. The live contract burns shares into a loss-adjusted AID claim and pays it out in FIFO order after a 30-day cooldown, subject to whatever liquidity the operator makes available, while GAIB's documentation still describes monthly cohorts. The offering memorandum gives holders no direct claim on vault contents and no repayable debt obligation from any sAID entity. Pharos scores that difference directly: exit is the weakest of the three pillars because no same-size route can be measured, economic control is the strongest, and the {{grade}} overall grade is held at the parent AID rating, since a vault share cannot rate above the asset it wraps.

msy-main-street.title: A Vault Share That Followed msUSD Down
msy-main-street.text: msY was Main Street's ERC-4626-style {{term:yield-bearing}}yield share{{/term}} over msUSD, accruing value from the protocol's options and derivatives strategy while final exit ran back through msUSD's capped, cooldown-gated USDC {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. That layering stopped being theoretical on June 20, 2026: reserve verifier Accountable terminated its relationship with Main Street, saying the protocol failed its verification standards, and msUSD traded around 30 cents in the following week. The vault share had no independent backing of its own and followed the parent down; Pharos's frozen snapshot from June 30 shows msY near $0.29. Main Street disputed the characterization and said its assets remained backed, but redemption capacity was never shown to be adequate. Pharos now carries msY as frozen, a derivative casualty of counterparty failure rather than an active dollar instrument. Every risk in the stack, from strategy to {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, sat on top of a base redemption whose capacity was never demonstrated when it mattered.

yusd-yieldfi.title: YieldFi USDC Strategy Vault
yusd-yieldfi.text: YieldFi's yUSD is an ERC-4626 share over USDC that its manager routes into Pendle principal tokens, Morpho and Silo vaults, private credit, and hedged carry. The manager makes discretionary allocations while the product is priced as a dollar, at a NAV struck at least twice a week. On paper yUSD is backed by USDC; whether it holds a dollar depends on allocator judgement and on the exit terms of venues under no obligation to be liquid on a holder's schedule. Backing sits mid-scale, held back by reserve concentration and the absence of any published funding-stress result. Economic control is the weakest pillar for a concrete reason: alongside deposit-minted shares, the manager holds a discretionary mint path with no supply ceiling, and two externally owned admin accounts can change the operator set immediately. The same admin role can blacklist holders. Exit offers no relief, with no comparable same-notional route out on record, and the {{grade}} overall grade follows from the two. The durable constraint is that a dollar-priced share rests on a manager's discretion, both in where USDC is allocated and in how many shares exist.

sbold-k3-capital.title: K3 Stability Pool BOLD
sbold-k3-capital.text: sBOLD is K3 Capital's ERC-4626 wrapper around BOLD deposited into Liquity V2 Stability Pools. It earns interest and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} gains while automating the conversion of liquidated ETH and LST collateral back into BOLD. The base BOLD system is immutable and fully on-chain with {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-based issuance, but sBOLD adds K3-controlled vault, oracle, and solver risk, so it belongs as a separate wrapper exposure. The wrapper itself is a non-upgradeable contract with no selective holder blacklist. Its 2-of-3 owner Safe can still pause deposits and redemptions for every holder at once. The same Safe holds a fee switch: an entry fee of up to 5% on deposits and up to 2.5% on collateral-to-BOLD swaps, paid to an address it sets, though every rate read zero on 19 October 2026.  The {{grade}} overall grade is held by a shared-dependency cap rather than by the parent: Pharos applies it when many reviewed assets exit through the same instant ERC-4626 redemption rail with a shared critical control identity. The durable constraint is that sBOLD's value depends on liquidation proceeds being swapped back into BOLD by machinery K3 controls.

ybold-yearn.title: Yearn's BOLD Stability Pool Vault
ybold-yearn.text: yBOLD is Yearn's ERC-4626 vault around BOLD deposited into Liquity V2 Stability Pool strategies, layering vault and strategy risk onto Liquity's CDP-redemption design. Each share is documented as one BOLD and redeems for BOLD with no withdrawal fee or waiting period; yield accrues only when yBOLD is staked in the separate ysyBOLD auto-compounder. Allocation across the Stability Pools stays dynamic, so the backing carries Liquity's {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} execution and smart-contract risk on top of BOLD's own {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} design. The share token has no blacklist, freeze, or pause, but a Yearn role manager can install a withdraw-limit module that would gate redemptions; that module is currently unset. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by a shared-dependency cap rather than by BOLD: yBOLD is one of dozens of assets whose instant ERC-4626 redemption rail Pharos treats as a single critical control identity, and every pillar scores above that cap. Exit is the lowest of the three. The durable constraint is that holders exchange plain BOLD exposure for Yearn's vault governance and Liquity's pool mechanics.

stkgho-umbrella-aave.title: Sunset GHO Umbrella Staking
stkgho-umbrella-aave.text: Aave Umbrella stkGHO is a slashable staking receipt over GHO, built to cover GHO deficits on Aave's Ethereum Core Pool in exchange for Umbrella rewards. That bargain has been wound down. AIP 507, executed on 27 July 2026, cut stkGHO emissions to zero, set target liquidity to the one-GHO protocol minimum and raised the GHO deficit offset from 115,000 to 3 million GHO. The Aave DAO now absorbs deficits up to that offset before any slashing while stakers exit, and future GHO deficits fall to the DAO treasury. Pharos assesses stkGHO separately from the non-slashable sGHO savings vault. Slashing remains live code: anyone can trigger it once a reserve deficit exceeds the offset, and it reduces the GHO every staker can redeem. Exit is the weakest pillar, with a 20-day cooldown followed by a two-day withdrawal window; a missed window restarts the clock while funds stay slashable. Aave governance controls the slashing configuration, oracle, offset and exit timing, and the Umbrella owner can pause share transfers. The {{grade}} overall grade is capped at the parent GHO rating.

myrc-blox.title: Blox's eKYC-Gated Ringgit Coin
myrc-blox.text: MYRC is Blox's ringgit stablecoin, minted and redeemed 1:1 over Malaysian banking rails for users who clear Blox's eKYC onboarding, which accepts MyKad or passport. Its strongest evidence is recurring: Tommy Ung & Partners PLT issues monthly ISAE 3000 reasonable-assurance examinations reconciling reserves to MYRC in circulation, and the August 2026 report splits the book roughly two-thirds ringgit bank cash and one-third Halogen Shariah MYR Liquid Fund. That composition supports the {{grade}} overall grade, with exit the strongest pillar and economic control the weakest. Minting is economically unbounded: a two-of-three Safe holds it on the EVM chains and a two-of-four Squads multisig on Solana, and reconciliation arrives monthly rather than on-chain. The reserve banks, their shares and the account safeguards remain undisclosed. Blox holds no Bank Negara Malaysia or Securities Commission licence, and its own terms say MYRC is not a payment instrument under Malaysian law without local approvals. The durable constraint is that a monthly examiner, not a supervisor, carries the oversight.

krwq-iq.title: Korean Won Stablecoin, Still Dollar-Backed
krwq-iq.text: KRWQ is a won-referenced stablecoin that IQ launched with Frax in October 2025, with KYC-gated institutional access and a reserve held entirely in dollar stablecoins. Ethereum is the canonical mint chain; Base, Polygon, Fraxtal, Codex and Morph carry LayerZero OFT representations that share one pooled supply. The issuer's custodian-assets feed reports frxUSD as most of the reserve and USDC, partly held in a Base treasury Safe, as the rest, and Pharos reproduced those balances on-chain. A February 2026 issuer release said KRWQ had begun buying Korean government bonds held at Shinhan Securities, yet the feed still shows no bond position, and circulating-liability reconciliation remains unverified. Mint and redemption are restricted to institutional counterparties such as exchanges, market makers and OTC desks, and KRWQ is not offered to South Korean residents while domestic legislation is pending. Economic control is the weakest pillar on the card: a 3-of-5 Safe can authorize any new minter, and the token's mint function checks neither collateral nor a token-level cap, so Pharos scores issuance as unbounded. Chainlink Proof of Reserve has run since June 2026, but no CPA-style monthly attestation has been named. Holders today carry Frax and Circle counterparty risk behind {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} that only institutions can use.

reur-royal-euro.title: Royal Euro, Delisted to Private Channels
reur-royal-euro.text: REUR is RIB Digital Holdings' Hong Kong-domiciled euro token, a claim on euro bank deposits whose bank and account details the issuer redacts. Its identified public markets closed in mid-2026: AscendEX suspended REUR deposits on 30 June 2026 and ended withdrawals on 3 July, delisting every REUR pair. Pharos no longer tracks REUR as an active stablecoin, and the issuer now describes access through approved institutional, OTC and private settlement channels. That leaves no ordinary public route to acquire the token, and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} terms are discretionary. Transparency decayed in parallel: the self-signed proof-of-reserves snapshots, pitched as real-time, stalled at a late-April 2026 snapshot that reported cash. On-chain, single admin EOAs on Ethereum, BSC and Tron can authorize an uncapped master minter. Without a public market, a current reserve snapshot or an open redemption route, holders depend on RIB Digital's private discretion.

kgst-kyrgyz-som.title: Central Asia's On-Chain Som
kgst-kyrgyz-som.text: KGST is a Kyrgyz som stablecoin on BNB Chain with a second deployment on TRON, presented by its issuer as backed 1:1 by som cash and cash equivalents in licensed Kyrgyz banks and custodial institutions. The issuer claims regulatory oversight and ongoing audits but publishes no dated independent reserve report, current balance or bank-level allocation, so Pharos cannot check the 1:1 claim. On the reviewed BSC contract, minting is uncapped and sits with a 2-of-5 Safe that also owns the proxy admin, with no timelock or guard, and the same owner can freeze individual holders or pause the token. Whether the TRON supply is native issuance or a representation remains unresolved. Pharos leaves KGST not rated because critical evidence is insufficient for a research grade: missing {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, undisclosed {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and an undocumented {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route are recorded as gaps rather than read as safety. Until the issuer publishes a dated reserve report and a holder-exercisable route back to som, the 1:1 claim rests on its word.

audx-aussie-dollar-token.title: Assured AUD Cash, Narrow Exit
audx-aussie-dollar-token.text: AUDX is the centralized Australian dollar stablecoin of TAU Pty Ltd, trading as AUDX Token, designed for 1:1 AUD {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, backed by AUD cash and government-backed instruments, and tracked across Ethereum, Polygon, Conflux, and XDC. The issuer describes AUSTRAC registration and 1:1 AUD reserves held in regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at financial institutions. Aura Partners publishes monthly limited-assurance reports under ASAE 3000 and 3100 that confirm designated reserve balances directly with the banks and reconcile them to issued supply, though the banks are not named and the firm shares a Sydney floor with the issuer. That evidence carries the backing line; the exit pillar is the weakest of the three on the {{grade}} card, because primary redemption is eligibility-gated. Pharos treats the reserve story as verified and the exit as narrow: a holder who does not qualify for the issuer's route has only secondary markets.

cngn-compliant-naira.title: Naira Settlement Goes Multichain
cngn-compliant-naira.text: cNGN is a Nigerian naira stablecoin for local-currency settlement, issued natively on Bantu and distributed to eight tracked networks through the issuer's lock-and-mint bridge. An ISAE 3000 examination as of August 31, 2026 reports naira reserves above circulating cNGN, in a book led by money-market funds with bank deposits, Treasury bills, and fixed-term placements behind them. Pharos cannot admit that report as dated assurance because neither the accountant's signature nor the management stamp carries a date, and the banks, allocations, and successor-custody terms remain undisclosed. Regulatory standing rests on a Nigerian SEC approval-in-principle under its Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme; no final licence has been granted. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects low scores on all three pillars, with economic control the weakest: the Bantu issuer account carries no economic cap or timelock, and upgrade authority on several destination representations is unresolved. After a clean first year, a single-source quote pushed cNGN materially below par in July 2026, an episode still open. Until the report is dated and the licence final, backing and legal standing both rest on provisional evidence.

brl1-brl1.title: A Consortium-Issued Real
brl1-brl1.text: BRL1 is a centralized Brazilian real stablecoin on Polygon, issued by BRL1 CONSORTIUM S.A. and targeting a 1:1 peg with a reserve mix of Brazilian federal LFT bonds, repurchase agreements, and a BRL bank balance, all reported in a segregated account at Banco XP. It adds another BRL-denominated route alongside the other Brazilian real tokens Pharos tracks. Its disclosure is limited: the reserve report is prepared internally, board-approved, and explicitly not audited, and there is no regular third-party {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. The latest report, dated October 1, 2026, ties the reserves to the Polygon supply at a named block, but that reconciliation is the issuer's own ledger work rather than an independent check of the off-chain balances. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down less by backing than by economic control, the weakest of the three pillars: a single EOA holds the only minter role with no supply cap, and another EOA can grant minting or upgrade rights immediately. The repo counterparty and the individual securities are undisclosed, so the reserve story stays issuer-asserted.

wars-argentine-peso.title: Ripio's Peso Token on a Single Certification
wars-argentine-peso.text: WARS is the Argentine peso token in Ripio's wFIAT suite, issued natively at the same contract address on Ethereum, Base, World Chain, BNB Chain, Polygon and Gnosis and moved between chains by Ripio's own burn-and-mint {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} rail. Reserve evidence arrives one accountant certification at a time. The latest, as of 30 June 2026, reconciled about 7.62 billion outstanding wARS across eight chains to about ARS 7.91 billion of deposits at unnamed Argentine financial institutions, in an engagement that expressly is not an audit or review and expresses no opinion. That balance date sits well outside the live adapter's 33-day freshness window, and the institutions, allocations and account terms remain undisclosed. One issuer address holds admin, mint, upgrade and pause roles on every native deployment, while a 4-of-7 Safe can authorize further minters. The overall score falls below the F threshold, but with no measured adverse fact in the record the card is published as not rated. Ripio advertises conversion to pesos through its platform, yet the whitepaper grants holders no direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} right. Redemption confidence therefore rests on Ripio's KYC-gated off-ramp, not on anything a holder can verify on-chain.

pusd-polymarket.title: Polymarket's USDC Account Token
pusd-polymarket.text: Polymarket USD is the application dollar behind Polymarket account balances on Polygon: supported USDC deposits mint PUSD, and the backing sits as USDC and bridged USDC.e in one identified vault that Pharos reads on-chain. The {{grade}} overall grade splits sharply by pillar. Backing is the strongest line on the card, since the claim is a pass-through on USDC with Circle's freeze reach inherited, though Polymarket publishes no legal segregation or insolvency terms for the vault. Exit is weaker: the on-chain unwrap pays out Polygon PoS USDC.e rather than native USDC, sits behind an administrative pause gate, and does not count as a same-notional route in Pharos scoring. Economic control is the weakest of the three. Deposit ramps mint only against collateral, but the token owner, a 3-of-7 Safe behind a 12-hour timelock, can add a minter with no collateral or cap check and can upgrade the token logic. The token has no direct blacklist or holder-freeze path, and Polymarket's official Bridge API remains an undisclosed cross-chain route. Launched in April 2026, PUSD still sits under a track-record ceiling. Its USDC is visible on-chain; the limit on new PUSD minting is a 12-hour delay and one Safe.

rusd-royal-dollar.title: Private Settlement Only
rusd-royal-dollar.text:
A delisted Royal/R Coins dollar whose public markets closed while bank-level reserve detail stayed undisclosed.

Royal Dollar is no longer tracked as an active stablecoin. AscendEX, home to every identified public RUSD market, suspended deposits on 30 June 2026 and closed withdrawals on 3 July, and the issuer now describes access through approved institutional, OTC, and private settlement channels. No ordinary public acquisition or redemption route remains. The issuer's reserve snapshot dated 23 April 2026 classified the backing as cash and bank deposits administered through The Royal Investment Bank of Kelantan, without naming the deposit banks, balances, or liquidity terms. Segregation, bankruptcy remoteness, and rehypothecation all remain undisclosed, and Pharos found no recurring whole-supply {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. On the immutable Ethereum, BNB Chain, and Tron contracts, chain-local admin accounts can still re-enable direct minting. The Hong Kong-domiciled issuer's discretionary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} terms and KYC-gated processes now operate out of public sight, alongside sister token REUR, whose AscendEX pairs the same notice removed. What remains public is a reserve and redemption framework, not verified current balances or an unconditional holder redemption right.

usdr-ring.title: The Ring Protocol Dollar
usdr-ring.text: Ring Protocol's USDR is a small Ethereum dollar whose backing is undisclosed. Ring's current documentation covers its swap and token tooling but publishes no USDR reserve inventory, and the verified token contract is a role-gated mint-and-burn ERC-20 with no reserve ledger, bonding curve, or holder {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} function. The launch transaction minted the initial supply directly to a minter address with no collateral argument, and three EOA minters can still mint to any address without a cap, alongside a launchpad contract whose minting is constrained by its own logic. Pharos therefore records the reserve stack as a single undisclosed position and does not model a redemption backstop. On the {{grade}} card, backing and economic control are the two weakest pillars while the exit pillar leads, because secondary-market exit routes exist even though they share a failure domain. USDR is a long-tail dollar whose peg rests on issuer discretion and protocol liquidity rather than any documented reserve.

uusd-anything-labs.title: Owner-Controlled, Reserves Undisclosed
uusd-anything-labs.text: Unity USD is Anything Labs's dollar token on BNB Chain, and its defining feature is what is not published. Pharos re-opened the website, whitepaper and contract repository in July 2026 and found no disclosure of reserve assets, custodians, {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rails or any reserve {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. The whitepaper is a conceptual AI-settlement essay with no reserve section, and DefiLlama's line that UUSD is backed by USDT and USDC is not corroborated by any issuer primary. What is visible is the control surface. UUSD is an upgradeable proxy whose 4-of-7 owner Safe can mint and burn directly, freeze any address and pause all transfers, and the same Safe sits at the end of the upgrade chain.
