The peg has held near par on single-source pricing, which says little when no mechanism for maintaining it is described. Pharos has strong evidence that the owner can mint without an economic bound. Backing and exit score slightly higher, but both are bounded estimates: no reserve inputs are published and no same-value exit route has been observed. Until Anything Labs publishes what stands behind the token, holders rely entirely on the seven keyholders behind that Safe.

jusd-jusd-stable-token.title: Polygon-Minted Dollar With Undisclosed Reserves
jusd-jusd-stable-token.text: JUSD is a long-tail dollar token with BSC and Polygon contracts, issuer/protocol-managed crypto collateral, and an unverified reserve composition. Pharos models its reserves as protocol-managed crypto collateral because public materials do not provide a reviewed, granular collateral breakdown: the 2023 whitepaper describes a diversified reserve but names no assets, custodians, or amounts and publishes no attestation. Canonical issuance sits on Polygon, where an owner EOA can call an uncapped mint, while the BSC deployment is a Chainport bridge representation, so BSC supply also depends on Chainport's lock-and-mint controls. The main risk is the limited transparency around reserve composition and live redemption depth. Since mid-July 2026 Pharos has held JUSD in quarantine because no permitted runtime source reports a positive circulating supply or market cap. Until JUSD publishes a third-party {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} and discloses {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop and reserve quality remain unmodelled by Pharos.

jusd-juicedollar.title: Juice Dollar Wind-Down
jusd-juicedollar.text: Juice Dollar was a Citrea-native USD stablecoin built on the Frankencoin and d-EURO architecture: oracle-free {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} positions collateralized by wrapped cBTC, permissionless challenge auctions standing in for a price feed at {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, and an ownerless accepted-minter registry with no admin key. In practice the bitcoin path was barely used. Pharos's July 2026 review of the issuer API and Citrea RPC found zero WCBTC held across all positions and roughly 56,700 JUSD outstanding, almost all of it minted 1:1 through the StablecoinBridge against bridged USDT.e, so the token was in effect a wrapper on bridged Tether with Tether's freeze power sitting on the reserve. The project announced a wind-down on 6 August 2026, and Pharos delisted JUSD on 10 August after {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} ended, issuer control was lost, the website and app were permanently shut down, and a new uncontrolled minter became active on-chain. In this design an accepted minter can mint an unrestricted amount and the contracts are immutable and ownerless, so the shutdown notice is the issuer's last word and the open mint is the record's durable fact.

usda-alpha-partner.title: Fiat-Backing Claim Without a Report
usda-alpha-partner.text: Alpha Partner USDA is a BSC-only dollar token with no published reserve report. When Pharos re-opened the issuer's website, full documentation and publication archive in October 2026, the only USDA-specific backing claim was an October 2025 article asserting 1:1 off-chain fiat reserves audited by independent third parties. It names no assets, weights, custodian, auditor or report, so Pharos keeps the whole reserve as an undisclosed, very-high-risk slice. Historical FDIC-protection marketing attributed to the issuer could not be reproduced, and FDIC deposit insurance does not cover stablecoins. On-chain, the token carries an uncapped mint role held by a contract and an externally owned account, and the default-admin role can appoint new minters and blacklist addresses. That makes economic control the weakest pillar behind the {{grade}} overall grade, with backing and exit only slightly higher, because there is no documented mint, {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} or peg-maintenance process to measure. The peg record shows a long tail of episodes below par, and an active depeg was open at this October 2026 refresh. Until the issuer publishes a reserve report and a redemption path, Pharos has nothing to score beyond the contract's admin keys.

xdai-gnosis.title: The Native Gnosis Dollar
xdai-gnosis.text: xDAI is the native gas token of Gnosis Chain, credited only when the canonical xDAI bridge escrows USDS on Ethereum, so its peg quality cascades from Sky and from Gnosis bridge infrastructure. Unlike a normal ERC-20 stablecoin, its canonical supply is native-chain accounting, so Pharos lists the WXDAI wrapper as a traded contract rather than using it as the supply contract. The reserve view is a {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} escrow: after the completed migration from DAI, the Foreign Bridge holds almost all of its collateral as sUSDS, Sky's savings vault, with a small liquid USDS buffer, and pinned reads reconcile that escrow to bridge-minted-minus-burnt xDAI with a slight surplus. Peg quality therefore depends on Sky's USDS, itself a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-backed dollar, on the sUSDS vault's liquidity, and on a 4-of-7 validator set and 8-of-15 admin Safes with no contract-enforced timelock. Native balances carry no local freeze, but a Sky-side freeze could impair the escrow and the exit path. The authority behind the selected bridge route remains unresolved. The durable constraint is that the peg rests on Sky's USDS and on Gnosis bridge governance, neither of which xDAI controls.

usdx-kava.title: The Legacy Kava Debt Dollar
usdx-kava.text: Kava USDX is the legacy Kava Mint {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} debt token, backed by crypto collateral and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} mechanics, and it trades at a deep discount to the dollar; Pharos keeps it in the catalog as a live depeg case rather than a healthy par dollar. The live CDP inventory is readable on-chain and is dominated by HBTC, the Huobi-wrapped bitcoin, with BTCB, XRPB, KAVA, BNB, and a sliver of stablecoins behind it, and the collateral value still exceeds outstanding supply. That is why backing is the strongest of the three pillars even as the {{grade}} overall grade sits at the floor: {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} has not been enough to defend the peg, no viable exit route is established, and an active depeg of more than a quarter limits the card to the F range by rule. CDP parameters and debt ceilings can be raised by the Stability Committee and by KAVA stake governance, and the chain's governance can pause sends of the usdx denom, though it has not done so. Its tracking value is mostly analytical: it shows how a fully collateralized debt token can still trade far from par when nothing forces convergence.

xtusd-xt.title: XT.com XSC CDP Dollar
xtusd-xt.text: XTUSD is XT.com's exchange-issued dollar, and its live deployment on XSC is a Maker-style Vat carrying a single debt-bearing collateral type, Wrapped XT. What the on-chain read found is what is missing. No Spotter, price feed, or other update contract is authorized on that Vat, so the collateral price sits at a fixed value with no identified mechanism to move it. No Cat, Dog, auction, or global-settlement module is authorized either. The 2022 announcement promised a 150% minimum collateral ratio and an auction for risky vaults. Its 3% annual fee matches the Jug's duty exactly, so interest accrues as advertised, while the auction has no contract standing behind it. The Median/OSM/Spotter stack that does exist on XSC is wired to the issuer's legacy TAI deployment, not to this one. The market then ended: XT.com's xtusd_usdt pair stopped updating on 18 July 2026, CoinGecko's feed ended two days later, and Pharos froze XTUSD on 23 September 2026 as an archived market-ended asset. Roughly $1.25 million remained in circulation at the last snapshot, held in a vault system that can neither reprice nor liquidate its collateral.

hbd-hive.title: The Hive Conversion Dollar
hbd-hive.text: HBD is Hive's {{term:algorithmic}}algorithmic{{/term}} dollar, a protocol-native liability redeemable on-chain for $1 of HIVE through a 3.5-day conversion priced at the witness median, with a haircut when system debt runs too high. There is no cash or Treasury {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} behind it. Pharos scores the backing as Hive's own conversion capacity, a self-referential reserve whose value moves with HIVE and with Hive governance. At Pharos's August 27 2026 chain read, the debt ratio stood at about 26%, above the 20% print-stop threshold and below the 30% haircut line, so new HBD issuance was paused while conversions still paid full value. Consensus has also intervened in balances before: the HF23 hard fork moved HBD held by a named set of Steemit accounts to the Hive treasury, which is why Pharos records holder freeze exposure as possible. The exit pillar is the weakest line on the {{grade}} report card, because the defense mechanism converts holders into the very asset they may be fleeing. The durable constraint is that every protocol {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} pays out in HIVE, so its dollar value depends on HIVE's market depth at the moment of exit.

jpyc-jpyc-v1.title: The Legacy JPYC Series
jpyc-jpyc-v1.text: JPY Coin v1 is the original JPYC token series, issued from 2021 as a prepaid payment instrument under Japan's Payment Services Act and tracked separately from the current funds-transfer JPYC. Yen paid in advance was issued 1:1 as tokens backed by JPYC Inc.'s yen reserves, but the tokens were non-refundable to cash by design, usable only for payments and free transfers. JPYC Inc. ended new issuance and exchange support on June 1, 2025, as the revised Payment Services Act took effect, and moved to the redeemable funds-transfer token. Existing balances on Ethereum, Polygon and Gnosis can still be spent and transferred but have no primary issuance path and no cash exit. Pharos keeps v1 frozen as the historical legacy series, and its remaining control risk sits in the Ethereum contract, whose owner key can still mint arbitrary amounts.

nxusd-nereus.title: The Nereus CDP Dollar
nxusd-nereus.text: NXUSD is a crypto-backed debt token minted through Nereus Finance on Avalanche and Polygon via {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics. Pharos prices it from a low-volume fallback feed, and the token has drifted on both sides of par, including a discount of several hundred basis points in July 2026. Those episodes were short enough to leave the peg score intact, so the {{grade}} overall grade comes from structure instead. Economic control is the weakest pillar: minting is economically unbounded, and the Cauldron markets price collateral through single-source or laggy oracle routes with no common freshness check. Exit sits close behind because no holder redemption route is documented, and the borrower-repayment path is not open to ordinary holders. The reserve stack is modeled as {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} lending positions across more than twenty debt-bearing Avalanche markets, but Nereus publishes no per-market collateral weights, so the notional backing depends on collateral volatility and {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}}. The durable constraint is that holders have no exit of their own, so the peg rests on borrowers repaying and liquidators acting.

wemix-dollar-wemix.title: The WEMIX Ecosystem Dollar
wemix-dollar-wemix.text: WEMIX Dollar was the WEMIX ecosystem's issuer-managed dollar, described as fully backed by USDC in the WEMIX3.0 Treasury with the DIOS stabilizer holding the peg. In April 2026 the WEMIX Foundation moved ecosystem dollar activity to bridged USDC.e, withdrew its liquidity from WEMIX$ pools and ended swap support across WEMIX.Fi and WEMIX PLAY. Holders kept a conversion route through the WEMIX$ Module and a longer claim window for discontinued pools, and Pharos froze the listing on 2026-07-11. The record did not close there. WEMIX disclosed that dormant DIOS and AMA ownership was seized on 2026-07-26, enabling about 5.23 million unauthorized WEMIX$ to be minted and about 723,000 USDC.e to be removed. Pharos found no post-incident reconciliation of supply against reserves. Minting was always controlled by a single owner address with no documented supply bound, on a chain Pharos does not index. The durable constraint is that the remaining float and its backing cannot be reconciled from any source Pharos can read.

suiusde-sui.title: Sui Ethena-Style Synthetic Dollar
suiusde-sui.text: suiUSDe is Sui's Ethena-whitelabel synthetic dollar, built on USDe's design. Ethena's whitelabel transparency feed identifies the backing as predominantly USDe with a smaller USDC share, held across Anchorage and Coinbase custody wallets and a Sui mint-redeem wallet, so the reserve inherits USDe's {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} hedging, {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} execution, off-exchange {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and exchange dependency. Deployment control is concentrated on Sui: a single admin role holder also controls the package upgrade path. Pharos's peg tracking has recorded no depeg events for the coin as of this review. Minting and redemption run through USDC only, priced by a single Pyth feed and gated by eligibility, with no comparable secondary route reviewed. The {{grade}} overall grade sits between backing, the strongest pillar, and that thin, permissioned exit.

vcred-vcred.title: Hemi Token With a Declared Peg Only
vcred-vcred.text: VCRED is a Hemi ERC-20 whose verified source declares a U.S. dollar peg, but Pharos's October 2026 identity review found nothing in the contract to hold it there. The token has no collateral, NAV, oracle or {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} logic: the owner can mint without limit, and holder burns destroy tokens without paying anything out. That owner is a 1-of-2 Safe with no modules or guard, which is why economic control is the weakest pillar on a {{grade}} card. The linked vcred.trade site describes AI and perpetual-futures market-making vaults and staking for portfolio access, but it does not tie those products to this contract or publish mint and redemption terms. Pharos has therefore withdrawn the earlier credit-fund reading and carries the backing as wholly unverified rather than as an observed portfolio. Transfers are permissionless because the bytecode has no freeze or blacklist function. No reviewed DEX venue or exit route exists, so a holder's way out is undisclosed. The constraint is identity: until the issuer binds an economic mechanism to this address, the dollar peg exists only as a declaration in the source code.

mai-qidao.title: CDP Dollar With a Stranded Fantom Loan Book
mai-qidao.text: MAI is a multi-collateral {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar whose most important number is the share of its loan book that no longer functions. An on-chain sweep of 71 QiDao vault contracts across twelve chains found roughly 2.1 million MAI of recorded vault debt, and about 72% of it sits in fifteen Fantom markets where every price source reverts. Because the price call fails, {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, collateral withdrawal and new borrowing all revert with it: this is Multichain-era debt that cannot be cleared, only waited out. QiDao's transparency dashboard carries those Fantom liabilities as isolated, and its homepage says the Fantom tokens return to holders once an unnamed dispute is resolved, with no date or mechanism given. Only Base and Polygon are described as fully live. The markets that do still price read exactly one Chainlink feed with no staleness check, no heartbeat enforcement and no fallback, which Pharos treats as a weak oracle branch. No deployment carries a stability pool or insurance fund, and some underwater vaults cannot be liquidated at all, because the collateral payout underflows before the keeper can be paid. Economic control is the weakest pillar on the card, and the {{grade}} overall grade reflects a loan book whose working part is the smaller one.

spusd-soulpeg.title: Wrapped sUSDC receipt on BNB Chain
spusd-soulpeg.text: spUSD is SoulPeg's freely transferable BNB Chain wrapper around a soul-bound sUSDC receipt; SoulPeg's operator routes the USDC behind that receipt into Venus lending markets. Pharos records the wrapper's immediate backing as that single sUSDC receipt. What sits behind the receipt is unresolved: Pharos has no verified Venus allocation, current underlying portfolio or native Circle USDC identity for it. Unwrapping returns sUSDC, not USDC. The sUSDC-to-USDC step is an owner- or operator-controlled call that depends on available reserves, so Pharos models no {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route a holder can exercise.  The token's mint function checks only a role and a nominal one-billion-token ceiling, an externally owned admin key can grant that role, and an active burner role can burn tokens from any holder. Weak control and exit pillars together produce the {{grade}} overall grade. Holders depend on the operator both for supply discipline and for conversion back to USDC.

inalpha-nest.title: A Dust-Sized Nest Credit Vault
inalpha-nest.text: inALPHA is the share token of Nest Credit's original Alpha vault, a NAV-priced BoringVault designed to hold tokenized RWAs and private-credit and trade-finance positions behind a buffer of yield-bearing stablecoins and nTBILL. It references a dollar base but behaves like a vault share, so Pharos marks it {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} and NAV-style rather than a par stablecoin. The vault has since been emptied. On February 19, 2026, a queued {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} on Plume burned about 9.96 million shares from two holders for roughly 10.09 million pUSD, and Pharos's October 2026 contract reads found under two shares left, all on Ethereum. Nest's current API lists a new nALPHA vault at a different address. Pharos suspended live reserve reads on September 9, 2026, because the reported NAV and positions no longer reconcile and the accountant price was last set on February 23. With no reviewed reserve composition, the {{grade}} report card scores backing on mechanism evidence alone. Control is concentrated: shares mint only through an authorized Teller, and the 3-of-6 Safe that owns the vault can burn shares from any holder. The durable constraint is that a vault share is only as informative as its accountant price, and this one stopped updating in February.

eusd-telcoin.title: The Telcoin Bank Dollar
eusd-telcoin.text: Telcoin eUSD is a bank-issued dollar token from Telcoin Digital Asset Bank, operating under a Nebraska digital-asset depository charter. Reserve disclosure is thinner than the charter suggests: the customer agreement permits dollars at FDIC-insured banks, Treasuries, agency paper and other assets Nebraska law allows, held in segregated accounts, yet names no reserve bank, publishes no weights and points to no eUSD-specific independent report. That gap makes backing the weakest pillar on a card graded {{grade}} overall. Exit is the strongest, graded on the bank's own 1:1 redemption rail through KYC and banking partners including Battle Creek State Bank. Since June 2026, US residents can also open a Telcoin Wallet bank account tied to their eUSD balance. On Ethereum, Base and Polygon a 3-of-6 Safe holds minting and admin roles and a 2-of-7 Safe controls beacon upgrades; on Solana one issuer account holds both mint and freeze authority. No reconciliation between minted supply and reserves has been established. The trust boundary is the bank: holders get a chartered issuer and a clean peg record, but take the reserve mix largely on contract terms.

money-defi-money.title: The defi.money Stablecoin
money-defi-money.text: MONEY is defi.money's crvUSD-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar on Arbitrum, Optimism, and Base: borrowers deposit approved crypto collateral, and LLAMMA soft-{{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} bands convert it as prices move. Pharos reads that collateral from a live on-chain census of the market contracts rather than from issuer statements, and the book is mostly ETH and Lido's wstETH, with smaller custodied-BTC slices. The project itself is in sunset: defi.money ended team and interface support in May 2025, leaving the contracts open for direct position management. Economic control is the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card. The same 3-of-7 Safe owns the token on all three chains and can authorize new minters, and the token's mint function checks only that authorization, not collateral or the controllers' debt ceilings. Overcollateralized loans therefore back the supply only as long as that Safe adds no minter outside the CDP path. Each market prices its collateral through a single Chainlink-based EMA path.

fusd-freedom-dollar.title: The Zano Privacy Dollar
fusd-freedom-dollar.text: FUSD is a Zano privacy-chain dollar token minted against staked ZANO reserves, with no Pharos-supported chain {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} and no contract Pharos can attach, so reserve sync cannot run and the record rests on the issuer's own disclosures. Those disclosures are a self-reported dashboard showing the ZANO reserve wallet, the fUSD held back in reserve, and a stated coverage ratio, plus a view-only path for watching the reserve wallet directly. What the on-chain record adds is less comforting. Issuance is a consensus-level EMIT operation that a single asset-owner key can sign up to a ceiling far above circulation, and the white paper's DAO and over-collateralization language is an off-chain operating policy that Zano consensus never checks. Supply integrity was tested in September 2026, when the issuer reported unauthorized fUSD created through a Zano inflation bug, said it would absorb the losses, and asked users to pause fUSD activity pending a patched chain. An issuer-linked market-making bot source is now public, but its live operators, pricing configuration and fallback behavior are unverified, so the oracle path is still reviewed as opaque. With no independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} or verifiable {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} disclosures, the {{grade}} overall grade is bounded by that opaque oracle topology and by an exit that only a ZANO-denominated market can provide.

fusd-finchain.title: A Rebasing Bermuda Dollar
fusd-finchain.text: FinChain Dollar is a {{term:yield-bearing}}rebasing{{/term}} dollar that FinChain describes as issued under a Bermuda Monetary Authority licence and backs with tokenized {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} shares. The token targets a fixed $1 value while balances rebase daily, so yield shows up as more FUSD instead of a rising price. The reserve is now visible on-chain: Pharos's pinned read finds three fund tokens, about half in a Finloop token referencing a BNY Mellon liquidity fund and a quarter each in Taikang and ChinaAMC tokenized classes, matching the issuer's published ratios. Those are issuer-marked values with no independent reconciliation to the funds' underlying holdings, and an exact-name search of the BMA register returned no FinChain record, which Pharos treats as unresolved rather than proof either way. The {{grade}} overall grade has all three pillars in a narrow low band, with economic control the weakest: issuer-administered gateways on five EVM chains mint without a cap behind zero-delay upgrade admins. Exit is eligibility-gated, and holders redeem for USDT rather than dollars within up to three business days. The peg has tracked par since launch; every layer behind it is attested only by the issuer.

zsd-zephyr-protocol.title: Zephyr's ZEPH-Reserve Dollar
zsd-zephyr-protocol.text: Zephyr Stable Dollar is a Djed-inspired reserve-backed dollar on Zephyr's Monero-derived private chain, minted and redeemed against the protocol's native ZEPH reserve with reserve-ratio constraints intended to preserve {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}. Pharos sources ZSD supply and the reserve ratio from Zephyr's own scanner API, since the chain is not a supported contract path, and keeps the reserve slice high risk because the backing asset is volatile native ZEPH. Zephyr's self-reported snapshots have recently shown several times the ZSD liability in ZEPH, which is why backing is the strongest of the three pillars. Economic control is the weakest line on the {{grade}} card: every node validates pricing records against a single hard-coded RSA key controlled by the Zephyr foundation and may reuse the last accepted price for up to ten blocks, so one signing authority sits under every mint, redemption, and reserve-ratio gate. There is no admin mint path and no standing address blacklist. The 2025 audit hard forks still count: they halted transfers and invalidated unmigrated balances, so Pharos records freeze exposure as possible. The failure domain is chain consensus, its release process, and its oracle input.

zys-zephyr-protocol.title: The Zephyr Yield Share
zys-zephyr-protocol.text: Zephyr Yield Share is the NAV-style {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper for Zephyr's ZSD yield reserve, tracked separately from base ZSD so that protocol yield is attributed to the token that actually earns it. ZYS supply, price, and APY come from Zephyr Scanner because CoinGecko and DefiLlama do not expose the wrapper as a market row. Each share is a consensus-level claim on the ZSD yield reserve, minted and redeemed through native MINT_YIELD and REDEEM_YIELD transactions with no admin mint route and no standing address blacklist. Freeze exposure is still recorded as possible, because the 2025 audit hard forks halted transfers and invalidated unmigrated yield-share balances. The {{grade}} overall grade is a ceiling rather than the wrapper's own arithmetic: a child cannot rate above the ZSD it requires, and ZYS inherits Zephyr's private-chain and volatile ZEPH-collateral risk through that dependency. Economic control is the weakest pillar for the same reason as ZSD, a single hard-coded oracle signing key under the yield-reserve accrual, while the wrapper's own reserve review covers only the ZSD yield reserve and leaves the ZEPH collateral beneath it to ZSD's card.

iusd-indigo-protocol.title: The Cardano Synthetic Dollar
iusd-indigo-protocol.text: iUSD is Indigo Protocol's synthetic dollar on Cardano, minted against overcollateralized {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} vaults of ADA and DAO-whitelisted native tokens, with governed peg-stability modules that can mint or redeem against approved stablecoins. Its risk profile is a classic crypto-CDP profile: collateral volatility against the {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} ratio, {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} execution through per-asset Stability Pools, oracle quality, and DAO governance all matter. Pharos now reads the composition from Indigo's public CDP index and Koios supply: at the September 2026 review roughly nine tenths of iUSD debt sat on ADA collateral, a sliver on NIGHT, and a residual of several percent could not be attributed to individual vaults or the USDCx peg module, so it is carried as unresolved rather than normalised away. The {{grade}} report card is weakest on exit, and economic control is held down by an oracle topology that relies on a single Pyth Lazer feed per branch with no documented fallback. The peg record has stayed clean for as long as Pharos has tracked it. The durable constraint is that iUSD is only as liquid and as well-priced as the Cardano venues and feeds beneath it.

cdp-enosys.title: Flare's CDP Experiment
cdp-enosys.text: CDP is Enosys Loans' Flare-native dollar, minted against FXRP, wFLR, sFLR, and stXRP vaults priced by the Flare Time Series Oracle. The mechanism is a Liquity V2 friendly fork: user-set borrow rates, a Stability Pool for liquidations, and redemptions against the lowest-rate positions when CDP trades below its dollar peg. That peg engine shows in the backing pillar, the strongest line on the {{grade}} card. The other two pillars sit far lower. Exit is held down because no reviewed DEX route matches the supply, and economic control is the weakest: the token proxy's owner, a 2-of-6 Safe at the last review, keeps branch-registration powers that leave holder-balance intervention possible, an EOA owns the proxy admin, and the oracle connector discards the FTSO timestamp and enforces no maximum age, so a stale price never triggers branch shutdown. FXRP, itself an agent-collateralized XRP representation, made up most of the collateral at the last review, so Flare collateral depth is the other standing exposure. The design is mechanically legible, but the admin keys and the oracle path decide how far that legibility protects a holder.

luausd-lumi-finance.title: The Lumi Floor-Dollar
luausd-lumi-finance.text: Lumi Finance LUAUSD is a dollar-referenced token on Arbitrum tied to LUA floor-price and protocol-owned liquidity mechanics rather than 1:1 fiat {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, so Pharos marks it as a NAV-style asset with exotic collateral. Lumi's current documentation says circulating LUAUSD can be exchanged for USDT 1:1, yet the token has traded persistently below $1. The backing split is unpublished: Pharos models the reserve as one very-high-risk envelope of LUA collateral and USDT/USDC protocol-owned liquidity because Lumi does not disclose the weights. The token is direct, non-upgradeable code with no freeze or blacklist function, but minting is an owner-only call behind a 3-of-5 Safe with no cap, so issuance is effectively unbounded. Since September 24, 2026 Pharos has held LUAUSD in quarantine: CoinGecko has no coin page, DefiLlama returns no price, and its only venue, an Arbitrum Curve pool, carried a few thousand dollars of effective liquidity with no daily volume. Without an admissible price, the floor-price claim cannot be checked against a market, and no third-party {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} fills the gap.

susd-solayer.title: Solayer Token-2022 Treasury Dollar
susd-solayer.text: Solayer sUSD is a Solana Token-2022 interest-bearing dollar whose balances grow from Treasury-bill yield instead of staying as a static par token. Since November 2025 its sole reserve instrument has been OpenEden's cUSDO, a compounding wrapper of the USDO stablecoin issued by OpenEden Digital, with Adam Eve Capital managing the underlying bills, held through Solayer's qualified liquidity providers. That makes sUSD a stablecoin backed by another stablecoin, with the Treasury exposure one layer further down. Solayer workflows handle minting, the interest extension handles balance growth, and the mint, freeze, and rate authorities resolve to an upgradeable Solayer program with no timelock on upgrades. Pharos has no runtime evidence for the redemption route, so the card cannot score a same-size way out. Backing scores somewhat higher; the reserve asset and obligor are identified, but the Treasury-fund mix, custodian split, and provider balances are not published. The peg record is clean on limited price coverage, and the {{grade}} overall grade reflects that unmeasured exit behind a single-entity issuer. Whether a yield-passing token of this kind counts as a payment stablecoin under the GENIUS Act is unresolved.

usx-dforce.title: Overcollateralized on Paper
usx-dforce.text: dForce USD is now a read-only archive: Pharos froze USX on 2026-07-18 after it slid to roughly $0.39 with on-chain liquidity measured in tens of thousands of dollars and daily volume under $10. The {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style design launched in 2021 and peaked above $205M in mid-2022, but it never truly recovered from that bear market. Legacy debt positions on the dForce/Unitus lending protocol left circulating USX without a credible par-{{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route, and the discount widened from cents to a chasm over four years. The terminal slide came in 2026: below $0.75 in February, below $0.45 by April, and near $0.39 by the July freeze, with the DF governance token near zero and no published remediation plan to point at. Pharos's epitaph states the result: {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} on paper, unredeemable in practice. Collateral a holder cannot claim at par does not function as a backstop.

home-homecoin.title: The Property-Lien Dollar
home-homecoin.text: HOME is HomeCoin's dollar stablecoin backed by U.S. home-loan liens and property-backed receivables originated through the HomeCoin/Bacon lending process, rather than cash, T-bills, or crypto collateral. The deployed Pool16 contract routes USDC/HOME swaps through Curve with a caller-set minimum output rather than guaranteeing 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, and HomeCoin publishes no current holder redemption terms, capacity or fees. Behind that sits a foreclosure right, which is not the same thing as exit liquidity. Reserve risk is dominated by mortgage-lien {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} quality rather than cash {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}: the issuer publishes no current loan tape, valuation, or independent report, so Pharos scores the entire collateral category as undisclosed. Pharos marks HOME yield-bearing on the basis of home-loan payment distributions. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down on two fronts that score equally low. Exit has no documented same-notional route, and economic control rests on a 3-of-5 Safe that both services the pool and can upgrade the token's proxy with no recorded delay. The peg record has stayed close to par. The durable constraint is that a lien portfolio cannot be turned into dollars on demand.

cdxusd-cod3x.title: The Facilitator-Minted Dollar
cdxusd-cod3x.text: cdxUSD was Cod3x's GHO-style credit dollar on Base, minted and burned by protocol-permissioned Facilitators against strategy-managed crypto and stablecoin collateral. In practice one Facilitator did all of it: a 3-of-9 Safe labeled Multisig, with its bucket level equal to the entire supply and a 24-hour timelock owning the token. No reviewed source published the facilitator collateral inventory or a coverage ratio, so Pharos carried the backing as a single undisclosed high-risk slice, and holders had no burn-for-reserve {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route of their own. That design was tested on August 27, 2026, when the price fell below $0.90; it went through $0.54 the next day and bottomed near $0.25 on September 17. Supply did not move during the collapse, holding at 6,150,000 cdxUSD, so no token was burned at par to defend the peg. By then Cod3x's site and documentation described only AI trading agents, and the deepest executable side of the remaining pools held about $1,600. Pharos froze cdxUSD on September 23, 2026 as an abandoned asset. Without a holder redemption route or a disclosed reserve, the last pool price was the only exit the token ever offered.

susd-hedgecore.title: HedgeCore Venus Yield Wrapper
susd-hedgecore.text: HedgeCore sUSD is a BSC yield wrapper minted from USDC and routed through Venus lending. The reserve dependency is explicit: USDC enters HedgeCore's strategy layer, earns through Venus, and comes back through operator-triggered reward mints and operator-controlled exits. HedgeCore's documentation describes the token as soul-bound, but the verified contract executes ordinary transfers except where a wrapper lock is active, and the wrapper owner can burn a named holder's balance without allowance. That owner is a single externally owned account, which can also grant a minting role whose issuance requires no USDC deposit. HedgeCore publishes no current position inventory or reconciliation of supply to vault assets, so backing scores barely above exit. Early redemption is operator-controlled, the hUSDC wrapper only opens one direction, and Pharos finds no route an ordinary holder can use to redeem. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects a clean peg record sitting on an undisclosed exit and a single-key admin.

usd3-reserve-protocol.title: The Reserve Basket Dollar
usd3-reserve-protocol.text: USD3 is a Reserve Protocol RToken/DTF that turns yield-bearing wrappers into a dollar basket with four upstream dependencies. The backing is split evenly across Savings USDS, Aave USDC, wrapped Compound USDCv3 and a Steakhouse USDC vault, so holders are buying a governed portfolio of stablecoin yield rather than a single clean reserve. That basket is the strongest part of the card: every constituent contract is identified, Pharos's on-chain checks confirmed that the Aave and Steakhouse positions redeem into USDC, and Reserve publishes a self-reported real-time reserve feed. Anyone can mint by depositing the basket and redeem back into it, and governance changes pass through a three-day timelock that a guardian Safe can cancel. Exit is the weakest of the three pillars, because Pharos finds no comparable same-notional route beside basket {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, and the float is small. RSR stakers absorb and manage losses, so parameter choices and collateral onboarding matter as much as the assets themselves. The {{grade}} overall grade is bounded by the route out rather than the reserve: a holder who wants dollars still has to unwind four positions to get them.

sofid-sofi.title: National-bank dollar with Fed-held reserves
sofid-sofi.text: SoFiUSD is the first stablecoin issued by a U.S. national bank. SoFi Bank, N.A. holds its reserves as cash, mostly in its Federal Reserve master account, and keeps the interest on them. BitGo runs the 1:1 mint and redemption infrastructure. Distribution came first: after a December 2025 enterprise launch on Ethereum, the SoFi app opened retail access on 27 May 2026 to nearly 15 million members, and Mastercard settlement went live on 22 September 2026 as SoFi migrates its $25 billion card program to the token. Pharos re-admitted the listing on 29 September 2026, once CoinGecko and DefiLlama published a circulating supply that matched on-chain totals on Ethereum and Solana; it now stands at {{supplyUsd}}. The {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} record has since caught up. Deloitte examined the 31 August 2026 reserve report, which shows all reserves in USD cash, with a small balance in a BitGo fiduciary account at an unnamed commercial bank, and reconciles them against redeemable tokens. It does not establish that the Fed-held cash is legally segregated or bankruptcy-remote from SoFi. Exit is the weakest pillar and the main drag on the {{grade}} overall grade, because Pharos has not established the cost or settlement terms of issuer redemption.

usdb-bridge.title: Stripe's Closed-Loop Dollar
usdb-bridge.text: Bridge's USDB was Stripe's first stablecoin rail: launched in May 2025, it powered Stripe's Stablecoin Financial Accounts in 101 countries, backed 1:1 by cash and BlackRock {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}}. Its role narrowed on September 30, 2026, when Bridge launched Open USD as its open-loop token and Stripe began listing only OUSD and USDC for stablecoin balances. Bridge's documentation now keeps USDB in its API for closed-loop use and names no sunset date. The regulatory picture is narrower than the charter news suggests: the current issuer, Bridge Building Inc., operates under money-transmitter permissions, and the conditional OCC approval from February 2026 covers a proposed national trust bank rather than today's USDB. Bridge's Open Issuance platform separately mints branded dollars such as MoneyGram's MGUSD and Deel's DLUSD. DefiLlama began tracking a Tempo deployment as USDBridge in September 2026, including a one-day supply jump on September 19 that came with no Bridge statement. Pharos delisted USDB on October 25 2026 as out of scope: Bridge's documentation says the token is not traded on the public market or transferable to third parties, and is usable only within Bridge wallets and payment rails.

hkdap-anchorpoint.title: Anchorpoint's HKMA-Licensed HKD Stablecoin
hkdap-anchorpoint.text: HKDAP is Anchorpoint's HKD stablecoin, issued under an HKMA stablecoin issuer licence effective April 10 2026. Standard Chartered Trustee (Hong Kong) Limited holds its HKD reserve assets on trust for holders. It has been live on Ethereum since August 12, when Anchorpoint's own release opened Beta Access through authorised distributors for institutions, corporate clients and professional investors. Supply reached 103.1 million HKDAP across 14 holder addresses on November 1 2026, roughly a hundred times the late-September float. About 87.0 million of that was minted on October 30. The same day Anchorpoint announced exploratory partnerships with Mastercard and Visa, starting with settlement options for card issuers, but gave no launch date or volumes. No accepted source returns a price for HKDAP, which keeps the coin outside Pharos runtime coverage. Anchorpoint's unaudited weekly figures for October 30 show reserves slightly above circulation; independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} is promised only after full launch. BlockSec's August 14 review of the deployed contract found that the KYC proof is discarded, so any proof, including an empty string, passes. A single key can mint, burn, pause or freeze, two keys control all upgrades and roles, and no timelock guards any of those powers. Build artifacts point to a pre-production deployment. The durable constraint is that contract: until it is upgraded or replaced, the licensed token runs on code carrying those findings.

hkd-hsbc.title: HSBC's PayMe-Bound HKD Stablecoin
hkd-hsbc.text: HSBC RedCoin is an HKD stablecoin available through PayMe on HSBC's private permissioned chain. The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited launched it on October 23, 2026 under HKMA licence FRS02. Distribution runs through the bank's own channels, and HSBC Digital Assets Custody provides safekeeping. HSBC describes 1:1 backing by segregated HKD-denominated reserves and redemption at par through permitted channels, subject to its terms. The product page now publishes issuer-reported circulation and reserve figures, alongside a whitepaper, a reserve assets policy and redemption terms. These documents are the issuer's account of the backing, not independent verification of public-chain supply. The first independent attestation is expected after Q4 2026; this review found no published monthly series. Pharos keeps RedCoin in pre-launch until public on-chain issuance and a verifiable price and supply path exist.

okrw-hashed.title: The Native Won of Hashed's Maroo L1
okrw-hashed.text: OKRW is the planned Korean Won stablecoin of Maroo, the Layer 1 that Hashed Open Finance built specifically to host it, where it doubles as the network's native fee token. Maroo is presented as the first sovereign L1 purpose-built for KRW stablecoins, with a dual-track design: regulated activity passes pre-approval and compliance checks, while open-path activity stays permissionless. The testnet went live in May 2026 with OKRW as its native token, and mainnet is targeted before the end of 2026. The design specifies a KRW peg, but the issuer and reserve arrangements are not yet decided and no redemption terms are published, so there is nothing to score. The durable constraint is that the token's credibility will rest on reserve and redemption terms that are not yet public.

arc-anq.title: A Rupee Stablecoin Without a Green Light
arc-anq.text: ARC is Anq's proposed Indian rupee stablecoin, announced with Polygon in November 2025 as India's first regulated INR token and designed for a 1:1 peg backed by cash, fixed deposits and Indian government securities. The design keeps the token inside India's regulated payments perimeter: issuance runs through business accounts, transfers are whitelisted, and Uniswap v4 whitelisting carries the compliance check onto a public chain. It is pitched as a two-tier complement to the RBI's digital rupee and as a brake on USD liquidity outflow. The tentative January 2026 debut passed with no RBI confirmation and no live supply. In July 2026 the RBI told a Parliamentary Standing Committee that it favors barring banks and regulated entities from private stablecoins, rupee-backed ones included. With no source supporting a 2026 launch, Pharos removed the launch expectation in September 2026. The architecture is settled on paper; ARC's constraint is whether the RBI will let a private rupee stablecoin operate beside its CBDC.

brl-b3.title: B3's Settlement Real, Still in Testing
brl-b3.text: BRL-B3 is the pre-launch real settlement stablecoin from B3, Latin America's largest stock exchange, built for its tokenized {{term:rwa}}real-world-asset{{/term}} platform. Brazilian press and B3's digital-assets director have named Polygon as its chain, and backing is planned to be mainly cash and Tesouro Nacional securities. B3's own second-quarter results note confirmed in August 2026 that infrastructure testing had begun. The launch has slipped repeatedly. A first-half 2026 window passed, the August-to-September window B3's director named at Expert XP passed with no deployment, and at B3 Week on September 15 the company framed readiness for new use cases, including tokenized collateral, for the start of 2027. Pharos moved the expected launch to 2027 on September 27. On October 8 a B3 executive went further: B3RL will not settle the first tokenized shares targeted for early 2027, and the settlement currency for those trades is still undecided between stablecoins, tokenized deposits and a possible Drex link. Pharos moved the launch phase back to testnet on October 18. The constraint has changed shape: B3RL no longer has a confirmed first job on B3's own platform, so its launch now depends on B3 choosing it over those alternatives.

usdf-flipcash.title: Coinbase's White-Label Dollar
usdf-flipcash.text: Flipcash's USDF is the first stablecoin minted through Coinbase's Custom Stablecoins platform, a stablecoin-as-a-service product that lets a business launch a branded dollar backed 1:1 by USDC. Coinbase, not Flipcash, is the issuing entity: it handles issuance, {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, custody, and compliance, while Flipcash uses USDF as the settlement asset for its user-created currencies. The dependency chain is explicit: USDF is a wrapper around USDC, so its backing is only as good as Circle's reserve stack, and its existence depends on Coinbase continuing to run the platform. USDF went live on Solana in May 2026 with Coinbase Onramp access. Pharos's October 25 review recorded a small Jupiter pool and a DefiLlama quote for the mint; neither is an admitted price source. An October 26 follow-up could not confirm which market the quote comes from, so Pharos lists USDF as launched but awaiting data while the quote's source is unresolved. No independent monthly reserve attestation for USDF has been located. Its operating dependency remains Coinbase's issuance and conversion service, with USDC underneath the branded token.

krw-imbank.title: Bank-Led Won Pilot on Kaia
krw-imbank.text: KRW-iM is iM Bank's pre-launch won stablecoin, which Pharos records as South Korea's first bank-led KRW proof of concept. The original May 2026 pilot with Finger on Kaia leaned on BTQ Technologies' post-quantum cryptography, a security feature rather than a reserve or {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} term. The token itself, iMKRW, has since been issued and transacted on Kaia in two closed pilots: OpenAsset's full-lifecycle test in May, covering issuance, QR payment, merchant settlement and burn, and a Coocon and Beatoz payment-ecosystem test in July. In June iM Bank also joined the Korea-EU Pangea project testing KRW-EUR stablecoin exchange, though iMKRW was not named there. Pharos marks the phase as testnet, but these are private pilots rather than a public network. Production mint, redemption and reserve reporting terms are unpublished, and the production ticker is unconfirmed. Commercial launch is gated on the Digital Asset Basic Act, whose September public hearing fell through after the government bill was delayed.

gldy-streamex.title: The Yield-Bearing Gold Ounce
gldy-streamex.text: GLDY is Streamex's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} tokenized gold ounce on Base: each token represents one troy ounce of bullion, with gold-leasing receivables through Monetary Metals as the source of returns paid in additional gold. Reserve evidence has two strands. An EisnerAmper examination as of March 2026 reported reserve ounces at or above tokens outstanding, and a Chainlink feed on Base publishes the issuer-reported ounce count daily, although that feed transports Streamex's own figures rather than attesting them independently. The main caveat is that the yield comes from issuer-managed gold leasing rather than passive vault storage, so lease-counterparty concentration and bar-level custody allocation remain undisclosed. The exit pillar is the weakest line on the {{grade}} report card: primary-market {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is limited to eligible investors, Streamex can gate large redemptions for up to 12 months while leases roll off, and the route carries no explicit same-notional USD output, so Pharos records the primary exit as undisclosed. Control sits with Streamex through two Safes, a 2-of-3 holding the treasury role and a 3-of-5 holding default admin, after the earlier single-key paths were revoked; an operator role can also freeze addresses and remove holders from the transfer whitelist. GLDY is tracked as a commodity token that Streamex describes as a tokenized security and markets to accredited investors, and that eligibility gate is the durable constraint on the claim.

vnxau-vnx.title: The Liechtenstein Gram-Gold Token
vnxau-vnx.text: VNX Gold is a Liechtenstein gold token from VNX Commodities AG, with each unit representing one gram of allocated physical gold. The newest reserve evidence Pharos holds is AREVA's agreed-upon-procedures report as of 31 December 2025, which reconciled 13,100 tokens across chains to 13,100 gross grams on Philoro Edelmetallhandel AG's custody statement in VNX Commodities AG's name. AREVA did not physically observe the gold or validate its quality, value or legal title. That composition is now older than the methodology's freshness bound, one reason the card is not rated. The exit path has also narrowed. The legacy vnx.li platform suspended exchange operations on 30 June 2026 and allowed remaining-balance withdrawals only until 31 July, and VNX Commodities AG now offers no purchase, sale or custody service, leaving token cancellation to the contractual arrangement. Reviewed physical-redemption evidence exists, but no score-eligible runtime route does. The durable constraint is a reserve report older than the freshness bound and an issuer that no longer runs a trading rail.

xagm-matrixdock.title: Matrixdock's Silver Ounce
xagm-matrixdock.text: Matrixdock's silver token entered the Bureau Veritas programme this year. XAGm's first inclusion involved a full physical count of 66 Good Delivery bars against the parcel ownership list, with no anomalies. The certificate examines the vault as of the end of June, and the card now scores that assurance as stale until the next cycle. The certificate is assets-only: it inspects the metal but does not reconcile it against the XAGm tokens issued. Economic control is the weakest pillar on the card. An operator can add local mint budget manually with only a four-hour request-to-execute delay in the way, and Matrixdock supplies its own mint and redemption quotes. Exit is next: physical {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is documented, but Pharos has compiled no score-eligible runtime route. Together they hold the {{grade}} overall grade down. The larger bar count Matrixdock has published since that inventory is issuer disclosure that no inspection has yet covered.

gramg-token-teknoloji.title: Turkey's Gram-Gold Token
gramg-token-teknoloji.text: GRAMG is Token Teknoloji's one-gram gold claim from Turkey, and the open question is what, exactly, sits behind it: the issuer's product copy says equivalent PAXG is held on-chain, while the same page's FAQ and reserve disclosures describe physical gold at Turkish banks, the Central Bank, and company vaults. No current primary evidence reconciles the two stories. The reserve proof page has its own gaps: the supply widget renders empty, the evidence link points at an Ethereum address while the copy talks about Avalanche, and there is no independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, only the issuer's word at self-reported tier. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} remains unscored because the issuer exposes no reviewed direct-holder redemption schedule. Since mid-July 2026 the coin has been quarantined on Pharos because no permitted runtime source reports a positive circulating supply or market cap. It is a gold token whose backing form is disputed and whose token count is unverifiable.

grams-token-teknoloji.title: Turkey's Gram-Silver Token
grams-token-teknoloji.text: GRAMS is Token Teknoloji's one-gram silver claim, the sibling of its gold product, with proof pages naming physical silver at Kuveyt Türk, VakıfBank, Ziraat Participation, and Akbank. The disclosures conflict: the product page describes company-vault {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} while the shared proof-of-reserves page names the banks, the reserve page reuses the gold token's contract address, and leftover platinum copy points to text carried over from another product page. There is no independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. The live feed Pharos wires up reads token supply on Avalanche, which proves the token exists, not that the silver does. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} stays unmodeled because the issuer exposes no reviewed direct-holder redemption schedule. Since mid-July 2026 the coin has been quarantined on Pharos: no permitted runtime source reports a positive circulating supply or market cap. The durable constraint is evidentiary: no independent source ties the token supply to silver held at a named custodian.

euroe-membrane.title: Redemption-Only EUROe
euroe-membrane.text: EUROe was Membrane Finance's euro e-money token, issued under a Finnish EMI licence from 2023. Paxos completed its acquisition of Membrane in February 2025 to absorb that licence and its EU issuance rails, and as Paxos consolidated its product line the EUROe business was decommissioned. Since May 2026 the platform has been redemption-only, with no new minting or trading, and holders have been told to complete KYC and redeem 1:1 for euros via SEPA through Paxos Issuance Europe. The reserve was described as euro fiat and euro-denominated assets, but the current proof source is the redemption notice itself rather than any continuing reserve report. Pharos still records six issuer-native deployments, from Ethereum to Solana, whose EVM mint and admin roles sit with single keys behind upgradeable contracts with no timelock. Those controls matter only while EUROe remains outstanding, and the residual float is now a small fraction of its peak.

gbpm-mento.title: Mento's CDP Pound
gbpm-mento.text: GBPm is Mento's British pound stablecoin on Celo, minted from {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}} collateralized by USDm with oracle-priced {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, extending Mento's Celo FX set into sterling on a Liquity v2 fork instead of the older shared reserve basket alone. Backing is therefore one tracked stablecoin exposure, USDm, which in turn rests on the shared Mento Reserve, and the public reserve API is a portfolio view, short of a full borrower-position inventory. The {{grade}} overall grade is led by the exit pillar, with Liquity-style redemption and Stability Pool liquidations giving holders a permissionless route out, while economic control is the weakest of the three: a 4-of-6 Mento Safe owns the token and can replace mint logic, and the TroveManager and Stability Pool hold burner and operator roles over any holder balance. The primary risk is dependency on Mento oracles, Celo execution, and USDm collateral quality.

jpym-mento.title: Mento's CDP Yen
jpym-mento.text: JPYm is Mento's yen stablecoin on Celo, minted by borrowers against USDm collateral in a JPYm-specific {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} branch, with a Wormhole representation on Monad. The Mento reserve dashboard exposes the branch's collateral and debt live, so the backing is observable even though it rests on Mento's own dollar and on oracle-priced FX. Exit scores highest of the three pillars: oracle-priced FPMM swaps and CDP {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} give holders a route back into the collateral, though price-dependent withdrawals and normal redemptions are restricted while FX markets are closed.  A 4-of-6 Mento Safe can authorize a new minter that bypasses the CDP collateral checks and can replace the Celo token implementation without delay, and that unbounded-mint finding is the binding cap holding the overall grade at {{grade}}. Supply remains small. The durable constraint is that a yen peg built on dollar collateral and an FX oracle also depends on one Safe's restraint.

chfm-mento.title: Mento's CDP Franc
chfm-mento.text: CHFm is Mento's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-backed Swiss franc stablecoin on Celo, minted by borrowers against USDm collateral rather than fiat reserves, which gives it a very different risk profile from the fiat-backed VCHF. The collateral rows are exposed directly by the Mento reserve API, so the backing path is visible enough for reserve tracking even though the asset is small. {{term:overcollateralization}}Overcollateralization{{/term}} at a 110% minimum ratio and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} through the Stability Pool drive peg maintenance, and the exit pillar leads the card. The {{grade}} overall grade comes from the economic-control pillar, the weakest of the three: the token owner and proxy admin resolve to one 4-of-6 Mento Safe that can authorise a burner able to destroy any holder balance and can replace the implementation without delay. The residual risks are the single SortedOracles CHF/USD feed with no fallback, and the USDm collateral path.

bfusd-binance.title: Binance's Account Dollar
bfusd-binance.text: BFUSD is a Binance account product redeemable inside Binance against USD stablecoins, backed by a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-hedged{{/term}} collateral pool, staked crypto, and a reserve fund, all legally and beneficially owned by Binance, leaving holders with product terms rather than claims. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} runs entirely through Binance-controlled terms that permit fees, limits, delays, and outright suspension, with self-reported, ad-hoc disclosures standing in for independent proof of reserves. Binance does not publish a dated allocation of the pool, so its composition is wholly undisclosed. Pharos delisted the entry in July 2026 as out of scope: BFUSD is a non-withdrawable account balance rather than a transferable production token, so there is no on-chain supply to measure and no independent {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} to verify. BFUSD's durable constraint is that a balance which cannot be withdrawn, transferred or audited gives an outside observer nothing to measure.

pathusd-bridge.title: Tempo's Bridge Dollar
pathusd-bridge.text: pathUSD is the Bridge-issued dollar quote token for Tempo: users mint it by depositing USDC through Bridge-supported flows and redeem it back into USDC through Bridge {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rails, against a reserve Bridge describes as cash, short-dated Treasuries, overnight Treasury repo and money-market-fund exposure, with BlackRock and Fidelity named as custody partners. Bridge's public API reports cash and Treasury totals, and its issuance FAQ says audits and transparency reports will be issued quarterly, but no pathUSD-specific assurance report or instrument-level split has been published, so Pharos scores the composition as an unresolved basket. Exit is the weakest pillar behind the {{grade}} overall grade because Pharos has no reviewed same-notional route through those Bridge rails. Control is concentrated: the issuance proxy's sole administrator, an externally owned account, can upgrade mint logic and raise the supply cap without delay, and a chain-global Tempo blacklist policy applies to every transfer. The same administrator address and blacklist policy also govern Open USD. The peg record is short: since the March 2026 launch, Pharos has recorded one depeg episode, a move of a few hundred basis points in October 2026. The durable constraint is that one Bridge key sits behind both of Tempo's Bridge-issued dollars.

djed-coti.title: Cardano's Reserve-Coin Stable
djed-coti.text: DJED is Cardano's reserve-coin stablecoin: ADA sits in the reserve, DJED is the dollar claim, and SHEN absorbs surplus and volatility inside the protocol's 400% to 800% reserve-ratio band. That design gives the peg a clear mechanical buffer, and the reserve balance is readable at a single Cardano script address, but it also ties the whole system to ADA collateral risk and to the COTI/IOG oracle role. The minting policy is immutable Plutus code rather than a discretionary issuer desk, and there is no holder blacklist or freeze path. The public Tweag review Pharos holds covers pre-launch validator code, not the script deployed today. The {{grade}} overall grade is held back by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three: redemption is permissionless but runs only through the protocol's ADA reserve at a single aggregated ADA/USD rate, with no fiat route and thinner evidence behind it. The durable constraint is that the dollar claim and its buffer both sit in ADA, so a sharp ADA drawdown tests the reserve band and the exit route at the same time.

usdv-solomon.title: Solomon’s Legacy Strategy Dollar
usdv-solomon.text: Solomon's original USDv is a Solana synthetic dollar backed by Ceffu-custodied spot crypto hedged with exchange perpetuals, a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} run by Solomon Labs. It is now a legacy mint in wind-down: Solomon announced that front-end support would end on October 16, 2026, after an October 9 sUSDv unstaking-request deadline, and the token does not convert automatically into the replacement USDv. Supply is visible on-chain, but Pharos cannot currently track the reserves behind it. At its last reviewed observations, the issuer's protocol-data API identified less than a third of reported protocol TVL, and the feed has since switched to describing the replacement mint, so Pharos parked live reserve tracking and serves the last reviewed composition. The only external artefact is an aggregate Ceffu custody attestation dated April 2026. Direct mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are limited to Solomon-approved participants. A 3-of-9 multisig can replace the mint program with no timelock, and minting is economically unbounded. The SPL freeze authority is null, so holder balances cannot be frozen on-chain. What remains outstanding is a transferable claim on a book Solomon no longer reports.

fxd-fathom.title: XDC's Native CDP Dollar
fxd-fathom.text: FXD is Fathom's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-minted dollar on XDC, giving the XDC ecosystem a native {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} dollar backed by XDC and Fathom collateral-pool positions and stabilized by {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}} plus a stability module. Pharos's on-chain read shows the collateral is now mostly PrimeStakedXDC, which the protocol prices 1:1 as XDC without a market exchange-rate feed, and the price path itself runs through a single configured aggregator on a fifteen-minute delay with no secondary feed. Economic control and exit both sit at the bottom of the card and the {{grade}} overall grade follows: one externally owned account owns the ProxyAdmin and can upgrade the token and adapter logic with no delay, and the primary exit is eligibility-gated. The mechanism itself is familiar CDP machinery: mint against collateral, burn to repay, liquidate weak positions, and use a stability module for peg support. The durable constraint is what sits around it: a collateral book concentrated in one XDC staking derivative valued without its own price, guarded by a single upgrade key.

dllr-sovryn.title: Rootstock's Mynt Basket
dllr-sovryn.text: DLLR is Sovryn's BTC-backed dollar on Rootstock, minted 1:1 through the Mynt aggregator against a basket of Rootstock stablecoins that is almost entirely ZUSD with a trace of DOC, and the basket balances can be read on-chain. Both bAssets are BTC-backed {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoins whose own collateral and liquidation risks sit upstream, and the backing pillar still grades reasonably despite the concentration. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three: Mynt {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} returns ZUSD or DOC rather than a same-notional dollar, and Pharos has no viable exit path to score. Governance is the other soft spot. Sovryn's 48-hour timelock can appoint a new manager able to mint DLLR without a deposit or cap, and other burn routes cannot be ruled out, and a GovernorAlpha guardian can change the timelock's admin without a token vote. The residual risks are concentration in Rootstock liquidity, Sovryn governance, and the quality of the underlying BTC-backed stablecoins; opaque {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} is not among them.

xusd-babelfish.title: The Rootstock Stablecoin Basket
xusd-babelfish.text: XUSD is BabelFish's Rootstock basket stablecoin, minted 1:1 from accepted {{term:bridge}}bridged{{/term}} stablecoins and redeemed into them through a basket-level {{term:psm}}PSM-style{{/term}} module with balancing fees. Pharos tracks live branch balances directly from the basket holder, and that read puts Sovryn DLLR at well over half the basket, bridged USDT at most of the rest, and smaller DAI, USDC, and Money on Chain DOC balances behind them. The model is useful but recursive: XUSD inherits the risks of Rootstock {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} liquidity, DLLR's own basket, and BabelFish's balancing fees. Two control facts sit under the card. The token's owner is an upgradeable masset manager that can call a holder-burn function, although whether its current, unverified code can reach arbitrary holders remains unresolved. Its documented custody chain also accounts for only about half of the supply-backing balances, with the rest unlocated. Exit is the weakest pillar: no comparable same-notional route is on file, and no fiat issuer stands behind the basket.

susdd-tron-dao-reserve.title: Savings USDD Wrapper
susdd-tron-dao-reserve.text: sUSDD is a savings wrapper over USDD with no peg mechanism of its own. Users deposit USDD, receive a wrapper whose exchange rate appreciates, and ultimately inherit USDD's reserve, PSM, and redemption assumptions on the way out. The wrapper contract has immutable DSR-style mechanics and no owner or proxy, but the base asset below it carries the main risk. USDD's reserve data in Pharos is self-reported in real time, not independently assured. The card shows the split directly: the wrapper's own exit and control pillars score high, yet the {{grade}} overall grade is capped at the parent USDD score, so sUSDD cannot rate above the coin it wraps.

onyc-onre.title: The Reinsurance NAV Token
onyc-onre.text: ONYC is a Solana NAV token tied to OnRe-managed structured insurance and reinsurance yield rather than a par-value payment stablecoin with cash in a bank account. Its value is meant to accrue from insurance-market collateral returns, with monthly Apex agreed-upon-procedures NAV statements and OnRe's Bermuda segregated-account licensing providing the institutional wrapper. The reserve picture is more conventional than the reinsurance label suggests: OnRe's October 2026 schedule of assets puts more than half the collateral in short-term Treasury bills and just under a quarter in USDG, with the remainder spread across sUSDS, syrupUSDC, Kamino lending positions, sUSDe, USCC and smaller stablecoin and cash balances, while the bound reinsurance contracts sit on top as contingent obligations rather than extra assets. The mint surface runs through an upgradeable Solana program whose upgrade authority is a 4-of-7 Squads multisig with a six-hour timelock. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three: whitelisted holders can redeem on-chain into USDG atomically, but neither the vault's available balance nor the size-dependent liquidity haircut is measured, so Pharos cannot establish a same-notional exit. The durable constraint is an exit that settles instantly but has no measured depth.

apyusd-apyx.title: Apyx Savings Share
apyusd-apyx.text: apyUSD is the ERC-4626 savings wrapper over apxUSD: holders deposit apxUSD, and dividends and preferred-equity yield accrue inside the vault as a rising exchange rate. The wrapper adds no cash layer. Pharos reads its holdings straight from the vault, and all of them are apxUSD, so the reserve underneath is Apyx's Digital Asset Treasury preferred equity and liquidity buffers rather than Treasury bills. That parent fell below the dollar when Strategy's preferred stock traded under par in June 2026, and Pharos still records it in an active depeg. A child cannot rate above its required parent, so the parent's ceiling sets the {{grade}} overall grade, and compounding inside the vault cannot lift it. The Chainlink CCIP representations on Base, BNB Chain and Solana carry controls whose authority and economic semantics Pharos has not resolved. A savings share compounds on whatever the parent is worth, and here the parent's discount comes first.

susd1plus-lorenzo.title: Lorenzo Strategy Dollar
susd1plus-lorenzo.text: sUSD1+ is a non-rebasing share in Lorenzo's USD1+ on-chain traded fund on BNB Chain, accruing yield through unit NAV across a managed mix of RWA, CeFi quantitative and DeFi strategies. Deposits arrive in USD1, USDT or USDC, and withdrawals settle in USD1 at settlement-day NAV, normally over a three-to-six-day cycle that Lorenzo can extend. Lorenzo publishes no weights for those inputs or strategy sleeves, so Pharos treats the whole portfolio as unclassified rather than crediting it as USD1. The strategy layer is equally opaque: no {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} distribution, exchange margin, liquidation data or funded first-loss capital is disclosed.  A 2-of-3 Safe holds the vault manager's top roles with no timelock, and can assign a direct minter with no amount cap or replace the upgradeable logic. Exit scores little better, since the queued withdrawal has no established access, capacity or execution evidence. The parent USD1 rating sets a ceiling, but sUSD1+ already scores well beneath it. The durable constraint is that a holder owns a NAV share in an undisclosed portfolio, settled on the operator's schedule.

savusd-avant.title: Avant Staked Dollar
savusd-avant.text: savUSD is Avant's staked avUSD receipt, with the exchange rate rising as the senior tranche earns from actively managed market-neutral strategies. Avant places a Reserve Fund and the junior avUSDx tranche ahead of savUSD in the loss order, and Pennyworks supplies the weekly NAV calculation. Unstaking has a one-day cooldown with no yield, and the final exit still inherits avUSD's 1:1 USDC {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} process. That inheritance also sets the {{grade}} card: a wrapper cannot rate above its required parent, so avUSD's score caps savUSD below what its own pillars would earn.

steakusdc-steakhouse.title: Steakhouse USDC Lending Vault
steakusdc-steakhouse.text: Steakhouse USDC is an immutable Morpho Vault V2 share over USDC, so the base dollar is Circle's but the yield comes from borrowers in Steakhouse-curated Morpho markets. The vault leaves Circle's reserve story unchanged and adds curator choices, lending collateral, and withdrawal liquidity on top of it. User shares mint only against USDC deposits, so Pharos inherits the underlying USDC issuer risk and tracks the Steakhouse governance surface separately. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by a structural cap: Pharos finds the vault's own mint-control identity on reviewed paths of two independent tracked root liabilities, at deployment exposure of 25% or more. Withdrawals draw on idle USDC and a configured liquidity adapter, so exits still depend on available Morpho liquidity.

bbqusdc-steakhouse.title: Smokehouse's Higher-Risk USDC Vault
bbqusdc-steakhouse.text: Smokehouse USDC is Steakhouse's high-yield MetaMorpho vault over USDC, built to lend into Morpho markets with wider and more exotic borrower collateral than the Prime line. The wrapper is an immutable ERC-4626 vault with no proxy, minting shares against USDC deposits and as performance fees. A 5-of-10 Steakhouse Safe can steer allocations and fees but cannot create base dollars or block a holder's transfer. That structure gives economic control the strongest line on the {{grade}} card. The exposure depends on collateral a curator chooses and on USDC, whose reserve quality and freeze power the vault inherits from Circle. The binding limit on the grade is a structural cap rather than the parent ceiling: this vault shares the instant ERC-4626 redemption rail and a critical control identity with dozens of other reviewed assets. Shares redeem against whatever USDC the Morpho markets can release. The durable constraint is exotic collateral chosen by a curator, behind an exit that depends on Morpho markets unwinding faster than depositors leave.

srusde-strata.title: Strata's Senior USDe Tranche
srusde-strata.text: srUSDe is Strata's senior ERC-4626 tranche over a strategy that stakes USDe into Ethena's sUSDe, with the junior jrUSDe tranche taking first loss before senior holders are touched. That subordination gives senior capital principal protection and a benchmark-rate yield floor, but a junior-exhausting event can still impair senior principal. It is still not a plain dollar: exits depend on Strata tranche liquidity and settlement rules rather than 1:1 issuer redemption, and Pharos has no exact DEX or redemption route observation for the token. That is why exit is the weakest of the three pillars and the main drag on the {{grade}} overall grade. The token is an upgradeable proxy whose admin can replace the implementation, so the current absence of a freeze function is not permanent. The senior wrapper also inherits Ethena's liquid-stablecoin, BTC, ETH/LST, exchange-hedge and custody assumptions; tranching reorders who absorbs a loss within that stack but does not remove it.

syzusd-yuzu.title: Yuzu Staked Wrapper
syzusd-yuzu.text: syzUSD is the staked wrapper for Yuzu USD, so its dollar exposure sits in the parent token, yzUSD. The wrapper appreciates against yzUSD as curated DeFi strategies accrue yield, while exits inherit Yuzu's KYC-gated redemption and liquidity-buffer constraints. Unstaking back to yzUSD on Plasma carried no delay or fee at Pharos's latest contract read, but that step only returns the parent token. Yuzu publishes a real-time reserve feed through Accountable, and Pharos scores the wrapper's backing through yzUSD so the same underlying risk is not counted twice as fresh backing. syzUSD holders take strategy-vault risk, parent-coin risk and young-chain deployment risk in one receipt: Plasma is the only native issuance route, and the Ethereum, Monad, HyperEVM, Sei, Pharos Network, Berachain and Aptos units are Chainlink CCIP representations administered by Yuzu. Of the wrapper's own pillars, control scores strongest and exit weakest, because no comparable same-size dollar exit is established. The overall card reads {{grade}}: the methodology withholds a letter until the card's weakness can be attributed to measured adverse evidence or bounded uncertainty. Whatever the grade, a syzUSD exit ends in yzUSD, so Yuzu's KYC-gated redemption is the durable constraint.

fxsave-f-x-protocol.title: f(x) Stability Vault
fxsave-f-x-protocol.text: fxSAVE is an auto-compounding ERC-4626 receipt over f(x) Protocol's Stability Pool, so a deposit is a strategy position from the first block. The exit path runs through fxSP into a fxUSD-and-USDC mix, then onward into fxUSD's CDP machinery backed by WBTC and wstETH. That gives holders strategy yield and peg-support exposure in one package, but it also imports oracle, liquidation, Curve-pool, and governance-tuned collateral risk. Pharos classifies it as a strategy-vault variant of fxUSD, so its {{grade}} overall grade cannot exceed its parent's. Every route out shares the same fxUSD failure domain. The wrapper reads like savings, but the engine underneath is still a leveraged crypto collateral system.

steakusdt-steakhouse.title: Steakhouse USDT Lending Vault
steakusdt-steakhouse.text: Steakhouse USDT is a Morpho Vault V2 share over USDT; yield comes from borrower interest in Steakhouse-curated lending markets. Pharos keeps the Tether issuer and blacklist dependency attached while separately treating the wrapper as a lending vault whose withdrawals draw on idle USDT and a configured liquidity adapter. Backing is the weakest of the three pillars because the Tether reserve is inherited, and the {{grade}} overall grade is capped at the parent USDT rating. Exit depends on available Morpho market liquidity, and the base dollar remains Tether's liability.

susn-noon.title: Yield Receipt, Seven-Day Exit
susn-noon.text: sUSN is the staked form of Noon USN: deposits mint appreciating shares, and Pharos's pinned reads show the vault holding its backing entirely as idle USN. Exits run a holder-initiated request and claim rail with no operator step. A withdrawal locks USN in a non-upgradeable WithdrawalHandler, and claimWithdrawal pays once the handler's seven-day period has passed. That period is enforced on-chain but admin-owned: changes pass a 48-hour timelock, yet the value has no bounds and a change applies retroactively to requests already waiting. Wrapper upgrades now carry the same 48-hour notice, after an expiry-free upgrade scheduled in June 2026 left the vault logic replaceable without warning for four months until its cancellation on October 12. The 3-of-5 Noon Safe that owns the vault can still pause new unstake requests, replace the withdrawal handler or grant itself blacklist powers instantly. Nearly a fifth of supply sits on Base, where the deployment's own Safe holds an active blacklist role. Those instant admin powers make control the weakest of the three pillars on the {{grade}} report card. Backing inherits the parent's private-credit-led mix, so the exit queue and Noon's credit book set the constraint together.

mre7yield-midas.title: Midas Re7 Yield Token
mre7yield-midas.text: mRe7YIELD is a Midas and Re7 Capital liquid-yield token, with NAV appreciation sourced from DeFi lending, liquidity provision, restaking, funding-rate trades and options strategies. None of those strategies is a cash equivalent, so the token's value depends on how they perform. Disclosure is the binding gap. The latest issuer-prepared weekly report Pharos verified, dated September 10, 2026, splits roughly $8.2 million into a market-neutral strategy bucket and small settlement balances, with no positions, venues, liabilities or custody named; by early October the transparency endpoint returned no usable report for the token. Backing is the weakest pillar on the card, and Pharos leaves the overall rating unrated for insufficient evidence.
