Primary redemption runs through Midas rails for eligible holders, while native minting on Ethereum, Etherlink and TAC rests with an operator EOA and deposit vaults that Pharos scores as unbounded. It is a managed strategy note; the durable constraint is that the positions behind its NAV are not published.

hbusdt-hyperbeat.title: Hyperbeat USDT Vault
hbusdt-hyperbeat.text: hbUSDT is Hyperbeat's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} vault share on HyperEVM, built on Midas vault contracts and taking USDT0 as its enabled deposit token. Pharos records the reserve as one dynamic strategy envelope: Hyperbeat describes automated deployment into HyperEVM lending and strategy protocols but publishes no venue or position weights. The Accountable proof-of-solvency dashboard meant to supply live visibility returned server errors in August 2026 and could not be resolved at the October 9 review, so no current allocation proof is retrievable. The {{grade}} overall grade sits below its USDT parent. Hyperbeat documents a liquidity-conditional instant redemption and a two-day request route, but neither has established same-size capacity. The parent leg carries Tether's redemption discretion and USDT0's cross-chain settlement assumptions. The share itself is directly freezable: at an October 19 2026 chain read, an externally owned address held the role that blacklists holders from sending or receiving. Any depositor can mint, and the deposit cap is currently disabled, though a 3-of-5 Hyperbeat Safe can set one. A Midas admin address, which Midas says sits under a 4-of-7 MPC signing policy, can grant the mint role without delay. A two-day timelock guards upgrades. The durable constraint is that the strategy book behind each share is not independently reconciled.

witry-brix.title: Wrapped Turkish Lira Yield
witry-brix.text: wiTRY is Brix's ERC-4626 staking wrapper over iTRY, a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} claim that accrues fund yield against a token backed by shares of the Digital Liquidity Fund, a regulated basket of Turkish-lira money-market funds. The Ethereum wrapper can be verified on-chain, and Brix's Accountable dashboard publishes an assets-and-liabilities snapshot showing reserves matching iTRY and wiTRY supply. The snapshot omits the fund look-through: the underlying money-market funds, their weights, and their maturities stay undisclosed, so Pharos carries the whole reserve as one high-risk {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund-share position. Exit runs through a cooldown unstake or a fee-bearing fast {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} into iTRY, with final lira exposure inheriting the iTRY issuer and its Zodia Custody arrangement. Supply is now split almost evenly between Ethereum and MegaETH. Pharos rates wiTRY {{grade}}, with exit the weakest pillar: the track record is under six months, and no reviewed same-notional exit route exists across that multi-chain supply. The undisclosed fund look-through remains the durable constraint.

srusd-reservoir.title: Reservoir Savings Token
srusd-reservoir.text: srUSD is Reservoir's savings wrapper over rUSD, so the immediate asset is a yield-accruing share and the underlying risk is the Reservoir balance sheet. That balance sheet is a mixed book: stablecoin PSM liquidity, RWA allocations, Morpho and Euler lending vaults, and governance-approved credit strategies. The wrapper is minted by burning rUSD and redeemed by minting it back, so it adds exchange-rate and exit-to-rUSD mechanics while rUSD itself still depends on PSM liquidity and protocol risk controls for the actual stablecoin exit. Reservoir self-attests the parent book on a real-time reserve page, but Pharos does not compute srUSD backing from live reserves and inherits it from rUSD. Economic control is the weakest pillar and the main drag on the {{grade}} overall grade. Pharos scores effective minting as unbounded because no qualified governance, reconciliation or supervisory process limits it, the token's admin is a single externally owned account, and the share of supply carried over the LayerZero route to Berachain is still unresolved.

usdn-smardex.title: Delta-Neutral USDN
usdn-smardex.text: SMARDEX USDN is an Ethereum synthetic dollar built around a wstETH-backed vault and delta-neutral protocol mechanics, unrelated to Noble's USDN despite the shared ticker. Users mint and redeem through the vault, but the process can be throttled by protocol imbalance and a two-step oracle validation flow, so mint and redemption are not always available on demand. The token also rebases, which turns yield into a protocol accounting event rather than a separate savings wrapper. The {{grade}} overall grade turns on economic control, the weakest of the three pillars: the protocol proxy is USDN's sole minter and rebaser, and its 2-of-3 governance Safe can grant the upgrade role and replace the implementation immediately.

scusd-rings.title: Rings Stable Collateral
scusd-rings.text: Rings scUSD is the liquid scAsset, distinct from the stkscUSD savings wrapper that carries the advertised yield, so any yield figure belongs to a different token. The collateral model accepts stablecoins and routes a strategy sleeve through Trevee/Veda BoringVault infrastructure into venues such as Aave and Morpho, so the backing is part cash-like collateral and part curated DeFi exposure. Proof is still self-reported through published backing addresses, with Pharos carrying an explicit notice that deeper on-chain reserve tracking is pending, and no dated split by stablecoin or strategy exists. Backing is therefore scored on limited evidence. On both Ethereum and Sonic, governance runs through a 4-of-6 Veda/Paladin Safe, a one-day timelock, RolesAuthority and Teller contracts. That machinery can authorize a new caller to mint vault shares without depositing assets. Pharos scores that minting as economically unbounded, which makes economic control the weakest of the three pillars behind the {{grade}} overall grade. The durable constraint is a share token whose issuance is bounded by governance restraint rather than by collateral.

weusd-picwe.title: PicWe's Disputed Dollar Wrapper
weusd-picwe.text: WEUSD is PicWe's omni-chain dollar token, minted and redeemed through PicWe-operated contracts on BSC, Base, Arbitrum, Plume, and Movement. The backing claim is the problem. PicWe's current documentation describes 1:1 USDC mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, earlier PicWe materials describe a basket of roughly nine USDT to one MOVE, and no attestation or itemized reserve inventory reconciles either story. Pharos' July 2026 contract reads deepen the doubt: the EVM mint contract held under one USDC against tens of thousands of WEUSD outstanding, and the Movement package that carries most of the supply stores dual MOVE and stablecoin reserve counters far below circulating supply. Pharos therefore treats the composition as a single unresolved envelope rather than a USDC link. Mint authority is uncapped and held by a PicWe admin key. The durable constraint is a backing claim that no published evidence reconciles.

gbpe-monerium.title: GBP E-Money Rail
gbpe-monerium.text: GBPe is Monerium's British-pound e-money token, issued under an Icelandic EMI licence, with mint and burn handled through KYC'd bank-transfer rails. The stated reserve model is safeguarded GBP client funds and permitted EMI reserve assets, with e-money holders holding a statutory priority claim under Icelandic bankruptcy law. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects how little of that model is documented at the token level. Monerium publishes entity-wide safeguarding figures drawn from its audited statements, but no GBPe-specific asset split, provider weights or independent token-level reserve attestation, so Pharos cannot reconcile GBPe reserves to GBPe liabilities. MiCA coverage is also narrower than the EMT framing suggests: Pharos's review of the EU register found a notified white paper for Monerium's EURe, not for GBPe. Backing and exit are the two weakest pillars, while economic control, with three chain-local 3-of-6 Safes over six issuer-native deployments, is the strongest line on the card. Primary redemption runs only through Monerium's onboarding, and current terms require a separate agreement for non-EUR issuance and redemption, which the card scores as eligibility-gated. The constraint is disclosure: a regulated claim that the public record cannot yet reconcile at the token level.

qcad-stablecorp.title: Regulated CAD Stablecoin
qcad-stablecorp.text: QCAD is Stablecorp's Canadian-dollar stablecoin, minted and redeemed at 1 CAD by qualified holders through Stablecorp or authorized partners. Its regulatory scaffolding is heavier than most small fiat tokens carry: FINTRAC registration, an Ontario Securities Commission order creating the QCAD Digital Trust, and monthly reasonable-assurance {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} from Davidson & Company. Stablecorp's balances API also gives Pharos live supply and reserve totals. The gaps sit in the fine print. Tokens issued before November 20, 2025 fall outside the trust and hold reserves separately, and the reviewed attestations cover only the trust's Ethereum book, not the Base and Solana deployments, so Pharos cannot yet tell how much of the circulating supply the trust wrapper covers. No source publishes instrument weights for the reserve basket, and Pharos maps no exit that handles size at par beyond the issuer, so the report card reads {{grade}}. Control is conventional for an issuer token: 3-of-6 Safes own the contracts and their upgrades, and the code can block addresses and pause transfers.

usdxl-last.title: Last USD in Wind-Down
usdxl-last.text: Last USD (USDXL) is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style synthetic dollar minted on HypurrFi, an Aave V3 fork on HyperEVM, against HYPE, HYPE LSTs, {{term:bridge}}bridged{{/term}} BTC and ETH collateral. Its issuance venue is in wind-down: HypurrFi announced that its Legacy and Pooled markets would close by July 15, 2026, raised USDXL borrow rates to 30% to push repayment, and suspended new pooled borrows. The token's access-control roles are now empty, leaving a 2-of-2 proxy-admin Safe's upgrade power as the remaining mint-relevant control. Holders can burn HyperEVM USDXL through the GSM for USDT0 at the configured rate, but only up to available liquidity, and no full-supply {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} guarantee is established. Neither Last nor HypurrFi publishes a dated collateral inventory, so backing is scored on an undisclosed allocation. Economic control is the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card, with a single-source oracle topology among its caps. The peg record has deteriorated: the latest 90-day window shows repeated threshold crossings and time spent outside the band. Whatever remains outstanding is a claim on a market that is closing rather than growing.

bnusd-balanced.title: The Dollar Left Behind
bnusd-balanced.text: This entry tracks bnUSD(old), the legacy Balanced v1 dollar issued on ICON since 2021 and minted only through the Balanced Loans {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} and Peg Stability contracts, with xCall burn-mint representations on other chains. Balanced v2 launched on April 7, 2026 with a distinct Sonic-based bnUSD, and the issuer offers a 1:1 migration into it. The deadline matters: Balanced says v1 goes offline on December 1, 2026, when outstanding loans will be liquidated and the contracts made inaccessible ahead of ICON's announced end-2026 shutdown. Pharos no longer borrows the v2 collateral census for this token, because new-bnUSD reserves are not a claim on the legacy liability, so no backing composition is admitted and the backing pillar is bounded by that gap. Exit is equally thin, with no reviewed DEX route for the tracked supply. The token's debt ceiling now reads zero, but a single EOA owns the Governance SCORE that could raise it or replace mint-critical logic. The peg feed records no events, but its coverage is limited, so that clean record says little. For holders of the legacy token, the migration route and its December deadline are the exit that counts.

dusd-fluid.title: An Oracle Ceiling Without an Issuer
dusd-fluid.text: Fluid Finance's DUSD was designed as an Arbitrum stablecoin backed by safeguarded partner-bank cash, with an issuer oracle capping minting at the reported off-chain balance. That linked bank reconciliation to smart-contract supply control, but only for as long as the issuer kept operating. Fluid Finance SA was dissolved through bankruptcy and entered liquidation in April 2024, and its DUSD and issuer websites no longer resolve, so Pharos tracks DUSD as a frozen legacy asset with no live safety grade. No current reserve report, oracle operation, banking provider or {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route has been verified, and the 2021 design now reads as historical architecture rather than present assurance. Single-chain deployment removed bridge risk but offers no comfort once the issuer behind the evidence path is gone. An oracle-enforced ceiling is only as current as the entity still publishing the number.

iusd-initia.title: Initia's AUSD-wrapped ecosystem dollar
iusd-initia.text: iUSD is the native dollar on Initia, a recently launched Move-based Cosmos L1: a single-chain wrapper backed 1:1 by Agora's AUSD bridged in through LayerZero. The reserve trace therefore ends in Agora's short-dated U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}}, overnight repos and cash, reported for AUSD as a whole rather than for the wrapper. Unlike standard fiat-backed stables, holding iUSD carries no claim on reserve yield; Initia says reserve-related revenue may support ecosystem incentives, development and grants. Initia publishes no dedicated proof-of-reserves feed for the wrapper, so the backing pillar scores well by leaning on Agora's AUSD reporting. The exit pillar is the weakest on the card. Getting out means Initia's bridge converting iUSD to AUSD, a LayerZero {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} hop to Ethereum and a swap into USDC, and Pharos has no same-notional route evidence for that path at size. It holds the overall grade at {{grade}} despite a clean peg record. Holders depend on the LayerZero bridge for any exit, on Agora's {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} terms beyond it, and on Agora's reserve {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and freeze controls for the asset itself.

usdcx-movement.title: Movement's native USDC-backed dollar
usdcx-movement.text: USDCx is Movement's native dollar, issued through Circle's xReserve contract: deposit USDC, mint USDCx one-for-one, and move it back out via CCTP and Gateway without a third-party {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}. Its solvency is borrowed: the sole reserve is USDC locked in a Circle-deployed contract, so USDCx is a claim on Circle's reserves and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} routed through xReserve. Backing sits near the top of the scale for that reason, and the Movement token exposes no local free-mint path. The attester, admin, pause, and package-upgrade powers on the Movement side are scored as bridge controls whose share of supply Pharos has not resolved. A 3-of-6 multisig can upgrade the Movement package with no timelock, so holder-level controls could be added later, and Circle can freeze the USDC in reserve. Exit runs through one issuer-native burn-and-mint route back to Ethereum, on an implementation launched in March 2026. The reserve contract is observable on-chain, but no independent party is documented as reconciling it to USDCx supply. The durable constraint is that USDCx is only ever as good as the wrapper, the route, and the parent underneath.

usdh-hubble.title: Solana CDP Dollar, Now Mostly PSM USDC
usdh-hubble.text: Hubble's USDH is a MakerDAO-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin launched on Solana in January 2022, minted against {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} vaults of SOL, mSOL, BTC, and ETH with Stability Pool {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}}. That is the history; the present is a much smaller and mostly different asset. At the latest on-chain read, the large majority of outstanding USDH had been issued through the {{term:psm}}Peg Stability Module{{/term}} against deposited USDC, with the CDP branch a sub-material remainder led by mSOL and SOL. Backing therefore inherits Circle, and it is the strongest pillar on the card. The {{grade}} overall grade sits near the bottom because the other two pillars fail. The borrowing program is upgradeable through a DAO council where three of seven votes clear the threshold with no hold-up. Exit leans on the PSM swap back to USDC, which Pharos can model only with low confidence, on a single chain with negligible secondary volume. The token itself is clean, with no freeze authority and no holder blacklist; Circle can freeze the PSM's USDC, but it cannot touch a wallet's USDH. The team's focus has shifted to sister protocol Kamino and no formal wind-down has been announced. Hubble's documentation and app were reachable on October 26, 2026, but Pharos has not verified that borrowing or redemption works. USDH is structurally dormant rather than growing. The USDH ticker is shared with Native Markets and Hermetica, three distinct issuers with three distinct collateral models.

zkusd-goal3.title: Goal3 zkUSD, Reserves Unevidenced
zkusd-goal3.text: zkUSD is an issuer-controlled token on ZKsync Era minted through Goal3's lockdrop portal, originally the in-house dollar of the Goal3 sportsbook. The verified portal code accepts owner-configured stable tokens, forwards deposits to a treasury address, and mints the return token through a vesting flow. That is the whole evidenced mechanism; 1:1 USDC {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, reserve coverage, and a peg-maintenance route are not established. The only reserve-adjacent address Pharos could identify, the portal treasury, held no USDC or USDC.e at the reviewed block, and explorer history shows its USDC.e moved out in tranches through October 2024 to addresses no source identifies. Goal3's documentation site, main site, and X account no longer resolve. The reserve is therefore carried as fully unknown, and the token and portal are UUPS proxies owned by a single EOA with no upgrade delay. That owner can also place holds on existing holder balances. No exit route is observed and no primary exit is disclosed. Backing and exit rest on limited evidence, and the overall grade is {{grade}}. The peg line rests on a single price source; with no evidenced backing and no issuer presence, that record cannot be read as a working dollar.

ist-agoric.title: Sunset by Governance
ist-agoric.text: IST was Agoric's interchain dollar, minted through Inter Protocol as an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} against IBC-bridged ATOM and stATOM, plus a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} that minted IST 1:1 against USDC, USDT, and DAI bridged from Ethereum. The sunset proposal cited declining appetite for decentralized stablecoins and rising operating costs. Agoric's on-chain Proposal 93 passed on May 1, 2025 and opened a planned 60-day wind-down. Minting stopped, the plan set the vault liquidation fee to zero so borrowers could repay IST and reclaim collateral, and weekly liquidation-ratio increases were scheduled to close whatever vaults remained. The sunset completed on June 26, 2025, and the IST redemption grace period ended on June 30. Pharos records the cause as abandonment and keeps IST as a frozen archive because nothing mints anymore. Its June 2026 frozen snapshot still showed about $200,000 of IST on Agoric and Osmosis, priced near $0.92. Those balances now depend on whatever secondary market remains rather than on the vaults or the PSM. The durable constraint is that a governed shutdown ends the mechanism on a fixed date, while tokens left outside it outlive the deadline.

benji-franklin-templeton.title: The Onchain '40 Act Fund
benji-franklin-templeton.text: BENJI is the on-chain share token for Franklin Templeton's FOBXX, an SEC-registered U.S. government {{term:money-market-fund}}money market fund{{/term}} with a stable $1.00 NAV, custodied at JPMorgan Chase with Franklin Templeton as transfer agent and the token as the share record. Yield is distributed by rebasing the holder's share count on-chain rather than letting the price drift, so BENJI behaves like a par dollar even though it is legally a fund share. Subscriptions and redemptions are limited to KYC-verified Benji wallets, settling by USD wire or into USDC. Pharos tracks deployments on eight chains, from Stellar and Ethereum to Solana and Aptos, while the BNB Chain and Canton issuances remain unintegrated. The catch is telemetry: reserves run on a curated weekly snapshot of the official factsheet, and since mid-July 2026 Pharos has quarantined the listing. The price resolves, but no permitted source reports a positive market cap or circulating supply, and Aptos and Stellar have no runtime supply reader, so a complete multi-chain count remains unproven. BENJI's constraint is the gap between a registered fund with daily published holdings and an on-chain footprint the dashboard cannot yet add up.

wtgxx-wisdomtree.title: WisdomTree's 24/7 Dealer-Traded Treasury Fund
wtgxx-wisdomtree.text: WTGXX is the digital share class of WisdomTree's Treasury Money Market Digital Fund, renamed from 'Government' in late 2025, a Rule 2a-7 '40 Act-registered {{term:money-market-fund}}money market fund{{/term}} that received SEC approval in early 2026 to support 24/7 dealer trading at a fixed $1.00 NAV. Subscriptions and {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} are gated to WisdomTree Connect users with USDC dealer settlement and USD-wire alternatives; holdings are short-duration U.S. government obligations: {{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}}, floating-rate notes, and repos, which are the {{term:rwa}}real-world asset{{/term}} backing. The open problem is visibility: since mid-July 2026 Pharos has held WTGXX in quarantine because none of its permitted runtime sources report a positive circulating supply or market cap, so the token sits ungraded while the fund side keeps publishing its daily NAV. The share token spans seven networks from Ethereum to Stellar, and the Stellar shares have no runtime reader at all. Chainlink's NAV feed still prices the reserves. Until a runtime source counts the on-chain shares, the fund's reported holdings cannot be matched to a tokenized float.

vbill-vaneck.title: VanEck's Securitize-Administered Treasury Share
vbill-vaneck.text: VBILL is the on-chain share token for VanEck's Treasury Fund, a BVI Professional Fund advised by Van Eck Absolute Return Advisers, with State Street as custodian and Securitize handling fund administration, tokenization, transfer agency and KYC. The fund holds short-duration U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills and Treasury-collateralized repos, though current weights across bills, repos and cash are not published. The token seeks a stable $1.00 NAV and pays yield as newly issued tokens rather than accreting in price; Pharos reads the live NAV from the Chainlink NAVLink feed. The public disclosures stop short of the fund's legal terms: no holder loss waterfall, liquidation priority or account-segregation mechanics are published. Primary access runs through Securitize Markets for institutional investors, and newly issued tokens cannot be transferred or redeemed for 72 hours. The Ethereum, Avalanche, BNB Chain and Solana supplies are each issued natively by Securitize. On the EVM chains one owner key holds uncapped mint authority; on Solana the controller's upgrade authority is a single plain key shared with the controller that mints STAC, and no threshold or timelock protects any of these surfaces. Exit is the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card, because the only route out is the institutional Securitize window. The Treasury assets are conventional; the constraints are single-key issuance control, unpublished loss terms and an exit only eligible investors can use.

acred-apollo-securitize.title: Private Credit, Not Treasuries
acred-apollo-securitize.text: ACRED is a tokenized, NAV-accreting feeder share into Apollo Diversified Credit Fund, a multi-strategy private credit portfolio combining direct lending, structured credit, performing credit, and dislocated credit. Unlike BUIDL or BENJI, the collateral is illiquid private credit rather than {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, so its risk profile is medium-to-high and closer to syrupUSDC than to a stable-NAV vehicle. Subscriptions and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run at fund NAV through Securitize Markets for qualified purchasers, with quarterly repurchase offers of at least 5% of shares and an on-demand liquidity pool or secondary-market sales for intra-quarter exits, and RedStone publishes a NAV oracle used by integrations. Pharos tracks the Ethereum issuance plus Avalanche, Ink, Polygon, Sei, Solana, and Aptos deployments, with the EVM chains linked through Securitize's Wormhole transport. Exit is the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card: the only route Pharos credits is the issuer redemption queue, which settles over weeks and fills only part of a large request. Converting a large ACRED position to cash at NAV therefore follows Apollo's repurchase calendar.

eutbl-spiko.title: Spiko's Euro T-Bill Fund Share
eutbl-spiko.text: EUTBL is a tokenised share of Spiko's EU T-Bills Money Market Fund, an AMF-authorised UCITS short-term VNAV sub-fund of Spiko SICAV that holds Eurozone government bonds and money-market instruments. The mandate caps weighted average maturity at 60 days and any single instrument at six months, and the token accretes value as that portfolio earns rather than holding a fixed euro. Twenty First Capital manages the fund and CACEIS Bank is depositary, with fund assets legally segregated from both. Pharos reads the reserve as one fund-share identity priced by a Chainlink NAV feed; that feed does not publish current security weights, and no dated PwC audit report was obtained in Pharos's review. Backing and economic control both grade well, but the {{grade}} overall grade is held down by exit, the weakest pillar. Subscriptions, redemptions and even transfers run through Spiko Finance's permissioned shareholder register, with an 11:30 Paris cutoff and execution at the last known NAV, and Pharos has not established a settlement term for that route. The fund underneath is conservative; the constraint is that only investors inside Spiko's register can reach it directly.

ustbl-spiko.title: Spiko's USD Treasury Bill Fund Share
ustbl-spiko.text: USTBL is the USD-denominated sibling of Spiko's EUTBL: a share in an AMF-authorized UCITS short-term {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} holding short-dated U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills and operational bank balances instead of Eurozone sovereigns. The prospectus lists issuer-native deployments on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon, Base, Etherlink, Stellar, Starknet and Solana; Spiko announced Chainlink CCIP for cross-chain movement, but no production adapter has been identified. The VNAV share accretes value as T-bill yield compounds, so USTBL behaves as a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} fund share rather than a par stablecoin. CACEIS Bank is custodian, BNY Mellon sub-custodian for the bills, and the prospectus names PwC as statutory auditor certifying annual accounts rather than issuing a periodic {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. Pharos has not verified a current dated annual audit report; the latest semiannual report names PwC but carries no audit opinion. Exit is the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} card. Subscriptions and redemptions run only through Spiko's transfer agent for KYC-cleared, allowlisted wallets at a daily 11:30 Paris cutoff, and the management company can gate redemptions once they pass 10% of net assets. A holder outside that allowlist has no issuer-side route out, and the fund's regulated wrapper does not change that.

jtrsy-anemoy.title: Janus Henderson's Tokenised T-Bill Fund
jtrsy-anemoy.text: JTRSY is the Janus Henderson Anemoy Treasury Fund, a BVI Professional Fund holding short-duration U.S. {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, where Janus Henderson acts as sub-advisor and Centrifuge runs the on-chain ERC-7540 vault. The fund carries an S&P fund credit rating and settles primary subscriptions and redemptions at fund NAV for whitelisted non-U.S. Professional Investors via Centrifuge's issuer rail. Pharos reads the Chainlink JTRSY NAV feed as live reserve evidence; the feed proves the share value but does not reproduce current holdings, cash sleeve, or named custodians, so the backing pillar is held below the level a fully disclosed T-bill portfolio would reach. The exit pillar is the weakest line on the card because redemption is eligibility-gated: a holder outside the whitelist has no comparable open route. The issuer also publishes no loss-recovery procedure for restoring NAV after an economic loss, which leaves the mechanism review bounded. Pharos records eight deployments; Centrifuge V3's burn-and-mint share bridge covers the EVM ones, while the Solana deployment's issuance architecture remains unresolved. Mint authority resolves to a 4-of-9 Centrifuge protocol Safe. Holdings remain a tokenized {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund share with permissioned Centrifuge {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and daily NAV {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, settled same day or next, for those admitted.

bib01-backed.title: Backed's Dollar Treasury Tracker
bib01-backed.text: bIB01 is Backed Finance's tracker certificate for the BlackRock iShares $ Treasury Bond 0-1yr UCITS ETF (IB01), registered under the Swiss DLT Act and not pegged to $1: the price accretes as the underlying {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} ETF earns, making it a tokenised {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund share rather than a payment dollar. Backed plans to wind down its bTokens by the end of 2026. New bIB01 issuance is closed, existing holders keep the KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} process, and Backed lists TBLLx as the upgrade destination at an issuer-set ratio. Reserves are reported daily through a Chainlink Proof of Reserve feed that reads the ETF share count, but Backed publishes no product-specific administered NAV method or dated reserve-to-liability reconciliation. Since September 2026 Pharos has quarantined the listing and has now archived it as frozen: CoinGecko's price stopped updating on September 17, DefiLlama only repeats that stale value, and without an admissible price the supply across seven chains cannot be valued. The durable constraint is a closing product whose NAV no longer reaches Pharos through any admissible feed.

bc3m-backed.title: Backed's EUR Govt Bond Tracker
bc3m-backed.text: bC3M is Backed Finance's EUR-denominated tracker certificate for the Amundi GOVIES 0-6 Months Euro Investment Grade UCITS ETF, registered under the Swiss DLT Act and administered from Jersey. It is not pegged to one euro: the price accretes with the short-dated euro government bond ETF, which makes it the euro analogue of a {{term:treasury}}Treasury-bill{{/term}} tracker rather than a payment token. Backed plans to wind down its bTokens by the end of 2026. New bC3M issuance is closed, existing holders keep the KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} process, and Backed lists TBLLx as the upgrade destination at an issuer-set ratio. Reserves are reported daily through a Chainlink Proof of Reserve feed that publishes the ETF share count, but Backed publishes no product-specific administered NAV method or dated reserve-to-liability reconciliation, which bounds the backing review. bC3M holds a {{grade}} overall grade and the exit pillar is the weakest of the three, because primary redemption is eligibility-gated and the Uniswap and CoW Protocol venues do not change that on the card. The durable constraint is the calendar: the product is winding down, and its exit runs through Backed's KYC process.

ntbill-nest.title: Nest's On-Plume Treasury Vault
ntbill-nest.text: nTBILL is Nest Credit's {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} vault: a NAV-accreting share whose value tracks a curated book of Superstate USTB and Janus Henderson JTRSY positions, plus a small stablecoin liquidity buffer, with primary mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through Nest at vault NAV rather than par. Reserves are sourced live from the Nest Credit positions API, and both underlying funds publish short Treasury-bill maturities with daily or market-day liquidity. Pharos tracks nTBILL because it references a dollar base, but the token behaves like a tokenised {{term:money-market-fund}}fund-of-funds{{/term}} share rather than a par-redeemable stablecoin. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects the Nest wrapper rather than the Treasury book. Minting is unbounded with no independent whole-supply reconciliation, and Pharos cannot resolve who controls several of its bridged deployments. Exit is held back as well, because redemption is eligibility-gated through a rail shared by five Nest vaults, and Nest publishes no vault-level maturity, assurance, or custody-continuity inputs. The durable constraint is a strong underlying book behind a single, permissioned exit.

nbasis-nest.title: Nest's Basis-Trade Vault
nbasis-nest.text: nBASIS is Nest Credit's {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} vault: a NAV-accreting share whose book is mostly the USCC crypto carry fund, managed by Bitwise since June 2026 after its move from Superstate, with a smaller Superstate USTB {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} sleeve and a thin stablecoin buffer. The futures carry therefore sits inside the underlying fund rather than being run by Nest directly. Closer in profile to Midas mRe7YIELD than to a par stablecoin, the token's value drifts with {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} performance rather than holding $1. Pharos lists it because the strategy references the dollar as its base and the Nest Credit positions API publishes live NAV, but it classifies the collateral as exotic and carries a NAV-token notice. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three: primary redemption is eligibility-gated through Nest, five Nest vaults share the same redemption rail, and no margin or liquidation disclosure for the underlying fund is published. The durable constraint is that a Nest share is only as redeemable as Nest's single rail.

nopal-nest.title: Nest's BlackOpal Credit Vault
nopal-nest.text: nOPAL is Nest Credit's BlackOpal LiquidStone II vault: a NAV-accreting share over tokenised private-credit positions in a Brazilian credit-card receivables fund, plus a small nTBILL {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} sleeve and stablecoin liquidity buffer. Like other Nest vaults, primary access runs through Nest at vault NAV, and it is not a par-redeemable stablecoin. Pharos flags nOPAL as a private-credit vault share; the reserve slice rated high-risk reflects the underlying LiquidStone II credit positions, and the fund's obligor-level receivables, service providers, and any fund-level audit are not public. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by economic control, the weakest pillar, with exit close behind. Issuance is unbounded with no independent whole-supply reconciliation, and the same 3-of-6 Nest Safe that runs nOPAL's Teller and Manager also controls minting for another Nest vault. Redemption is eligibility-gated through Nest's queue, with settlement measured in weeks rather than days. The durable constraint is a credit book Pharos cannot see behind a single Nest rail.

nwisdom-nest.title: Nest's WisdomTree-Backed Vault
nwisdom-nest.text: nWISDOM is Nest Credit's vault share built around WisdomTree Connect tokenised fund exposure (xCRDYX) with a small nTBILL and stablecoin liquidity buffer, classified as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent vault exposure rather than a par stablecoin. Yield accretes through the underlying WisdomTree fund NAV; primary mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through Nest at vault NAV against USDC and pUSD. The {{grade}} overall grade is low across all three pillars. The September 2026 positions capture shows almost the entire book in xCRDYX, and the capture publishes no underlying securities, obligors, custody, or holder seniority, so the backing pillar treats that slice as opaque. The exit pillar is held back: redemption is eligibility-gated and shares the Nest Credit redemption rail with four sibling vaults, so one operational failure would hit all of them. Minting is issuer-direct with no evidenced supply cap, which keeps the economic-control pillar down as well.

susdc-spark.title: Spark's USDC share class on the vault savings rate
susdc-spark.text: Spark Savings USDC lets USDC holders earn Spark's vault savings rate without first converting into USDS, with idle deposits taken out and deployed by the Spark Liquidity Layer. The share is denominated in USDC, but Spark documents its V2 vaults as economically backed by USDS, so a loss that exhausted Sky's capital buffers and SKY-token recapitalization would be socialized across USDS holders, Spark Savings vaults included. On the vault's last reviewed accounting only a small slice sat idle in USDC; the rest was an aggregate deployed position whose assets, venues and custodians are not published. spUSDC is also a UUPS proxy whose logic can be replaced through Sky's 48-hour governance pause on Ethereum and through Spark's LayerZero-driven executor on Avalanche. Even so, backing is the strongest of the three pillars, with economic control close behind. Withdrawals draw on idle vault liquidity, with Savings Liquidity Intents for large exits, and Pharos cannot score a same-size route through either. That unmeasured exit holds down the {{grade}} overall grade, and the durable constraint is that large withdrawals depend on liquidity Spark has deployed elsewhere.

susdt-spark.title: USDT-denominated Spark Savings vault
susdt-spark.text: Spark Savings USDT is the Tether-denominated version of Spark's savings vault: deposits earn a vault savings rate set by Spark while a permissioned Spark Liquidity Layer taker deploys idle USDT into lending and other strategies. The wrapper gives USDT holders a rising share price, but the risk stack layers Tether issuer exposure, Spark vault mechanics and Sky's USDS system on top of one another. Spark documents these V2 vaults as fully backed by USDS, so a loss that exhausts Sky's junior capital and surplus buffers would be socialized across USDS holders, spUSDT included. Backing is the weakest of the three pillars. Spark does not publish the current strategy split or downstream custodian set for its deployed positions, and the Arbitrum and X Layer deployments hold USDT0, a LayerZero representation of Tether's Ethereum USDT. The {{grade}} overall grade is held at the parent ceiling, which takes the weaker of USDT and USDS. The durable constraint is liquidity: instant withdrawals stop at the vault's idle USDT balance, and anything beyond it depends on recalling deployed positions.

sgho-aave.title: Aave's non-slashable GHO savings module
sgho-aave.text:
Aave Savings GHO (sGHO) is an ERC-4626 savings vault on Ethereum whose shares increase in GHO value as yield accrues. Deposits mint shares at the prevailing exchange rate, so one sGHO does not represent a fixed one GHO. The conversion rate follows a target savings rate set through an Aave governance role rather than a balance-derived ratio. Deposited GHO stays in the vault, while the DAO funds yield separately.

The savings vault is non-slashable and distinct from Umbrella stkGHO, whose stakers absorb GHO-market deficits. Shares can be redeemed for GHO without a cooldown, although a pause guardian can halt deposits, withdrawals and transfers across the whole vault. Pharos records GHO as the wrapper's single backing asset, so the savings layer adds no collateral diversification, and the {{grade}} overall grade is capped at the parent GHO rating. Holders remain exposed to GHO's underlying collateral and peg risk, alongside the vault's smart-contract controls and governance decisions over the savings rate.

gtusdcp-gauntlet.title: Gauntlet's three-chain USDC Prime vaults
gtusdcp-gauntlet.text: Gauntlet USDC Prime is a three-vault line: immutable Morpho vaults on Ethereum, Base, and Arbitrum that turn chain-local USDC into curated exposure over Morpho lending markets, each with its own share price rather than one fungible cross-chain token. Immutability is the strongest thing on the card, and economic control leads the three pillars. Each vault mints shares only against its chain-local USDC, the share-gate setters on the Ethereum Vault V2 deployment have been abdicated so the curator cannot switch on transfer gating, and the parameter Safes steer allocations and nothing else. Withdrawals depend on Morpho market liquidity and on the curator not having optimised the book into a queue at the wrong moment. The {{grade}} overall grade is held by a critical-dependency cap: the vault's instant ERC-4626 redemption rail is shared with dozens of other reviewed assets, so Pharos treats a failure there as correlated, with the USDC parent ceiling and the short track record further back. Share price appreciates on borrower interest. Freeze exposure is inherited from Circle's authority over the USDC beneath the shares. The durable constraint is that the vault can never rate above the dollar it wraps.

gtusdc-gauntlet.title: Gauntlet's V1 USDC MetaMorpho vault
gtusdc-gauntlet.text: gtUSDC is the Ethereum-only V1 Morpho Prime vault curated by Gauntlet, an ERC-4626 wrapper compounding {{term:yield-bearing}}lending yield{{/term}} across vetted USDC markets on Morpho Blue. Pharos's 2026-10-01 read found seven funded markets lending USDC against cbBTC, WBTC, wstETH or WETH at 86% LLTV, and Pharos tracks the vault apart from the V2 vault at a different address. Economic control is the strongest of the three pillars: the vault is immutable, mints shares only against USDC deposits, and the Gauntlet 4-of-7 Safe steers fees, caps, timelocks, and market allocation, and nothing else, with no holder-transfer gating anywhere in the verified source. Withdrawals depend on whatever USDC the underlying Morpho markets can return and can queue when those markets are fully utilised. The {{grade}} overall grade is held by a critical-dependency cap rather than by the USDC parent ceiling: the vault's instant ERC-4626 redemption rail is shared with dozens of other reviewed assets, so Pharos treats a failure there as correlated. Circle can still freeze the USDC beneath the shares. Share price appreciates on borrower interest, so the token trades above par by design, and the durable constraint is that its safety can never exceed Circle's.

yvusdc-yearn.title: Yearn USDC Vault
yvusdc-yearn.text: yvUSDC-1 is the canonical Yearn v3 USDC vault: an ERC-4626 {{term:yield-bearing}}share token{{/term}} whose price appreciates as Yearn's allocator rotates capital across governance-whitelisted strategies. The whitelist is broader than the book. At Pharos's 9 October 2026 block read, four funded strategies carried the vault's debt: two routing USDC into the Sky ecosystem through USDS and sUSDS, a Yearn USDC strategy, and a Pawn Broker market lending USDC to a single borrower against stcUSD collateral. That loan held close to a third of the debt and sits outside the vault's default withdrawal queue, while the Spark lender held nothing. Exits queue against aggregate strategy liquidity, which matters in a drawdown. Economic control is the weakest pillar by a wide margin, and it is what pulls the overall grade down to {{grade}}. The vault is not deposit-only: Yearn's role manager can appoint an accountant whose reported fees mint new shares with no enforced ceiling, so repeated reports could dilute holders without matching USDC deposits. The durable constraint is that holding the vault means trusting Yearn's role holders as well as the strategies they fund.

aa-falconx-mev-capital.title: FalconX Credit Vault
aa-falconx-mev-capital.text: AA_FalconXUSDC is the senior tranche of Pareto's FalconX Credit Vault and is unrelated to Falcon Finance's USDf or to MEV Capital strategy tokens. Depositors' USDC goes directly to FalconX under an institutional credit facility curated by M11 Credit, so the vault's asset is a single-obligor FalconX receivable and USDC is only the unit of account and repayment asset. Pareto does not disclose the facility's collateralisation, loan tape, or claim priority. Exits are monthly through the vault's {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} process, and withdrawal requests require a wallet approved by the vault's Keyring allowlist.  The IdleCDO owner can switch on minted-interest accounting, which creates strategy receivables and AA fee shares without the matching interest arriving in USDC; upgrades to that mint logic sit behind a one-day timelock.

vndc-jade-labs.title: A Dong Token Under Criminal Investigation
vndc-jade-labs.text: VNDC has circulated as a Vietnamese dong token since 2019 and is now frozen on Pharos. On 2026-03-23 Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security opened a criminal case against the ONUS/VNDC founder and eight others for property appropriation and money laundering, alleging that the bank deposits advertised as backing VNDC 1:1 were never made, so Pharos treats {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and reserve claims as high risk. The backing disclosures had already changed: VNDC 2.0 describes USDT/USDC smart-contract collateral pools on Polygon and BNB Smart Chain rather than direct VND bank reserves. Those disclosures are self-reported by Jade Labs, with no published reserve split, no independent audit cadence and no verified third-party attestation. The issuer's own reference has also lapsed: vndc.io returned errors on repeated checks in August 2026 and in October redirected to an unrelated login page. Pharos quarantined the listing on 2026-07-15 because no permitted runtime source still reports a positive circulating supply or market cap. The durable constraint is that neither the float nor the reserves behind it can be confirmed independently, and the issuer's disclosure site no longer serves them.

hkdr-rd-technologies.title: A Sandbox Pioneer Without a Licence
hkdr-rd-technologies.text: HKDR is the planned HKD stablecoin of RD InnoTech, a subsidiary of RD Technologies, the Hong Kong fintech founded by former HKMA chief executive Norman Chan. RD InnoTech entered the first HKMA stablecoin issuer sandbox cohort in July 2024, testing digital-asset trading and cross-border trade payments, and later named HashKey Exchange as a distribution partner with Ethereum as the deployment chain. The build-out continued into the licensing regime: a $40M Series A2 led by ZA Global closed on July 30 2025, alongside a ZA Bank memorandum to explore reserve {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and distribution. The licence did not follow. On April 10 2026 the HKMA granted its first two issuer licences to Anchorpoint and HSBC, and in June it said the remaining applications stay under review with no timetable for further grants. At Pharos's September 13 2026 check, the HKMA register still listed only those two licensees and RD Technologies' 2026 announcements did not mention HKDR, so Pharos carries no expected launch date. The planned design is 1:1 backing in HKD high-quality liquid assets at licensed institutions, with periodic {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} and regulated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. The durable constraint is that none of it can start until the HKMA grants RD InnoTech a licence.

brd-volpon.title: Selic-Linked Yield, In a Token
brd-volpon.text: BRD is a Brazilian real stablecoin announced on January 6, 2026 by Tony Volpon, a former deputy governor of the Central Bank of Brazil, to be issued through his company CF Inovacao. The distinctive structural choice is yield: BRD is meant to be backed by Brazilian National {{term:treasury}}Treasury bonds{{/term}} and to pass the Selic-linked return, around 15% at announcement, back to holders rather than keep it as issuer revenue. Volpon positioned it as the first BRL token to make that {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-sharing{{/term}} the core product, aimed at institutional investors, against a field that includes Crown's Paradigm-backed BRLV. The project has not moved past the announcement. As of September 2026 CF Inovacao's website listed no BRD product page and no source had given a launch timeline, so Pharos dropped its 2026 launch expectation. The regulatory backdrop has hardened since the announcement: Brazil's stablecoin framework took effect on February 2, 2026 as BCB Resolutions 519 to 521, and Resolution 561, effective October 1, 2026, bars authorised FX providers from settling cross-border remittances in stablecoins. Until CF Inovacao publishes documents and a deployment, BRD remains a stated design rather than a product.

krw1-bdacs.title: Won Stablecoin Awaiting the Digital Asset Basic Act
krw1-bdacs.text: KRW1 is BDACS's won stablecoin, which Pharos still tracks as pre-launch: the September 2025 Avalanche proof of concept put won reserves in escrow at Woori Bank, and commercial issuance awaits Korea's Digital Asset Basic Act. September 2026 widened the gap between distribution and law. BDACS partnered with Rain to make KRW1 spendable across Visa's card network, joined Circle's Arc mainnet at launch as the only won stablecoin, and selected Fireblocks for institutional custody. On September 16 the Seoul Economic Daily reported that BDACS's 2026 whitepaper describes KRW1 as a commercial product already in operation under its existing virtual-asset-service-provider filing, a reading critics said conflates a filing with issuer status; BDACS said it would review the wording. The Act's September public hearing was then cancelled over a delayed government bill. In October Pharos re-pointed its registry to the July 2026 production contracts on Ethereum, Avalanche and Arc named in BDACS's September accountant reserve report, dropping the BNB Chain, Polygon and Plume proof-of-concept rows. Tracked supply remains at proof-of-concept scale, and commercial issuance still waits on the Digital Asset Basic Act.

rusd-revolut.title: A Revolut-Branded Dollar With Bridge as Issuer
rusd-revolut.text: Revolut's EEA crypto terms of September 15 2026 name USDR, beside the live euro EURR, as one of two Revolut-branded e-money tokens. They make Bridge Building S.A., Stripe-owned Bridge's e-money institution in Luxembourg, the sole legal issuer, with exclusive financial liability for the reserves. Revolut Digital Assets Europe, authorised by CySEC, acts only as offeror. A holder's {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} right runs directly against Bridge, at par and free of charge. On September 2 2026 the OCC conditionally approved Revolut Bank US, N.A., with opening targeted for the first half of 2027. The decision records that the bank plans to offer Revolut-branded stablecoins through a third party, will not be the issuer, and will not manage reserves. Pharos moved the expected launch to 2027 on the strength of that timeline. Reserve composition, custodians and safeguarding arrangements for USDR are unpublished. ESMA's register listed a white paper for EURR but none for USDR on October 30 2026, and no USDR contract, chain or launch date had been published. Under Revolut's own terms, no Revolut e-money token is offered before its white paper is published.

brl-itau.title: Brazil's Biggest Private Bank, Still Undecided
brl-itau.text: Itau Unibanco, Brazil's largest private bank by assets, confirmed in April 2025 that it was evaluating its own stablecoin; Head of Digital Assets Guto Antunes told a Sao Paulo industry event the bank is 'always open to understanding whether it makes sense for our clients to have a stablecoin, even one in real, within Itau'. That remains the extent of the public commitment. Brazil's virtual-asset framework, finalised as BCB Resolutions 519 to 521, took effect on February 2, 2026, and Resolution 561, effective October 1, 2026, bars authorised FX providers from settling cross-border remittances in stablecoins. Neither produced an Itau decision. In August 2026 Antunes argued that stablecoins and tokenized deposits must coexist, and in September he described the bank as closely tracking stablecoins as potential payment enablers, with no issuance decision, peg choice, ticker or date. The Drex wholesale pilot, which gave Itau distribution-rail experience, has ended. Pharos tracks the placeholder as BRL-denominated because Brazil's retail base makes a real-denominated first launch the more likely design, though a USD option has not been ruled out, and Pharos removed its 2026 launch expectation in September. The rules Itau was waiting on are in force; the remaining constraint is the bank's own product decision.

moveusd-cfx.title: CFX's Solana Deposit Dollar
moveusd-cfx.text: MoveUSD is a CFX-issued dollar settlement instrument on Solana with a DefiLlama supply feed and a live price path. The token is best read as tokenized-deposit infrastructure rather than a permissionless DeFi-native stablecoin: minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through the issuer for approved customers, while the SPL mint gives Pharos a concrete on-chain supply anchor. Reserves are described as U.S. dollar deposits held 1:1 in segregated custodial accounts at FDIC-member banks, which CFX says are spread through U.S. sponsor banks across a network of more than 3,000 institutions; it names none of them, and no dated reserve report, balance or attestation is public. The mint and freeze authorities sit with a program-derived address whose program remains upgradeable, so issuance is concentrated and unreconciled, and backing and economic control are the two weakest pillars on the card. The detail page carries a tokenized-deposit caveat so users do not confuse the market cap with open retail redemption coverage.

hlusd-hela.title: HeLa's Native Runtime Dollar
hlusd-hela.text: HLUSD is the HeLa ecosystem's centralized dollar stablecoin and the native gas token of HeLa's own runtime, a chain Pharos does not model as a contract platform. HeLa's documentation states that HLUSD is fully backed by custodial USDC managed by a licensed financial institution in Australia, which it does not name, and that one HLUSD equals one dollar. No dated {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, auditor report or reserve-to-liability reconciliation is published, so the backing claim rests on issuer text alone. Issuance runs through on-chain MintProposer and MintVoter roles under an Admin that sets the quorum, and a parallel blacklist vote can stop a holder from sending any state-changing transaction. Pharos coverage depended on CoinGecko's price and market-cap row, which has been stale since August 14 2026, when Biconomy suspended HLUSD trading. With no tracked contract on a supported chain there is no on-chain supply path to replace it, so Pharos quarantined the coin on September 24 2026 and publishes no current report card for it. The durable constraint is that HLUSD's supply, reserves and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} can only be seen through HeLa's own disclosures.

xmd-metal-dollar.title: A Stablecoin Basket on XPR Network
xmd-metal-dollar.text: Metal Dollar is Metallicus's basket-backed dollar token on XPR Network, minted and redeemed 1:1 against whitelisted reserve stablecoins held in the xmd.treasury contract. Issuer materials describe a USDC, PYUSD, and Paxos-dollar basket, but Pharos's live on-chain read of the treasury tells a narrower story: the overwhelming majority is XUSDC, a Metallicus bridge wrapper over Circle's USDC, and most of the remainder is MPD, a Metallicus-issued dollar token that Pharos does not track and scores as high risk. XMD is therefore a proportional claim on a basket that is almost entirely one wrapper, and its safety leans on Circle plus that wrapper's unverified upstream {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. Control sits with a 2-of-4 Metallicus operator multisig that owns both the token and treasury contracts and can change the basket, and XPR Network's block producers can blacklist an account at the protocol level. Pharos admits the asset through CoinGecko's price and market-cap path because XPR Network is not a supported contract chain. Redemption is eligibility-gated, and exit and economic control both trail backing on the card. No dated independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} exists: the treasury is visible on-chain, but the wrapper reserves behind it are not.

vusd-virtue.title: IOTA-Backed CDP Dollar
vusd-virtue.text: Virtue USD is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar on IOTA Rebased, minted by borrowing against {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} IOTA-family positions with {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} as peg defense, plus a wrapped copy on IOTA EVM. On 28 August 2026 an attacker compromised Switchboard's IOTA oracle keys, reported a $10 million IOTA price, minted 4.94 million VUSD against about one IOTA, and cut protocol backing to 8%; 45 users were liquidated before the protocol froze. Virtue relaunched on 19 October 2026 with a peg stability module that mints VUSD 1:1 against USDT0, but the attacker-held VUSD has not been burned. Pharos reads the vaults directly: at the September 2026 capture, stIOTA made up almost all collateral, with only fractional IOTA, vIOTA and iBTC slices, so peg defense rests on one liquid-staking derivative of a volatile Layer-1. Every collateral is valued through a single oracle configuration, IOTA/USD or iBTC, with no fallback. The package is immutable and has no freeze or blacklist function, but an AdminCap held by a single address controls supply limits and module versions. Pharos quarantined the listing on 24 September 2026: no configured reader can count the native IOTA Move supply, the IOTA EVM leg alone is not a defensible circulating figure, and CoinGecko data stopped updating in mid-August. Until a native supply reader exists, the vault data describes collateral against a float Pharos cannot measure. Even with liquidation as peg defense, holders remain exposed to one collateral, one oracle path and one admin key.

stusd-stoneyield.title: StoneYield BNB Chain Yield Wrapper
stusd-stoneyield.text: StoneYield USD is a BNB Chain yield wrapper whose reserve lineage runs through StoneYield's StrategyRouter into a Venus-linked vault holding Binance-Peg USDC. Pharos can trace that lineage on-chain, but not complete strategy balances, allocation weights or a reconciliation to outstanding tokens. No independent audit, proof of reserves or {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} covers the path. StoneYield's homepage calls its contracts audited but names no auditor or report, and the repository's own security file still lists the external audit as planned for Q2 2025.  A single EIP-7702 delegated account holds the default admin role and can grant a minting role whose issuance requires no deposit, so only the immutable 1B supply ceiling bounds new tokens. The same owner can extend or revive wallet locks on balances holders already own. Exit also scores low: the published wrapper code offers no holder unwrap function and Pharos finds no comparable redemption route, leaving market sales as the way out. Until strategy balances are reconciled to supply, the backing rests on the operator's own accounting.

lvusd-leverup.title: Monad Perps Collateral in Stablecoin Form
lvusd-leverup.text: lvUSD is the dollar token of LeverUp's liquidity layer for perpetuals and margin trading on Monad. It is minted inside the protocol's trading engine when positions open against USDC collateral, so {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and reserve depth depend on a trading system rather than a bank balance sheet. That dependency shows in the reserve read: at an October 1, 2026 Monad block, the single issuer-designated vault held about 906,000 USDC against roughly 1.41 million lvUSD outstanding. LeverUp's own documentation says trader profit and loss can pull reserves and supply apart, so the gap of about 500,000 lvUSD is a coverage shortfall rather than a second reserve asset. Issuance is gated only by an upgradeable engine owned by a 3-of-5 Safe, and Pharos scores effective minting as unbounded. The token also carries an operator-gated blacklist, and an operator was appointed as of that October read. The exit pillar is held down because no comparable same-notional redemption route is compiled. A holder's dollar here is a claim on a trading venue's net book, not on a segregated reserve.

nusd-nexus.title: Legacy Synapse Bridge Liquidity
nusd-nexus.text: Nexus USD is a legacy Synapse {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}-liquidity stable asset backed by a pool of DAI, USDC, and USDT, closer to bridge routing infrastructure than to a standalone modern issuer. It is included because DefiLlama still returns both a current price and circulating supply. Fixed-block reads of the Ethereum nexus pool in August 2026 put USDT at more than half of the basket with DAI and USDC splitting the rest, so the upstream reserve basket gives NUSD inherited freezability and stablecoin dependency risk. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects that split: the economic-control pillar leads the card because the LP token and pool are fixed clones with no holder freeze path, while the exit pillar is the weakest of the three because no comparable same-notional redemption route is disclosed. The thirteen reviewed deployments are one native Ethereum LP token plus twelve bridge representations, so the Synapse bridge machinery carries the cross-chain risk.

brlm-mento.title: Mento's Brazilian Real Rail
brlm-mento.text: BRLm is Mento's oracle-priced Brazilian real on Celo, minted and burned against USDm through the Mento Broker at the BRL/USD SortedOracles rate and backed by the shared, diversified Mento reserve rather than by a BRLm-specific trove. Unlike the Mento {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} rows, this entry uses the reserve-wide Mento feed because the CDP trove API only covers GBPm, JPYm, and CHFm. The reserve is diversified but still a mix of CELO, AUSD, sUSDS, USDT, euro stablecoins, USDC, stETH, and smaller assets, so Pharos classifies collateral quality as mixed rather than fiat-reserve grade. The Broker swap is permissionless. The binding cap is unbounded minting, and an oracle finding sits at the same level because the BRL/USD feed runs on a single relayer reporter with a 360-second expiry and no failover. The two-day Mento timelock can also change the token's broker and upgrade the contracts. BRLm is small in absolute supply, and its backing and upgrade path both run through the shared Mento reserve and timelock rather than anything specific to BRLm.

kesm-mento.title: Mento's Reserve-Backed Shilling
kesm-mento.text: KESm is Mento's Kenyan shilling stablecoin on Celo, issued and retired through the USDm/KESm Broker: a swap in burns USDm and mints KESm, and the reverse burns KESm for USDm at the oracle rate. Unlike Mento's GBPm, JPYm and CHFm, which are USDm-collateral {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}}, KESm has no borrower trove or {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} path; its backing is the shared Mento Reserve. That reserve is a mixed basket led by CELO, Agora's AUSD and Sky's sUSDS, with smaller USDT, euro-stablecoin and staked-ETH positions, so reserve risk tracks Mento's own token and several upstream issuers. Exit scores highest of the three pillars because the Broker swap is open to anyone, though Pharos flags its exit routes as correlated.  The token owner can set an arbitrary Broker or minter with no token-level collateral check behind a two-day timelock, and that unbounded-mint finding is the binding cap on the overall grade. Pricing rests on one KES/USD reporter relaying a single Chainlink aggregator, with a six-minute report expiry and a 4% median-delta breaker. The durable constraint is that every KESm {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} depends on that single feed and on a reserve Mento manages for the whole suite.

copm-mento.title: Mento's Colombian Peso
copm-mento.text: COPm is Mento's oracle-priced Colombian peso stablecoin on Celo, minted and burned through the Mento Broker against the shared Mento Reserve rather than fiat held in a bank. That reserve is a mixed basket readable live from the Mento reserve API: CELO, AUSD, and sUSDS hold near-equal leading shares, USDT and euro stablecoins sit behind them, and stETH and ETH make up a small volatile tail. The exit pillar grades well on that conversion route, and the token contract itself has no blacklist, freeze, or pause function, though its owner can replace the implementation. The {{grade}} overall grade is held at a structural cap because the token owner can appoint an arbitrary minter with no token-level collateral check, so issuance is economically unbounded; a two-day Mento timelock delays that power without limiting the amount.  The oracle carries an equal cap: the USDm/COPm exchange prices off a single relayer with a 360-second expiry and no second source. Pharos has limited price coverage for the asset, so the peg line rests on thin observation. The durable constraint is that COPm's supply has no economic bound beyond the owner's minter appointments, and a single relayer sets the price at which the reserve trades against it.

cadm-mento.title: Mento's Canadian Dollar Rail
cadm-mento.text: CADm is Mento's oracle-priced Canadian dollar stablecoin on Celo, issued and retired against USDm through the Mento Broker at the CAD/USD SortedOracles rate and backed by the shared Mento reserve rather than Canadian bank reserves. Circulating supply is small next to the Canadian-issued CAD stablecoins Pharos tracks. The collateral story is therefore Mento reserve exposure: an on-chain basket led by CELO, AUSD, and sUSDS, with USDT, euro stablecoins, stETH, USDC, and smaller assets, held under Mento governance. Pharos classifies that collateral as mixed rather than fiat-reserve grade, so resilience depends on Celo, Mento governance, and the value of the basket. The {{grade}} overall grade is driven by exit, the weakest of the three pillars: {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Mento reserve swaps rather than fiat off-ramps, and Pharos has not established a viable exit path for the tracked supply. Economic control also carries an oracle finding, since the CAD/USD feed has a single reporter and no failover. Backing is the strongest line on the card, which says more about the shared reserve than about CADm's own market.

audm-mento.title: A Shared-Reserve AUD on Celo
audm-mento.text: AUDm is Mento's Australian dollar on Celo, issued and retired through an oracle-priced Broker pool against USDm rather than through a borrower-specific {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}. It is distinct from Macropod's bank-backed AUDM despite the similar ticker. Swapping USDm in burns it and mints AUDm; the reverse burns AUDm and mints USDm, subject to the oracle, spread, trading limits and circuit breakers. Behind that sits the shared Mento Reserve, a multi-asset mix led by CELO, Agora's AUSD and Sky's sUSDS, with no Australian-dollar bank deposit in it. The AUD/USD rate comes from a single relayer reporter with one configured aggregator, and minting is economically unbounded. Exit grades best, because the Broker pool offers a direct on-chain route back to USDm. Circulating supply stands at {{supplyUsd}}. AUDm's durable constraint is that an Australian dollar on Mento is only as sound as a multi-currency crypto reserve and the single oracle feed that prices it.

ghsm-mento.title: Mento's Cedi Stable
ghsm-mento.text: GHSm is Mento's Ghanaian cedi stablecoin on Celo, swapped into and out of existence through Mento's broker pool against USDm and backed by the shared Mento Reserve, a mixed basket of tracked stablecoins such as AUSD, sUSDS, USDT, and EURC alongside CELO and staked ETH. What the card shows is a reserve-backed FX stable whose exit pillar leads, with permissionless swaps back to USDm through the broker, while backing and economic control trail it: the token sits behind a Mento timelock with the veMENTO governor as sole proposer, and Mento's published plan keeps GHSm on the older V2 pool while GBPm and others move to the borrower-CDP model. The {{grade}} overall grade also carries a short track record. The durable constraint is upstream: GHSm is only as sound as the Mento Reserve basket and the oracle rate that prices cedi against it.

zarm-mento.title: Mento's Rand Stable Asset on Celo
zarm-mento.text: ZARm is Mento's South African rand stable asset on Celo, issued and retired through an oracle-priced USDm/ZARm Broker pool rather than against rand bank collateral. Its backing is the shared Mento Reserve: a basket of AUSD, sUSDS, USDT, EUROP, EURC, and USDC alongside CELO, stETH, and ETH, self-custodied in protocol contracts under a 48-hour governance timelock. Reserve quality is therefore the Mento basket's quality, and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} risk sits on that basket rather than on the South African banking system. The {{grade}} overall grade is driven by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three: Pharos has no comparable same-notional exit route on record, and Mento governance is winding down the V2 Broker pools with per-token trading limits capped at outstanding supply plus 10%. Backing grades higher, and economic control sits between the two because Pharos classes the oracle design as single-source or laggy, so the main constraint is the exit route rather than the reserve. The peg line on the card is strong, but price coverage is limited and the token has one Celo deployment with no cross-chain route.

wbrl-ripio.title: Ripio's Wrapped Brazilian Real
wbrl-ripio.text: WBRL is the Brazilian real token in Ripio's wFIAT suite, natively issued at the same contract address on Ethereum, Base, World Chain, BNB Chain, Polygon and Gnosis, with Celo and HyperEVM deployments added in September 2026, and moved between chains through Ripio's first-party burn-and-mint {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} rail. Reserve evidence comes one accountant certification at a time. The latest, as of 30 June 2026, reconciled about 2.59 million outstanding wBRL across seven chains to roughly R$2.59 million in an unnamed Brazilian bank account, expressly not an audit or review. That balance date already sits outside the live adapter's 33-day freshness window, and pinned reads on 19 October 2026 put supply across all eight chains at about 16.7 million wBRL. The weaker point is control. On the six original deployments one Ripio address holds mint and upgrade roles while a 4-of-7 Safe holds admin, and minting is economically unbounded with no qualified reconciliation or supervisory check. The wFIAT whitepaper expressly denies holders any issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} right, leaving exits to secondary markets and Ripio's own on/off-ramp. Local-currency {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at one undisclosed bank is the durable constraint.

wclp-ripio.title: Chilean Peso Token Without a Redemption Right
wclp-ripio.text: WCLP is Ripio's wrapped Chilean peso, one of its wFIAT tokens, targeting one peso per token and backed by Chilean-peso cash and liquid local instruments at institutions Ripio does not name. The central fact is in Ripio's own whitepaper: wFIAT holders have no issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} right and no claim to the funds. Exits run through secondary markets, Ripio's on- and off-ramps, or issuer-managed market operations. The reserve evidence is thin. Ripio's attestation archive links a wCLP certification headed June 30, 2026, but its liability procedure names March 31 and its reserve statements mix Chilean pesos with Argentine pesos, so Pharos cannot use its balances as a reserve composition.  A single Ripio externally owned account directly holds the minting and upgrade roles on six of the token's native deployments, so both new supply and any exit depend on Ripio's discretion. Most supply sits on World Chain, with the rest spread across Polygon and smaller EVM deployments.

wcop-ripio.title: Ripio's Colombian Peso wFIAT Token
wcop-ripio.text: WCOP is Ripio's Colombian peso wFIAT token, admitted through DefiLlama's price and supply coverage with reviewed native deployments on seven EVM chains, linked by Ripio's own burn-and-mint {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} rail. It overlaps thematically with Mento COPm but uses a different issuer model: off-chain local-currency {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and issuer-native issuance on each chain, rather than Celo's Mento reserve. COP is still grouped under OTHER pending broader peg-currency support. Reserve evidence stays thin. The latest accountant certification, as of 30 June 2026, reconciles outstanding wCOP to a Colombian bank account, yet it is expressly not an audit or review, the bank is unnamed, and the wFIAT whitepaper denies holders any issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} right. Ripio announced a further Arc deployment in September 2026 whose controls and supply Pharos has not yet reviewed, so the seven-chain census is incomplete. Issuance on every reviewed chain answers to Ripio-held keys with no qualified reconciliation or supervisory check. Pharos observes no exact DEX or redemption route, so exit scores low as well.

wpen-ripio.title: Peruvian Sol Coverage from Ripio
wpen-ripio.text: WPEN adds Peruvian sol exposure to Pharos through Ripio's local-currency wFIAT suite. DefiLlama supplies price and circulating-supply data, and Pharos has reviewed native issuance on eight EVM chains, from Ethereum and Base to Celo and HyperEVM, linked by Ripio's own burn-and-mint {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} rail. PEN is grouped under OTHER because it does not yet have a dedicated peg category. Reserve transparency is the limiting factor: Ripio's attestation archive publishes accountant certifications for wARS, wBRL, wCOP and wMXN but none for wPEN, so the backing is identified only as a Peruvian-sol cash and liquid-instrument envelope under issuer {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. The wFIAT whitepaper also denies holders any issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} right, so exits depend on markets and Ripio's ramps. A single Ripio address holds mint and upgrade roles on the six original deployments, which leaves economic control the weakest pillar on a {{grade}} card. No sibling-token certificate can stand in for the missing wPEN one, and that gap is the durable constraint.

jaaa-janus-henderson-anemoy.title: AAA CLO Exposure as a Tokenized Fund
jaaa-janus-henderson-anemoy.text: JAAA is a NAV-accreting Janus Henderson AAA CLO fund share issued through Anemoy and Centrifuge rails, permissioned and KYC-gated rather than a $1 redeemable stablecoin. Pharos treats the Chainlink NAV feed as live reserve evidence, while the reserve-risk model stays conservative because even AAA CLO tranches are structured credit rather than cash or Treasury bills, and the feed proves the share value without publishing security-level holdings. The token has multi-chain contract coverage, but the exit pillar is the weakest line on the card: primary-market access is whitelisted, so no comparable open exit route exists for a holder outside it. Mint authority runs through Centrifuge's ward system to a 4-of-9 protocol Safe, which keeps the economic-control pillar well short of the top of the range. The fund share is {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} structured-credit {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}, with Centrifuge {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and permissioned {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at NAV rather than open par exit.

acrdx-anemoy-apollo.title: Apollo Credit Through Anemoy
acrdx-anemoy-apollo.text: ACRDX is a permissioned, NAV-accreting share token from Anemoy and Centrifuge giving on-chain access to Apollo's diversified private credit strategy, not a par stablecoin or cash-like asset. The token is a feeder share in a BVI segregated portfolio that invests in Apollo Diversified Credit Fund, whose book spans corporate direct lending, asset-backed lending, performing credit and dislocated credit, so Pharos classifies the reserve as high-risk {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} credit with a liquidity horizon beyond a week. Chronicle proof-of-asset coverage gives daily NAV visibility on the feeder's holdings, though it covers assets only and does not reconcile them against shares outstanding. Backing is the strongest of the three pillars. Exit is the weakest: {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is a KYC-gated fund process at NAV on documented terms that settle over weeks rather than days, and that holds the {{grade}} overall grade down. The share moves across several EVM chains through Centrifuge's burn-and-mint messaging, but every path back to cash still runs through the fund's own redemption window.

stac-securitize.title: CLO Fund Access on Securitize
stac-securitize.text: STAC is a Securitize-issued tokenized share of a BVI private fund that invests substantially all its assets in AAA-rated CLO tranches, with BNY as custodian and BNY Investments as sub-advisor. Shares are issued natively on Ethereum and, since a June 2026 expansion, on Solana. The token is priced by fund NAV, and investor access runs through Securitize's qualification, transfer-control and primary-market process, so there is no open $1 redemption backstop behind the ticker. Chronicle's daily proof of asset names the fund's CLO positions and publishes a supply breakdown across both chains, but Chronicle disclaims any attestation or audit of the underlying records. Pharos treats the collateral as high-risk structured credit with a liquidity horizon beyond seven days rather than as cash-like reserves. Issuance control is concentrated: on Ethereum a single owner account can mint and authorize upgrades, and on Solana the controller program's upgrade authority is one key with no timelock, shared with the controller that mints VanEck's VBILL. Exit is the weakest pillar by a wide margin and the main drag on the {{grade}} overall grade, because redemption runs through Securitize's offchain issuer process.

hlscope-hamilton-lane.title: Hamilton Lane Private Credit Rail
hlscope-hamilton-lane.text: HLSCOPE is Hamilton Lane's Senior Credit Opportunities Fund tokenized through Securitize as a feeder LP interest for qualified purchasers, priced at fund NAV rather than $1. Subscriptions are monthly and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs on demand at the previous quarter's NAV through Securitize's permissioned rail, so the asset belongs in the NAV-token cohort rather than among open-liquidity stablecoins. The backing is a single slice of feeder exposure to floating-rate senior secured private loans, valued monthly by Hamilton Lane's own valuation team with no independent portfolio verification. Brown Brothers Harriman is depositary for the Luxembourg main fund, but the Delaware feeder's custody of that interest is not publicly documented, and no HLSCOPE-specific recovery waterfall is public.  Issuance and upgrades on the four EVM deployments run through one owner EOA, and Pharos finds that address controlling other Securitize-issued fund tokens too, so a single key failure would reach several funds at once. Distribution spans Ethereum, Polygon, Optimism, Plume, and Tron, with Wormhole interoperability advertised but no HLSCOPE-specific bridge controller verified.
