This is an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund share on {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} rails, and its durable constraint is a qualified-purchaser gate in front of a single issuance key.

pc0000031-tradable.title: Tradable Rent-Financing Term Note
pc0000031-tradable.text: PC0000031 is a KYC-gated Tradable senior secured term note on a North American rent-financing platform, tokenized on zkSync and contract-priced at $1.00 note par with no liquid secondary market. Pharos tracked it as a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} private-credit note ({{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure) with CoinGecko price and market-cap coverage but zero reported volume and no integrated APY feed. Exit is classified as discretionary: holders rely on issuer servicing and note repayment rather than a modeled {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route. Minting runs through Tradable's permissioned DealManager, where two EOAs hold immediate mint permission and one of them also controls the shared token and DealManager beacons. Pharos delisted the entry in July 2026 as out of scope: a permissioned, deal-specific private-credit ownership note priced at contractual par is not a transferable stable-value monetary instrument.

pc0000033-tradable.title: Tradable APAC Consumer-Credit Note
pc0000033-tradable.text: PC0000033 is a Tradable senior secured term-note token backed by APAC consumer-financing receivables, including line-of-credit and BNPL exposure, with the notes issued by Victory Park Capital Advisors. It is contract-priced at note par and not defended by a liquid secondary-market peg: while tracked, CoinGecko showed a par price and market cap with zero 24-hour volume. Minting is permissioned through Tradable's zkSync deal machinery, where two EOAs hold immediate mint permission and one also controls the shared token and DealManager beacons, and Pharos never integrated a yield source for it. Pharos delisted the entry in July 2026 as out of scope: a permissioned, deal-specific private-credit ownership note priced at contractual par is not a transferable stable-value monetary instrument. The token is private-credit infrastructure whose value rests on note servicing and repayment.

pc0000101-tradable.title: Legal Finance at Par
pc0000101-tradable.text: PC0000101 is Tradable's tokenized exposure to a Victory Park senior post-settlement legal-financing facility for a U.S. law firm. The token is priced at $1 note par by contract and issuer servicing rather than by a liquid market defending a payment-stablecoin peg. While listed, Pharos treated the CoinGecko price as a private-credit reference point and flagged zero reported volume rather than implying deep exit liquidity. The reserve is classified as 100% high-risk legal-finance receivables, and minting runs only through Tradable's permissioned zkSync DealManager. Pharos delisted the token on 15 July 2026 as out of scope: a permissioned, deal-specific private-credit ownership note priced at contractual par is not a transferable stable-value monetary instrument. Holder value rests on issuer servicing and repayment of one senior term-loan facility to a single U.S. law firm.

pc0000089-tradable.title: Tradable LatAm Residential Credit Note
pc0000089-tradable.text: PC0000089 is a Tradable token for a Latin American residential-lending senior secured term-loan note, issued through Victory Park and represented on zkSync. The $1 reference is contract par rather than a market-cleared stablecoin peg. The collateral is a single high-risk LatAm residential credit exposure with no public loan-level allocation, collateral valuation or independent reserve assurance, and minting is permissioned through Tradable's DealManager, where two issuer EOAs hold immediate mint permission. While listed, CoinGecko reported a $1 price and market cap against zero volume, and Pharos kept its yield as an intentional gap with no public APY feed wired. Pharos delisted the token on 15 July 2026 as out of scope: a permissioned, deal-specific private-credit ownership note priced at contractual par is not a transferable stable-value monetary instrument. Holder value rests on Victory Park's servicing and repayment of a single credit note.

asusdf-astherus.title: Astherus Yield Wrapper
asusdf-astherus.text: asUSDF is Aster's staked wrapper over USDF: the share accrues NAV from upstream delta-neutral and funding-fee strategies, while the base stablecoin risk remains USDF's stack of USDT held through Ceffu and deployed on Binance and MirrorX. Deposits mint asUSDF against USDF, and withdrawals return USDF after a documented waiting period of an hour or two, with no mint or withdrawal fee. Pharos records the direct reserve as one wrapped USDF position rather than crediting the wrapper with a balance sheet of its own. The wrapper's own weak point is its token contract. The deposit contract mints shares only after receiving USDF, but the token itself lets any holder of its minter role mint without a deposit, and the role's timelocked admin can grant that role to a chosen caller. That makes economic control the weakest of the three pillars, below backing, while exit through the protocol's own withdrawal route scores highest. The {{grade}} overall grade is held at the parent USDF rating in any case, so asUSDF cannot score better than the dollar it wraps.

mf-one-midas.title: Fasanara F-ONE tokenized strategy certificate
mf-one-midas.text: mF-ONE is a Midas tokenized certificate over Fasanara's F-ONE strategy, spanning fintech receivables, SME lending, real-estate-backed credit, and digital-asset strategies. It is a permissioned NAV product rather than a bank-reserve stablecoin, so its price follows strategy valuation instead of resting on a hard $1 redemption floor. The legal chain runs through several layers: the reference fund is a Fasanara SICAV-RAIF sub-fund, Infinite Tokens S.A. holds the note, and Midas Software GmbH is the note's beneficiary and the token's issuer. Midas publishes a daily NAV and reserve dashboard, but the reported reserve does not reconcile cleanly to the note, and loan-level composition, borrower concentration and holder custody rights remain undisclosed. Pharos classifies the collateral as high-risk private credit with a liquidity horizon beyond a week. Control is concentrated too: a 1-of-3 Safe and a separate key can rotate mint operators immediately, though upgrades sit behind a two-day timelock. With the reserve envelope unresolved and no same-size exit route measurable, the report card is currently not rated for insufficient evidence, which records missing disclosure and carries no safety verdict.

mglobal-midas-fasanara.title: Fasanara Receivables Note on Midas Rails
mglobal-midas-fasanara.text: mGLOBAL is a tokenized note issued by a Luxembourg securitisation compartment through Midas rails, giving exposure to Fasanara's receivables strategy: largely short-dated trade receivables and digital invoices bought from SMEs. It accrues NAV from portfolio performance, so it is not a fixed $1 payment stablecoin. Pharos models the reserve as a single high-risk private-credit slice; the latest dated proof-of-reserve claim it could inspect valued the underlying fund as of May 31, 2026, and no current loan tape is published. Holders sit several layers away from the receivables, and the reviewed terms subordinate the notes to compartment unitholders in the payment waterfall. Primary issuance and redemption run through permissioned Midas rails behind a documented multi-route liquidity waterfall, and the exit pillar is still the weakest line on the card. Since June 23, 2026, holders can also post mGLOBAL as collateral on Aave's Horizon RWA market to borrow USDC, RLUSD or GHO, though Pharos flags thin secondary-market volume. The durable constraints are private-credit opacity, token-level subordination and a 1-of-3 admin Safe that can rotate mint operators immediately.

mhyper-midas.title: Hyperithm Market-Neutral Certificate
mhyper-midas.text: mHYPER is a Midas NAV certificate tracking a Hyperithm-managed reference portfolio of market-neutral stablecoin strategies. It accrues through daily NAV rather than holding a fixed $1 peg, and tokenholders hold a qualified subordinated claim on the issuer, not ownership of the underlying assets. The signed July 2026 final terms require delta neutrality and cap gross leverage at 8.0x across basis arbitrage, market making and on-chain and off-chain yield. Pharos can value the token through the Midas attestation stack published via Chainlink, but the issuer API reports only protocol-level totals and three anonymous exchange balances, with no position inventory. Custody runs through Fordefi under issuer-admin controls. The exit terms are documented rather than measured: standard USDC redemption is gated at 15% of outstanding tokens per settlement day, and instant redemption costs 0.5% with up to half retainable under a deferred-price method. With the position book unpublished and no comparable same-notional exit route compiled, Pharos leaves the card unrated. The strategy label is market neutral; the holder's exposure is to Midas as obligor and to venues it does not name.

mmev-midas.title: Discontinued Midas Strategy Wrapper
mmev-midas.text: mMEV is a Midas NAV token whose original strategy manager no longer runs it: Midas ended its MEV Capital partnership in February 2026 and handed the strategy to RockawayX. Midas's April 30 recap then announced mMEV's discontinuation on May 10, 2026 and directed holders to withdraw or reinvest in mROX. The token accrues through NAV appreciation, and its exit runs through Midas redemption rails rather than an open par path built for payments. Midas's own transparency page says mMEV shares its underlying strategy and wallets with the mROX token, and the only fresh reporting covers the two jointly, so no standalone mMEV allocation exists to check; the token-specific API book has not updated since June 18. An October 8 instant redemption returned about 59 USDC through the redemption vault, one small residual execution rather than evidence of funded capacity, and no comparable same-notional exit route is compiled. On those gaps the card is unrated for insufficient evidence. Mint operators sit behind 1-of-3 admin Safes with immediate rotation rights and two-day timelocked upgrades on each of three native chains. The durable constraint is that the outstanding supply of a discontinued product depends on a residual redemption channel and a reserve book shared with its successor.

mapollo-midas.title: Apollo Crypto Strategy via Midas
mapollo-midas.text: mAPOLLO is the Midas liquid-yield certificate over an Apollo Crypto managed strategy, distinct from Apollo's credit-fund tokens and from a transactional stablecoin; the signed July 2026 final terms name ACM International Ltd as reference-portfolio manager. Its value follows NAV through permissioned Midas mint and redeem rails, and holders have a claim on Midas as issuer rather than on the strategy's assets. The terms require the portfolio to stay delta-neutral across basis trading, market making, on-chain and centralized yield, and derivatives, with gross leverage capped at 8.0x. Midas's transparency API shows how much of that room is in use: its October 7 checkpoint reported about $45 million of protocol-level assets against roughly $39 million of borrow liabilities, leaving under $7 million of equity. Those buckets mix assets and debt and do not reconcile to token liabilities, so Pharos keeps the reserve as one unresolved high-risk envelope. With no comparable exit route compiled either, the card stays unrated for insufficient evidence. The durable constraint is reconciliation: no published book ties the strategy's positions to mAPOLLO's token liabilities or shows the delta-neutral mandate being met.

safo-spiko-usd.title: Spiko Smart Cash USD Share Class
safo-spiko-usd.text: SAFO is the USD share class of Spiko and Amundi's Smart Cash exposure, built around fully collateralized overnight total-return swaps rather than direct T-bill ownership. Pharos classifies the reserve as medium-risk RWA strategy exposure because the holder is exposed to fund structure, the swap counterparty (currently BNP Paribas), collateral packages, and regulated NAV mechanics. The AMF/UCITS framework and the CACEIS depositary help. Audit evidence is still thin: PwC certifies the Spiko SICAV's accounts at a December year-end, and SAFO, launched in March 2026, has not yet reached one. The AMF-hosted June 2026 semiannual statement is not an audit opinion. Primary market access remains permissioned through Spiko rails, with subscriptions and redemptions at fund NAV. The eight reviewed deployments are issuer-native Spiko share registers, so no third-party bridge carries the claim. The {{grade}} overall grade is held back by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three, where that eligibility-gated primary market shows up. SAFO is a NAV-accreting fund share, and the ticker does not make it a par-redeemable stablecoin.

spkcc-spiko.title: Regulated Cash-and-Carry Fund Share
spkcc-spiko.text: SPKCC is the dollar share class of Spiko's Digital Assets Cash & Carry Fund, a French professional specialised fund whose NAV tracks a cash-and-carry index of BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP {{term:basis-trade}}basis trades{{/term}}, with cash held when carry is insufficient. It is a fund share carrying a stablecoin's ticker rather than a dollar promise. The fund takes that exposure by buying a note issued by Marex Financial, so holders bear Marex's default risk and the underlying spot positions are not direct fund holdings. CACEIS Bank acts as custodian and depositary, and CACEIS Fund Administration strikes a daily NAV that is published on-chain. The prudential hook is the AMF-authorised management company; the fund itself is registered rather than authorised. Reporting is annual and the first financial year closes in December 2026, so no PwC statutory opinion exists yet. On the reserve side, Pharos sees one unsplit strategy envelope with no published spot, derivative, venue or cash weights. Exit is the weakest pillar and the main drag on the {{grade}} overall grade. Holdings are restricted to KYC-allowlisted addresses, the prospectus allows redemption gates and exceptional settlement of up to thirty days, and Pharos has not established the settlement terms for issuer redemption.

eursafo-spiko.title: EUR Smart Cash Through Spiko
eursafo-spiko.text: EURSAFO is the euro share class of Spiko and Amundi's Smart Cash fund, an AMF-authorised UCITS sub-fund whose NAV accretes from fully collateralized overnight total-return swaps rather than from bank deposits. BNP Paribas is the current swap counterparty and CACEIS Bank the depositary, so Pharos records the reserve as medium-risk fund exposure instead of euro cash. Disclosure has improved: Spiko's holdings feed now publishes dated equity, swap-leg and cash rows, and the June 2026 semiannual report locates the share class within the fund's filed inventory. Neither is an audit opinion, and no SAFO-specific opinion from PwC, the named statutory auditor, has been verified. On the {{grade}} overall card, economic control grades highest and exit lowest: subscriptions and redemptions run through KYC-gated Spiko rails at NAV, and Pharos has not established a settlement term for that route. Backing sits between them because counterparty, custody-continuity, default-recovery and NAV-reconciliation detail remain unpublished. The exposure is conservative fund risk with euro accounting, and the only exit runs through Spiko's eligibility check.

eurspkcc-spiko.title: Euro Carry, Fund First
eurspkcc-spiko.text: EURSPKCC is the euro share class of Spiko's Digital Assets Cash & Carry Fund, a French FPS alternative investment fund rather than a euro payment token: NAV accrues from fund performance and primary access is KYC-gated through Spiko's transfer rails. The strategy holds long spot crypto against short CME futures alongside short-duration cash and T-bills, with Marex as structured-note counterparty and CACEIS Bank as custodian and depositary. The share class's own disclosure is thin. Spiko's feed publishes aggregate assets and NAV with no constituent weights, and that NAV reaches the chain through one permissioned administrative oracle rather than a redundant feed. On a {{grade}} overall card, exit is the weakest pillar and economic control the next: Pharos has not established a settlement term for the issuer redemption route, and the prospectus lets the fund gate net redemptions above 10% for up to twenty NAVs within a month. PwC is the appointed statutory auditor, but the first financial year closes in December 2026, so the recurring check today is CACEIS Fund Administration's daily NAV rather than an audit opinion. The packaging is regulated; the {{term:basis-trade}}basis{{/term}} exposure underneath is a crypto strategy whose positions Spiko does not itemise.

uktbl-spiko.title: Sterling T-Bills, Gated
uktbl-spiko.text: UKTBL is Spiko's GBP-denominated UK Treasury-bill money-market fund share, not a dollar product and not a retail payment stablecoin. The backing is dull by crypto standards: short-dated UK T-bills with a settlement cash buffer, run as an AMF-authorised UCITS short-term VNAV money-market fund with PwC as statutory auditor, though the audit reports are available on written request rather than published. The tradeoff is access, because subscriptions, transfers, and redemptions are KYC-gated through Spiko fund rails at NAV rather than settled by permissionless on-chain arbitrage, which is why exit is the weakest of the three pillars behind the {{grade}} overall grade. Backing is the strongest pillar, scored as tokenized {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure, while Pharos keeps centralized issuer controls, blacklistability, and the single-key minter accounts on Starknet and Stellar visible. The durable constraint is operational: the reserve is short-dated sovereign debt, but every entry and exit runs through Spiko's fund administration.

gbpsafo-spiko.title: GBP Overnight Swap Fund Share
gbpsafo-spiko.text: GBPSAFO is the GBP share class of the Spiko Amundi Overnight Swap Fund, an AMF-authorized UCITS sub-fund whose permissioned token accretes NAV against a SONIA-linked objective. The fund earns that return through total-return swaps: its September 2026 prospectus permits bonds, equities and money-market instruments hedged with one or more swap counterparties, names BNP Paribas as the initial counterparty, and uses CACEIS Bank as depositary. Pharos has no current holdings or counterparty weights, so the {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure is a named structure rather than a measured book. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three by a wide margin. Subscriptions and redemptions run through Spiko's KYC perimeter at NAV, no comparable same-notional route is disclosed for anyone outside it, and the prospectus lets the manager cap redemptions for up to 20 valuation days once net requests reach a quarter of the sub-fund. Transfers are whitelisted on both sides, and on Stellar, where most supply sits, Spiko's permission system can de-list holders and burn balances. The token is a fund share for onboarded investors, and its constraint is access: outside that perimeter there is no documented way out at NAV.

eur0-usual.title: Usual's Euro Treasury Wrapper
eur0-usual.text: EUR0 is Usual's euro stablecoin, minted on Ethereum against tokenized Eurozone T-bill collateral, in practice Spiko's EUTBL, through Usual's collateral module, with {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} swapping EUR0 back into that collateral through the dApp. The reserve thesis is a {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}}-bill fund dependency rather than a euro bank-deposit account: on-chain reads show the EUR0 collateral treasury holding EUTBL and nothing else, with supply reconciled against it, so EUR0 is an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-backed dependency token whose backing rests on Spiko's fund and its depositary, CACEIS Bank. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects three pillars clustered in the middle of the range, and economic control shows the sharpest concentration: two Usual modules hold the mint role, but the same 8-of-15 Safe signer set can add minters and replace the token implementation, and the token carries an admin-managed blacklist. Market coverage is thin: the price comes from a single source and depeg-event coverage is limited, so the clean peg record carries less weight than it appears to. What Pharos shows is a fully reconciled one-asset reserve behind a Safe that can widen minting without a numeric cap.

emxn-telcoin.title: Telcoin's Mexican Peso Cash Token
emxn-telcoin.text: eMXN is Telcoin's centralized Mexican peso stablecoin on Polygon, an eXYZ Digital Cash token issued by Telcoin LLC for payments and settlement in the Telcoin Wallet, with reserves that are issuer-reported and carry no public per-token feed. Reserve confidence depends on Telcoin's off-chain controls and reporting: the terms describe segregated accounts at regulated financial institutions but name no institution, and the monthly attestations Telcoin says it will publish had not appeared in the reviewed materials. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} sits with the issuer, and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Telcoin's wallet rails at 1:1 for verified account holders, minus a 0.15% issuer fee plus bank and partner charges, typically within one to three business days and longer for requests above $2,000. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects that gap: backing and exit are both held back, and no depeg episode is on record across more than two years of tracking, though the price feed is a low-volume fallback. The durable constraint is a peso claim whose reserves holders cannot see.

hchf-hedera-swiss-franc.title: Hedera's Small CHF Experiment
hchf-hedera-swiss-franc.text: HCHF is HLiquity's Swiss-franc synthetic on Hedera, minted against overcollateralized HBAR troves in a Liquity-style design rather than issued from a regulated franc account. Borrowers create HCHF from HBAR positions at a 110% minimum collateral ratio, undercollateralized troves are liquidated through the Stability Pool, and face-value redemptions against collateral are the peg-defense mechanism. The upside is unusually clean on-chain control: the Hedera token has no admin, freeze, wipe, or pause key, the core protocol contracts have renounced ownership, the token contract accepts mint calls only from the fixed borrowing contract, and Pharos marks governance as immutable-code rather than issuer discretion, which is why economic control leads the {{grade}} report card. The downside is equally plain: collateral is volatile HBAR, the float is small, and the exit pillar is the weakest of the three. Prices come from a Pyth and Supra oracle pair, and Pharos's review has not settled which one is primary on the live deployment. Anyone expecting the comfort of a Swiss bank attestation will not find one; the durable constraint is that the franc claim is only as good as HBAR and the pools that hold it.

eurot-token-teknoloji.title: Token Teknoloji's Euro Token
eurot-token-teknoloji.text: EUROT is Token Teknoloji's centralized euro stablecoin issued from Turkey, deployed on Ethereum, Avalanche and Polygon and described as backed 1:1 by euro bank reserves at Ziraat Participation Bank and Akbank. The reserve evidence is thin: the proof-of-reserves page is shared across seven tokens, the bank letters it links are bare balance certificates dated 2024, and no current balances, bank split or {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} feed are published, so backing is graded on an undisclosed composition. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down hardest by economic control, the weakest pillar: single externally owned accounts own each deployment and can mint without an on-chain cap, and the contracts carry an issuer-controlled external transfer rail whose counterparts are unidentified. Exit is barely stronger: holders can trade through Bitlo, but no direct redemption route is disclosed and no comparable same-notional exit is on record. The peg has no episode on record over three years of tracking with single-source coverage. Without a dated reserve statement or a disclosed redemption route, both backing and exit rest on issuer assertion.

mxne-real-mxn.title: Brale and Etherfuse's MXN Rail
mxne-real-mxn.text: MXNe is a Mexican peso token issued by Brale in partnership with Etherfuse, deployed on Base, Solana, and Stellar with issuer-managed mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through Brale onboarding. The backing is the Etherfuse CETES Stablebond, a token over short-duration Mexican federal Treasury bills held at regulated Mexican {{term:custody}}custodians{{/term}}, mostly BBVA Mexico, through INDEVAL. BHR Mexico publishes monthly reasonable-assurance {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} reconciling CETES tokens in circulation to backing assets, but that examination covers Etherfuse's whole CETES program rather than an MXNe-specific ledger, so Pharos records the backing category without an MXNe balance claim. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects an exit pillar that is the weakest of the three, with redemption gated to onboarded customers. Control risk is concrete: on each chain a single issuer-controlled key holds all mint and admin rights, and the Base contract is an upgradeable proxy under that key. The durable constraint is that the reserve assurance belongs to Etherfuse while the token liability belongs to Brale.

wmxn-ripio.title: Ripio's Mexican Peso wFIAT Token
wmxn-ripio.text: wMXN is the Mexican peso token in Ripio's wFIAT suite, issued natively by a Ripio affiliate at one address on Ethereum, Base, World Chain, BNB Chain, Polygon and Gnosis, with further catalogued deployments and Ripio's own burn-and-mint {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} rail between them. DefiLlama provides the live price and circulating-supply path. The peg relies on Ripio's on/off-ramp conversion and DEX arbitrage, because the wFIAT whitepaper expressly denies holders any issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} right. Reserve evidence is thin rather than absent. The latest accountant certification, as of 30 June 2026, reconciled about 969,000 outstanding wMXN across seven chains to about MXN 2.09 million in an unnamed Mexican bank account, more than twice the outstanding supply, and the report does not explain the surplus. It is expressly not an audit or review, and its balance date already sits outside the live adapter's 33-day freshness window. Ripio's issuer address holds mint and upgrade roles on every reviewed native deployment, with a 4-of-7 Safe as admin. Issuer-held {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at one undisclosed bank, with no holder claim on it, is the durable constraint.

jpyt-dephaser.title: Dollar-Collateral Yen Under Single-Key Control
jpyt-dephaser.text: JPYT is Dephaser's yen-pegged token on Optimism and Base. Users lock USDT on Optimism or USDC on Base and mint JPYT at the USD/JPY rate from Chainlink and Pyth oracles; {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} burns JPYT for the underlying dollar token. The locked collateral is supplied to Aave V3 rather than held directly, so the reserve is a claim on Aave deposits, mostly USDT, and never yen cash. Holders carry the dollar stablecoins' issuer risk, Aave's withdrawal liquidity and the oracle's FX pricing in one position. Economic control is the weakest pillar by a wide margin. On each chain a single EOA holds the admin role over minting and can grant itself the minter role and mint without bound. The deposit managers that hold the collateral are upgradeable proxies whose own single-key admins can replace the mint implementation. Supply is small. The durable constraint is that every JPYT rests on one key per chain that can create unbacked supply or rewrite the contract holding the collateral.

euro3-3a-dao.title: A Tiny Overcollateralized Euro CDP
euro3-3a-dao.text: EURO3 is 3A DAO's {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} euro {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin on Polygon and Linea, minted against whitelisted crypto and stablecoin collateral in user-owned vaults and burned when borrowers repay or redeem. Backing is the strongest of the three pillars: Pharos's live read of both vault factories puts the bulk of a small collateral pool in Mendi meUSDC receipts on Linea, with WETH and WBTC making up most of the rest, so the collateral is real but leans on a single lending market wrapped around freezable USDC. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by economic control, the weakest pillar. The token contracts are immutable with no freeze or blacklist hook, but minter authorization on both chains runs through owner proxies controlled by a single externally owned account with no multisig. Collateral pricing divides by one Chainlink EUR/USD feed with a 24-hour staleness bound and no fallback. Exit is held back too: the collateral redemption route has no established cost, and the float is tiny. The peg record shows no episode, but Pharos flags depeg-event coverage for EURO3 as limited, so the clean record is weak evidence. The binding constraint is control: a single externally owned account stands behind minting on both chains.

xofm-mento.title: Mento's CFA Franc Stable
xofm-mento.text: XOFm is Mento's West African CFA franc stablecoin on Celo, minted and burned through the Mento Broker: a USDm-to-XOFm swap burns the incoming USDm and mints XOFm at the XOF/USD oracle rate, the reverse burns XOFm back into USDm, and every swap passes spread, trading-limit, freshness, and circuit-breaker checks. There is no trove, health factor, or {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} path; the claim sits on the shared Mento Reserve. Pharos's live read of that reserve shows CELO, AUSD, and sUSDS as the three largest lines, with USDT, euro stablecoins, stETH, and smaller USDC and ETH sleeves making up the rest. The swap path is permissionless and the token contract exposes no blacklist or freeze, with upgrades gated by a two-day timelock, which is why exit leads the card. Pharos classes the oracle design as single-source or laggy, and the token owner can appoint a new minter with no token-level collateral check. Backing is held back because Mento publishes no default-recovery procedure, encumbrance inventory, or dated liability reconciliation for the shared reserve. The durable constraint is that XOFm's franc peg is only as good as an oracle feed and a reserve shared across every Mento currency.

xnk-kinka.title: Japanese Gold Bullion Token
xnk-kinka.text:
Kinka's XNK represents one fine troy ounce equivalent of 99.99% Japanese-brand physical gold bullion, issued on Ethereum and Cardano against centralized issuer custody.

The whitepaper places the bars with Loomis International under Gold Management LLC, and the reserve model treats the backing as physical gold with centralized custody and issuer-controlled exchange terms. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} into physical bars is possible only through the documented KYC process and size thresholds, and no dated XNK-specific reserve {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} was located in the issuer's published materials. On 18 August 2026 the issuer announced final exchange trading suspensions and set 30 October 2026 deadlines for buyback and gold-exchange requests, and Pharos delisted XNK the same day. What remains is a wind-down window in which holders must act through the issuer's buyback or gold-exchange process before the deadline passes.

gynusd-gyndore.title: The cbBTC-Only CDP
gynusd-gyndore.text: gynUSD is Gyndore's pre-launch {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin on Base, built around a single proposition: cbBTC is the only collateral. Borrowers can mint at a 110% minimum collateralization ratio, roughly 90.91% LTV, with on-chain redemptions for $1 of cbBTC below peg and a Stability Pool absorbing liquidations. Seventy percent of borrow fees go to Stability Pool depositors. GYND holders can move the borrow rate only in ±10bps steps through the Pareto Controller, with 80% consensus and a 24-hour challenge window, and a bootstrapping admin key holds that power until the fee switch triggers. Launch preparation has advanced without reaching the product. A public testnet on Base Sepolia was live by late August 2026, the GYND governance token was deployed on Base mainnet in September, and a liquidity bootstrapping event sold out that month. No gynUSD contracts are published, and Sherlock, named as audit partner, has produced no published report. The cbBTC dependency is the structural limit: Coinbase can freeze cbBTC addresses, so a custodian sits under every loan however the protocol governs itself.

tgld-tenbin.title: Synthetic Gold Debt-Note
tgld-tenbin.text: tGLD is Tenbin's tokenized gold note, but unlike PAXG or XAUT it holds no vaulted metal. Each token is a Tenbin AssetCo (BVI) debt-note representing the U.S.-dollar value of one troy ounce of gold, collateralized by USDC and hedged with CME gold futures. Off-chain, the USDC sits with Ripple Prime (formerly Hidden Road), the prime broker Tenbin's docs name as custodian. Mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are KYC-gated through a Controller and a backend signer that holds the on-chain minter role, and redemptions settle in a USD stablecoin instead of physical metal. It went live on Ethereum mainnet in February 2026 after four security audits and remains in private beta. The float was about 140 tGLD on September 27 2026, up from roughly 54 in June. Public trading is thin: a dormant Uniswap V4 pool, plus 1inch routing since September in which Tenbin itself quotes liquidity against USDC. Pharos lists it pre-launch because its gold data path needs a fresh CoinGecko market cap, which was 54 hours stale on October 25 2026. Since September 15 a Chainlink Proof of Reserve feed on Base has published an enclave-computed figure for Tenbin's off-chain reserves. It reports one total across all Tenbin assets, and no independent attestation of tGLD's own reserves has been published.

ejpy-jbfd.title: Japan Open Chain's Trust-Type Yen
ejpy-jbfd.text: EJPY is Japan Blockchain Foundation's pre-launch yen stablecoin, structured as a trust-type Type III electronic payment instrument under Japan's Payment Services Act. That classification exempts it from the ¥1M-per-transaction cap that constrains fund-transfer-type issuers such as JPYC. JBFD, the operator of Japan Open Chain, would be the settlor, with reserves held by a licensed trust bank it has still not named. The design rests on trust-segregated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and bankruptcy-remote reserves, yet the trustee, the reserve mix, and the issuance date are all undisclosed. In September 2026 JBFD opened a roughly six-month pilot in which 26 enterprises, financial institutions and local governments, Toshiba among them, explore use cases with test EJPY tokens; the pilot announcement says the trust structure, issuance and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} processes, and legal compliance are still in preparation. Commercial issuance is targeted on Japan Open Chain within fiscal 2026, which runs through March 2027, with Ethereum next, for B2B payments, remittances and settlement. Until a trustee is named and commercial issuance begins, test tokens are the only EJPY in circulation.

aed-rakbank.title: The First Commercial-Bank Dirham
aed-rakbank.text: AED-RAKBANK is RAKBank's pre-launch dirham stablecoin, notable less for its design than for its issuer: the first conventional commercial-bank AED payment token under the Central Bank of the UAE's regime, distinct from Zand AED, AE Coin and the FAB/ADQ/IHC dirham initiative. The in-principle approval came on January 7, 2026 under the Payment Token Services Regulation, conditional on RAKBank completing the remaining regulatory and operational requirements. That regulation shapes the product before any code ships. A bank may not act as a payment token issuer itself, so the token has to come from a licensed subsidiary, affiliate or related entity, and a licensed issuer may only issue dirham tokens to UAE residents. The announced design covers the expected ground: 1:1 dirhams in segregated regulated accounts, full par {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, audited smart contracts and real-time reserve {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, aimed at payments, asset tokenization and cross-border settlement. No ticker, chain, issuing entity or launch date has been disclosed, and the bank says only that a pilot phase will follow in due course. Until contracts and a first reserve report exist, the approval describes intent rather than a token Pharos can assess.

bils-bitsofgold.title: Israel's First Regulated Shekel
bils-bitsofgold.text: BILS is the first shekel stablecoin to clear an Israeli regulator. Bits of Gold, a Tel Aviv crypto broker and custodian, spent two years in a sandbox before the Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority approved a limited launch on April 28, 2026. The approval conditions are concrete: 1:1 New Israeli Shekel backing in segregated bank accounts inside Israel with foreign custody excluded, an Ernst & Young audit, Fireblocks issuance infrastructure, and QEDIT zero-knowledge privacy, all on Solana via token extensions. The regulator also required a deliberately gradual, small-scale rollout. Bits of Gold announced in July 2026 that the pilot was complete and BILS was moving to wide distribution, but the on-chain record has not followed. The published Solana mint still held 100,000 BILS on November 1, 2026, unchanged since August 6. The issuer's transparency page shows the same 100K ILS in circulation and 105K ILS in reserves, with its Q3 2026 Ernst & Young report listed as pending. Pharos also tracks the peg as OTHER until shekel support exists, so BILS stays in pre-launch. The approval sits under the CMISA rulebook; Israel's broader Stablecoin Law is still in draft. Until the Ernst & Young report is published, the approval is better documented than the token.

autousd-auto-finance.title: An Autopool Dollar Wrapper
autousd-auto-finance.text: autoUSD is Auto Finance's USDC autopool share token on Ethereum: holders own a vault receipt rather than a fiat-reserve stablecoin, and the share price is expected to rise as strategy earnings auto-compound. Autopools rebalance across eligible DeFi destinations, so the dollar anchor comes from USDC as the vault asset while the extra risk comes from destination selection, liquidity, and controller operations. Pharos reads the Ethereum contract directly for supply and price, and Royco Dawn's senior/junior tranche market wraps the same vault token. The overall grade is {{grade}}, and economic control is by far the weakest of the three pillars: the 6-of-11 Safe that owns the proxy admin can replace the implementation without a contract-enforced delay, any of four emergency-pauser accounts can halt every holder transfer, and Pharos treats effective minting as economically unbounded. Exit grades best of the three; withdrawals redeem shares for USDC subject to autopool liquidity and destination unwinds rather than through an issuer's redemption desk. The durable constraint is structural: this is a strategy wrapper over USDC rather than a redeemable issuer dollar.

eearn-ember.title: Ember's Royco-Listed Vault Share
eearn-ember.text: eEARN is Ember's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} USDC vault share, issued natively as separate vault tokens on Ethereum and Sui, whose value follows the vault's USDC share price rather than a flat par claim; Royco Dawn wraps eEARN into senior and junior tranche vaults. The card behind the {{grade}} overall grade splits sharply. Economic control leads, because Ethereum shares are minted only against deposited USDC. Backing sits in the middle: almost all deposits are deployed into Ember-managed strategies whose holdings, custody terms and reconciliation are not disclosed. The exit pillar is the weakest of the three by a wide margin, because withdrawals go through an operator-processed request queue with no proven settlement bound and an admin-set withdrawal fee. Issuer control is real but narrow: a protocol guardian can blacklist owners and receivers at redemption and again at queued settlement, and the implementation can be replaced through a timelock whose proposer, executor and canceller roles each sit with a single externally owned account behind a one-day delay. Upstream USDC freeze exposure passes straight through.

dusd-dialectic.title: Dialectic's Book, Tokenised
dusd-dialectic.text: DUSD is a USDC-accounted Makina strategy share whose price follows Dialectic's marked AUM per share rather than a fixed dollar claim. The operator rotates deposits through credit, lending and liquidity venues under a curated instruction set, and Pharos reads first-party live accounting for allocations, supply and NAV. Exits run through a queue that the operator finalizes once it frees USDC; the Machine Terms grant no contractual redemption right or queue priority, and requests may remain unfilled indefinitely. Ordinary DUSD transfers are unrestricted, but the redeemer screens requests and claims against a sanctions oracle whose owner is a single externally owned account. Custody is equally blunt: Dialectic owns the deployed assets outright, and holders receive no trust, priority or bankruptcy-remote claim. The {{grade}} overall grade is held back most by economic control, because fee-share minting has raiseable maxima that can dilute holders without new AUM. The durable constraint is an exit that depends on the operator's discretion and on upstream USDC, which Circle can freeze.

ousd-open-standard.title: A Consortium Dollar on Bridge's Terms
ousd-open-standard.text: Open USD is issued by Bridge Building Inc. for Open Standard, whose initial founding partners are Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe and Visa. Onboarded partner businesses mint and redeem 1:1 with no issuer fee and earn rewards in proportion to the supply and activity they drive. Holders sit outside that economics: Bridge's binding terms give them no property interest in the reserve and entitle Bridge to its net returns. The same terms extend {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} to later holders only if they are eligible and onboard as Bridge users, with processing due within two business days of compliance approval. That gate makes exit the weakest pillar behind the {{grade}} overall grade. The backing evidence is Bridge's own live dashboard: cash and short {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}}, with BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY named as reserve institutions and monthly {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} announced but no independent report yet linked. Tempo carries the largest share of the four-chain supply. Every deployment is restrictable: one administrator address holds default admin rights on the Tempo, Ethereum and Base tokens, including transfer-policy and pause control, and the Solana mint carries freeze and permanent-delegate authorities. Partner rewards can grow the float without widening what an outside holder can claim.

rd-rai-dollar.title: Reflexer's Controller-Steered $1 CDP
rd-rai-dollar.text: RAI Dollar, from the Reflexer team behind RAI, keeps RAI's on-chain controller but pins the target at $1. RD is a pre-launch immutable CDP stablecoin on Ethereum where a PI controller reads a 24-hour TWAP of the market price and moves one system-wide borrow rate, bounded to 0.25-50% APY around a 2% bias, while Liquity-style redemption at par less a fee sets the floor. A second lever adjusts the internal redemption price within a $0.75-$1.30 band, at no more than a tenth of a cent an hour, and only under sustained extreme deviation. Collateral sits in seven isolated branches: WETH, wstETH, rETH, weETH, WBTC, tBTC, and PAXG. Three are issuer-controlled tokens that can freeze addresses or be upgraded, and the documented response is to shut the affected branch down rather than freeze RD holders. Borrowers can pay a surcharge for Redemption Shield, which keeps their trove out of redemptions outside shutdown and gives unshielded troves on that branch a rate discount. Bad debt left after a shutdown is repaid from half of MOAI stakers' interest share, plus healthy branches' redemption fees and a 0.5% redemption surcharge, so MOAI stakers act as risk capital. None of it is deployed yet: the address registry reads TBD, the core repository is private, and the audits, part-funded by an August 2026 Ethereum Foundation subsidy, are still in progress. With no governance, admin keys or upgrade path, whatever configuration launches is permanent, so the pending audits carry the review burden.

eurr-revolut.title: The Neobank That Rented Its Own Coin
eurr-revolut.text: EURR is live, and Pharos tracks it pre-launch anyway. Revolut launched it on August 26 2026 as the first product of its stablecoin programme, in euro rather than the dollar or sterling tokens it had been expected to ship first, phased into Denmark, Poland and Portugal with wider EEA availability targeted later in 2026. The issuer is Bridge Building S.A., the Luxembourg arm of Stripe-owned Bridge, which holds the EMI licence and MiCA authorisation from the CSSF; Revolut Digital Assets Europe distributes the token under its CySEC MiCA licence. Revolut built the distribution and outsourced the balance sheet. Supply passed 1.67 million EURR in early September and stood near 1.69 million on October 25; the Polygon deployment holds three. Bridge's reserve page reports reserves equal to supply, held entirely as cash deposits at credit institutions, and the white paper commits to par {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} to an EEA IBAN within two business days. Ernst & Young issued a reasonable-assurance {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} on the reserves as of August 31 2026, though custodian names remain unpublished. No accepted price source resolves the token, and that missing price path is what keeps EURR outside the tracked set.

usdv-solomon-v2.title: Solomon’s Separate Reserve Dollar
usdv-solomon-v2.text: Solomon’s replacement USDv uses a new Solana mint and the Chancery program, with no automatic conversion from the original Ceffu-backed token. Its observed program reserves hold USDC and USDG, so holders depend on those stablecoin issuers as well as Solomon’s settlement controls. The reserve-account review identifies the assets in that selected scope; it does not establish a complete financial reconciliation or legal segregation for token holders. Direct minting and redemption require approved-counterparty onboarding, while ordinary holders rely on secondary-market liquidity. Privileged roles can change operating controls and freeze token accounts, and a separate delayed upgrade authority can replace program logic. Rewards require eligible participation and are separate from the token’s dollar peg. The central constraint is the gap between transferable on-chain balances and permissioned access to the underlying reserves.

usd-bank-consortium.title: The 21-Bank Consortium Dollar
usd-bank-consortium.text: On September 1 2026 twenty-one financial institutions led by Bank of America, Citi, Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank, Santander, and UBS announced they will found a joint company, name to be announced, to issue a dollar stablecoin spanning wholesale, institutional, and retail payments, with a euro token as the next priority. The company is to be established in H2 2026, subject to closing conditions, with market entry targeted for H1 2027 and GENIUS Act and MiCA compliance intended where applicable. The commitment extends exploration that began with ten banks in October 2025 around a 1:1 reserve-backed digital money for public blockchains. Everything Pharos measures is still absent: no company name, ticker, chain, contracts, reserve composition, custodian, or attestation. Until those land, this entry records intent by named institutions rather than a measurable issuer.

jpy-megabank-consortium.title: The Three-Megabank Yen
jpy-megabank-consortium.text: Japan's three largest banks said on June 10 2026 that they will jointly issue a yen stablecoin under a trust agreement, with MUFG, Mizuho, and SMBC as joint settlors and a trust bank or similar institution as trustee, and they aim to begin actual commercial transactions during fiscal year 2026, which ends in March 2027. A memorandum of understanding establishes a voluntary council to work through issuance infrastructure, schemes, and governance. On October 16 2026 the banks reported a July trial of that model, selected in November 2025 for the Financial Services Agency's FinTech Proof-of-Concept Hub, with Mitsubishi UFJ Trust and Banking as trustee, an SMBC-provided blockchain built by TISI, and Mitsubishi Corporation cross-border payments as the test case. The trial design holds trust assets in bank deposits, sets no issuance cap, and limits circulation to users verified by the banks; the release calls that design provisional. Nikkei reported the token would start yen-denominated on MUFG's Progmat platform with a dollar version to follow, though the banks name neither a production platform nor a chain. No ticker, production trustee, or reserve composition is public. The durable constraint is concentration: joint issuance rests on three systemically important banks and a trust structure still being settled.
